name: Hanjin Ligidi (Nigerian Lollipops)
description: A cone-shaped Nigerian confection similar to a lollipop, made from tamarind-soaked syrup poured into paper or foil cones and set on sticks. A sweet treat mostly enjoyed by children.
instructions: Shape food-safe paper or aluminum foil into cones.
Clean any dirt or dust from the tsamiya, then wash it in a clean bowl of water and drain thoroughly.
Soak the tsamiya in hot water for about 5 minutes.
Transfer the tsamiya soaking liquid to a pot over medium heat.
Gradually stir in sugar, making sure it dissolves, until it becomes very thick.
Stir in your desired flavoring and/or coloring.
Divide the syrup between the prepared cones, let cool slightly, then insert a toothpick or other stick.
Let set and harden completely, then unmold and serve.

name: Spicy Tomato Soup
description: A rich and creamy tomato soup blended with heavy cream and seasoned with a warming kick of cayenne and white pepper. Smooth, hearty, and perfect served hot.
instructions: In a blender or food processor, working in batches if necessary, puree tomatoes, cream, sugar, pepper, salt, garlic and cayenne.
Transfer soup to a saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until soup thickens, 20–30 minutes.
Serve hot.

name: Simple Boiled Chickpeas
description: Dried chickpeas are easy to prepare with a little patience, and they taste far better than the canned version. Simmered with celery, they make a versatile base for many dishes.
instructions: Cover the chickpeas completely with water, and let them soak overnight. Drain the chickpeas.
Combine the chickpeas and celery in a pot. Add enough water to completely cover the contents by a few inches.

Bring the pot to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for about 2 hours until the chickpeas are tender—the cooking time is not an exact science, and you will need to bite into a chickpea to see if it is fully cooked.
Once the chickpeas are done, drain the cooking liquid. If desired, you can reserve it to use as aquafaba.
Use the cooked chickpeas as you would canned chickpeas. Alternatively, you can season them with salt, pepper, and a dash of olive oil and vinegar if you would like to eat them plain.

name: Easy Nachos
description: Tortilla chips topped with melted cheddar cheese and optional green chiles and onion, baked until hot and bubbly.

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup (80 ml) chopped canned peeled green chiles (optional)
ingredients.name: green chile

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lay the tortilla chips on a cookie sheet.
Toss together the cheese, chilies and onion; sprinkle over the tortilla chips.
Bake for about 2 minutes, or until the cheese has melted.
Serve hot.

name: Vegemite Sandwich
description: A simple toasted sandwich layered with butter and Vegemite, with optional cheese and onion for a hearty breakfast or lunch.
instructions: Toast the bread slices.
Spread butter thickly and evenly on bread.
Spread Vegemite a little less thickly, and evenly on bread.
Add cheese and onion.

name: Atomic Fudge Cake
description: A rich chocolate cake with a thin, bubbly batter, layered and frosted with a warm dark chocolate fudge that soaks into the crumb. Served warm with ice cream for a heavenly dessert.

ingredients.text: 1 ¾ cups (415 ml) baking cocoa powder
ingredients.name: baking cocoa powder

instructions: Mix the dry ingredients well in a large bowl. For better texture, sift the dry ingredients together with a sieve or sifter.
Add the eggs, milk, vanilla, and vegetable oil, and mix well. Add the water, and mix it until it has a lot of little bubbles. This batter will be very thin.
Pour into two greased 9-inch round baking pans.

Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 30 minutes (about 20 minutes for a convection oven), or until a cake tester comes out clean. Remember not to over-bake the cake, as it may become really dry and lose all its moisture.
Cool the cakes completely, then unmold them.
Melt the chocolate by placing it in a double boiler.
Mix the sugar and cocoa together in a small bowl, then mix in the water.
Stir the sugar/cocoa/water mix into the melted chocolate.
Quickly stir in the cream and mix until it has a nice smooth consistency.

Immediately 'frost' the cake with this, making sure that there is quite a bit between the two layers of cake. The cake will need to be refrigerated to harden the fudge, so don't worry about its relatively liquid nature.
Refrigerate cake.
Serve warm after refrigeration. To serve, slice a piece and microwave it for about 20 seconds. It is heavenly as the fudge melts and soaks into the cake. Serve with ice cream if you so desire.

name: Adobo Chicken (Philippine)
description: Traditional Philippine adobo chicken simmered in vinegar and soy sauce with garlic and peppercorns, then seared until browned and coated with the reduced sauce.

ingredients.text: 6–8 chicken pieces, preferably legs and wings
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup (80 ml) vinegar made from coconut juice (as a variant, try balsamic vinegar)
ingredients.name: coconut vinegar

ingredients.text: ½ tsp (2.5 ml) freshly cracked (not ground) black peppercorns
ingredients.name: black peppercorn

instructions: Put chicken, garlic, peppercorn, soy sauce and vinegar in a pan and bring to a boil.
When chicken is cooked, put chicken pieces in a colander and drain. Put aside the pot with soy sauce and vinegar.
When chicken pieces are no longer draining, fry them in hot oil at medium heat. Have a cover ready for splatters.
Sear the chicken, browning on all sides.
Put chicken pieces back in the pot with soy sauce and vinegar and bring to simmer. Add 1–2 pieces of bay leaf.

Cook until the sauce has largely evaporated; some take this to an extreme and cook until the sauce has thickened and adhered to the chicken, which begins to make a popping noise due to the high, direct heat.
Serve over hot steamed rice. May be eaten with tomato slices in fish sauce, tapsilog, soy sauce, vinegar, hotdog, etc.

name: Chicken and Corn Empanadas
description: Baked turnovers filled with a savory mixture of chicken, corn, peppers, onions, and Monterey Jack cheese, wrapped in flaky crescent dough.

ingredients.text: Kosher salt and fresh ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.name: salt and black pepper

ingredients.text: 1 egg, lightly beaten with 1 tablespoon water
ingredients.name: egg

instructions: In large skillet, heat oil and lightly brown onions.
Add pepper, crushed red peppers, corn, and oregano. Cook 5 minutes over moderate heat or until liquid has mostly cooked away.
Remove from heat; stir in chicken and cheese, season to taste and chill.
Unroll crescent dough into two perforated squares. Place one square over second square. Roll out with a little flour to form a single large rectangular sheet.
Cut out four circles about 5 inches in diameter. Repeat with remaining package of rolls.
Refrigerate circles on waxed paper until firm, about 30 minutes.
Spoon ¼ cup filling into center of each circle, leaving a 1-inch border.
Brush edges with egg mixture. Fold over to seal, stretching dough slightly. Press edges together while pushing out any air pockets. Seal by crimping with the tines of a fork.
Brush top with egg wash. Prick with fork.
Arrange empanadas on buttered and floured baking sheet. Refrigerate until ready to bake, up to two days ahead of time.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until puffy and brown and filling is bubbling hot.

name: Pease Pudding
description: A traditional English dish of split yellow peas simmered with a ham hock until soft, then whisked with butter to a hummus-like consistency. Light yellow in colour with a mild taste, it is often served with ham and stottie cakes.

ingredients.text: 1 uncooked ham hock or ham joint (from a butcher shop)
ingredients.name: ham hock

instructions: Put the ham hock in a pressure cooker and cover with water. With the lid on, bring to the boil (full pressure).
Lower the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
Remove from the heat and release the pressure. Take out the hock and put to one side.
Add the split peas. With the lid on, bring back to the boil.
Lower the heat to a simmer (as low as possible) and simmer for 25–30 minutes.
Remove from the heat and release the pressure.
Put the contents into a bowl with the butter, and mix with a balloon type whisk.
Leave to cool.
Serve on white bread or stottie cake, alone or with ham from the hock. Refrigerate when cool.

name: Brazilian Shrimp and Cassava Sauce (Bobó de Camarao)
description: A rich Brazilian shrimp and cassava sauce with tomatoes, coconut milk, herbs, and olive and palm oils. The tender cassava is mashed into the sauce and served over Brazilian white rice.

ingredients.text: 6 medium tomatoes, peeled and seeded (or a large can of whole tomatoes)
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: ¼ cup palm oil (also known as dendê)
ingredients.name: palm oil

instructions: Peel and cut the manioc and put in a pan with cold water and salt.
Cook until tender, drain and reserve both the cooked manioc and the liquid.
Discard any manioc fiber.
Using a fork, mash the manioc while still hot. Use some of the liquid to help in the process. Do not use a blender or food processor.
Peel and de-vein the shrimp.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the olive oil until wilted.
Add ½ of the chopped cilantro and the tomatoes, stirring well.
Add the shrimp, and cook it for about 15 minutes.
Add the puréed manioc. Check the amount of liquid and add more of the reserved manioc liquid to thin the mixture, if necessary.
Add the coconut milk, the remaining cilantro and the palm oil.
Check for salt and pepper.
Serve over Brazilian white rice.

name: Smoky Tuna Melts
description: Smoky tuna and melted mozzarella cheese layered on white bread, then broiled until the cheese melts.

ingredients.text: 1 container (4.5 oz) hickory smoke-flavored albacore tuna
ingredients.name: tuna

instructions: Combine tuna, melted butter, and lemon juice.
Spread some of the tuna mixture on each slice of bread. Top with cheese.
Broil until the cheese is melted.

name: Salza Criolla (South American Onion Relish)
description: A refreshing South American onion relish made with finely sliced onion and lime, similar to salsa. It pairs well with toast, potatoes, seafood, meat, rice, tamales, and quesadillas.
instructions: Cleave the onion from top to bottom, along the grain, then slice it fine across the grain, forming half-rings.
Rinse in cold water, soak in cold water for around 5 minutes, and rinse again.
This procedure washes away the contents of the plant cells destroyed by the knife, taking the sting out of the onion's flavor.
Squeeze over it the juice of the lime.
Optionally toss in the cilantro, potatoes, beets, or avocado.

name: Quail Egg and Chili Jangjorim
description: A Korean jangjorim featuring quail eggs simmered in a savory soy sauce, sugar, rice wine, garlic, and ginger, then finished with dried red chile peppers.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the quail eggs, and boil for about 10 minutes.
Carefully drain the eggs, and cool in cold water.
Peel the cooled eggs.
Combine the water, soy sauce, sugar, wine, garlic, and ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Add the eggs to the pot, and simmer until the liquid is reduced by half.
Add the peppers, and cook just for 1–2 minutes.

name: Tres Leches Cake I
description: A classic Latin American sponge cake soaked in a sweet mixture of three milks and topped with a toasted meringue.

ingredients.text: ½ tsp cream of tartar (optional but used for stabilizing the egg whites; increasing their heat tolerance and volume)
ingredients.name: cream of tartar

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour cake pan.
Using a standing mixer with the whisk attachment, whip egg whites until frothy, slowly bringing the mixer to the fastest speed and stopping for a minute on each speed.
Slowly beat in the sugar and vanilla.
Mix in the egg yolks, and finally the flour.
Transfer batter to prepared cake pan, and bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven.
Remove cake and let cool to room temperature. Poke several holes in the cake.
Combine the condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream, and vanilla.
Heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly. The idea is just to bring all the flavors together, so don't overheat the milk.
Let the milk mixture cool to room temperature.
Slowly pour the milk mixture over the cake. Since you greased the cake pan the milk will flow around and under the cake. The cake will absorb most of the milk.
Place the egg whites in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment. Slowly bring the mixer to the fastest speed stopping for a minute or so on each speed.
Add the cream of tartar and slowly beat in the granulated sugar.
Spread the meringue on top of the cake.
Use a blowtorch or the oven broiler to gently toast the meringue. Once the meringue starts to change color you have a few seconds before it burns, so stay alert.

name: Mushroom Soup (Gabi Supa)
description: A creamy mushroom soup made with fresh mushrooms, bouillon, and noodles, finished with lemon juice and parsley.

ingredients.text: 1 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced if too big
ingredients.name: mushroom

ingredients.text: 2 cubes of mushroom base (bouillon) plus 1 cup of noodles OR 1 cube and 1 package of ramen-type mushroom noodle soup
ingredients.name: mushroom base

ingredients.text: The juice of ½–1 lemon, or to taste
ingredients.name: lemon juice

instructions: In a pot, fry the flour in the melted butter until slightly golden (about 3 minutes).
Add the water and stir until smooth.
Add the milk, the mushrooms, and the cube(s) of soup base.
Boil for less than 10 minutes or until the mushrooms are cooked but not soft.
Add the noodles and boil until cooked.
Take the pot off the burner, add the lemon juice, the parsley, and more milk if you like the soup to be less thick.

name: Cayenne Hot Sauce
description: A fiery, vinegar-based cayenne hot sauce with a bold kick, much like Tabasco.
instructions: Combine all ingredients.
Store indefinitely at room temperature in a squirt bottle.

name: Ful Medames (Egyptian Fava Beans)
description: A classic Egyptian breakfast and hearty street food made from slow-simmered fava beans with garlic, olive oil, lemon, and cumin. Rich in protein and fiber, it is served warm with fresh herbs and pita bread.

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
ingredients.name: parsley or cilantro

instructions: Rinse the dried fava beans under cold water and remove any impurities or debris. Place the beans in a saucepan and cover them with water.
Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low and let the beans simmer for about 1–1.5 hours, or until they are tender.
Check the beans periodically and add more water if needed.
Once the beans are tender, drain them in a colander and return them to the saucepan.

Add the minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper to the saucepan with the cooked beans. Stir well to combine the ingredients and allow the flavors to meld together over low heat for a few minutes.
Remove the ful medames from the heat and transfer it to a serving dish.
Garnish the dish with freshly chopped parsley or cilantro.
Serve the ful medames warm with fresh pita bread or other bread of your choice.

name: Tempura
description: A classic Japanese fried dish where meats, fish, and vegetables are dipped in a light batter and deep-fried until lightly golden.

ingredients.text: Oil for deep-frying (peanut oil is best)
ingredients.name: oil

instructions: Heat oil in a deep pan to 340–350°F (~171–176°C).
Beat the egg in a bowl and add ice cold water. Warmer water will produce a sticky batter and more oily tempura.
Add flour and mix lightly. Do not overmix batter—a few lumps actually improve the result, adding crispiness.
Dip meat or vegetables briefly in the batter, and fry until brown.
Remove from the oil and drain.
Serve hot.

name: Homemade Peanut Butter
description: Roasted peanuts are blended with vegetable and olive oils into creamy homemade peanut butter, with optional sugar and honey for sweetness.

ingredients.text: 1½ teaspoon vegetable oil, peanut oil or canola oil
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

instructions: Combine the peanuts and vegetable oil (peanut oil or canola oil) in a bowl.
Place tinfoil on a baking pan, and bake the peanuts at 200–350 °F for about 10 minutes.
Let peanuts cool.
Mix with olive oil. Process or blend for a while.
Add in sugar, honey and salt. Process or blend until you are satisfied.

name: Tropical Squares
description: A delicious tropical square with a coconut and crushed pineapple topping.
instructions: Stir together flour, sugar and baking powder using a wooden spoon.
Cut in the margarine until the mixture looks like fine crumbs.
In a small bowl, beat the egg well.
Mix into dry mixture using wooden spoon until combined.
Press into lined and lightly greased square tray.
Drain all of the juice out of the pineapple by wringing it in a cloth.
Add and mix remaining ingredients with the pineapple using a wooden spoon. Do not overwork it.
Spread evenly over base.
Bake at 350°F (180°C), or until topping is set and coconut is light brown.
Let cool before removing from pan.

name: Meatloaf III
description: A hearty baked meatloaf made with ground beef, eggs, crackers, onion, and tomato sauce, shaped like a football and served warm.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Pound the Ritz crackers until fine like bread crumbs.
In a separate bowl, add the meat and the other ingredients and mix with your hands until the mixture is smooth.
Grease a glass baking dish with vegetable shortening.
Put the meat mixture in the pan and shape like a football.
Bake in the oven for 1 hour.
Take out the meat loaf and serve warm.

name: Bean Soup (Vegetarian)
description: A savory bean soup made with fat-free vegetable broth, mixed vegetables, tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, and angel-hair pasta, seasoned with Italian seasoning and garlic powder. It is finished with grated Parmesan cheese and served immediately or simmered until ready to serve.

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup broken angel-hair pasta, in 1- to 2-inch lengths
ingredients.name: angel hair pasta

instructions: Pour broth and water into a 4½-quart Dutch oven or soup pot. Place pot over high heat.
While liquid is heating, add frozen vegetables, stewed tomatoes with their juices and uncooked pasta.
Cover pot and bring to boil.
Meanwhile, rinse and drain beans.
When soup comes to a boil, uncover it and stir well. Scrape the pot with a wooden spoon to loosen any pasta.
Add beans, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder.
Reduce heat to medium-high or medium, maintaining a moderate boil.
Stir frequently and cook until pasta is tender, about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and add Parmesan.
Stir occasionally and simmer for 5 minutes to develop the flavor.
Serve at once or simmer on low until ready to serve.

name: Chicken Cabbage Salad
description: A tasty chicken cabbage salad with cilantro, green onions, almonds, sunflower seeds, ramen noodles, and rice vinegar dressing. It works well as either a side salad or a main dish.

ingredients.text: 2 packages of ramen noodles, Oriental flavor
ingredients.name: ramen noodle

ingredients.text: ½ cup of vegetable or canola oil
ingredients.name: oil

ingredients.text: 1 packet of Oriental flavoring (from one of the ramen packages)
ingredients.name: flavoring

instructions: Chop the cabbage, cilantro leaves, and green onion until it is an even consistency among the three. Mix together.
Add the almonds and sunflower seeds.
Break up the ramen noodles and place in the salad.
Mix oil, rice vinegar, and flavoring. This is now your dressing.
Pour dressing over salad, and add salt and pepper to taste.
Leave salad to sit and absorb flavor for an hour for best taste.

name: Tchari (Jollof Rice)
description: A vibrant West African one-pot rice dish cooked in a rich tomato-based sauce infused with aromatic spices, peppers, and mixed vegetables. Perfect for gatherings, celebrations, and everyday feasting.

ingredients.text: 2–3 cups chicken or vegetable broth (or water)
ingredients.name: broth

ingredients.text: 1 cup frozen mixed vegetables (e.g. peas, carrots, corn)
ingredients.name: mixed vegetables

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until they become translucent.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot, and cook for about 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in the blended or finely chopped tomatoes, red and green bell peppers, and blended Scotch bonnet peppers. Cook the mixture for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate.
Add the thyme, curry powder, paprika, ground nutmeg, and bay leaf to the sauce. Stir well to ensure the spices are evenly distributed.
Rinse the rice thoroughly in cold water until the water runs clear. Drain the excess water.
Add the rice to the pot with the sauce, stirring gently to coat the rice with the flavorful mixture.
Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water) into the pot. The liquid level should be about 1 inch above the rice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot with the lid, ensuring it is tightly sealed to trap steam inside.

Let the rice simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until the rice is tender and fully cooked. Avoid opening the lid too frequently, as this may interfere with the cooking process. If the liquid is absorbed before the rice is fully cooked, add a little more water or broth as needed.
Once the rice is cooked, add the frozen mixed vegetables to the pot. Stir them gently into the rice.
Optionally, add a tablespoon of butter for extra richness. Stir it into the rice until it melts.
Remove the pot from the heat and let it sit, covered, for a few minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.

name: Jollof Couscous
description: A savoury couscous dish with bite-sized beef, colourful vegetables and a tomato sauce made with tomato paste and beef stock.

ingredients.text: Beef, cooked and in bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: Red and green bell peppers, chopped
ingredients.name: bell pepper

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a pan. Add chopped beef, and fry until golden brown. Set aside.
Add onions and carrots, and fry for a minute.
Add the chopped peppers and peas.
Add seasoning cubes and salt to taste.
Stir in the corn kernels.
Transfer the cooked vegetables to a plate, and set aside.
Heat some more oil in the same pan, and add the blended tomatoes.
Stir in the tomato paste, and fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in some beef stock or water.
Stir in the couscous, making sure the couscous is well-coated with the sauce. Cover with a lid, remove from the heat, and let rest until the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the cooked beef and cooked vegetables.
Serve.

name: Smokehouse Turkey Panini
description: A grilled panini layered with mesquite-smoked turkey, crispy bacon, and melted Monterrey Jack cheese between slices of white bread.
instructions: Assemble a sandwich with the turkey, bread, bacon, and cheese. Set aside.
Preheat 2-burner grill pan over medium high heat.
Brush both sides of sandwiches with oil then place on grill.
Cook until ingredients are heated through and bread is marked, turning as needed. Serve hot.

name: Samp and Beans
description: A hearty South African winter dish of samp (hominy) and dried beans simmered with braised meat, onions, and tomato, finished with butter. Often served with rice or buttered bread.

ingredients.text: 2 lb beef or mutton, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: beef

instructions: Add the samp and beans mix to a large pot. Rinse the mixture well, and half fill the pot with water.
Add salt and bring to a boil. Boil on low heat until the samp and beans are cooked. Drain and discard the cooking liquid.
In another pot, sauté the onions in a pot with oil.
When onions are cooked, add the meat and braise until tender.
Add grated tomato and the drained samp and beans mixture. Cook on low heat for about one hour and a half.
Season with salt and pepper. Before serving, add the butter and let it simmer.
Serve in a bowl with a side plate or buttered bread or rice.

name: Easy Pasta Sauce
description: An easy and tasty pasta sauce made with tomatoes, garlic, oregano, and fresh cream. It pairs well with pasta and a variety of vegetables, with quantities adjusted to taste.
instructions: Finely chop tomatoes or purée them in a food processor—this depends on what consistency you want. Chopping gives a chunkier sauce while using puréed tomatoes yields a smoother sauce.
Grind garlic to paste.
Heat oil in a frying pan. Using a pan with non-stick coating necessitates less oil.
When oil is hot (but not too hot), turn down heat and add garlic paste.
When garlic is golden-brown, add tomatoes.
Tomatoes have to be cooked until done—they'll look and smell cooked instead of raw, and will be a deeper, redder colour.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
When tomatoes are almost done, add fresh cream to taste. Cook for about 30 seconds.
Add oregano, then cook for another minute.
Add cooked pasta and vegetables.
Serve hot, garnished with herbs (e.g. basil, rosemary).

name: Mozzarella Sticks
description: Breaded mozzarella sticks are dipped in egg, coated in seasoned bread crumbs, and fried until the cheese is just beginning to ooze out.
instructions: Preheat deep fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Slice mozzarella into sticks 1–3 cm in diameter.
In a small bowl, whisk egg.
Fill another small bowl with bread crumbs.
Dip 3–4 sticks at a time into the egg.
Shake excess egg off sticks and place them in the bread crumbs.
Shake bowl of bread crumbs, evenly coating all sticks. Add more bread crumbs as needed.
Place coated sticks to the side and repeat for remaining sticks.
After all sticks have been coated, repeat the egg-dip and crumb-coat for each once more.
Place all sticks in fryer basket and submerge in 350°F oil.
Let sit for 30 seconds, gently rocking basket occasionally.
Lift basket and let cool for a few seconds.
If cheese is not beginning to ooze out from half the sticks, re-submerge in oil for another 10–15 seconds, gently shaking the basket.
Repeat until the cheese is just starting to ooze out.
Dump onto paper towel and pat off excess oil gently.
Serve hot.

name: Blueberry Pancakes
description: Blueberry pancakes made with a cinnamon-and-nutmeg buttermilk batter and served warm with your preferred topping.

ingredients.text: 1½ tsp cream of tartar (or baking powder)
ingredients.name: cream of tartar

instructions: Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, cream of tartar, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg. Set aside.
Whisk together buttermilk, butter and egg yolks in a large bowl.
Mix the flour mixture into the buttermilk mixture, then mix in the blueberries.
Whip egg whites in a small bowl until stiff, but do not let dry peaks form. Fold into the pancake batter.
Heat a large pan or griddle over medium heat. Lightly spray or brush with vegetable oil.
Ladle in a ¼ cup of batter for each pancake; cook until set and bubbly on the top.
Turn the pancake over, then cook for 1 more minute.
Serve warm with whatever topping you prefer.

name: Custard Creams
description: Custard creams are sandwich biscuits made with a soda-leavened dough and filled with thick custard.

ingredients.text: 200 g (7.1 oz / 1½ cups) plain flour, plus extra for dusting
ingredients.name: flour

ingredients.text: 80 g (2.8 oz / ⅔ stick) unsalted butter
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 125 g (4.4 oz / ⅝ cup) superfine sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: 180 g (6.3 oz / ¾ cup) thick custard, such as pastry cream
ingredients.name: custard

instructions: Combine the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter, sugar and vanilla in a mixing bowl until soft and fluffy.
Beat in the egg.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients, and bring together until a dough forms.
If the dough is too wet, mix in 1 tablespoon of plain flour.
Knead the dough for 2 minutes on a floured surface until smooth.
Shape the dough into a flat disc.
Cover with clingfilm and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C (374 °F).
Line 2 baking trays with parchment paper.
Roll out the dough to 5 mm (0.20 in) thick.
Cut out into 24 circles with a cookie cutter.
Transfer the biscuits to the prepared baking trays.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until well-cooked.
Place the biscuits on a wire rack and leave to cool completely.
Spoon 1 tablespoon of custard onto one biscuit. Sandwich it together with another biscuit.
Repeat the biscuit assembly, using remaining biscuits and custard.
Enjoy!

name: Grilled Portobello Mushrooms
description: Large portobello mushrooms brushed with olive oil and grilled until marked, perfect as a vegetarian entrée or a substitute for hamburger patties.
instructions: Remove the stems from the mushrooms, then wash and dry them.
Brush with olive oil.
Grill for about 10 minutes, alternating sides, until both sides are grill-marked.

name: Balsamic Dressing
description: A quick dressing made by whisking aged balsamic vinegar with extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper, then serving it over assorted salad greens.
instructions: Whisk together vinegar and seasonings.
Slowly whisk in oil.
Serve over assorted salad greens.

name: Classic American Apple Pie
description: A classic American double-crusted apple pie filled with sweetened and spiced Honeycrisp apples, brushed with reduced apple liquid for a glossy finish.

ingredients.text: 8 ounces cold butter, cut into ½-inch pieces
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 5–7 tbsp applejack (apple brandy) or hard cider
ingredients.name: applejack

ingredients.text: 6 Honeycrisp apples, peeled, cored, and cut into 12ths
ingredients.name: apple

ingredients.text: ¼ tsp freshly-ground grains of paradise
ingredients.name: grains of paradise

instructions: Combine dough ingredients to get a mealy dough. Split in half by weight, shape into 2 disks, and chill for 1 hour.
Toss apples with ¼ cup sugar and place in a colander set over a large bowl. Let drain for 1 ½ hours.
Transfer liquid from bowl into a saucepan, and bring to a boil over medium high heat. Cook until reduced to 2 tbsp. Set aside.
Toss apples with remaining filling ingredients. Set aside.
Roll out both disks of crust into rough circles. Place one inside a 9 ½–10-inch tart pan and attach.

Add apples to the crust in a concentric circle, starting from the outside and working to the inside, making the center slightly taller than the outside. Pour any liquid in the bottom of the bowl over the apples.
Top with the second sheet of dough, and seal the edges. Crimp the edges if desired, then snip 3 incisions in the center. Brush top with reduced apple liquid.
Bake at 425°F on the floor of the oven in a half sheet pan lined with parchment for 30 minutes. Transfer to the lower rack, and bake for another 20 minutes.
Remove and cool for 4 hours. Serve.

name: Nigerian Egg Pepper Soup
description: A popular Nigerian soup combining eggs, peppers, and aromatic spices for a rich and warming meal. Quick and easy to prepare, it is a satisfying dish with bold flavors.

ingredients.text: 2 bell peppers (red, green, or a combination), thinly sliced
ingredients.name: bell pepper

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper (adjust to your preferred spice level)
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper

ingredients.text: Fresh cilantro or parsley, for garnish (optional)
ingredients.name: cilantro

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and minced garlic, and sauté until the onions become translucent and slightly golden.
Add the sliced bell peppers and chopped tomatoes to the saucepan. Cook for a few minutes until the vegetables start to soften.
In a separate bowl, crack the eggs and whisk them until well-beaten. Set aside.

Add the chicken or vegetable broth to the saucepan with the vegetables. Stir in the ground cayenne pepper, paprika, cumin, and coriander. Season with salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Slowly pour the beaten eggs into the simmering soup, stirring gently with a wooden spoon or spatula in one direction. This will create thin strands of cooked egg throughout the soup.
Continue cooking the soup for about 3–4 minutes, allowing the egg to cook and thicken the soup slightly.
Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning if needed. Add more salt or spices according to your preference, then remove from the heat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro or parsley if desired.

name: Papadam (Black Gram Flatbread)
description: A traditional Indian and Sri Lankan flatbread made from black gram flour seasoned with cracked black pepper and cumin, dried in the oven, then fried until crisp and golden.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup water (or more if needed)
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Mix together the flour, pepper, cumin, and salt.
Add water and knead the dough until it is smooth. You may have to add some water, depending on the flour.
Split the dough into 10–15 balls.
Roll out one ball at a time to a very thin round layer on a slightly oiled surface.
Dry the papadams in the oven for an hour (at about 100°C or 200°F).
Keep them in an airtight container.
Fry the papadams in oil until they are crispy but not too brown.

name: Jalapeno Glazed Seared Salmon
description: Spicy seared Coho salmon filets brushed with a jalapeño and chicken broth paste, pan-seared on all sides and finished with a reserved chile glaze.

ingredients.text: 2 ea. (12 ounces) Coho or silver salmon filets
ingredients.name: salmon filet

instructions: Pulse chiles with broth in a food processor until a thick paste is formed. Set aside a small amount from the rest.
Brush salmon filets on all sides with chile mixture. Sprinkle liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper, and discard the chile mixture used to brush it.
Heat oil in a large nonstick pan over medium heat. Place salmon filets and cook, skin side up, 1½ minutes.
Turn on one of the smaller sides and cook 1 minute. Flip onto one of the bigger sides and cook 1½ minutes. Again, turn onto the uncooked smaller side and cook another 1 minute.
Remove to a plate and brush all sides liberally with reserved chile mixture. Cover with foil and let rest 5 minutes before serving with clean chile sauce.

name: Fattoush
description: A Lebanese salad for hot weather, combining romaine, vegetables, fresh herbs, and purslane with a lemony sumac dressing, served with toasted pita.

ingredients.text: 1 head romaine lettuce, torn into bite-size pieces
ingredients.name: romaine lettuce

ingredients.text: ¼ cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.name: parsley

ingredients.text: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
ingredients.name: bell pepper

ingredients.text: 4 pita rounds, toasted and torn into pieces
ingredients.name: pita bread

instructions: Mix the water and cornstarch in a small saucepan over medium-high heat until thickened.
Remove from heat, and mix in lemon juice, garlic, sumac, salt, and pepper.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a large bowl, toss together the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, green onions, parsley, mint, bell pepper, purslane, and arugula.
Toss with the dressing, and serve with pita.

name: Henry Thiele's Pancake
description: A classic German-style pancake from a historic Portland restaurant, baked in the oven after pan-frying and finished with lemon juice, maple syrup, and powdered sugar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F.
Combine milk, salt, and sugar. Mix in flour gradually. Mix in eggs.
For each pancake, melt 2 Tbsp butter in a pan. Pour about 1¼ cups batter into melted butter. While batter is frying gather up the batter in some places to make ridges.
When batter is consistency of medium scrambled eggs, put into oven for 5 minutes.
Remove from oven; flip pancake in pan; replace into oven for another 2.5 minutes.
Remove from oven; add generous amount of lemon juice and small amount maple syrup. Roll pancake into a cigar shape. Add lemon juice, maple syrup, and powdered sugar in that order. Eat.

name: Butter Tart
description: A classic Canadian dessert featuring a flaky pastry shell filled with a sweet, gooey mixture of brown sugar, corn syrup, currants, and walnuts.

ingredients.text: 3 ½ cups pastry flour or 3 cups all-purpose flour
ingredients.name: pastry flour

instructions: Beat the shortening, butter, and hot water together until creamy.
While still warm, sift in the flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix gently until a dough forms. Try not to knead it while forming it into a large ball.
Separate the dough into two equal portions and chill 20 to 40 minutes.
Divide the dough into two dozen equal balls. Roll each ball into a flat disc.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175˚C).
Beat the eggs well. Add sugar, syrup, and melted butter and beat again.
Add the currants, walnuts, vinegar, salt, and vanilla extract and mix vigorously.
Put a small amount of cornmeal into small tartlet pans, or count out 24 cupcake papers.
Fit the flat circles of pie crust into the pans, or fit them into cupcake papers and insert them into the pans.
Fill the shells ⅔ full with the prepared filling.
Bake until the pastry is light brown (about 20 minutes).
Remove from the oven and let cool.

name: Spicy Cheddar Dip with Olives
description: A rich, filling dip of spicy cheddar, black olives, and green chiles, served with golden pita chips for parties or game-day snacking.

ingredients.text: 8 oz (225 g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded or diced very small
ingredients.name: cheddar cheese

ingredients.text: 3 oz (80 g ) black olives, sliced into rings
ingredients.name: black olive

ingredients.text: 4 oz (110 g) canned diced green chiles
ingredients.name: green chile

ingredients.text: 2 green onions, cut into ¼-inch pieces
ingredients.name: green onion

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp garlic powder, or to taste
ingredients.name: garlic powder

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp hot sauce, or to taste
ingredients.name: hot sauce

instructions: Slice pitas as you would a pizza, into triangles. Separate pita triangles into halves, and place on a cookie sheet, inside surface up.
Toast in oven until golden brown, but not dark and bitter. This results in novel chips used to scoop the dip.
Combine the cheese, mayonnaise, chiles, half the olives, garlic powder, and hot sauce.
Microwave on high until the edges liquefy and bubble, then mix until everything is of the same consistency. Repeat this process until the whole bowl is creamy and a rich orange color.

Garnish the dip with the remaining olives, green onions, and tomatoes. Standard garnishing technique calls for arranging the remaining black olives, green onions, and diced tomatoes into a bulls-eye pattern.
Serve the dip with the pita chips.

name: Broccoli Salad
description: A creamy broccoli salad with crisp bacon, sweet onion, raisins, and nuts, chilled overnight for serving at potlucks.

ingredients.text: 7–8 slices of crisp fried bacon, crumbled (smoked bacon works well)
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: 1 red or sweet onion, chopped (Vidalia are recommended)
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: 1 cup (80 g / 2.8 oz) raisins, plumped in boiling water
ingredients.name: raisin

ingredients.text: ½ cup (110 g / 3.9 oz) granulated sugar (or equivalent artificial sweetener)
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: ½ cup (40 g / 1.4 oz) pecans or sunflower seeds
ingredients.name: pecans

ingredients.text: dash of cider vinegar or lemon juice
ingredients.name: cider vinegar

instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, sugar, and vinegar together.
Mix the remaining ingredients and combine completely in a large bowl.
Cover and cool in the refrigerator overnight before serving.

name: Watergate Salad
description: A creamy, fruity dessert salad combining crushed pineapple, pistachio pudding, mandarin oranges, marshmallows, and whipped cream. Best chilled overnight for the flavors to meld.

ingredients.text: 2 small cans of mandarin oranges, drained
ingredients.name: mandarin oranges

ingredients.text: 1 large tub whipped cream or Cool Whip
ingredients.name: whipped cream

instructions: Combine the crushed pineapple and juice with the pudding mix in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in the marshmallows and mandarin oranges.
Fold in whipped cream, and refrigerate overnight.

name: Puri
description: A traditional Indian fried flatbread made with whole-wheat flour, semolina, and white flour, puffed up golden and crispy. Perfect as a snack or accompaniment to a main dish.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp vegetable oil for the dough
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

ingredients.text: About 500 ml (1 pint) vegetable oil for deep frying
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

instructions: Put all the dry ingredients into a bowl.
Add salt and drizzle the 1 tbsp oil over top. Mix well.
Gradually mix in enough water to get a stiff dough.
Knead the dough well for a few minutes.
Cover the dough and leave to rest for about half an hour.
Pour the oil for deep frying in a wok or other deep pan. Heat the oil.
Meanwhile, divide the dough into 8 small balls and roll each into a small circle (about 3 in / 7.5 cm in diameter). You can use a bit of hot oil to roll the dough so it will not stick to the surface.
Check if the oil is hot enough—when you put a tiny piece of dough in the oil it should immediately rise to the surface.
When the oil is ready, lay the flattened dough over the oil, press the top slightly with the slotted spoon until it inflates itself, and turn to other side. Adjust the flame as necessary.
Remove the puri from the oil after it turns golden brown and place on a wire rack or kitchen paper towel for excess oil to drain.

name: New Orleans Style Chicken Wing Dipping Sauce
description: A tangy Creole-style dipping sauce that blends chunky blue cheese dressing with Creole mustard, scallions, and Creole seasoning. Best served chilled alongside chicken wings or fresh vegetables.

ingredients.text: 1 jar (12 ounces) of refrigerated chunky blue cheese dressing
ingredients.name: blue cheese dressing

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup scallions, finely chopped (reserve a teaspoon of chopped green tops for garnish)
ingredients.name: scallion

instructions: Combine all ingredients and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving (overnight is preferable).
Garnish with the reserved scallions.

name: Spicy Black Beans
description: A quick, spicy side dish of black beans tossed with chile oil, soy sauce, and Thai bird chile. Serve warm as a side or cool as a salad.

ingredients.text: 2 cups canned black beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: black bean

instructions: Heat both oils in a large skillet over medium high heat.
Add all remaining ingredients and toss; cook just until heated through.
Serve immediately as a side dish, or cool slightly and serve as a salad.

name: Homemade Paneer
description: Fresh paneer made by coagulating milk with lemon juice or vinegar, then pressing and chilling the curds until firm.
instructions: Bring milk to a boil in a large pan.
Just before the milk starts to boil, add the lemon juice or vinegar to coagulate the milk.
Pour the coagulated milk through a cheese cloth to discard most of the water within.
Press the water out firmly and place a weight on top of the paneer.
Allow to rest and harden for 2–3 hours in the refrigerator.

name: Steamed Pork With Mustard Greens
description: A classic Hakka Chinese dish of pork tenderloin and mustard greens, marinated in soy sauce and rice wine, then stir-fried with black bean and garlic sauce.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp cornstarch combined with 1 tsp cold water
ingredients.name: cornstarch

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp black bean and garlic sauce
ingredients.name: black bean and garlic sauce

instructions: Wash greens and discard tough stems.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add greens, and cook for 2 minutes.
Drain greens and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking. Drain again, then cut greens into long diagonal strips.
In a medium bowl, combine cornstarch and water. Stir in sugar, soy sauce and rice wine. Cut pork into thin slices and add to the mixture. Marinate about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Heat oil in a preheated wok or large heavy skillet over medium heat. Add black bean sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add mustard greens and water. Mix well and simmer gently about 4–5 minutes, until pork is cooked through and greens are tender.
Season with pepper and serve.

name: Consommé
description: A clear consommé made from chicken, veal, or beef stock, clarified with egg whites and finished with Madeira, port, or cognac.

ingredients.text: 1 quart (950 ml) chicken, veal, or beef stock
ingredients.name: stock

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup (85 ml) Madeira, port, or cognac
ingredients.name: wine

instructions: Having degreased the stock thoroughly, taste it for seasoning and add salt if necessary.
If the consommé is to be served cold, over-salt it slightly as more salt is needed for a cold dish.
Beat 1 cup of stock with the egg whites in a large bowl.
Bring the rest of the stock to a simmer in the saucepan.
While beating the egg white mixture, gradually pour the hot stock into the egg white mixture in a thin stream.
Pour the stock back into the saucepan and bring back to a simmer over medium heat. While it is heating, stir it with a wire whisk.
As soon as the stock reaches a simmer, stop stirring.
Move the pot to the edge of the flame, and continue heating over a low flame for 5 minutes.
Turn the pot a quarter turn and heat for 5 minutes, then turn again after 5 minutes, and once again for a final 5 minutes.
Line a colander with the dampened cheesecloth and place it over the bowl.
Carefully ladle the stock and egg whites into the colander, agitating the egg whites as little as possible.
When finished, allow it to drain for 5 or 6 minutes.
Remove the colander and stir the wine or cognac into the consommé.

name: Ghraiba bil Loz (Libyan Almond Ghraiba)
description: Delicate, crumbly Libyan almond cookies with a rich almond flavor that melts in your mouth. They are a festive treat, perfect for serving with a cup of tea or coffee.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
In a mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the flour, ground almonds, and vanilla extract to the butter mixture. Mix until well combined and a soft dough forms.
Pinch off small portions of the dough and roll them into balls about the size of a walnut. Place the balls on the prepared baking sheet, leaving some space between them.
Press a whole almond into the center of each cookie ball, gently flattening the cookies slightly.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12–15 minutes, or until the edges of the cookies turn golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Potatoes Excaloped
description: A classic preparation of boiled and mashed potatoes shaped in ramekins, topped with breadcrumbs and melted butter, then baked until golden on both sides.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain.
Mash the potatoes well.
Grease small pans or ramekins with butter, and divide the mashed potatoes between them. Smooth the tops.
Make a cross in the top of the potatoes, and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Use a brush to sprinkle with a few drops of melted butter.
Bake in the oven until browned on top. Carefully remove the potatoes from the molds, and bake to brown the other side.
Serve hot.

name: Puttu (Steamed Rice Flour and Coconut)
description: A Kerala breakfast made with rice flour and grated coconut, steamed and served with chickpea curry, chicken curry, boiled green gram, pappad, or steamed bananas.
instructions: Grate the coconut flesh finely.
Mix the puttu powder and salt in a wide bowl. Add half of the grated coconut.
Rub the mixture with your fingertips, sprinkling in water until it is moist and develops a coarse texture.
Leave the mixture for an hour if the flour is ready made, as it absorbs more water.
Check the consistency of the flour. One should be able to make a ball out of the flour that can be easily crumbled. Adjust the water content accordingly.
Spread a little coconut over the bottom of the puttu vessel (puttu kutti), and fill it with the moist flour. Layer it with coconut.
Steam it on the puttu vessel or on the pressure cooker nozzle.
In a few minutes, steam will start escaping through the top of the puttu vessel. It will be done in 4 minutes.
Serve hot with kadala curry, boiled green gram and pappad (payarum pappadavum), or with steamed bananas.

name: Desert Rubbed Strip Steaks
description: New York strip steaks are rubbed with cumin, coriander, rosemary, red pepper, salt, black pepper, and ginger, then grilled and rested for a robust finish.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24–32 ounces) New York strip steaks, 1–1¼ inches thick
ingredients.name: New York strip steak

instructions: Brush steak with olive oil. Set aside.
Combine seasonings in a small bowl. Pat mixture into both sides of steaks and refrigerate as long as possible.
Preheat kettle grill with a chimney starter. Add steaks and cook about 4–5 minutes per side for medium rare, or to desired doneness.
Remove steaks to a plate and cover tightly with aluminum foil. Let rest about 5 minutes before serving.

name: Pasta with Sausage
description: Spaghetti and sausages are boiled together, then tossed with butter or oil and pasta sauce or ketchup.
instructions: Bring 2 liters water to a boil, and add salt.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add sausages to pasta, and boil for 5 minutes.
Drain the water. Add butter to the pasta, then mix in sauce or ketchup, and serve.

name: Not Quite Eggs Benedict
description: A breakfast of beaten egg whites, bacon, and a thick lemon-butter sauce, served with warm crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Separate the eggs. Mix the whites with milk and parsley, then add salt and pepper. Beat with a fork until slightly bubbly. Set aside.
Cook the bacon on medium-high heat in a large, nonstick skillet and set on paper towels or napkins to drain.
Pour off all but 1–2 tablespoons of fat. Turn the heat down to medium-low and add the egg whites.

As the egg whites cook, mix the egg yolks with water in a double boiler over medium to medium-high heat. The water in the double boiler should simmer, not boil. Stir constantly with a fork until the yolks increase in size and thickness and turn a pale, opaque yellow.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in the melted butter. Then add lemon juice, salt, and cayenne pepper to taste.
Place the cooked egg whites on a plate, top with bacon, then cover with Hollandaise sauce. Serve with warm crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.

name: Spice Rubbed Grilled Chicken Breast
description: Boneless chicken breasts coated in Dijon mustard and a bold spice rub of smoked and sweet paprika, cayenne, rosemary, cinnamon, and lemon peel, then grilled over charcoal for a smoky, flavorful finish.
instructions: Combine paprikas, salt, pepper, rosemary, cayenne, cinnamon, and lemon peel. Set aside.
Rub mustard all over chicken. Apply seasoning mixture, and press lightly to aid adhesion.
Grill on a preheated charcoal grill, turning often, until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove and let rest for 3 minutes. Serve.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
description: Crispy oven-roasted Brussels sprouts tossed in olive oil and seasoned simply with salt and pepper, browned to tender perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Trim the bases of the sprouts, discard any loose outer leaves, and wash and dry them.
Halve the sprouts with a sharp knife—you can quarter any really big ones—and transfer them to a mixing bowl.
Drizzle the sprouts with some olive oil and toss to coat. You should add enough oil so that all the sprouts are thinly coated, but not so much that they're dripping with oil.
Season the sprouts with a pinch of salt and pepper. Don't over-salt them, as the sprouts will lose water in the oven.
Spread the sprouts on baking sheets so that they're all in a single layer—double-layering them will cause them to steam not brown.

Roast the sprouts in the oven until they are browned on the outside and tender to your preference. Use a spatula to stir/flip them periodically through the cooking process to make sure they brown evenly.
Remove from the oven and adjust the seasoning to taste.

name: Garbanzo Bean Stew
description: Garbanzo bean stew with red pepper, saffron, paprika, potatoes, and tomatoes, served over hot rice.

ingredients.text: 1 red bell pepper, peeled, cored and chopped
ingredients.name: red bell pepper

ingredients.text: ½ pound new or boiling potatoes, unpeeled and cut into bite-sized chunks
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 2 teaspoons smoked sweet paprika (such as Pimenton de la Vera)
ingredients.name: paprika

ingredients.text: 2 cups cooked chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained or 1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: chickpea

ingredients.text: 1 can (14½ ounces) diced tomatoes plus their liquid
ingredients.name: tomato

instructions: In a Dutch Oven or large soup pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Sauté onion, red pepper, garlic, saffron, and potatoes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes start to soften, about 15 minutes.
Stir in paprika, then sherry and cook about 1 minute.
Add chickpeas, tomatoes, stock, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and cook partially covered until potatoes are tender and stew thickens, 30–40 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand about 15 minutes to meld flavors and thicken slightly.
To serve, make a pyramid of rice in the center of each of 4 bowls, then ladle hot stew around rice.
Garnish with parsley, if desired.

name: Adalu (Bean and Corn Porridge)
description: A hearty Nigerian porridge of beans and corn, seasoned with pepper, onion and palm oil. Known as Ẹwa ati Agbado in Yoruba and Agwa na oka in Igbo, it is traditionally served with bread and garri.
instructions: Pick over the beans to remove dirt and stones.
Boil water. Add the corn, and cook until the corn becomes soft.
Add the cleaned beans to the cooked corn, and allow both to boil together.
After few minutes of cooking, add all remaining ingredients.
Smash everything together, then allow it to cook for like five minutes. Add any of the optional ingredients, if using.
Serve with bread and garri.

name: Maharashtrian Deep Fried Chickpea Dough Curry Snacks (Pakoda)
description: Crisp, golden-brown pakoda made with sliced onions, green chiles, and a spiced gram-flour dough, served hot with green chutney or tomato ketchup.

ingredients.text: 2–3 green chiles, washed and finely diced
ingredients.name: green chile

instructions: Combine onions and chiles. Mix in salt, and let sit 10–15 minutes.
Mix in turmeric, chili powder, cumin, and coriander.
By this time, the onion mix should be moist due to added salt and spices. If a moister mix is required, allow it to stand another 5 minutes.
Start adding gram flour to the onion mix a little at a time. The mixture should not be dry.
Add the flour just to absorb the moistness. You should end up with a somewhat sticky mixture.
Heat sufficient oil in a wok or frying pan.
Once heated sufficiently, carefully take around 2–3 tbsp of hot oil and add to the onion and gram flour mix. Mix well.
Drop a few small to medium chunks of dough at a time in the medium hot oil.
Fry until it gets a golden brown colour.
If you have used 4–5 large onions and a medium wok, you are likely to need 3–4 batches of frying to finish the mixture.
Serve hot with green chutney or tomato ketchup.

name: Steak and Kidney Pudding
description: A hearty steak and kidney pudding layered with seasoned meat and kidneys, encased in suet crust and slowly boiled for at least four hours.
instructions: Cut the steak into about 2.5 cm (1 inch) squares. Cut each kidney into 8 pieces.
Line the basin with crust, leaving a small piece of crust to overlap the edge.
Cover the bottom with a piece of the steak and a few pieces of kidney; season with salt and pepper, then add another layer of steak, kidney and seasoning.
Continue layering the steak, kidney and seasoning until the basin is full.
Pour in sufficient water to come within 5 cm (2 inch) of the top of the basin.
Moisten the edges of the crust, cover the pudding over, press the two crusts together so that the gravy does not escape, and turn up the overhanging pastry.
Wring out a cloth in hot water, flour it and tie up the pudding; put it into boiling water and let it boil for at least 4 hours.
If the water diminishes, always replenish with hot water from a jug, as the pudding should be kept covered all the time and not allowed to stop boiling.
When the cloth is removed, cut out a round piece in the top of the crust to prevent the pudding bursting.
Send it to table in the basin, either in an ornamental dish or with a napkin pinned round it. Serve quickly.

name: Boiled Chicken with Broth
description: Tender chicken is slowly boiled in seasoned water with rice or barley, then served with fresh parsley, clarified butter, and hot broth.
instructions: Cut the chicken into quarters and place in a large pot with the water, rice, and salt.
Bring the pot to a slow boil, removing any scum that rises to the surface.
Cook until the chicken is thoroughly done.
Remove the chicken and place in a serving dish. Garnish with parsley.
Strain the broth.
Serve the chicken with clarified butter and the hot broth on the side.

name: Benachin (Gambian Rice with Meat and Vegetables)
description: A flavorful and vibrant Gambian one-pot rice dish loaded with tender meat, colorful vegetables, and aromatic spices. This hearty and versatile meal is a staple in Gambian cuisine, perfect as a main course or side.

ingredients.text: 500 g chicken, beef, or fish, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: 1 cup chopped vegetables (such as green beans, peas, or corn)
ingredients.name: mixed vegetables

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot or saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and minced garlic. Sauté until they become translucent and fragrant.
Add the chicken, beef, or fish to the pot and cook until browned on all sides. Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, thyme, and curry powder. Cook for a few minutes to enhance the flavors.
Add the diced bell peppers, carrot, and other chopped vegetables of your choice. Stir well to combine.
Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain the excess water.
Add the rice to the pot and stir until it is well-coated with the vegetable and meat mixture.
Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Avoid stirring the rice during this time to prevent it from becoming mushy.
Once the rice is cooked, gently fluff it with a fork.
Taste the benachin and season with salt and pepper according to your preference.
Serve hot as a main course or as a side dish alongside grilled meat or fish.

name: South Indian Millet Swallow (Mudde)
description: A compact ball swallow made from finger millet, a lunchtime staple of rural South India that provides long-lasting energy. Traditionally eaten by dipping pieces in a watery sauce and swallowing without chewing.
instructions: Boil the water in a pot, add a little of the flour to make a paste, then add the rest of the flour.
Stir once with the handle of a wooden spoon and leave it in the pot.
Keep on low heat for about 10 minutes until it smells cooked.

Stir until the mixture turns dark reddish-brown. Once it begins to leave the sides of the pot, remove the pot from the fire and stir vigorously for 5–10 minutes—it's hard work, but the longer you keep at it, the lighter it will be.
Pull the mixture out and form into balls of about fist size.

name: Pie Floater
description: A traditional South Australian dish featuring a meat pie served upside down in a bowl of pea soup, popular as a late-night snack for revelers.
instructions: Heat the pie in an oven. A microwave will not work as well, as the pie pastry will not be crisp.
Heat the pea soup separately.
Place the pie upside down in the dish, and pour the pea soup around it until the dish is full.

name: Pot Stickers
description: Traditional Chinese dumplings with a filling of your choice, pan-fried until the bottoms are lightly browned and then steamed in the pan.
instructions: Begin with your filling.
Brush a gyoza wrapper with a little water around the edges.
Put 1 tablespoon of filling into the center of the wrapper.
Bring the sides of the wrapper together, with the filling contained inside.
Pinch one side of the wrapper into small folds, working down both sides, until a familiar pot sticker shape results.
When finished with the folds, the pot sticker should be fully sealed.
Uncooked potstickers can be stored in the refrigerator for a day, or in the freezer for weeks or months, before cooking.
Pan-fry the pot stickers in a little oil.
Fry the pot stickers a few minutes until the bottoms look slightly browned.
Pour in ½ cup water.
Steam the pot stickers, covered, until the water cooks away (5–10 minutes).
Your pot stickers are now ready to eat. Enjoy!

name: Yetsom Shiro (Ethiopian Vegan Chickpea Stew)
description: A flavorful and hearty Ethiopian stew made with ground chickpeas and a blend of aromatic spices like berbere, turmeric, and cumin. This vegan dish is traditionally enjoyed as a main course with injera or rice.

ingredients.text: 1 cup chickpea flour (also known as besan or gram flour)
ingredients.name: chickpea flour

ingredients.text: ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper

ingredients.text: Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped, for garnish
ingredients.name: cilantro

instructions: In a dry medium-sized saucepan, toast the chickpea flour over medium heat for a few minutes until it becomes fragrant and lightly browned. Remove from heat and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, paprika, turmeric, cumin, cayenne pepper, and salt. Mix well to coat the onions and garlic with the spices.
Add the toasted chickpea flour to the saucepan and stir to combine it with the spice mixture.
Gradually add the vegetable broth or water to the saucepan, stirring continuously to prevent lumps from forming.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the stew for about 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpea flour is fully cooked and the stew has thickened to your desired consistency.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt or additional spices if desired.
Remove from heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve hot as a main course, accompanied by injera or rice.

name: African Cabbage Stew
description: A hearty, nutritious stew of cabbage, potatoes, and carrots simmered with aromatic seasonings in a savory broth. Easy to prepare and packed with wholesome vegetables.
instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the neatly chopped onions and cook until tender for about 2 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and celery and cook until fragrant.
Add the cabbage, potatoes, carrots, Italian seasonings, onion powder, garlic powder, bouillon cubes, smoked paprika, and water. Cover the saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let simmer for about 20 minutes.
Check the seasonings and adjust where necessary.
Remove and serve warm with any complimentary dish of your choice.

name: Liberian Butter Rice
description: Liberian butter rice is a rich, flavorful and comforting dish made with long-grain rice, onion, garlic and butter. The fluffy rice pairs well with a variety of proteins and vegetables.

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain the rice and set it aside.
In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
Stir in the drained rice and coat it well with the buttery mixture.
Pour in the broth and add the bay leaf to the pot.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pot with the lid and let the rice simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is cooked and fluffy.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the rice rest for a few minutes before fluffing it with a fork.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro before serving.

name: Stovetop Mac n' Cheese
description: A creamy stovetop macaroni and cheese that blends Fontina, Gruyere, Cheddar, and Monterey Jack with egg yolk for extra richness.

ingredients.text: 1 cup each shredded mild Cheddar, Gruyere, Fontina, and Monterey Jack cheese
ingredients.name: cheese

instructions: Heat 1 gallon water to a rolling boil. Add salt and macaroni, and cook macaroni until al dente.
While pasta boils, melt butter in a saucepan or a saucier over medium low heat, and cook until bubbling ceases.
Whisk in flour and cook, whisking continuously, until blonde color is achieved.
Temper in egg yolk. Add cheese and bring to just below a simmer. Cook, whisking continuously, until slightly thickened.
Fold in macaroni and serve warm.

name: Pork Chops Cacciatore
description: Boneless pork chops are browned and simmered in a tomato sauce with garlic, onion, and carrot, then served over polenta.

ingredients.text: 6 ea. (1 kg) 4 cm thick boneless pork chops
ingredients.name: pork chop

ingredients.text: 1 can (28 oz) tomatoes, preferably "fire roasted" or similar
ingredients.name: tomato

instructions: Slice onion into 1 cm half-rings. Start making the polenta.
Once the polenta is stable, sweat onions with olive oil and butter.
When onions are translucent, clear spaces for the pork chops and put the pork chops into these spaces.
Lightly brown the pork chops on both sides, remove from pan, and set aside.
Allow fond to develop slightly, then deglaze with a quarter of the tomatoes.
Grind the rest of the tomatoes along with the garlic in a blender until a rough paste is formed. Add to the onion mixture.
Turn heat to high and allow the sauce to simmer and darken slightly in color. When this occurs, turn heat to low.
Finely chop the carrot and stir it in.
Nestle the pork chops into the sauce and allow to simmer until the pork chops are done to your liking, about 20 minutes or so.
Serve as soon as possible. To serve, spoon polenta onto plates or bowls and place pork chop and sauce on top.

name: Ugali (Maize Porridge)
description: A staple Kenyan and Tanzanian porridge-like dish made by cooking maize meal in water until thick, served hot with stews or saucy dishes.

ingredients.text: 4 cups white cornmeal or ground maize
ingredients.name: cornmeal

instructions: Boil the water in a saucepan.

Add salt if desired, and pour the corn flour slowly into boiling water, stirring continuously. Try to mash up any lumps that do form—the aim is to get a smooth consistency. A whisk makes this easier, as does sifting the flour.
Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until it has the consistency of thick oatmeal.
Serve hot ugali immediately with any meat or vegetable stew, or any dish with a sauce or gravy.

name: Whole Wheat Pancakes (Vegan)
description: Fluffy whole wheat pancakes made with soy milk and a touch of cinnamon, cooked on a lightly oiled griddle until golden brown on both sides.
instructions: Mix together flour, baking powder, and sugar.
Mix soy milk into the dry mixture.
Heat a griddle until water sprinkled on it quickly evaporates. Spread a thin film of oil on the griddle.
Pour pancake batter on griddle to form 2–3-inch circles. Bubbles should start forming.
When the underside is light brown, flip the pancake.
When the other side is light brown, serve.

name: Cheese Spread on French Bread
description: A creamy cheddar and cream cheese spread flavored with Dijon mustard, sage, and pepper, served on sliced French bread.

ingredients.text: 1 loaf French bread, cut in small slices
ingredients.name: French bread

instructions: In a large bowl, mix together mustard, butter, and sage.
Add the apple juice, cheddar cheese, and pepper, then stir well.
Add the cream cheese, blending well.
Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours.
When ready to serve, remove from refrigerator and allow to stand for ½ hour.
Spread on bread and serve with milk.

name: Tomato Curry
description: A mild, buttery curry of apple, onion and tomato seasoned with curry powder, served surrounded by a wall of boiled rice.
instructions: Fry apple and onion in the butter until blended.
Mix curry powder in a little milk, and stir in.
Season with salt and pepper.
Fry tomatoes in a separate pan.
Cover them with the curry mixture, and serve within a wall of boiled rice.

name: Lefse (Norwegian Potato Flatbread)
description: A traditional Norwegian potato-based flatbread that's soft and versatile, perfect as a sweet dessert, a savory side, or a main course with your favorite fillings.

ingredients.text: 8 cups boiled and mashed russet potatoes, still hot
ingredients.name: russet potato

instructions: Mix mashed potatoes with melted butter.
If preparing ahead, refrigerate mixture overnight, and take the potatoes out one hour before beginning the rest of the preparation.
Mix sugar, salt, cream, and potato mixture in a large bowl. Gradually stir in flour.

Using about 2 tablespoons (or a golf ball-sized chunk) of mix at a time, roll mix into flat, round shapes on a flat, smooth surface. Use flour to keep the mix from sticking to the surface and the rolling pin.
Place the round lefse on the griddle, cook until browned on bottom. Flip and repeat.
Add toppings, and serve hot!

name: Baked Potato Halves
description: A simple potato dish made without peeling the potatoes, baked until the flat sides form a tasty orange crust.
instructions: Select potatoes of similar size—around 250 grams each.
Wash potatoes well and cut out any bad parts. Do not peel.
Cut every potato in two halves, in the direction that will produce the thinnest halves.
Put ¼ to ½ tsp of salt onto the flat side of one half, and rub both halves together, so that they are both salted.
Place the potatoes onto a greased pan, flat side down, and into the oven preheated to 220°C.
The potatoes should be baked after 45 minutes. The flat sides should form a tasty orange crust.
Serve hot. The potatoes can be peeled by hand while eating or eaten unpeeled.

name: Fruit Salad with Orange Juice
description: A simple, quenching fruit salad with apples, bananas, oranges, maraschino cherries, and orange juice, ideal as a snack or dessert.
instructions: Peel the apples and bananas. Dice them into small pieces.
Peel and separate the orange sections. Cut sections into smaller pieces if desired.
Cut the cherries into halves or quarters, depending on the size. Pour a bit of the cherry juice in bowl.
Mix everything together, and add orange juice as desired.
If desired, refrigerate prior to serving.

name: Oreo Pie
description: A creamy frozen pie made with softened ice cream, Cool Whip, and crumbled Oreo cookies, then spread evenly into three pie crusts.

ingredients.text: ½ gallon (1.9 litres) ice cream (usually vanilla)
ingredients.name: ice cream

ingredients.text: 3 crumb crusts (preferably Graham cracker or chocolate)
ingredients.name: pie crust

instructions: Begin by softening the ice cream enough to spread.
Mix the softened ice cream with the Cool Whip.
Crumble the Oreos. This can be done by putting the Oreos into a plastic bag and crushing them with a rolling pin.
Mix the Oreos into the ice cream mixture.
Spread the mixture evenly into the 3 pie crusts.
Freeze for at least 2 hours.

name: Coconut Pudding II
description: A silky steamed pudding made with eggs, rich coconut milk, sugar and a hint of jasmine water. Light, fragrant and gently sweet.
instructions: Combine eggs, coconut milk, sugar and Jasmine water in a dish. Beat until foamy.
Pour the mixture into a heatproof dish, and place on top of a bamboo steamer basket.
Cover the basket and place above a large wok of boiling water.
Steam the pudding for 30–40 minutes, or until no longer fluid. If the pudding is cooked too fast, it becomes rubbery.
Take the pudding out of the steamer and allow to cool.

name: Pear and Almond Smoothie (Vegan)
description: A simple vegan pear and almond smoothie made with unsweetened almond milk and lemon, with no added refined sugar.
instructions: Cut the pear into chunks, discarding the core. Place the chunks of pear in a blender.
Squeeze the juice of the lemon over the pear.
Add the almond milk. Blend. Serve immediately.

name: Bean and Bacon Bake
description: A hearty microwave casserole of green beans, bacon, and potato seasoned with onion powder and salt, finished with toasted sliced almonds.

ingredients.text: 6 strips bacon, cooked until crisp, or microwave ready fully cooked bacon
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: ⅛ cup (15 g / 0.53 oz) sliced almonds
ingredients.name: almond

instructions: Peel and dice the potato.
Crumble crisp bacon into small pieces.
Drain green beans, keeping ½ cup of the liquid.
Put beans, bean juice, bacon, and potato in a microwave-safe baking dish.
Sprinkle onion powder and salt on top.
Cover with clear wrap.
Cook in microwave oven 5 minutes, stir, and cook another 5 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Garnish with sliced almonds.

name: Simple Flatbread
description: A simple, no-fuss flatbread made with just flour, water and oil, stretched paper-thin and cooked on a hot pan until bubbly.
instructions: Take 2 handfuls of flour and put in a bowl. Using a spoon, make a well in the middle.
Fill the well halfway with vegetable oil and the other half with water.
Fold in the flour and mix until a dough comes together in the bowl.
Let rest for 1 hour.
Divide dough into 4 parts. Taking 1 piece of dough, flatten it with your palms and then stretch the dough until it is thin as a tissue.
Cook on a pan or other hot surface until small to medium bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip onto other side (with your hand or spatula) to let cook for 30–40 seconds more.
Repeat cooking steps until all the dough is used up.

name: Garlic Lemon Marinade
description: A bright garlic lemon marinade that works well with fish and chicken, and can also be used as a sauce to accompany lobster.
instructions: Process all ingredients in a blender until smooth.
Keep refrigerated for up to 1 ½ weeks. Shake well before using.

name: Poutine
description: Crispy potatoes fried from scratch are topped with fresh cheddar cheese curds and warm poutine sauce or gravy, creating rich contrasts of texture, temperature, and viscosity.

ingredients.text: 1 L vegetable oil for deep frying
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 1 can (290 g) of poutine sauce (French: mélange à sauce poutine) or gravy
ingredients.name: poutine sauce

ingredients.text: 2 cups fresh cheddar cheese curds or mozzarella
ingredients.name: cheese curd

instructions: Slice the potatoes into finger-width fries and rinse them well to remove any dirt.
Begin warming the gravy, keeping the temperature low enough for slow heating.
Heat the oil to 185°C (365°F).
Cook the sliced potatoes in the oil for about 5 minutes.
After the first frying, remove the potatoes and fry them again for about 1 minute to crisp the outside.
Remove the fries from the oil; optionally place them on a paper towel mat to absorb excess oil.
Move the fries to a serving dish and put room-temperature cheese curds over the fries.
Pour the gravy over the top; serve before the cheese curds start to melt.

name: White Fish Ceviche (Cebiche de Pescado)
description: Fresh white fish is cold-cooked in lime juice with peppers, onion, cilantro, and garlic, then served with lettuce, corn, and sweet potato.

ingredients.text: 4 pounds (1.8 kg) of white fish (mahi mahi is an excellent choice), although most fish will work
ingredients.name: white fish

ingredients.text: juice from about 8 large sour green limes
ingredients.name: lime

ingredients.text: 3 finely-diced rocoto peppers or habanero peppers
ingredients.name: rocoto pepper

ingredients.text: 16–24 corn cobs cut into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces, cooked as usual
ingredients.name: corn

instructions: Wash and debone the fish, and cut it into ½ x ½ inch (about 1 x 1 cm) chunks.

Season the fish with salt, pepper, ají limo, and rocoto. Marinate the fish for a few minutes to “cold cook” them; leaving it for too long will “overcook” the fish. You should have enough lime juice to completely cover the fish.
Add the onion and mix gently.
Serve on a bed of lettuce, and add two pieces of corn on the cob and a portion of sweet potato.

name: Burple Nurples
description: A whimsical cookie recipe inspired by the animated show Chowder, made with butter, sugar, flour, egg, and a pinch of ground coriander.
instructions: Preheat oven to 320°F.
In a bowl, gently crack egg.
Mix in sugar, then butter, flour, and coriander to make a dough.
Shape dough into small balls.
Place dough balls on a cookie sheet.
Bake for 1 hour.

name: Frikadeller (Danish Meatballs)
description: Danish-style meatballs made with ground veal and pork, shaped into patties and fried in butter. They are traditionally served with boiled potatoes, gravy and braised red cabbage.

ingredients.text: 20% by volume (about ¾ cup) of bread crumbs
ingredients.name: breadcrumb

instructions: Mix all ingredients except butter together.
Shape mixture into small patties.
Fry in hot skillet with lots of butter.

name: Gulab Jamun (Fried Milk Balls in Syrup)
description: A popular Indian and Pakistani sweet of fried milk balls soaked in a sweet syrup flavoured with cardamom. These golden dumplings are crisp on the outside and infused with fragrant syrup.

ingredients.text: A little over ¾ cup (200 ml) warm milk
ingredients.name: milk

ingredients.text: 2 ½ cups (600 ml) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

instructions: Preheat canola oil 1.5–2 inches (4–5 cm) deep in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Combine the milk powder, Bisquick, and melted butter in a metal bowl.
Slowly add the warmed milk, 2 Tbsp at a time, mixing with a wooden spoon to form a firm, moist dough. If too wet, add more dry mixture maintaining a 3:1 ratio of milk powder to Bisquick.
Roll into evenly sized balls (they will not cook evenly if different sizes) and fry within a few minutes before they dry out.
Drop a few balls into the oil without overcrowding. They will sink, then float. Stir regularly for even browning.
When dark brown, remove and drain on paper. Repeat with remaining dough.
Break open the cardamom pods, separate the seeds, and bash them to release flavor.
Mix water, sugar, and cardamom and heat for 10 minutes—do not overheat or the syrup will caramelize.
Soak the finished fritters in the syrup overnight.
Serve hot or cold.

name: Grilled Pork Tenderloin
