description: A grilled pork tenderloin with a honey-lime marinade, smoky spices, and applewood chips for a rich barbecue flavor.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (~2.25 lb / 1 kg) pork tenderloin, trimmed
ingredients.name: pork tenderloin

instructions: Combine marinade ingredients in a small saucepan.
Pour half into a large zip-top plastic bag, reserving the other half in the fridge.
Add pork to the bag, remove extra air, and marinate in the fridge for 24 hours.
Remove pork from marinade. Discard the bag and the marinade in the bag. Allow the pork to drain as necessary.
Combine rub ingredients, and rub all over pork.
Moisten newspaper with oil and wad up under a large chimney starter with charcoal in it.
Light and wait 15 minutes.
Once charcoal has heated, disperse evenly around bottom of grill.
Add soaked chips, replace grate, and place pork in the center.
Cover and cook for 1 ½ minutes (or a bit more, use your judgment).
Flip to another side and cook 1 ½ more minutes and repeat until pork has cooked for at least 12 minutes and until the internal temperature reaches at least 145°F (63˚C).
Make a large foil pouch (or use a covered dish) and place pork inside.
Pour in reserved marinade (warmed to at least 145°F) and let rest for 10 minutes.
Serve.

name: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
description: A spicy, tangy and somewhat salty Italian pasta dish made with anchovies, olives, capers, tomatoes, and chili peppers. This classic Lazio recipe comes together quickly for a bold, savory weeknight meal.

ingredients.text: 115 grams (4 ounces) unsalted anchovy fillets, crushed into a paste (omit anchovies for Neapolitan version)
ingredients.name: anchovy fillet

ingredients.text: 200 grams (7 ounces) black olives, pitted and chopped
ingredients.name: black olive

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons salted capers, washed well and coarsely chopped
ingredients.name: caper

ingredients.text: 900 grams (roughly 2 pounds) plum tomatoes, peeled and puréed
ingredients.name: plum tomato

instructions: Put the butter, olive oil, garlic, and anchovy paste in a skillet over medium heat.
Before the garlic browns, add the olives, capers, tomato sauce, and chili peppers.
Add 2–3 pinches of salt, mixing over high heat.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in salted water (at least 4 quarts of water per pound of spaghetti being cooked). Strain it when it's al dente.
Place pasta in a large serving bowl, and coat it with sauce. Then, sprinkle it with chopped parsley.
Mix and serve hot.

name: Coconut Chicken
description: A Caribbean-inspired dish of chicken marinated in coconut milk, lime, mint, paprika, and ginger, then grilled to crispy perfection and served over fragrant basmati rice.

ingredients.text: Skin-on chicken legs, breasts, or wings (sufficient for the number of people you are cooking for)
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: 1 small knob of fresh ginger, grated
ingredients.name: ginger

ingredients.text: 1 cupful of basmati rice per person
ingredients.name: basmati rice

instructions: Stab the chicken in various places to a depth of about ½ inch so that they take on the taste from the marinade.

Combine all the contents of the marinade together in a dish, and place the chicken into it so that the chicken is covered by the marinade. Let marinate, turning occasionally, for at least 3 hours, or overnight is possible—the longer the better.

Place the chicken pieces on a barbecue, an electric grill, or even in the oven. Cook until done, making sure you coat the chicken with plenty of the marinade as you cook. You should aim for a nice crispy skin.

In a large saucepan bring some salted water to a boil, and add the cloves. Add the rice, and boil until the rice is cooked. Drain and rinse under hot water to remove excess starch. Take out the cloves and discard.

Return the rice to the pan and place over a low heat. Add about ½ cupful of the coconut marinade mixture (or any leftover coconut milk from the tin) to the rice, and heat through slowly. Add the butter at the last minute, and let it melt. If there is any left over, also add a handful of the chopped mint leaves to the rice as well. Fluff up the rice with a fork.
Place rice in the middle of your serving plate, place the grilled/barbecued chicken on top, sprinkle with a squeeze of fresh lime juice, and serve with a green salad.

name: Indian Potatoes
description: An extremely creamy and rich Indian-style potato dish simmered in coconut milk and tomatoes with garlic and red pepper flakes. It pairs wonderfully with Indian beans and rice.

ingredients.text: 6 small potatoes, peeled and cut in half
ingredients.name: potato

instructions: Sauté the garlic in olive oil.
Add tomatoes. Cook for 10 minutes, until the oil and tomatoes separate (they will bubble).
Stir in the coconut milk.
Add ½ teaspoon red pepper, and salt to taste. Boil it all together.
Add the potatoes. Cook over low-medium heat until the potatoes are done. They will become fairly soft; check with a fork.

name: Tod Mun (Thai Fish Cakes)
description: These Thai fish cakes combine ground fish, green beans, red curry paste, and Kaffir lime leaves, then are pan-fried until cooked on both sides. A popular street-food snack in Thailand, they are perfect for serving as an appetizer.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (120 ml) vegetable oil (for frying)
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 360 grams (about ¾ lb) ground fish or fish paste (pla kuud)
ingredients.name: fish

instructions: Stack the lime leaves and roll them together into a tube shape.
Slice them into thin strips.
Slice the green beans into small (½ inch) pieces.
Mince the fish.
Mix all the ingredients except the green beans and lime leaves in a bowl.
Stir until the mixture is smooth.
Add the green beans and lime leaves to the mixture and stir again.
Add the oil to a frying pan and heat to a medium temperature.
Drop a tablespoon of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly.
When the bottom is cooked, turn over.
When cooked on both sides, place on a paper towel to drain any extra oil.
Continue with the rest of the mixture.

name: Homemade Phyllo Dough
description: A simple, elastic dough made primarily from flour and water, rolled out extremely thin to create flaky baked goods.
instructions: Mix all the ingredients using a mixer with a dough hook or your hands until you get a smooth, elastic but not sticky dough.
Let the dough rest for a few hours, preferably wrapped in plastic in the fridge.
Cut the dough into small pieces.
Flatten each piece using a pasta maker. Pass it through the machine at size 1 several times, folding it in two each time, until the dough is nicely shaped.
Increase the pasta maker setting each time until you reach the desired size.
Alternatively, use a rolling pin with a lot of courage. The dough should be extremely thin.

name: Beske (Nigerian Soy Curds)
description: A Nigerian soy-curd dish made from boiled soy milk, seasoned with salt and optional spices, then fried until golden brown.
instructions: Remove any dirt or debris from the beans.
Soak for a few hours.
Drain the beans and peel off the skins.
Blend them to make a thick paste.
Strain all the liquid (milk) from the ground paste.
Bring the soy milk to a boil in a large pot, skimming off the froth.
Slowly add the coagulant, then turn off the heat. Solid curds should form.
Strain out the curds.
Knead in any salt and spices, then let the curds drain in cheesecloth and solidify.
Cut the solid curds into pieces, and fry until golden brown.

name: Sauerkraut Pierogi Filling
description: A savory filling of tangy sauerkraut and onion cooked in butter, perfect for stuffing homemade pierogi.
instructions: Place sauerkraut and liquid in a pot filled with just enough water to cover the sauerkraut. Bring to a boil, then remove from stove and transfer to a colander.
Drain and rinse the sauerkraut well with cold water to prevent further cooking. With your hands, squeeze as much liquid from the kraut as you can to prevent the filling from being too soggy.
Place the sauerkraut on a large cutting board and chop fine with a large, flat-bladed knife.
Fry the onion until it is translucent, then add the drained sauerkraut. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for 15 minutes and let it cool before using. For best results, refrigerate a few hours before using to fill pierogi.

name: Tajine bil Samak (Libyan Fish Tajine)
description: A fragrant Libyan fish dish with tender fillets simmered in a spiced tomato sauce, garnished with fresh herbs and served with rice or bread.

ingredients.text: 4–6 fish fillets (such as cod, haddock, or tilapia)
ingredients.name: fish fillet

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon ground cayenne pepper (adjust according to spice preference)
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for garnish
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: Heat the olive oil in the tajine over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
Place the fish fillets in the tajine, and cook for a few minutes on each side until lightly browned. Remove the fish fillets from the tajine or skillet and set them aside.
In the same tajine or skillet, add the diced tomatoes and tomato paste. Stir well to combine.
Add the ground cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, coriander, salt, and pepper. Mix the spices into the tomato mixture. Pour in the water and stir until the sauce is well combined.
Return the fish fillets to the tajine, nestling them into the sauce.
Cover the tajine with a lid and let the fish simmer in the sauce for about 10–15 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork.
Remove from the heat and sprinkle chopped parsley or cilantro on top for garnish.
Serve hot, accompanied by rice or bread.

name: Indian Mango, Chilli Powder, and Cumin Condiment (Chhundo)
description: A sweet and spicy Indian condiment from Gujarat, made with grated mangoes, spices, and sugar, sun-dried to a syrupy consistency. Traditionally served with roti and sabzi.
instructions: Peel and finely grate the mangoes.
Combine the grated mango evenly with the rest of the ingredients.
Spread the mixture in a shallow, wide-mouthed jar and cover with a thin cloth.
Keep the mixture in the sun for 5 days until the syrup attains a single thread consistency, stirring thrice daily.

name: Italian Rice Pilaf
description: A fragrant Italian-style rice pilaf cooked with bay leaves, thyme, rosemary, garlic, and Chianti wine for a rich, savory flavor.
instructions: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium high heat. Add rice and onion and cook until rice is golden.

Meanwhile, combine remaining ingredients. Once rice has toasted, remove from pot and add mixture. Bring to a boil and add rice. Cook, stirring occasionally, 30 minutes or until rice is desired tenderness.
Serve warm with a steak, a glass of red wine, and maybe a vegetable sauté.

name: Ghevar (Rajasthani Honeycomb Fritter)
description: A crisp, porous Rajasthani honeycomb fritter made with a delicate batter and soaked in warm sugar syrup.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp (10 grams) arrowroot starch or cornstarch
ingredients.name: arrowroot starch

ingredients.text: A few drops kewda essence (extract of Pandanus flower)
ingredients.name: kewda essence

instructions: Combine the sugar and water in a saucepan. Simmer until it reaches a 1-string consistency syrup.
Remove from the heat and keep warm.
Combine the flour, arrowroot, and melted ghee in a bowl.
Very gradually add 1 cup of water in a thin stream, whisking continuously and taking care to see that an emulsion is formed and the water and ghee do not separate.
Add 2 more cups of water again in a thin stream while whisking continuously. At no point should the ghee and water separate.

The batter should be of a very thin coating consistency, a little thinner than crêpe batter. More water can be added if required to achieve the required consistency. Keep the batter in a cool place away from the heat.
Add melted ghee to a kadhai or other pot/pan. If desired, place a ghevar mould or other metal ring mould in the pan. The ghee should come up to ¾ of the height of the mould.

Heat the pan over medium heat, and gradually pour a ladleful of the batter directly into the centre of the mould in a very thin stream. The batter should froth and migrate towards the edges of the mold.

When the froth subsides, gradually add another spoonful to the centre in a thin stream. If the batter builds up in the center, use a skewer to push it towards the edges and maintain a hole in the center. Repeat seven times, adding the batter to the centre hole each time.
Increase the heat, and pour a few ladlefuls of hot ghee into the centre to help the ghevar cook.

When the centre is firm and cooked and the whole thing is golden brown, pull the ghevar out gently by inserting a wooden skewer in the centre and pulling it out of the ghee. Let any excess ghee drip off.
Immerse ghevar in sugar syrup, drain quickly, and place on a serving plate.
Repeat the cooking steps, using the remaining batter to make 9 pieces of ghevar.

name: Beanburger
description: A vegetarian beanburger made with mixed beans, vegetables, and aromatic spices, best served in pita bread with tomato and lettuce or with a spicy tomato sauce.

ingredients.text: 1 red or yellow bell pepper, chopped
ingredients.name: bell pepper

ingredients.text: 1 generous pinch each of cumin, ground coriander, mild chilli powder, paprika and turmeric
ingredients.name: cumin, coriander, chilli powder, paprika, turmeric

ingredients.text: 2 tins of mixed beans or mixed pulses, drained
ingredients.name: mixed beans

instructions: Fry the onions and pepper (in a little bit of oil) with the spices for a couple of minutes. Leave to cool.
Mash the beans in a large bowl.
Add the carrot, onion, pepper and oats to the mashed beans and mix until well combined.
Add the egg gradually (you probably won't need all of it). You don't want a mixture that's too sticky.
Shape the dough into 6 to 8 burgers and lightly flour each side.
Fry the burgers (in a little bit of oil) for a few minutes on each side, until golden.
Serve hot.

name: Grilled Filet Mignon with a Cognac Reduction
description: Tender filet mignon crusted with coarsely ground black pepper and grilled to medium rare, finished with a rich cognac reduction.
instructions: Sprinkle filet mignons with kosher salt on both sides.
Coat filet mignons with mustard on both sides and press into the black pepper, pressing lightly to help adhesion.
Grill steaks over high heat for 1 minute per side, then place on a new medium burner until interior temperature reaches 140°F (60°C). Remove and keep warm.
Place cognac in a small saucepan, and boil over high heat until reduced by ⅓.
Serve filet mignons with cognac reduction drizzled on top.

name: Tortilla Española
description: A Spanish omelette of fried potatoes and onions set in eggs, fried to make a dish somewhat akin to a quiche which may be eaten like a pizza.

ingredients.text: About ¼ cup + 2 tbsp vegetable or olive oil
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

instructions: Heat the garlic and a small amount of oil in a 10-inch frying pan until garlic is browned.
Add the rest of the oil and heat to about 375°F (200°C).
Cube or slice the potatoes and coarsely chop the onion; add to hot oil and fry until brown.
Strain the potatoes, onions, and garlic and reserve about 2 tablespoons oil.
Beat eggs in a separate bowl.
Add potatoes, onions, and garlic to beaten eggs and allow to sit for about 15 minutes.
Put reserved tablespoons of oil in original 10-inch frying pan and place over low-medium heat.
Add egg/potato/onion/garlic mixture to frying pan; fry, lifting up edges of tortilla española to allow uncooked egg to run underneath and cook.
Serve after cooked as a pizza with your choice of toppings: salsa, sour cream, shredded cheese, chives, etc., are all very good choices.

name: Mussels with Potatoes
description: Chilled mussels tossed with cooked potatoes and carrots, then dressed with olive oil, wine vinegar, and seasoning.

ingredients.text: 450 g (1 lb) mussels, rinsed and scrubbed
ingredients.name: mussel

ingredients.text: 225 g (8 oz) potatoes, cooked and diced
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 175 g (6 oz) carrots, cooked and diced
ingredients.name: carrot

instructions: Place the mussels in a large pot or steamer with about 1–2 inches of boiling liquid (e.g. water, wine, or seasoned broth).
Cover and steam over high heat for approximately 5 minutes or until the shells open.
Discard any mussels that do not open.
Remove mussel meal from the shells.
Mix together the mussels, potatoes, and carrots and arrange on a suitable serving dish.
Thoroughly blend the oil, vinegar, and seasoning and pour over the salad.
Chill well before serving.

name: Tomato Pizza
description: A thick, satisfying pizza topped with mozzarella and a garlic-sautéed tomato sauce, then finished with grated Pecorino Romano.
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°C (450°F).
Stretch the pizza dough to cover a greased baking sheet. Dough should be about 3 cm (¾ inch) thick.
Allow the dough to rise while the sauce is prepared.
Heat a saucepan on medium heat, add the olive oil and garlic.
Sauté until garlic is just golden.
Add crushed tomatoes and oregano.
Cook until the sauce is thickened, about 15–20 minutes.
Cool the sauce until it is room temperature.
Top the pizza dough with mozzarella cheese, then any toppings such as sausage or pepperoni, then top with sauce.
Bake in the oven for about 15–20 minutes.
After removing the tomato-pie from the oven, sprinkle the grated cheese on top and then let the pizza cool to room temperature.
Serve at room temperature or reheat under the broiler or in a toaster-oven.

name: Monte Cristo Burgers
description: Grilled beef patties topped with melted cheese and served on golden, egg-and-cream-dipped hamburger buns for a savory take on the classic Monte Cristo sandwich.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°F.
Combine the egg, hot sauce, and cream in a pie plate. Dip cut sides of buns into egg mixture. Move to a cooling rack and let sit 10 minutes.
Heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat. Grease with cooking spray.
Add buns, one at a time, and cook until browned on cut side. Move to a clean plate and repeat until all buns have been cooked. Keep warm in the oven.
Form beef into 4 equal patties. Brush both sides with olive oil and sprinkle both sides liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat about 28 charcoal briquettes in a large chimney starter. Once hot, disperse evenly around the bottom of a grill and reapply grate.
Add patties and cook, turning often, until internal temperature reaches 145°F for medium rare, 160°F for medium, and 170°F for toast.
Remove to a plate, top with cheese, and cover with aluminum foil. Let rest 3 minutes.
Place a patty on the bottom half of each bun. Top with upper half and serve warm.

name: Nigerian Fish Pie
description: A sweet pie filled with mashed sardines, made with a smooth, elastic dough and fried until browned on all sides. It is a popular dish in Nigeria.
instructions: Sift the flour into a mixing basin, then stir in the sugar, salt, and nutmeg. Mix thoroughly.
Mix in the yeast thoroughly. Mix in the egg until it is completely incorporated into the flour.
Mix in the cold water in small increments until a thick dough ball is formed.
Transfer the dough to a tabletop, and knead it with your palm until it is very smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in the bowl, cover, and set aside for 10 minutes to rest.
Place the sardines on a platter and mash them with a fork before setting them aside. This may be somewhat challenging.
Knead the dough a second time. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 5 mm.
Cut the dough into rectangles.
Scoop some mashed sardines center of each rectangle. Fold the dough in half, enclosing the filling.
Use a fork to press the edges together and seal the pastries.
Fill a pot with vegetable oil to a depth of 3 inches. Heat the oil over medium heat.
Fry the pastries in the oil until browned on all sides. It will take approximately 12 minutes.
Remove the fish pies, and drain any excess oil.

name: Posho (Ugandan Cornmeal Porridge)
description: A hearty and nutritious Ugandan staple porridge made from maize flour and water, with a smooth, comforting texture. Traditionally served as a side dish with stews, beans, or greens.

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon butter or vegetable oil (optional, for added richness)
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: In a cooking pot, bring the water to a boil over medium heat.
Gradually add the maize flour to the boiling water, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or whisk to prevent lumps from forming.
Continue stirring the mixture until it thickens and begins to pull away from the sides of the pot, about 5–10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a lid, and let the porridge simmer for an additional 5–10 minutes.
If using, add butter or vegetable oil to the porridge and stir until well incorporated.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the posho rest for a few minutes before serving to allow it to set further.
Serve the posho warm as a comforting and nourishing side dish with stews, vegetables, or any other Ugandan delicacies.

name: Zippuli (Italian Potato Cheese Fritters)
description: Crisp Calabrian-style fritters made with potatoes, Parmesan, parsley, and eggs, fried until golden and served with marinara sauce.
instructions: Mix together all ingredients but the potatoes and eggs.
Mash in the potatoes, and mix together into a crumbly paste.
Mix in the eggs until a sticky dough is made.
Roll dough into hotdog-sized logs about 6–8 inches long.
Fry in hot grease, turning once to get both sides brown. Drain on paper towels.
Serve with marinara sauce.

name: Stuffed Courgette
description: Tender courgette halves filled with a savoury mix of sautéed onion, garlic, pepper, tomatoes, herbs and brown rice, topped with melted cheddar and baked until golden.
instructions: Slice courgettes in half lengthways, and scoop or cut out middles; reserve middles.
Chop onion and garlic, and sauté for a few minutes in olive oil.
Chop pepper, tomatoes, and herbs. Add to pan together with courgette middles.
Add rice, mustard, and seasoning to taste. Cook for 5 minutes and drain off any extra liquid.
Stuff the 4 courgette halves with the cooked mixture, and sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Bake in medium-hot oven for 20 minutes.
Serve with green salad.

name: Shrimp Scampi Angel Hair Pasta with Lemon and Pine Nuts
description: Angel hair pasta tossed with garlic-and-butter shrimp, fresh parsley, lemon zest and juice, and toasted pine nuts.

ingredients.text: 1 package (12 ounces) shrimp scampi, garlic and butter flavor
ingredients.name: shrimp

ingredients.text: ½ cup fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves, roughly chopped
ingredients.name: parsley

ingredients.text: Finely grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
ingredients.name: lemon

ingredients.text: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: salt and black pepper

instructions: Boil a large pot of cold water and salt it generously.
Add the pasta and cook, stirring occasionally until al dente, 4–5 minutes.
Drain the pasta, reserving about 1 cup of the cooking water.
Prepare the shrimp in a large skillet according to package directions.
Stir the lemon zest and juice into the shrimp.
Add the pasta, reserved pasta water, parsley, and pine nuts, and toss in the skillet to coat the pasta evenly.
Divide the shrimp and pasta among warm pasta bowls and serve.

name: Paella Valenciana
description: A traditional Spanish rice dish from Valencia featuring chicken, rabbit, beans, and saffron, slow-cooked in a wide pan to develop the prized crispy socarrat at the bottom.

ingredients.text: 250 g (10 ounces) chopped green bell peppers (optional)
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

ingredients.text: 500 g (17.5 ounces) diced or grated tomatoes
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: 125 g (4.5 ounces) large haricot beans (canned or fresh)
ingredients.name: haricot bean

ingredients.text: 100 g (3.5 ounces) small haricot beans (canned or fresh)
ingredients.name: haricot bean

ingredients.text: 125 g (4.5 ounces) fresh runner beans or green beans
ingredients.name: runner bean

ingredients.text: 8–10 threads of saffron and/or 1½ teaspoons yellow food coloring (see notes)
ingredients.name: saffron

ingredients.text: 400 g (14 ounces) calasparra rice, bomba rice, or pearl rice
ingredients.name: rice

instructions: Clean the snails, poultry and rabbit thoroughly. Cut the poultry and rabbit into small pieces and salt them generously.
Pour olive oil in a paellera and, when hot, sauté the poultry and rabbit pieces until golden brown.
Add green peppers and sauté for 1 minute. Add the garlic and sauté until brown. Be careful; garlic burns easily.
Once the garlic is brown, add the paprika followed quickly by the tomatoes to prevent the paprika from burning. Sauté until the tomatoes become dark and pulpy and the mixture has reduced a bit.

Add the water and bring it to a rolling boil. Then add the snails, fresh haricot beans (if canned, continue reading to see when to add these), runner beans, and saffron (and/or food coloring). Allow the mixture to boil for 10 minutes over a high flame. Sweep a rosemary branch through the broth for no longer than 30 seconds and then remove it.

After 10 minutes have passed, you should have a flavorful broth. It's customary at this point to allow your dinner guests to taste it. The purpose is to determine if the broth needs more salt. If so, add more salt, a pinch at a time, until everybody is satisfied.

Add the rice and stir it using the rice skimmer. Then, once again with the skimmer, spread the rice over the bottom of the paellera. The coating of rice should be one centimeter thick. Let it cook over a high flame for 10 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium and let it simmer for 4 minutes. Add the canned haricot beans, reduce the heat again to low, and let it simmer for another 4 minutes. Taste the rice frequently to determine when it's fully cooked. You'll know it's done when it's slightly firm to the bite.

At this point, there should be some toasted rice sticking to the bottom of the pan. This is a delicacy in Valencia called socarrat. If no socarrat has developed, increase the flame to high and listen for the crackling sound of rice toasting at the bottom.

Remove the pan from the heat when the rice is almost dry, and place the unused rosemary branches on top. Cover with a clean, white towel and wait 5 minutes before serving to allow the rice to absorb the remaining broth.

name: Oatmeal Banana Waffle
description: A wholesome breakfast waffle made by blending oatmeal, banana, and olive oil into a smooth batter, then cooking it in a waffle iron until golden.
instructions: Turn waffle iron on high.
Put all ingredients in a blender and blend on high until the contents are smooth.
Let the mixture sit for 10–15 minutes.
Spray the waffle iron with non-stick cooking spray.
Pour some of the batter onto the waffle iron.
Cook for about 10 minutes.
Repeat until you are out of batter.

name: Ofada Stew
description: A rich Nigerian stew of chicken and cow skin cooked in palm oil with bell peppers, fermented locust beans, crayfish, curry, and black pepper. The finished stew includes grilled meat and hard-boiled egg and is served with rice.
instructions: Boil the chicken, ponmo, maggi, salt, curry, thyme, and black pepper for 10–20 minutes. Remove the meat, reserving the stock.
Grill the meat until golden brown.
Add the palm oil to a clean dry pot. Cover the pot with a lid, and heat over medium-low heat for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat, and allow to cool completely.
Blend the scotch bonnet pepper and bell peppers to make a smooth paste. Add a little water if the consistency is too thick.
Heat the cooled palm oil, and add the chopped onions. Cook, stirring, for a few minutes until the onions are softened.
Stir the pepper paste, crayfish, and iru into the onions. Cover and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Add the reserved meat stock to the onion mixture, and allow to cook for 1 hour until oil begins to float to the surface.
Add boiled egg and grilled meat, and cook for another 10 minutes.
Serve stew with rice.

name: Chocolate Icing
description: A rich, creamy chocolate icing made with melted sweet chocolate, cream, and confectioner's sugar, perfect for frosting a cake.
instructions: Melt chocolate over hot water.
Add the cream.
Gradually beat in sugar until icing is creamy and thick enough to spread.

name: Salted Mustard Greens and Shredded Meat Noodle Soup
description: A Chinese noodle soup featuring salty, semi-pickled mustard greens and tender marinated pork strips simmered in a savory broth and served over noodles.
instructions: Wash and dry the mustard greens.
Add salt to the greens.
Seal in a plastic bag and store in the refrigerator for several days.
Cut the pork tenderloin meat into tiny strips. Marinate the meat with corn starch, soy sauce, and sugar.
Retrieve the semi-pickled mustard greens and dice them.
Using a wok, stir-fry the meat until it is slightly brown. Remove the meat from the wok.
Stir-fry the salted mustard greens until slightly brown.
Place the meat back into the wok and add soup stock and water. Simmer for a couple of minutes.
Serve the soup with noodles.

name: Enchiladas Rojas
description: A classic Tex-Mex dish of rolled tortillas filled with spiced sausage and cheese, smothered in a rich ancho chili and tomato sauce, then baked until bubbly.

ingredients.text: 6 tomatoes, peeled, seeded and coarsely-chopped OR 2 cups canned Roma tomatoes, drained and chopped
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: 6 chorizo sausages, skinned and chopped OR ¾ lb spiced pork, chicken or turkey sausage, skinned and chopped
ingredients.name: chorizo sausage

ingredients.text: 1 cup crumbled queso blanco OR freshly-grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: queso blanco

instructions: Soak the chilies in boiling water for 30 minutes.
Wearing gloves, stem, seed and cut the chilies into small pieces.
Put the chilies and 1 cup of soaking water in a blender and purée at high speed for 20 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, onions, garlic, epazote, sugar, salt, and black pepper and blend to a smooth purée.
In a frying pan, add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and heat over high heat for 3 minutes.
Pour in the tomato sauce and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from the heat.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs with the cream or half-and-half until well blended.
Slowly pour the egg and cream into the pan with the sauce, stirring constantly. Cover and set aside.
In another frying pan, fry the sausage meat over moderate heat for 5 minutes or so, until they are lightly browned.
With a slotted spoon, remove the sausage from the pan and drain on paper towels. Discard the fat in the frying pan.
Place the sausages in a small bowl and stir in 3 tablespoons of sauce and ½ cup cheese.
Heat the oven to 350°F.

In a heavy frying pan, fry the tortillas, one at a time, in very hot olive oil: dip a tortilla in the tomato sauce, fry for a minute each side, remove to a warm plate and place about ¼ cup of sausage mixture in the centre, then roll up the tortilla with the filling inside.
Place filled tortillas in a baking dish, seam side down. Pour the rest of the tomato sauce over them.
Sprinkle the top with the green onions and ½ cup cheese.
Bake for about 15 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the top has browned lightly.

name: Peach Chutney
description: A sweet and tangy peach chutney made with raisins, ginger, and warm Indian spices like garam masala and mustard seed. Perfect served with pork chops or curry.

ingredients.text: 1 hot banana pepper, seeded and chopped
ingredients.name: hot banana pepper

instructions: Blanch, peel, and pit peaches.
Coarsely chop peaches and combine with lemon juice in a large stainless steel or enamel saucepan. Stir in sugar.
Bring to a boil and cook, stirring frequently until the peaches are tender (about 15 minutes).
Add remaining ingredients. Boil over medium-high heat for about 45 minutes or until thick, stirring frequently.
Ladle chutney into six hot, sterilized, 1-pint (2-cup) preserving jars, leaving ½ inch of headspace. Wipe rims clean and seal according to manufacturer's directions.
Process for 15 minutes in a boiling water bath. Allow chutney to mature for at least one month before using.

name: Caramel Squares
description: A wonderfully rich and classic British treat with a crunchy shortbread base, a creamy caramel filling, and a smooth chocolate topping. Perfect with coffee or afternoon tea.

ingredients.text: 340 g good-quality chocolate (milk or dark), melted
ingredients.name: chocolate

instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas mark 4; 350°F). Rub flour, butter, and caster sugar together until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Press into a 25 x 38 x 4 cm Swiss roll pan.
Bake for 20 minutes or till golden, then cool.
Melt butter in a heavy-based saucepan over a low heat; add sugar, golden syrup, and condensed milk.
Stir continuously for 40–50 minutes. It should be golden brown in colour when ready to eat. To test, drop a little blob into a bowl of cold water; it should firm up.
Pour this caramel mixture over the base, and let it cool.
Pour melted chocolate over the top, spread evenly, and let set.

name: Egidi (Pounded Corn)
description: A traditional Yoruba dish from Ondo state made by grinding fresh corn into a paste, wrapping it in leaves, cooking, and pounding until smooth. It is typically served with soups such as okro, ogbono, or ẹgusi.
instructions: Grind the corn kernels to make a paste.
Wrap the paste using wrapping leaves.
Cook for few minutes.
Pound using mortar and pestle until the mixture is lump-free.
Serve with soup.

name: Chicken Parisian
description: A slow-cooker chicken dish simmered in wine and cream of mushroom soup, finished with sour cream and served over steamed white rice.

ingredients.text: Red or white wine (use cooking wine for more flavor)
ingredients.name: wine

instructions: Mix the wine and cream of mushroom soup together in a slow-cooker. If you added too much wine, sprinkle in some flour to keep the sauce from losing viscosity.
Take the chicken cuts, strip off the fat, and rinse well. Immerse the chicken in the sauce mixture in the slow-cooker, fully submerging the chicken.
Mix in sour cream, put the lid on, and set the slow-cooker to cook for 8 hours on low heat.
Serve the finished chicken with the steamed rice.

name: Onunu with Fish Sauce
description: A traditional Nigerian meal of pounded yam and plantains served hot with a spicy fish stew seasoned with tomato, onion, and pepper.
instructions: Peel and rinse the yams, then cut into small cubes. Do the same for the plantains.
Transfer the yam to a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Boil the yam until tender, then add the plantains. Cook until both are soft.
Drain the yam and plantains, then pound them together. Season with salt, add a small amount of palm oil, and pound well until combined.
Mold the onunu into small balls.
Season the fresh fish with a little dry pepper and stock cube. Marinate for about 23 minutes.
Steam the fish with a little water for about 7 minutes on low heat.
Heat a thin layer of palm oil in a pot. Add the onions, and fry until light brown.
Grind the tomato and fresh pepper to a purée, and stir into the onions. Cook for about 7 minutes.
Stir in the seasonings and a bit of water. Cook for a minute or two.
Add the fish and curry leaf, and allow everything to heat through.
Serve hot with the prepared onunu.

name: Shrimp Fritters (Accra)
description: Shrimp fritters made with chopped shrimp, peppers, onions, garlic, and herbs, fried until all sides are brown.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (60 ml) green pepper, chopped
ingredients.name: green pepper

ingredients.text: 1 Scotch bonnet or other hot pepper, minced
ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet

instructions: Combine green pepper, spring onions, onions, and scotch bonnet in a bowl.
Add remaining ingredients except water, and mix thoroughly.
Stir in enough water to make a soft mixture using a spoon. Beat mixture until is smooth.
Using a pan or deep fryer, drop spoonfuls in to hot oil, and fry until all sides are brown.

name: Crown Roast of Lamb
description: A savory lamb roast seasoned with thyme, rosemary, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and olive oil, then roasted to medium rare and rested before serving.

ingredients.text: 2 racks of lamb, trimmed and frenched
ingredients.name: lamb rack

instructions: Brush both racks of lamb with olive oil.
Sprinkle with paprika, garlic powder, and kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Rub seasonings into the meat.
Place both racks in a bundt pan and tie the end bones together with butcher's twine.
Place on the middle rack of the oven and roast for 30–35 minutes, until the meat reaches an internal temperature of 145°F for medium rare.
Remove and let rest 10 minutes. Serve.

name: Ginger Banana Cake with Chocolate
description: A gluten-free ginger banana cake made with buckwheat flour, very ripe bananas, and dark chocolate.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (60 ml/70 g) maple syrup
ingredients.name: maple syrup

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (60 ml/65 g) unsweetened applesauce
ingredients.name: applesauce

ingredients.text: 3 very ripe bananas (should have dark spots on the peel)
ingredients.name: banana

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (30 g) roughly-chopped dark chocolate or chocolate chips
ingredients.name: dark chocolate

instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C (338°F).
Mix the buckwheat flour, baking powder and baking soda in a bowl, and set aside.
Mix the maple syrup with the applesauce, the lemon juice, and the grated ginger.
Mash the bananas using the back of a fork before mixing them with the other wet ingredients.
Combine the dry ingredients with the banana mixture. Be careful not to overmix—you don’t want to beat out all of the air.
Once everything is well-mixed, add the dark chocolate and gently mix again.
Line a cake pan (20 x 20 cm/ 8 x 8 inch) with parchment paper and pour the batter into it.
Place in the oven and bake for about 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

name: Ground Tofu
description: Customizable ground tofu marinated with tamari, yeast extract, beet juice, shiitake powder, and onion powder, then sautéed until golden.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon beet juice (for example, from canned beets)
ingredients.name: beet juice

ingredients.text: ¼ teaspoon powdered shiitake mushroom (see notes)
ingredients.name: shiitake mushroom

instructions: Make the marinade by mixing together tamari, yeast extract, beet juice, shiitake powder, and onion powder in a small mixing bowl.
Make sure the mushroom powder and yeast extract are evenly incorporated with no lumps.
Drain the tofu, pressing it to get rid of as much moisture as possible.
Combine the marinade with the tofu, crushing the tofu into small pieces and allowing it to absorb the liquid evenly.
Place the tofu in a zip-top bag, pour the marinade over it, seal it, and crush the tofu with your fingers until no pieces are larger than a fingernail.
Allow sufficient time for the marinade to soak completely into the tofu, such as several hours or overnight.
Heat a medium-sized non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Using a small amount of canola oil, just enough to coat the cooking surface, sauté the tofu until browned to a golden color.
The tofu will achieve a medium-brown color from the marinade and heat, but it will not achieve the deep brown of ground beef or a commercial ground beef substitute.
Once the tofu is browned, it will still be quite soft.
Improve its texture by spreading it out in the hot pan and allowing it to cool for some time.
Store the ground tofu in the refrigerator.
Reheat it in a skillet for whatever application you desire.
Use it as a filling for tacos, sloppy joes, meat sauces for pasta, and the like.

name: Eggplant and Tahini (Moutabbal)
description: A smoky eggplant and tahini dip blended with garlic and lemon juice. Serve at room temperature, drizzled with olive oil and garnished with olives or herbs.
instructions: Roast the eggplant on open flame. If your stove is electric, split the eggplant lengthwise, place face down on a cookie sheet, and bake in a hot oven on the top rack 30–45 minutes.
For open flame roasting, use a fork to turn often.
The skin should wrinkle and char, and the flesh will shrivel and become soft.
When the eggplant is completely soft all over, remove it to a bowl, slash once or twice to drain out bitter juice, and let rest until cool enough to handle.
Some cooks suggest cooling the eggplant inside a brown paper bag.
Cut off the stem and peel away the skin. Scrape the flesh into the bowl of a food processor or blender.
Add garlic, tahini and lemon juice and process.
Quantities depend upon the size of the eggplant and your preferences—please taste frequently. Salt to taste.
Serve at room temperature, drizzled with olive oil, and garnished with a black or green Mediterranean olive or sprigs of cilantro or parsley.

name: Italian Rice with Wild Mushrooms
description: A creamy Italian risotto made with Arborio-style rice, sautéed wild mushrooms, Parmesan cheese, and a finishing touch of truffle oil.

ingredients.text: 4 ounces (commercial) wild mushrooms, sliced and sautéed
ingredients.name: wild mushroom

instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer before you begin. It's important that the temperature is as high as possible, without letting the stock boil. The surface of the stock should just be moving a little.
Sauté the shallots in olive oil until soft.
Add the rice, stirring for 3–5 minutes, until coated with oil.
Pour in wine and about ½ cup of the hot broth and continue stirring.
Keep adding liquid as necessary and stir for an additional 15 minutes, keeping the rice creamy.
Remove from heat and add Parmesan cheese, mushrooms, and truffle oil.
Serve immediately.

name: Boiled Custard
description: A classic custard with a light texture and mild flavor, carefully cooked without boiling so it does not curdle. Serve it warm or chilled.

ingredients.text: ¼–½ cup (55–110 g / 1.9–3.9 oz) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: white granulated sugar

instructions: Heat milk and salt (if using) in a double boiler until bubbles form around the edges.
Beat eggs with sugar until uniform.
Gradually mix approximately ½ cup (125 ml / 4.2 oz) hot milk into the egg mixture to temper it.
Slowly stir egg mixture into remaining hot milk.
Optionally, mix cornstarch and water and stir into custard.
Stir over heat until thickened (should coat the spoon), without bringing to a boil.
Remove from heat, and continue stirring to dry the custard slightly.
Stir in vanilla before the dish has cooled completely.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Ifumbe (Rwandan Cassava Fritters)
description: Crispy Rwandan cassava fritters with a soft interior, made from cassava flour, milk, and egg, fried until golden brown. A perfect snack or dessert for any time of day.
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the cassava flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, and ground cinnamon (if using). Mix well to evenly distribute the dry ingredients.
Add the milk, water, and beaten egg to the dry ingredients. Stir until a smooth batter forms. The batter should have a slightly thick consistency.
In a frying pan, heat enough vegetable oil over medium heat for frying.
Once the oil is hot, drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, making small fritters. Be careful not to overcrowd the pan; fry in batches if needed.
Fry the fritters for about 2–3 minutes on each side, or until they turn golden brown and crispy.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the fried fritters from the oil and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve the ifumbe warm as a tasty snack or dessert.

name: Ropa Vieja (Caribbean Shredded Beef)
description: A Cuban-style ropa vieja featuring shredded beef simmered with onion, garlic, peppers, tomato sauce, and red cooking wine or beer.

ingredients.text: 1 kg boiled beef (preferably flank steak, but any meat with long threads will do)
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: 1 cup red cooking wine or beer
ingredients.name: cooking wine

instructions: Cut the meat in pieces, not too small, not too big. Using a pressure cooker, boil the meat for about 15 minutes.
Add a teaspoon of olive oil to the water to avoid foaming; also, add a teaspoon of salt.
After boiling the meat, save 1 cup of the broth.
Shred the meat in thin strips using a fork. Chop the onion, cut the peppers in thin strips and mince the garlic cloves.
Sauté the garlic and the onion for a bit in hot oil, then add the peppers and sauté a bit more.
Add the meat and the rest of the ingredients, including the cup of broth.
Cook the mix over low heat for 20–30 minutes. Stir a few times and season to taste.

name: Bouillabaisse
description: A traditional Marseille fish stew made with assorted fish, vegetables, saffron and herbs. The broth is served over country bread with rouille, while the fish and potatoes are served separately.

ingredients.text: 660 g whole cleaned lotte, or monkfish
ingredients.name: monkfish

ingredients.text: 1 live octopus (optional)[3], cleaned and cut into pieces
ingredients.name: octopus

ingredients.text: 1 kg of potatoes, peeled and cut into large slices
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 5 ripe tomatoes, peeled, quartered and without seeds
ingredients.name: tomato

instructions: Scale the fish and wash them, if possible, in sea water. Cut them into large slices, leaving the bones.
Warm the olive oil in a large, deep saucepan.
Add the onions, along with 6 cloves of crushed garlic, the octopus pieces and tomatoes. Brown at low heat turning gently for 5 minutes.
Add the fish slices; first the large slices then the smaller ones.
Cover with boiling water and add salt, pepper, fennel, the bouquet garni and saffron.
Simmer at a low heat, stirring from time to time so the fish doesn't stick to the pan. Correct the seasoning.
Remove the bouillabaisse from the heat once the oil and water have thoroughly blended with the other ingredients. This should take about twenty minutes.
Prepare the rouille: Use a mortar to crush the garlic cloves into a fine paste after removing the stems.
Add the egg yolk and the saffron, then blend in the olive oil little by little to make a mayonnaise, stirring it with the pestle.
Cook the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes.
Open the sea urchins with a pair of scissors and remove the roe with a small spoon.
Arrange the fish on a platter.
Add the sea urchin roe into the broth and stir.
Rub several slices of bread with garlic and spread a tablespoon of rouille on each. Place at least two slices per serving bowl.
Remove the fish and potatoes from the broth and place them on a large serving platter.
Pour the hot broth in each bowl containing a slice of bread smothered in rouille.
Then serve the fish and the potatoes on a separate platter.

name: Holzknechtnocken (Austrian Boiled Dumplings)
description: Traditional Austrian dumplings made from a simple hot-water dough, then boiled and fried until golden. Serve them with sauerkraut or steamed apples.
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl and add water. Knead until you get a dough.
Form dumplings and add them to a pot of boiling water. When dumplings rise to the surface of the water, they are done.
Melt lard in a heavy-bottomed skillet with deep sides. Add dumplings, and fry until they are golden.
Serve with sauerkraut or steamed apples.

name: Nigerian Fried Noodles
description: Nigerian fried noodles combine instant noodles with stir-fried onion, bell peppers, carrot, and leafy greens, then finish with a slower fry before serving hot.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add the instant noodles, and cook until softened but still slightly firm.
Drain the noodles.
Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a frying pan.
Add the onion, peppers, carrot, and leafy greens, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Season the vegetables with stock cube or the instant noodle seasoning powder.
Add the cooked noodles to the vegetables, and stir-fry them until frothy.
Lower the heat so the noodles can fry more slowly for a few minutes.
Serve hot.

name: Watermelon Smoothie
description: A hydrating, healthful smoothie made with watermelon and milk, blended until smooth and strained through a sieve.
instructions: Cut the watermelon into small pieces after removing the seeds.
Combine all of the ingredients in a blender until smooth. Drain through a sieve.
Serve.

name: Crispy Salmon
description: Wild salmon fillets are dredged in seasoned flour and lemon juice, coated with panko, and baked before broiling until deeply browned.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24 ounces) skinless wild salmon fillets, pin bones removed
ingredients.name: salmon fillet

instructions: Combine flour, salt, and pepper in a pie pan, place panko in another pan, and place lemon juice in a large bowl.
Using wet-hand dry-hand, dredge salmon into flour then into lemon, then into panko. Coat with olive oil and place on a sheet pan.
Bake in the center of a 375°F oven for 27 minutes or until slightly underdone.
Remove from oven, and heat up the broiler. Place salmon under broiler and cook until deeply browned. Serve immediately.

name: Jamaican Banana Fritters
description: Jamaican banana fritters are a traditional Caribbean dessert and snack made with mashed ripe bananas and fried until golden brown. Serve them hot with cinnamon, coconut, sugar, or ice cream.
instructions: Peel the bananas and mash them in a bowl until runny.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan at medium heat.
Add the sugar, milk, vanilla, salt, and flour to the bananas and mix until approximately the consistency of pancake batter or a bit thinner.
Drop tablespoons of the mixture into the heated oil, and fry until edges are firm, then flip to cook the other side until golden brown.
Drain on a towel and serve hot.

name: Toast
description: Crisp, golden-brown toasted bread served with your choice of topping—from classic butter, cinnamon, and sugar to honey, jam, or trendy avocado.

ingredients.text: 1 or more slices of bread, sized to fit your toaster
ingredients.name: bread

instructions: Ensure that the toaster is plugged in, generally clean, and functional.

Place some bread slices into the toaster. Usually, you must place each slice into a separate slot. Some toasters can hold 2 slices in an extra-wide slot. If you use a toaster oven, you may need to lay the bread slices flat on a metal grill inside the toaster oven.
If the toaster has a darkness control, adjust it as desired.
Activate the toaster.
Watch the bread as it browns. If it starts to get excessively dark, activate the pop up mechanism and carefully remove the toast.
If you are unable to make the toast pop out, unplug the toaster. Do not reach into a slotted toaster, whether with your hand or a metal tool, while it is plugged in or very hot.
Spread your choice of topping on the toast with a knife, spatula, or spoon.

name: Corn Muffins
description: Moist and sweet corn muffins with a slightly crunchy crust, made with cornmeal, yogurt, and a touch of sugar.

ingredients.text: 1 cup plus 1 Tbsp (150 g) bleached all-purpose flour
ingredients.name: all-purpose flour

ingredients.text: 4 Tbsp plus 4 tsp (66 g) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

instructions: Mix the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together. Whisk together the egg and yogurt, and stir them quickly into the dry goods, leaving some lumps.
Add the melted butter and fold in.
Pour into ramekins or muffin tins.
Bake for 15–18 minutes at 400°F, or until the tops are golden.

name: Nigerian Wheat Swallow
description: A Nigerian wheat-flour swallow thickened until lump-free and served with soups and stews such as ẹgusi, okro, or ogbono.
instructions: Put water in a pot, and bring it to a boil.
Gradually stir in the flour, mixing until the mixture is thick and lump-free.
Add a small amount of water, and cook for few minutes.
Serve with the soup of your choice.

name: Black Bean Chili
description: A hearty, slow-simmered chili made with dried black beans, smoky chipotle and ancho chiles, and warm spices. Topped with a dollop of sour cream for a rich, tangy finish.

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons (30 mL) corn oil or other vegetable oil
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

instructions: Serve the chili hot, topped with sour cream.

name: Potato and Garlic Ravioli Filling
description: A smooth, garlicky potato filling seasoned with chives, olive oil, and bright fresh lemon juice.

ingredients.text: 6 cloves garlic, grated with a micro plane or finely chopped
ingredients.name: garlic

instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender when pierced with a fork.
Peel them as soon as they are cool enough to handle and mash in a bowl.
Sauté the garlic in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and mix well.
Add the chives, lemon juice and seasoning and mix well.
Cover and allow to cool while you prepare the pasta dough.

name: Crullers (Twisted)
description: Twisted crullers made with a buttery, nutmeg-spiced dough, deep-fried until golden brown and finished with confectioners' sugar.
instructions: Cream butter and sugar; add eggs.
Sift flour with baking powder, nutmeg, and salt.
Mix into batter alternately with milk to make a dough.
Chill dough.
Roll dough out ¼ inch (0.75 cm) thick.
Cut dough into strips measuring 1 x 8 inches (2.5 x 20 cm).
Fold each strip in half lengthwise; twist several times and pinch ends together.
Deep fry in hot (380°F / 200˚C) fat until golden brown, flipping to cook both sides.
Place crullers on absorbent paper to drain, and cool.
Sprinkle with confectioners' sugar.

name: Tahini Cookies
description: Whisked tahini, honey, and cinnamon are blended with oats and walnuts, then baked until the edges are lightly browned.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease cookie sheets.
In a medium bowl, stir together the tahini, honey, and cinnamon.
Mix in walnuts and oats until well blended.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets. Cookies should be about 2 inches apart.
Bake for 10 minutes in the preheated oven, or until edges are slightly brown.
Cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes before removing to wire racks to cool completely.

name: Hot Water Crust Pastry
description: A traditional savory pastry dough made with flour, lard, and hot water, used for classic British pies such as pork pie and steak and kidney pie.
instructions: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl. Make a well in the centre.
Place the water and lard into a saucepan over low heat. When the lard has melted, bring to a boil.
Pour the mixture into the centre of the flour.
Working very quickly, mix with a wooden spoon.
Knead briefly with hands to produce a smooth dough.

name: Long Island Roast Duckling with Citrus
description: A classic roast duckling with crispy golden skin, scented with lemon and orange and roasted until tender and juicy.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (4–5 pounds, 1.8–3.6 kg) whole pekin duckling
ingredients.name: pekin duckling

ingredients.text: 1 orange, cut into quarters or eighths
ingredients.name: orange

instructions: Defrost the duck in the fridge if it's frozen, and remove the giblets and any packages from the body cavity.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F and place an oven rack in the center of the oven.
Rinse the duck and pat it dry both inside and out with paper towels.
Pierce the skin every half inch with prongs, pushing the prongs through the skin and into the fat but not into the meat.
Rub plenty of salt and freshly ground pepper on the skin, then place 2 pieces of lemon and 2–4 pieces of orange inside the duck's cavity.
Tie the duck's legs together with a piece of butcher's twine to keep the citrus inside.
Place the duck breast side up on a rack set in a roasting pan with some depth so the fat drips into the pan and not the oven.
Push a meat thermometer into one of the thighs and place the bird on the center rack of the oven.
Cook for 1–1½ hours depending on size.
Remove the duck every 20 minutes to drain the excess fat, rotating it each time to help it crisp evenly.
The duck is done when the skin is golden brown and crispy and the thermometer reads no lower than 165 °F.
Remove the bird from the oven, pour out the liquid from the cavity and discard.
Allow the duck to rest for ten minutes before carving.

name: Thumbprint Jam Cookies
description: A tasty cookie with an "eye" of jam in the middle.
instructions: In a mixer, cream together the butter and sugar.
Once creamed, add the egg and vanilla. Beat until smooth.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the flour and baking powder.
Add flour to creamed mixture. Beat on low speed until thoroughly combined.
Portion out the dough into round, firm balls and place on sheet pan.
Using the end of a wooden spoon, press down on the dough ball to form wells.
Fill each well with jam.
Do not overfill the well, as they will overflow and burn. For the same reason, keep the edges of the dough clean.
Bake at 300°F (160°C) for 22–24 minutes, until a light golden brown.

name: Ofe Awa (Nigerian Awa Leaf Soup)
description: A traditional Nigerian soup made with awa leaves, assorted meats, and aromatic spices blended into a rich, flavorful broth. Especially enjoyed by the Nkanu people.

ingredients.text: Beef or any type of meat, washed
ingredients.name: beef

instructions: Boil the awa leaves in a separate pot for about 10 seconds to remove the bitter taste. Drain, remove excess water, and set aside.
Blend the crayfish, uziza, habanero pepper, yellow pepper, and ogiri into a smooth paste. Transfer to a clean pot.
Add the beef, dryfish, and stockfish to the pot. Wash the mixture from the blender, and pour the water into the meat.
Season with salt, and seasoning cube. Bring to a boil, and let simmer.
Stir in the palm oil, then the ground ogbono. Simmer for about 10 minutes.
Stir in the awa leaves, and remove from the heat.
Serve with semovita, eba, wheat, or any swallow of your choice.

name: Tegabino Shiro (Ethiopian Spiced Chickpea Dip)
description: A flavorful Ethiopian dip made with chickpea flour, aromatic spices, and sautéed onion. It is delicious served with injera or bread as an appetizer or snack.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for garnish
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: In a medium-sized saucepan, whisk together the chickpea flour and water until well combined, ensuring there are no lumps.
Place the saucepan over medium heat and cook the mixture, stirring continuously, until it thickens to a smooth consistency. This usually takes about 10–15 minutes.
In a separate pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes soft and translucent.
Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger, and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the berbere spice blend, paprika, cayenne pepper, and salt to the pan. Mix well to coat the onions, garlic, and ginger with the spices.
Transfer the spiced onion mixture to the thickened chickpea flour mixture and stir well to combine all the flavors. Continue cooking for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and cayenne pepper according to your preference.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let cool slightly. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley or cilantro before serving.

name: Sweet Italian Sausage Skillet
description: Sweet Italian sausage, spiral pasta, tomatoes, and green beans simmered together in a savory tomato sauce and topped with provolone or mozzarella.

ingredients.text: 2 cups (480 ml) rotini or other spiral pasta
ingredients.name: rotini

ingredients.text: 12 oz (330 g) sweet Italian sausage links
ingredients.name: sweet Italian sausage

ingredients.text: 14.5 oz (410 g) cut green Italian beans, drained
ingredients.name: green bean

ingredients.text: 2 oz (55 g) shredded provolone or mozzarella
ingredients.name: provolone

instructions: Cook pasta and drain.
Meanwhile, brown sliced sausage in hot oil in large skillet for 5 minutes, then drain away the fat.
Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato paste, broth, and drained beans.
Bring to boil, then reduce heat.
Simmer, covered, 10 minutes.
Stir in cooked pasta.
Sprinkle with cheese.

name: French Meringue
description: A simple meringue made by whipping egg whites with cream of tartar and sugar, ideal for baked cookies or a crisp dessert base.

ingredients.text: ¼ tsp cream of tartar or a few drops lemon juice
ingredients.name: cream of tartar

ingredients.text: 8 oz (250 g) superfine sugar or sifted confectioners' sugar
ingredients.name: superfine sugar

instructions: Whip the egg whites and cream of tartar until they reach soft peaks.
Add the first amount of sugar, little by little, while beating by hand or machine.
Whip until stiff.
Stop beating and fold in the remaining sugar, if used, with a spatula.
Use as desired or in your recipe.

name: Machacado con Huevo (Eggs with Shredded Beef)
description: A Mexican dish of scrambled eggs combined with shredded dried beef, served with warm flour tortillas, refried beans, cheese, and salsa.

ingredients.text: 10 ea. 8-inch soft taco-size flour tortillas, warmed
ingredients.name: flour tortilla

ingredients.text: 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack Cheese
ingredients.name: cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions: Heat butter in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add eggs; cook, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes or until eggs just begin to set.
Stir in shredded beef filling. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes or until eggs are cooked and beef is heated through.
Serve eggs with tortillas, beans, cheese, and salsa.

name: White Chocolate Cheesecake
description: A creamy baked white chocolate cheesecake with a shortbread, almond, and butter crust.
instructions: Mix ingredients for the crust (shortbread crumbs, ground almonds, sugar, almond extract, and melted butter) and press into the bottom of a springform pan.
Bake at 200°C for 5–6 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool.
When cool, grease the sides of the pan lightly.
Melt and cool the chocolate.
Mix together cream cheeses, then add eggs, one at a time.
Mix in sugar, flour, vanilla, and almond extract.
Stir 1 cup of mixture into the chocolate, then mix all.
Pour into the pan and bake at 160°C for 40 minutes.

name: Veal Stock
description: A rich, deeply flavored stock made from veal and chicken bones simmered with aromatic vegetables and herbs for hours. Perfect as a base for soups, sauces, and braises.

ingredients.text: 5 lb veal shank, sawn into 2-inch lengths
ingredients.name: veal shank

ingredients.text: 2 lb veal shin bones, sawn into 2-inch lengths
ingredients.name: veal shin bone

ingredients.text: ½ lb (2 medium) onions, in medium dice
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: 4 oz (2 medium) carrots, peeled and in medium dice
ingredients.name: carrot

ingredients.text: 4 oz (2 stalks) celery with leaves, sliced
ingredients.name: celery

ingredients.text: 4 oz (2 medium) leeks including 2 inches of the green part, sliced and washed thoroughly
ingredients.name: leek

ingredients.text: 2 medium ripe tomatoes (for brown stock only), peeled, seeded, juiced, and diced
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: ½ cup tomato purée (for brown stock only)
ingredients.name: tomato purée

instructions: Put the veal and chicken bones into a stock pot, and add enough water to cover the bones by 2 inches.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, and skim off any scum as it forms. Simmer for 30 minutes—do not boil.
Add the vegetables and seasonings and simmer for 6 to 8 hours.
Remove the bones with tongs or a spider and strain into another container. Rinse the pot.
Strain the stock back into the stock pot through a double layer of damp cheesecloth.
Place the pot in a sink of cold water and allow to cool, then refrigerate.
Remove from the refrigerator and lift off the layer of fat.
Divide into suitably sized portions and freeze.
Brown the bones and vegetables in a 400°F (180°C) oven in 2 tablespoons of butter, turning from time to time. Do not allow them to burn.
Add bones and vegetables to the stock pot, then deglaze the browning pan with water, and add it to the pot.
Simmer for 30 minutes, removing scum as it forms.
Add the tomato and the tomato purée and proceed with the recipe as above.

name: Pork Braised with Garlic and Onions of Indonesia (Babi Kecap)
description: A traditional Indonesian braised pork dish cooked with garlic, onions, ginger, and soy sauce until tender and flavorful.
instructions: Cut the meat into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes.
Add the onions, garlic and ginger to a pan and cook at around 200°C.
Add the pork and mix with the soy sauce and black pepper (and chili pepper if desired).
After about 3–4 minutes, reduce the heat to around 120°C and cook, covered, for one hour.
Serve with nice-tasting rice.

name: Apple Stuffing
description: A hearty cornbread stuffing with dried apples, walnuts, apple jelly, eggs, and Fontina cheese. It pairs beautifully with pork chops, pork roasts, or roast turkey.

ingredients.text: 4 egg whites, beaten to stiff peaks with ⅛ tsp cream of tartar
ingredients.name: egg white

instructions: Combine all ingredients except cheese and egg whites. Gently fold in whipped egg whites, in a few batches.
Pour into a roasting pan. Top with shredded cheese and bake at 325°F for 30 minutes, or until browned and bubbly on top.
Remove and let rest for 7 minutes. Serve warm or use for Apple Stuffed Pork Chops.

name: Cabbage Rolls in Yogurt Sauce (Sarmi)
description: A Bulgarian stuffed cabbage dish with significant Greek influences, these tender 'white' rolls are simmered and served coated in a yogurt sauce.

ingredients.text: 500 g (about 1 ⅛ lb) minced (ground) veal or beef
ingredients.name: veal or beef

ingredients.text: 30–40 grape or cabbage leaves (depending on the size, a substantially smaller number of leaves may be needed)
ingredients.name: grape leaf or cabbage leaf

ingredients.text: 100 g butter or ½ cup sunflower oil
ingredients.name: butter or sunflower oil

instructions: Boil the vine or cabbage leaves in salted water until they look cooked and are just bendable enough to roll. Drain and allow to cool during the following steps.
Lightly fry the finely chopped onions in a small amount of oil, and stir in a teaspoon or more of paprika.
Add the meat, rice, pepper, mint, and finely chopped parsley, then cook until the meat looks almost done.
Add ¾ cup of water, bring to a boil, then immediately cover and reduce heat to a bare minimum for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed by the rice.
Uncover and fluff as needed with a small spatula or spoon. Allow to cool to handling temperature.
Put 1 teaspoon of the meat mixture on each leaf and roll it into a fully enclosed package, similar to a small egg roll.
A bit more filling can be used if you are using large cabbage leaves, but try to make all the rolls somewhat uniform in size.
Arrange the rolls in a saucepan, add 1½ cups of warm water, cover, and simmer gently over low heat.
In the meantime, mix the yogurt with a bit of paprika for color (or omit if you wish to keep the dish somewhat white in color), and other spices as you desire.
When rolls are done, allow to cool a bit, gently transfer to a dish, and add the yogurt mixture to coat.
Serve with vegetables of your choice. Enjoy!

name: Nigerian Pepper Sauce with Beef and Eggs
description: A rich, fiery Nigerian pepper sauce made with beef and hard-boiled eggs. The blended pepper, tomato, and onion base is simmered with seasoned beef for a hearty accompaniment to rice, plantain, or yam.
instructions: Blend the red peppers, habanero peppers, tomatoes, onion, ginger, and garlic to a paste.
Heat the palm oil in a skillet. Stir in the chopped onions, and cook for a few minutes until the onions are softened.
Stir in the ground crayfish, chili flakes, salt, thyme, locust beans, and beef. Cook for a few minutes.
Stir in the pepper paste. Leave to simmer for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the boiled eggs, and leave to simmer for a few more minutes.
Serve with white rice, boiled yam, boiled potatoes and many others.

name: Cheesy Chicken Pasta
description: A quick and creamy pasta loaded with melted mozzarella, cheddar and cream cheese, tossed with tender chicken and a savoury hit of hoisin sauce.

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (85 g/3 oz) dried pasta (whatever shape you like)
ingredients.name: pasta

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (75 g/2.6 oz) cream cheese
ingredients.name: cream cheese

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (75 g/2.6 oz) grated mozzarella cheese
ingredients.name: mozzarella cheese

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (75 g/2.6 oz) grated cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: cheddar cheese

ingredients.text: 1 cup (125 g/4.4 oz) chopped cooked chicken
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: ½ cup (125 ml/4.2 US fl oz) heavy whipping cream
ingredients.name: heavy whipping cream

instructions: Bring a pot of water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook for about 10 minutes (or until the pasta is soft).
Drain the pasta so that no water remains in the pan. Return drained pasta to the pot.
Add the cream, cheeses, chicken, and hoisin sauce to the pasta.
Cook for a few minutes to warm everything through, then serve.

name: Boiled Plantain With Vegetable Sauce
description: Tender boiled plantain served with a flavourful Nigerian-style vegetable sauce made with tomatoes, spinach, crayfish and dryfish.
instructions: Cut the unripe plantains in half and wash them.
Put the plantains in a pot. Add just enough water to cover the peels, and season with salt. Turn the heat to low and cook for about 1 hour.
Check occasionally with a fork to see if it has fully softened; when done, you will notice the peels turning brown and the interior becoming more yellow.
Drain the plantains.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add the onion, and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, and cook until they are no longer sour.
Add seasoning cubes, ground crayfish, curry powder, salt, and pepper.
Add the green onion, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and dryfish.
Serve with boiled plantains.

name: Au Jus Sandwich
description: A classic American French dip sandwich featuring tender slow-cooked beef served on a hoagie roll, accompanied by rich meat drippings for dipping.

ingredients.text: 2–3 pounds (0.91–1.4 kg) roast or other cut of beef
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: 1 can (~2 cups / 16 oz / 470 ml) beef consommé, bouillon cube equivalent, or additional roast beef
ingredients.name: beef consommé

ingredients.text: 1 can (~2 cups / 16 oz / 470 ml) French onion soup
ingredients.name: french onion soup

instructions: Combine all the ingredients except the rolls in a slow cooker or crock pot. Let the mixture simmer for at least six hours. This step is critical because it makes the meat tender.
Serve beef on split rolls.

You can either pre-dip the sandwich, or serve with a bowl of meat drippings. When serving the drippings separately, remove the beef shreds from the juices and serve with a small bowl of meat drippings on the side. Dip the sandwiches in the drippings as you eat.

name: Roast Turkey with Stuffing
description: A traditional roast turkey with a savory cornbread, walnut, and dried fruit stuffing, perfect as the centerpiece of a Thanksgiving feast.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup dried cherries, stemmed and finely chopped
ingredients.name: dried cherry

ingredients.text: 2 ½ cups shredded cooked chicken or turkey
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: 1 ½ quarts turkey stock or chicken stock
ingredients.name: turkey stock

instructions: Combine stuffing ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Place the rack in the lowest position of the oven.
Remove the neck and giblets.
Rinse the turkey and pat it dry with paper towels.
Place the turkey, breast side up, on a rack in the roasting pan. Rub the skin with softened butter, and season with salt and pepper.
Fill the body cavity with stuffing.
Place a meat thermometer in the thickest part of one thigh.
Position an aluminum foil tent over the turkey.
Place the turkey in the oven and pour 2 cups of stock into the bottom of the roasting pan.
Roast the turkey for 2½ hours, basting the entire turkey every 30 minutes with the juices on the bottom of the pan. Add stock to the drippings as they become dry, about 1–2 cups at a time.
Remove aluminum foil tent.

Roast until the meat reaches 185°F and the stuffing reaches 165°F. This should take about 4 hours. If the stuffing isn't done by the time the turkey is ready, scoop the stuffing out and bake it alone in the oven until it reaches the correct temperature.
Serve immediately.

name: Causa Rellena con Pollo
description: A traditional Peruvian layered dish of creamy mashed potatoes sandwiching a seasoned shredded chicken filling, garnished with hard-boiled eggs, black olives, and lettuce.

ingredients.text: 10 medium potatoes (yellow, new, or red are a good choice)
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 1 pound of shredded boiled chicken meat
ingredients.name: chicken

instructions: Cook and peel potatoes. Allow to cool, then mash.
In a bowl combine the chicken, mayonnaise, onion, salt, and pepper.
Line a deep dish with plastic wrap, or place a molding cylinder on a plate.
Add the mashed potatoes to form a bed about 1 cm tall at the bottom.
Add a second layer of 1 cm of the chicken mixture evenly over the potato.
Top the chicken mixture with a final layer of potato, forming a sandwich of chicken inside two layers of potato.
Unmold or remove the cylinder.
Garnish with lettuce and mayonnaise.
Cut the hard boiled eggs in discs and place on top. Add black olives, if desired.
This dish can be served slightly cold.

name: Pierogi II
description: Soft homemade dumplings with a tender dough, filled and boiled then pan-fried in butter until golden brown. Serve warm or cold as a comforting dish.

ingredients.text: Pierogi filling, such as sauerkraut filling or cheese filling
ingredients.name: pierogi filling

instructions: Sift and measure flour with salt into a large bowl.
Slightly beat egg with fork, and add egg to flour mixture.
Mix in enough water to make a dough that's soft enough to roll out with a rolling pin but not so dry that it spits and cracks.
Roll out dough on a floured bread board to about the thickness of a cracker.
Use a large rimmed glass or a big biscuit cutter to cut rounds approximately 3–4 inches in diameter.
Fill each round with a generous spoonful of filling, and fold dough in half to make a half-moon.
Pinch and seal the edge of the dough with fingers then gently fold and pinch edge to make a ruffled edge with about ¼-inch folds.
Drop each pierogi into a large pot of boiling salted water and boil until they float to the top. Remove each carefully with a slotted spoon.
Fry the pierogi in a skillet with melted butter until golden brown.
Serve warm or cold.

name: Out of Salad Dressing Salad Dressing
description: A creamy homemade salad dressing made with lemon juice, Parmesan cheese, garlic salt, mayonnaise, and milk. Easy to whip up from pantry staples and tastes even better after chilling overnight.
instructions: Mix together lemon juice, Parmesan cheese, garlic salt, and mayonnaise until smooth.
Stir in milk, adjusting the amount or adding a little water, to make the dressing as thin or thick as you like.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours, or overnight.

name: Backyard BBQ Chicken
description: A classic American backyard barbecue chicken, rubbed with a smoky spice blend and glazed with a tangy tomato-honey sauce.

ingredients.text: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts and drumsticks
ingredients.name: chicken

instructions: Combine dry ingredients and rub onto chicken.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Combine liquid ingredients, bring to a boil, and simmer until reduced by ⅓.
Place on medium grill, and turn often, brushing with sauce when turned until interior temperature reaches 165 °F (74 °C).
Let rest for 10 minutes; serve.

name: Greek Salad
description: A fresh Mediterranean salad of chopped tomatoes, cucumber, onions, peppers and olives, tossed with olive oil and vinegar, and topped with a slice of feta cheese and oregano.

ingredients.text: Red or white onions, sliced into half-moons
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: Green bell peppers, cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, peppers, and olives in a deep bowl.
Add enough olive oil, vinegar or lemon juice, and salt to taste. Toss the ingredients for half a minute.
Place a feta cheese slice on top and season with a splash of olive oil.
Top with a sprig of oregano if desired.

name: Jalebi (Fritters in Syrup)
description: A sweet Indian fritter shaped like a slightly large, chaotic pretzel, fried until golden and soaked in fragrant rosewater syrup. Well-made jalebi has a tart element with a sweet taste.

ingredients.text: 3 cups of vegetable oil/ghee for deep frying
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

instructions: Mix up the batter ingredients until smooth.
Let the batter sit unrefrigerated and uncovered overnight (about 12 hours).
Mix the sugar, water, and cream of tartar for the syrup.
Stir the syrup over moderate heat until the sugar is dissolved.
Put on high heat and boil for 5 minutes.
Let the syrup cool, and stir in the rosewater. Use food coloring to tint it light orange.
Put the vegetable oil in a wide wok-like dish, and heat to about 350°F (175°C).
Put the batter into a pastry bag with about a ¼ inch opening. If it is too dry to squeeze out, mix in a bit of water.
Squeeze the batter into the oil, making a couple of figure-eight shapes and loops on top of each other. The shape should be about 3 inches on its longest side.
Fry each jalebi until golden brown, let the oil drain off, then soak in syrup for a minute before serving.

name: Egg Roast
description: A simple, tasty Indian dish of hard-boiled eggs coated in a fragrant masala of tomatoes, onions, spices, and curry leaves.

ingredients.text: 1 small tomato, chopped into large chunks
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: 1 sprig curry leaves, leaves separated from the stalk
ingredients.name: curry leaf

instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, add onions and a pinch of salt, and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add the coriander, chili, and turmeric powders, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the minced tomato to the kadai, and sauté until the oil separates from the mixture.
Add the green chillies, and fry for a few minutes.
Add the eggs, and coat the pieces with the mixture.
Add the chunked tomatoes, curry leaves, cinnamon, and clove. Sauté for a couple of minutes, and serve.

name: Teriyaki Salmon
description: Wild salmon filets marinated in a bright blend of soy sauce, ginger, garlic, chiles and citrus, then grilled over hardwood charcoal for a smoky, lacquered finish.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24 ounces) wild salmon filets with skin, pin bones removed
ingredients.name: salmon

instructions: Combine all ingredients except salmon in a blender until smooth. Pour into a plastic bag and add salmon. Toss to coat, seal, removing as much air as possible, and refrigerate up to 4 hours.
Remove salmon from marinade and pat dry with paper towels. Brush all sides with oil.
