Preheat 4½ pounds charcoal in starter. Once hot, disperse evenly around bottom of grill. Reapply grate and once hot, swab with towel.
Add salmon to hottest part of grill skin side up, and cook 3–5 minutes per side for medium, rotating 90 degrees halfway to make grill marks.
Remove to a plate and cover tightly with aluminum foil. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Zambian Fish Stew
description: Tender fish pieces simmer in a savory tomato-based sauce with colorful vegetables and aromatic spices. This rich, comforting stew is a popular Zambian dish often served with nshima or rice.

ingredients.text: 1 pound fish (e.g. tilapia, catfish, or any firm white fish), cut into pieces
ingredients.name: fish

instructions: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add the diced tomato, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper to the pot. Cook until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the fish stock or water and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Gently place the fish pieces into the pot, making sure they are submerged in the liquid.
Season the stew with ground cayenne pepper, ground paprika, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt. Stir well to distribute the spices.
Cover the pot and let the stew simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork.
Taste the stew and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or spices according to your preference.
Remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Candied Yams
description: Yams are boiled until half done, cubed, and baked in a rich brown sugar, vanilla, and margarine syrup until tender.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Boil yams in skins until about half done.
Drain water from yams, remove skins, and cut in cubes.
Place yam cubes in a greased baking dish and dot with margarine.
Make a syrup by boiling brown sugar, water, and vanilla together. Pour over the yams.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, basting frequently with syrup, until yams are tender.

name: Tequila Lime Strip Steak
description: Bold strip steaks marinated in tequila, lime juice, and olive oil, then grilled over mesquite wood for a smoky, zesty finish.
instructions: Combine liquid ingredients and salt in a gallon zip-top freezer bag. Add steaks and squeeze as much air out as possible. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Remove steaks from marinade and discard extra. Place steak rub in a pie pan and add steaks, pressing lightly to help adhesion on both sides.
Spray cold grill grate with nonstick cooking spray. Set up for direct and indirect heat and add some soaked mesquite chips to the coals.
Place steaks on hottest part of grill and cook for 2–3 minutes per side.
Move to the cooler part of the grill and cook, turning once, until internal temperature reaches 10° cooler than your preferred doneness.
Remove and let rest for 7 minutes. Slice thinly across the grain on a bias and serve.

name: Sweet Potatoes Sautéed with Honey
description: A simple and delicious side dish of sweet potato cubes sautéed in butter and oil with honey and a touch of smoked paprika.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp (5 g) flavorless oil (such as canola oil)
ingredients.name: oil

instructions: Peel the sweet potato, then chop it into 1 cm (0.4 in) cubes. The pieces should all be around that size to ensure even cooking. Discard the peel.
Heat a large frying pan on a stovetop burner over medium heat.
Mix the honey, salt, and paprika together in a small bowl.
Add the butter and oil to the pan, then wait for the butter to melt fully.
Add the potatoes to the pan and stir until evenly distributed around the pan, with no chunks on top of each other.
Pour the honey mixture over the potatoes and stir until it's evenly distributed across all of the potato pieces.
Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring the sweet potatoes every other minute.
Stir the potato pieces to prevent them from burning on one side, but don't stir too frequently or they won't brown sufficiently—once every 2 minutes or so is ideal.
Serve topped with extra salt to your liking and enjoy!

name: Potato and Sausage Casserole (Papa Turmada)
description: A baked Colombian casserole from Cúcuta layered with sliced potatoes, criolla hogao sauce, fried pork sausage, hard-boiled eggs, milk-soaked bread, and melted cheeses.

ingredients.text: 1 cup hogao with 6 sliced fried pork sausages
ingredients.name: hogao

instructions: Boil potatoes until tender (20 minutes).
Cut bread into small squares and wet with milk.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch (about 25 x 32-cm) Pyrex baking dish.
Put a layer of potato, then a layer of hogao and sausage, a layer of sliced egg, a layer of wet bread and a layer of mozzarella cheese. Optionally, add thyme to the hogao.
Repeat with another layer of potato, wet bread, and Parmesan cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°F (175°C), and serve.

name: Ashkenazi Charoset
description: A sweet, flavorful charoset made with chopped apples, walnuts, sweet red wine, cinnamon, and honey. Chilling it overnight brings out its best flavor.

ingredients.text: 1½ cups (360 g) peeled, cored, and chopped apples (e.g. MacIntosh)
ingredients.name: apple

instructions: Mix all ingredients together, and refrigerate overnight for best flavor.
Adjust seasoning, if necessary, after it's chilled.
Serve with matzoh, or just eat with a spoon.

name: Stewed Vegan Maki
description: A vegan sushi roll featuring a medley of vegetables stewed in a savory miso and sake sauce, wrapped with seasoned sushi rice and nori.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (60 ml) thinly-julienned daikon radish
ingredients.name: daikon radish

instructions: In a wok or saucepan, combine vegetables and sake. Bring to a simmer and let cook until most of the sake is gone, stirring often.
Add the water and miso, bring this to a simmer, and let it cook until the vegetables are soft (but not mushy), stirring often.
Remove the vegetables from the pan, and reduce the remaining liquid to a thick sauce consistency.
Pour the sauce over the vegetables and mix thoroughly. Let cool, then mix in vinegar.
Evenly spread rice over nori, dab half the wasabi across each, then place the vegetable mix across this. Roll tightly.

name: Mung Bean and Brown Rice Curry
description: A hearty vegetarian curry of mung beans and brown rice, seasoned with turmeric, cumin, curry powder, and ginger and finished with cabbage, carrots, and green pepper. It can be served hot or cold as a complete meal, with leftovers that keep for a week refrigerated.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan and add the mustard seeds.
When they begin to pop, add the turmeric and fold in the rice and beans until coated with oil.
Add the rest of the spices and water.
Simmer for about 45 minutes; most of the water will be absorbed.
Remove from heat and add vegetables.
Make the marinade and pour the mix in.

name: Phở Bò (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)
description: Vietnam's iconic beef noodle soup, featuring a deeply aromatic broth simmered for hours with beef bones, charred onions, and warm spices, served over rice noodles with rare sliced beef and fresh garnishes.

ingredients.text: 2 large white onions, cut into quarters
ingredients.name: white onion

ingredients.text: 5 lbs beef bones (choose ones with a bit of meat on them)
ingredients.name: beef bones

ingredients.text: Phở noodles (thin, flat rice noodles), soaked in hot water until soft and drained
ingredients.name: phở noodles

ingredients.text: Finely sliced beef sirloin (ask your butcher)
ingredients.name: beef sirloin

instructions: Fry onions in oil until lightly browned. Remove and drain.
Rinse the beef bones, place in a stockpot, cover with cold water, and bring slowly to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 10–15 minutes. For a clear broth skim off foam.

After this initial cooking, add cooked onions, ginger, cinnamon, cardamom, star anise, cloves, garlic and peppercorns. Bring to a boil again and gently simmer the stock, partially covered, for a minimum of 6 hours but up to 12 hours if you can, skimming regularly. If necessary, add more water to keep the bones covered.
Strain stock to remove the vegetable and spices and discard them. Return the broth to the stove to keep it boiling hot.

In a large soup bowl, place a handful of cooked phở noodles, top with thinly sliced raw beef, and ladle on generous amounts of very hot broth, which will cook the raw beef. Garnish with sliced onions, scallions and coriander, and serve immediately.

name: Sambal Tempoyak (Anchovies with Fermented Durian Chili Paste)
description: A spicy Indonesian sambal made with fermented durian paste, dried anchovies, and petai seeds, stir-fried with aromatic lemon grass and chillis. Best served with rice.
instructions: Remove heads and entrails from ikan bilis. Wash and soak for 10 minutes. Deep-fry until crisp.
Combine 2 tbsp of tempoyak, coconut milk, salt, chilis, chili paste, turmeric root, and petai seeds. Grind to make a paste.
Heat oil in a pan and stir-fry the sambal paste with lemon grass until it becomes fragrant.
Add the rest of tempoyak and boil gently over low heat until gravy is thickened.
Add salt to taste. Serve with crisp ikan bilis, petai and rice.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Oatmeal
description: A comforting bowl of oatmeal made creamy with milk, peanut butter, honey, and mashed banana for natural sweetness.

ingredients.text: 1 cup rolled oats or instant oats
ingredients.name: oats

ingredients.text: ½ tbsp (or more) honey, to taste
ingredients.name: honey

instructions: Cook the oats in water. If using regular oats this should take around 10 minutes, while instant oats will cook more quickly.
Put the cooked oats in a bowl.
Add milk, peanut butter, honey and sliced banana.
Mash until the banana and ingredients are all thoroughly combined.
Top with honey and serve warm.

name: Haupia (Hawaiian Coconut Pudding)
description: A traditional Hawaiian coconut pudding made with coconut milk, sugar, and cornstarch, gently cooked until thickened and set into delicate squares.
instructions: Mix coconut milk with sugar and salt over a medium heat.
Slowly add cornstarch and stir until thickened.
Pour into a pan or square form.
Cool for 1 hour or until fully set.
Unmold and cut into squares.

name: Grilled Sirloin Steak
description: A juicy, flavorful top sirloin steak grilled over high heat, seasoned with olive oil, salt, and black pepper, then topped with butter.

ingredients.text: 1 top sirloin steak (also known as top butt, center cut sirloin, or hip steak)
ingredients.name: top sirloin steak

instructions: Brush steak with olive oil. Sprinkle both sides liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Place steak on a high grill. Cook 1 minute, then rotate 90° and cook for another 1 minute. Flip and repeat this process for the other side.
Move to medium heat and cook, turning often, until desired "doneness" is achieved.
Remove to a plate and top with butter. Cover with aluminum foil and let rest 10 minutes.
Slice thinly across the grain on a bias. Serve warm.

name: Tomato Coulis
description: A rich, slow-simmered tomato sauce with onions, garlic, and herbes de Provence, reduced for hours to concentrate its flavor.
instructions: Fry onions in olive oil until translucent. Ensure that the onions don't burn.
Add lots of minced garlic. Again, ensure it doesn't burn.
Add a large amount of sugar. Don't caramelise it.
Add tomatoes to onions and garlic, along with additional olive oil.
Simmer for approximately 4 hours to lose as much water as possible.
Add salt, pepper, herbes de Provence, and vinegar.

name: Kekefia (Nigerian Plantain Porridge)
description: A tasty Nigerian plantain porridge made with pepper, crayfish, dried fish, palm oil, and aromatic scent leaves. It is a popular dish among southern Nigerians, especially the Ijaw people, and is easy to cook.

ingredients.text: Unripe plantain, peeled, washed, and diced
ingredients.name: plantain

ingredients.text: Fresh pepper, blended to a paste
ingredients.name: pepper

instructions: Add the diced plantain to a pot, and cover with water. Bring to a boil, and simmer until cooked.
Stir in the pepper paste, ground crayfish, and shredded dried fish.
Add scent leaves, palm oil, diced onions, periwinkles, and salt. Cook without stirring for about 10 minutes.
Stir and simmer over low heat.

name: Four in One Pizza
description: A creative pizza divided into four flavor quadrants, allowing you to enjoy four different topping combinations on a single crispy crust.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (2 ounces) shredded cheddar cheese
ingredients.name: cheddar cheese

ingredients.text: ½ cup BBQ sauce mixed with shredded chicken
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon thin strips of fresh basil
ingredients.name: basil

ingredients.text: 2 slices Canadian bacon, cut in quarters
ingredients.name: canadian bacon

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Spray cookie sheet with cooking spray and sprinkle lightly with cornmeal, if desired.
Unroll pizza dough and press out on cookie sheet into a 12 x 14-inch shape, then brush with olive oil.
Bake crust for 6–8 minutes.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over the crust in a cross shape to divide crust in fourths.
In each corner, spread one of the above toppings (or one of your own!).
Sprinkle mozzarella cheese over the top of all.
Bake another 10–14 minutes, until cheese is bubbly but not burned.
Cut each corner into 4 squares.

name: Tripe Soup (Shkembe Chorba)
description: Cooked tripe is simmered in beef stock with onion, bell pepper, tomato paste, and herbs to create a traditional Bulgarian soup. The finished bowls are topped with grated Kashkaval cheese, parsley, and crushed garlic.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. bell pepper, cut into thin-strips
ingredients.name: bell pepper

instructions: Combine onion, red pepper, butter in large saucepan.
Sprinkle flour over onion mixture, then stir in the tomato paste.
Cut tripe into thin strips.
Add tripe pieces, stock, salt, marjoram and bay leaf to onion mixture.
Partially cover the pot and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove and discard bay leaf.
Pour soup into a tureen or serve in individual bowls.
In a small bowl, combine parsley, garlic and cheese. Sprinkle over hot soup and serve immediately.

name: Spanakopita
description: A Greek spinach pie filled with feta, cottage cheese, Parmesan, herbs, and lemon. Layered with phyllo and baked until puffed and golden.

ingredients.text: 900 g (2 lbs) fresh spinach or 580 g (20 oz) frozen, thawed, and drained spinach
ingredients.name: spinach

ingredients.text: ¾ cup small curd cottage cheese
ingredients.name: cottage cheese

ingredients.text: ¼ cup freshly grated parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: parmesan cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Wash the spinach, remove large stems, and chop.
Place the spinach in a steamer over boiling water and steam for 2 minutes, or until wilted and reduced in volume.
Drain, pressing out any liquid with the back of a spoon.
Heat the oil in a large skillet. Add onion and cook over medium heat until slightly tender.
Add scallions and cook until limp. Remove from heat. Stir in parsley, dill, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Add the cheeses, spinach, and lemon juice to the skillet and mix.
Add eggs and mix again gently.
Brush a 9x12-inch baking dish with some of the butter.
Lay a sheet of phyllo dough across the bottom of the dish, covering the entire surface and letting the edges fold upward against the sides.
Brush with butter, and place another sheet on top.
Continue layering the phyllo, brushing each sheet, until the bottom of the dish is covered with about 8 sheets.
Place half of the spinach filling on top of the phyllo, smoothing it with a rubber spatula until evenly distributed.
Cover the filling with 5–8 phyllo sheets, brushing each layer with butter. Place the remaining spinach filling on top and smooth as above.
Cover with 5–8 phyllo sheets, brushing with butter as above.
Roll up all overhanging phyllo sheets and crumble any broken sheet bits on top.
Drizzle any remaining clarified butter over top.
Place the spanakopita in the oven on a medium rack.
Bake for 45 minutes, or until puffed and golden.
Let sit for 10 minutes before cutting and serving.

name: Trifle
description: A traditional layered dessert of sponge cake, sherry, fruit jelly, and peaches finished with creamy custard and whipped double cream.

ingredients.text: 1 swiss roll or similar sponge cake
ingredients.name: sponge cake

ingredients.text: 1 packet/sachet fruit-flavoured jelly (can be found under the brand names "Quick-Jel" or "Jell-O")
ingredients.name: fruit-flavoured jelly

ingredients.text: Hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other sweet topping (optional)
ingredients.name: sweet topping

instructions: Slice the Swiss roll approximately ¾-inch (2 cm) thick, and line the base of a Pyrex casserole dish with it.
Pour sherry over the swiss roll.
Drain the peaches, keeping the juice/syrup aside, and arrange the peaches over the swiss roll.
Prepare the jelly as per the instructions; you may wish to use the syrup from the peaches for this.
Pour the jelly into the casserole dish and allow it to set in the fridge.
Make the custard as per the instructions, using fresh or powdered custard rather than canned.
Allow the custard to cool to lukewarm, then pour it into the casserole.
Allow the custard to set in the fridge.
Whip the cream for the top of the trifle and spread it over the custard.
Garnish with hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other cake decorations.
Serve!

name: Pickled Herring
description: Herring fillets are brined overnight, then layered with lemon and red onion beneath a tangy, spiced vinegar pickling liquid.

ingredients.text: 2 cups distilled or white wine vinegar
ingredients.name: vinegar

ingredients.text: 1 lemon (thinly sliced, with rind removed; only the flesh should be left)
ingredients.name: lemon

instructions: Heat 4 cups of water enough to dissolve salt. Let cool to room temperature.
Submerge the herring fillets in the brine and refrigerate overnight, or up to 24 hours.
Meanwhile, bring the sugar, vinegar, the remaining cup of water and all the spices to a boil. Simmer 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and let this steep until cool.
When the herring have brined, layer them in a glass jar with the sliced lemon and red onion. Divide the spices between your containers if you are using more than one.
Pour over the cooled pickling liquid and seal the jars. Wait at least a day before eating. Store in the fridge for up to 1 month.

name: Tzatziki
description: Tzatziki is a cool, tasty yogurt sauce that's great over gyros, pitas, salads, lamb, or as a dip.

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon dill (sub. ¼ tablespoon of tarragon if no dill is available)
ingredients.name: dill

instructions: Drain yogurt in a sieve or a cheesecloth for about 3 hours prior to using it.
Drain the cucumber and salt it to further remove moisture.
Combine yogurt, garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice in a bowl and cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or more.
After refrigerating, add dill and cucumber into bowl and mix with a whisk until smooth.
Add pepper and salt to taste.

name: Cranberry Walnut Fudge
description: A creamy white chocolate fudge made with sour cream and folded with walnuts and dried cranberries, then chilled and cut into one-inch pieces.
instructions: Place butter, sour cream, and sugar into a saucepan. Put the saucepan on a stove and cook for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Remove from heat and add vanilla extract, marshmallow creme, and white chocolate chips.
Using a mixing spoon, stir until the mixture is smooth.
Fold in the walnuts and cranberries.
Pour the mixture into an 8x8-inch baking pan.
Put the pan into the refrigerator to cool for 1 hour.
Unmold and cut into 1-inch pieces.

name: French Fries
description: Crispy, light-golden French fries made from thin straw-like potatoes that are parboiled, deep-fried, drained, and evenly salted.

ingredients.text: Potatoes (those with a high dry matter content such as Russet or Maris Piper work best)
ingredients.name: potato

instructions: Peel potatoes, and cut into thin straw-like pieces.
Wash potatoes well with water to remove excess starch.
Place fries in a saucepan with water, and simmer or parboil on the stove for about 15 minutes.
Drain the fries, and dry them well.
Deep fry in 175°C vegetable oil, lard, or drippings for 4–5 minutes until light golden and crisp.
Remove from oil, and place on plate with paper towels to absorb the leftover cooking oil. Transfer to another plate if necessary.
Add salt and shake to ensure all French fries are evenly salted.

name: Mocha Delight
description: A rich layered cake with a graham cracker crust, fudgy brownie base, and espresso-spiked buttercream frosting, finished with whipped cream rosettes and dark chocolate hearts.

ingredients.text: 1 bag Dove Rich Dark Chocolate Hearts
ingredients.name: dark chocolate heart

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Line bottom of 9-inch springform pan with waxed paper; grease.
Add melted butter to graham cracker crumbs and press into bottom of pan.
Prepare brownie mix according to package instructions; spread over crumbs.
Bake until firm, approximately 35 to 50 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Remove from oven to a wire rack; cool completely and remove from pan.
Whisk egg whites and sugar together in a bowl over simmering water until sugar is dissolved.
Remove from heat; using electric mixer, whip until fluffy and cooled.
Add butter one nugget at a time while continuing to beat.
Dissolve espresso powder in warm water; beat into frosting.
Frost top and sides of cake.
Snip small corner of a resealable plastic bag; place whipped cream inside.
Pipe 3 rosettes around outside edges of cake; place a chocolate heart atop each rosette.
Place 8 chocolate hearts in a small resealable plastic bag; microwave until melted, about 15 seconds.
Cut a corner of the bag; randomly drizzle chocolate on dessert plates.
Place a cake wedge on each plate.

name: Lahoh (Spongy Flatbread)
description: Lahoh is a griddle-cooked flatbread similar to a pancake, with a distinctive spongy texture and a porous surface on one side.

ingredients.text: 3 cup of wheat flour or sorghum flour
ingredients.name: wheat flour or sorghum flour

ingredients.text: Dab of margarine or vegetable oil for greasing pan
ingredients.name: margarine or vegetable oil

instructions: Combine semolina and ½ cup of lukewarm water in a bowl.
Bring the mixture to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat, place in a bowl, and leave to thicken.
Stir cold water into the semolina mixture.
Stir in rock salt until fully dissolved into the mixture.
Stir in the wheat flour and yeast.
Mix in another 2 cups of lukewarm water until you get a thin batter.
Cover the batter and let it rest until it is risen and bubbly.
Grease a skillet or frying pan with a little margarine, and heat over medium heat.
Ladle some batter into the pan, and let it spread out. A tiny bit of flour sprinkled in the pan helps prevent sticking.
Cook the batter until the top surface is covered with air pockets like a sponge.
Flip to the other side, and cook for about 5 seconds.
Remove and let cool.
Repeat the cooking process with the remaining batter.

name: Zalabiyeh (Sweet Fritters) II
description: Traditional sweet fritters made from matzah meal, eggs, and water, shaped into patties and fried until golden. A classic treat, especially enjoyed during Passover.
instructions: Combine the salt and matzah meal in a bowl.
Add 4 cups of water and mix thoroughly.
Add another 2½–3 cups of water and mix thoroughly.
Add eggs, continuing to mix ingredients until left with a consistent batter.
If batter is too thin, let it rest for 7–10 minutes until it thickens.
Wet your hands with water, and form the dough into round, flat patties by using a moistened plate as a working base.
Fry patties in a skillet with oil.

name: Egyptian Lentil Soup
description: A hearty, nutritious soup of red lentils, onion, garlic, and aromatic spices, finished with tangy lemon juice and fresh parsley or cilantro.

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
ingredients.name: parsley or cilantro

instructions: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped onion to the pot and sauté until it becomes translucent and slightly golden.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to coat them with the onion and garlic mixture.
Sprinkle the ground cumin, ground coriander, ground paprika, and ground turmeric over the lentils. Stir well to combine and coat the lentils with the spices.
Pour in the vegetable broth or water, ensuring that the lentils are fully submerged.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot. Let the soup simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until the lentils are tender and fully cooked.
Using a blender, purée the soup until smooth and creamy. If using a regular blender, allow the soup to cool slightly before blending, and be careful when transferring hot liquids.
Return the soup to the pot and place it back over low heat.
Stir in the lemon juice and season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
Continue to heat the soup for a few more minutes until it is warmed through.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with chopped parsley or cilantro. Serve hot.

name: Sausage-Egg Breakfast Dish
description: A hearty make-ahead breakfast casserole layered with sage-flavored sausage, eggs, milk, cubes of stale bread, and melted cheddar cheese.
instructions: Brown sausage and sprinkle with pepper.
Drain off excess fat, and let sausage cool.
Beat eggs and add milk.
Fold in cubes of stale bread, cheese, and cooled sausage.
Pour into an 8 by 8-inch baking dish coated with cooking spray.
Refrigerate for at least an hour (or freeze for later).
Preheat oven to 325°F. Bake for 1 hour.
Cool and cut into squares.

name: Cheese Filling for Peynirli Börek
description: A creamy cottage cheese and feta filling seasoned with egg, parsley or dill, and pepper for peynirli börek.
instructions: Mix the feta into the cottage cheese by mashing together with a fork.
Add the beaten egg, chopped herbs and pepper, and stir until just mixed.
Place in a plastic covered container and refrigerate until ready to use.
See Börek recipe for further instructions.

name: Native Jollof Rice
description: A popular Nigerian rice dish made with palm oil and a smooth paste of tomatoes, onions, peppers and crayfish. The rice is cooked with meat stock or water and served hot with plantain (dodo), with optional fish or meat.

ingredients.text: A few fresh Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers (ata rodo)
ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet pepper

ingredients.text: 4 pieces bouillon cubes (or the equivalent amount of powder)
ingredients.name: bouillon cube

ingredients.text: Beef, turkey, and/or chicken meat (optional), boiled
ingredients.name: meat

instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onions, peppers, and crayfish into a smooth paste.
Pour the paste into a dry pot on the fire. Cook to evaporate the excess liquid.
When the water has completely evaporated, add the iru and palm oil. Leave to cook for 10 minutes.
Add meat stock or water, and bring to boil. Adjust seasoning with salt and maggi to taste.
Wash the rice very well with cold water.
Add the rice to the boiling stock, and stir well. Add more liquid if necessary, and allow to cook until the rice is almost tender.
When the rice is almost ready, add the cooked fish or meat. Add the scent leaf, if using.
Serve the jollof rice hot with plantain (dodo).

name: Sunglow Motel-Cafe Pickle Pie
description: A unique pickle pie from Utah's Sunglow Motel-Cafe, featuring sweet pickles in a cinnamon-, nutmeg-, and lemon-scented cream filling.

ingredients.text: 12 oz sweet pickles, drained and ground
ingredients.name: sweet pickle

instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until lemon-colored and thick; beat in cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon extract, cornstarch, cream and margarine.
Stir ground sweet pickles into mixture.
Pour pickle mixture into unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 350°F for 1–1.25 hours, until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.

name: Sindhi Vegetable Kofta
description: Golden-fried vegetable kofta made with carrot, cauliflower, potato, bell pepper, and chiles, served in a spiced tomato sauce with roti, naan, or rice.
instructions: Combine the water, a pinch of salt, and cornstarch. It should be thick and not watery.
Combine the carrot, cauliflower, mashed potatoes, bell pepper, chiles, salt to taste, pepper, and garam masala.
Wet the bread, squeeze it out, and mix it into the vegetables.
Shape the vegetable mixture into small balls. Dip the balls in the cornstarch mixture to coat well.
Fry balls in a pan of hot oil until golden brown. Remove from the oil and place on paper towels.
Fry the onions in a pan with a little oil until golden brown. Add the tomatoes, and fry until the tomatoes and the oil separate.
Add a little water, along with salt to taste, chili powder, and coriander powder. Bring to a boil.
Add the fried kofta to the sauce, and cook for a while.
Remove from the heat, and mix in the garam masala and pepper.
Serve hot with roti, naan, or rice.

name: Caramelized Pineapple
description: Crispy on the outside, sweet, and fruity, this caramelized pineapple is broiled with a vanilla-rum sugar glaze for a rich, golden finish.

ingredients.text: ½ cup dark brown sugar, divided
ingredients.name: dark brown sugar

instructions: Combine vanilla bean and liquid ingredients except rum and ¼ cup brown sugar.
Heat over medium heat until sugar is dissolved and has thickened slightly, 15–30 minutes.
Remove vanilla pod and let the sugar mixture sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Dip pineapple into sugar mixture then dredge in remaining sugar, adding more as needed.
Place pineapple on a greased baking sheet and place under broiler, shaking constantly until well browned.
Remove pineapple; keep warm.
Place baking sheet on two burners and heat over high heat. Add rum and ignite. Scrape browned bits off of pan and boil rum until reduced by half.
Add rum to remaining sugar mixture and stir. Serve pineapple with remaining sugar mixture on the side.

name: Mexican Tequila Marinade
description: A bold, tangy marinade of tequila, mesquite honey, lime, and habanero chile with a smoky mesquite finish.
instructions: Combine all ingredients in an 8-ounce mason jar.
Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
Shake well before using.

name: Szegedin Goulash
description: A hearty Hungarian goulash featuring pork shoulder, paprika, sauerkraut, and sour cream, simmered slowly and served warm.

ingredients.text: 600 g pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized cubes
ingredients.name: pork shoulder

instructions: Heat the lard in a pot, then add the pork and sauté it for about 3 minutes. Take out the pork and set it aside on a plate.
Put the finely chopped onions into the casserole and fry until they become golden brown.
Stir in the tomato purée and paprika, and add some water or stock.
Add the meat, bay leaves and garlic; pour in more water or stock and season with salt and pepper.
Reduce the heat and cook for about 30 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, and cook for another 40 minutes.
Add the sour cream, mix it thoroughly with the goulash, and serve it on warm plates.

name: Sweet Pumpkin Scones
description: Sweet scones made with butter, mashed squash, and warming nutmeg and ginger.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup butter or margarine, softened slightly
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 1 cup cooked, mashed butternut squash, pumpkin, or other squash
ingredients.name: squash

instructions: Stir together the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, salt, ground nutmeg and ground ginger.
In a separate bowl, beat butter and sugar together with an electric mixer.
Add in the egg and corn syrup, and mix with a spoon to prevent over-mixing.
Stir in the squash and half of the sifted dry ingredients.
Add the rest of the dry ingredients with just enough of the milk to make a soft dough.
If it is too sticky to work, add a sprinkle (or two) of flour.
Knead only a little, gently, until you can pat it out into a big flat rectangle about ¾ inch thick.
Cut into 12 pieces with a floured knife. Transfer to a lightly greased oven tray.
Bake at 230°C (450°F) for 18 minutes.

name: Fried Pickle
description: A classic American Southern snack of battered dill pickle slices, deep-fried until golden and crispy.
instructions: Combine the ingredients for the milk mixture, stirring well. Set aside.
Combine ingredients for the flour mixture, stirring well.
Dip pickles in milk mixture and dredge in flour mixture. Repeat process.
Deep fry in oil heated to 350 °F until pickles float to surface and are golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle with dried dill to your liking.

name: Clams Steamed in Aluminum Foil
description: Tender clams steamed in foil packets with aromatic celery, onion, bell pepper, garlic, and fresh herbs. A simple yet flavorful seafood main course baked right in its own pouch.
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C).
Clean clams.
Cut out four 18-inch aluminum foil squares.
Make squares into double foil pockets and put ingredients in them.
Fold edges so there is plenty of space for them to open. The edges themselves should be tightly folded several times to close up.
Bake for 15–25 minutes.
Eat right out of the foil or empty onto plate.

name: Tarhana (Turkish Yogurt Soup)
description: A traditional Turkish soup made from a fermented and dehydrated mix of flour, yogurt, onions, tomatoes and green peppers, served hot with tomato paste and garnishes.
instructions: Dissolve the sugar in the tepid water and sprinkle the dried yeast on top. Allow to soften 5 minutes or so and stir.
Blanche, peel, and seed the tomatoes. Peel and roughly chop the onions. Remove the stem, seeds and membrane from the green peppers and cut roughly.
In a blender or food processor, purée the tomatoes, onion, green pepper and yogurt in batches.
Combine all the ingredients except the flour and mix well. Gradually add enough flour to make a stiff dough. Knead for 5–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.

Place in a large non-reactive bowl and cover with waxed paper (don't use plastic wrap). Let stand at room temperature for 10–12 days. Punch down the dough once a day. If the dough becomes watery, knead in some more flour. Let stand until the dough no longer rises and has lost its stretch.

Rub the dough between your hands onto a tray covered with parchment paper so that it forms small pieces. Cover the tray with cheesecloth or other protective mesh and leave to dry in a cool, well ventilated place.

As it dries, break the dough into smaller pieces eventually crumbling it as small as you can. When it is completely dry (a week or more) pulverize in a blender, a little at a time. Store in freezer bags or large jars. Store in a cool place or refrigerate. May be kept up to 12 months.

To make tarhana soup, mix 1 cup of the dried dough mix with 3 cups of water or meat stock. Mix with a wooden spoon until softened. Add more water or stock to make a thickish soup with a creamy consistency.
Add 2 tablespoons of tomato paste and cook for 15–20 minutes. Pour into bowls and garnish with croûtons, parsley, or paprika-infused butter or olive oil, if desired.
Serve with Turkish bread or a crisp baguette.

name: Yeasted Rolls I
description: Soft, fluffy yeasted dinner rolls made with bread flour, milk, butter, and egg, brushed with melted butter and baked until golden.
instructions: Knead all the ingredients together, and let rise for 1 ½ hours. Alternatively, use the dough setting on a bread machine.
Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C).
Divide dough into 12 rolls.
Brush melted butter over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes.

name: Mirliton Casserole
description: An easy casserole of mirliton, onion, celery, green bell pepper, and garlic, with optional shrimp or ground beef and a browned bread-crumb topping.

ingredients.text: 1 medium to large green bell pepper, diced
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

ingredients.text: 1 lb (500 g) whole shrimp, peeled OR ½ lb (250 g) ground beef (optional)
ingredients.name: shrimp or ground beef

ingredients.text: 1 stick (½ cup / 113 g) butter (olive oil may be substituted)
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Place mirliton halves seed-side up in a microwave- or oven-safe dish with approximately 1 inch (2.5cm) of water in the dish.

Cover with foil (for oven) or plastic wrap (for microwave) and cook in oven (350°F/175°C) or microwave (high at 10 minute intervals) until mirliton are soft enough to stick a fork or knife through easily.
Allow mirliton to cool enough to be handled and dice into large pieces.
Sauté onion, celery, and garlic in butter over medium heat, adding garlic to sauté just before onion, celery, and garlic are fully softened.
Add shrimp or beef to pan until beef is lightly browned or shrimp are pink and cooked through.
Stir in diced mirliton, green bell pepper, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and parsley.
Transfer mixture to a greased baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs and dot with remaining butter.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25–30 minutes until heated through and topping is golden brown.
Serve hot.

name: Mango Avocado Salsa
description: A refreshing mango and avocado salsa with red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime, perfect for serving with tortilla chips.

ingredients.text: 1 small bunch of cilantro, chopped (about 1 cup, packed)
ingredients.name: cilantro

ingredients.text: 3 Hass avocados, peeled, cored, and diced
ingredients.name: avocado

ingredients.text: 1 ripe mango, peeled, cored, and diced (about 1 cup)
ingredients.name: mango

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Mix well with a spoon and serve with tortilla chips or use it as toppings for another dish.

name: Agbugbu (Nigerian Pigeon Pea and Yam Porridge)
description: A typical Igbo porridge made with tender pigeon peas and yam, seasoned with onions, ground crayfish, and palm oil. It is tasty and easy to prepare.

ingredients.text: Yam, cut into small pieces and rinsed
ingredients.name: yam

instructions: Pick any dirt or debris out of the pigeon peas, then wash them and soak in water overnight.
Drain away the soaking water.
Cover the pigeon peas in fresh water, and bring to a boil.
Cook until tender, then drain.
Boil the yam in water until tender, then drain.
Fry the onions, ground crayfish, and ground pepper in a pan with palm oil.
Add the drained yam and pigeon peas, and stir gently.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve.

name: Vegan Pate
description: A hearty vegan pate made with sweet peas and walnuts, perfect as a dip or spread for crackers or vegetables.
instructions: Sauté onion with walnuts in a pot for about 5 minutes.
In a different bowl, combine sweet peas, salt, black pepper and cumin. Mix the ingredients well.
Add the sweet pea mixture to the onion and walnuts, and continue sautéing for about 3 more minutes.
Turn off the heat and let cool. Purée with a hand-held blender or in food processor until you achieve a creamy, though slightly nutty texture similar to that of pate or dip.
Serve with crackers, bread, baby carrots and other snack type vegetables.

name: Ibihaza (Rwandan Beans)
description: A traditional Rwandan dish featuring hearty beans simmered with garlic, onion, and aromatic spices until tender. This flavorful staple can be enjoyed as a main course or as a side dish.

ingredients.text: 2 cups dried beans (such as red kidney beans or black-eyed peas)
ingredients.name: dried bean

instructions: Rinse the dried beans thoroughly under running water.
Place them in a large bowl and cover with water. Allow the beans to soak overnight or for at least 8 hours.
Drain and rinse the beans before cooking.
In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion is translucent and fragrant.
Add the soaked and rinsed beans to the pot, along with enough water to cover the beans by about an inch. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and add the cumin, paprika, coriander, thyme, and bay leaf to the pot. Stir well to combine.

Cover the pot partially with a lid and simmer the beans for about 1–1½ hours, or until they are tender and cooked through. Stir occasionally and add more water if necessary to maintain the desired consistency.
Season the beans with salt, to taste, and continue cooking for another 5–10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the beans rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Apple Brown Betty
description: An American dessert of apples and bread crumbs, baked with cinnamon and sugar until the apples are tender.

ingredients.text: 3 cups apples, sliced (they don't need to be peeled)
ingredients.name: apple

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Sauté bread crumbs in butter.
Add apples, cinnamon, sugar, and water.
If the skillet is oven-proof, cover and place in the oven.
If the skillet is not oven-proof, transfer to a greased casserole dish.
Cover and bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until apples are tender.
If mixture becomes too dry during baking, add another ¼ cup of water. (Apples vary as to moisture content.)

name: Coq au Vin I
description: Coq au vin is a French chicken stew featuring chicken simmered in red wine with mushrooms, garlic, basil, and thyme.

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg (about 3.5 lbs) chicken, jointed (or drumsticks, thighs, breasts); get the giblets, and the blood if you can; season beforehand; marrow is important.
ingredients.name: chicken

instructions: Mix flour, salt and pepper. Coat chicken, onion and carrot in flour mixture and set aside.
Sauté mushrooms, set aside.
Brown the chicken pieces a few at a time, set aside.
Brown onions and carrots.
Put chicken into large casserole on medium-high heat along with onions, carrots and mushrooms.
Combine wine, garlic, and basil; pour over chicken.
Cover the casserole, cook until chicken is ready (1–1.5 hours), stirring occasionally.

name: Catfish and Plantain Pepper Soup
description: A spicy West African soup featuring tender catfish simmered with ripe plantain and aromatic pepper soup spices, finished with fresh scent leaf and utazi.

ingredients.text: Ripe plantain, peeled and in pieces
ingredients.name: ripe plantain

instructions: Wash the catfish with salt and hot water to remove the slime.
Blend together the chile pepper, fresh pepper, ehuru, uda, and other spices.
Heat a pot of water over the fire. Add plantain, and allow to cook for a few minutes.
Add the catfish, spice mixture, ground crayfish, onions, seasoning cubes, and salt. Let simmer for about 10–15 minutes.
Add the scent leaf and utazi.
Remove from heat, and serve hot.

name: No-Bake Chocolate Oatmeal Cookies
description: Quick and easy no-bake cookies made with cocoa, oatmeal, and peanut butter, boiled together and set on a cookie sheet.

ingredients.text: ½ cup smooth or chunky peanut butter
ingredients.name: peanut butter

instructions: Combine the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan, and stir well.
Add milk and stir well. Add butter and place over medium-high heat.
Bring mixture to a boil. When it reaches a rolling boil that cannot be stirred down, boil while stirring for exactly 1 minute.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter and vanilla. Stir until peanut butter is melted and mixture is smooth.
Add oatmeal and stir to combine. Immediately spoon the mixture onto a cookie sheet, leaving enough space between them for spreading out.
Let stand on counter for at least 20 minutes to stiffen or refrigerate to speed up the process.

name: Nigerian Dryfish Stew
description: A simple, budget-friendly Nigerian stew made with tomatoes, dry fish, onions, garlic, herbs, and groundnut oil. Serve with boiled yam, white rice, or boiled plantain.
instructions: Combine blended tomatoes, onions, and pepper in a pot over high heat. Cook until all the water is dried up.
In another pot, cook dry fish, chopped onions, salt, and seasoning cube for about 20 minutes until the water is dried up. Debone the fish.
Heat some oil in a pan, and add onions, garlic, mixed herbs, salt, and seasoning cube. Stir, and cook for about 7 minutes.
Stir in the ground crayfish, and turn off the heat.
Introduce the fried fish and onions into the cooked tomatoes, add in some oil, and fry very well for about 15–20 minutes. Add in your scent leaf and turn off the heat.
Serve with boiled yam, white rice, or boiled plantain.

name: Alsatian Fresh Noodles (Nouilles fraîches à l'Alsacienne)
description: Fresh noodles made from eggs and flour, rested and rolled by hand, then simmered and tossed with melted butter.
instructions: Break the eggs and place in a large bowl. Mix in salt and vinegar.
While mixing, gradually add the flour.
Work the dough for several minutes until it is smooth.
Roll dough into a ball and wrap in a dry cloth. Allow to rest for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into pieces the size of a tennis ball and flatten on the work surface to a thickness of 2 mm (⅛ inch).
Allow the dough to dry for 30 minutes, turning the rounds frequently. One can also dry them by suspending them from a cord or over a broom handle place on the backs of two chairs.
Flour each round and roll it up on itself. Cut into slices 3–4 mm (¼ inch) thick.
Unroll to obtain the noodles, and spread out on a large tray without tangling them.
Fill a large pot with salted water; bring to a boil and plunge in the noodles. Simmer for 7–8 minutes.
Drain the noodles and toss with melted butter.

name: Yogurt Dip
description: A cool, refreshing yogurt dip with finely chopped cucumber and mint.

ingredients.text: ½ cucumber, seeded and chopped very fine
ingredients.name: cucumber

ingredients.text: ¼ tsp dried mint, crumbled, or 1 tsp fresh, chopped
ingredients.name: mint

instructions: Mix all the ingredients, and chill thoroughly to let the flavors develop.

name: Chola and Roti
description: Tender chana dal cooked with onions, tomatoes, green chiles, ginger, and warming spices, then finished with fresh coriander. Serve hot with naan or roti.
instructions: Soak the chana dal in water overnight.
Drain the chana dal and pressure cook until tender. Drain.
Fry the onions in hot oil until golden brown.
Add the tomatoes and fry until the oil separates out.
Add the chiles, ginger, salt, and drained chana dal. Boil for 1–2 minutes.
Stir in pepper and garam masala. Garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve hot with naan or roti.

name: Denderu (Kanuri Baked Mutton)
description: A traditional Kanuri preparation of ram meat rubbed with a pounded onion and chile pepper paste, then baked until tender.
instructions: Pound together the onions and pepper in a mortar to make a paste. Mix in the maggi cubes and season with salt to taste.
Rub the pepper paste all over the mutton.
Bake the meat until soft.

name: Chicken Pot Pie II
description: A savory chicken pot pie with a golden, flaky double crust, creamy thickened broth, and tender chunks of chicken with corn and peas.
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F.
Prepare pie crusts as directed on package for a two-crust pie in a 9-inch pie pan.
In a medium saucepan, melt margarine over medium heat.
Add onion; cook 2 minutes or until tender.
Stir in flour, salt, and pepper until well-blended.
Gradually stir in broth and milk; cook, stirring constantly, until bubbly and thickened.
Add chicken, corn, and peas; remove from heat.
Spoon chicken mixture into crust-lined pan.
Top with second crust and flute; cut slits in several places.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until crust is golden-brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

name: Christmas Ham
description: A boneless, lightly salted Finnish-style Christmas ham, roasted slowly and glazed with mustard and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (7–10 kg) ham, lightly salted and boneless
ingredients.name: ham

instructions: If the ham is frozen, thaw it in its plastic package for 3 days in the refrigerator for a 7 kg ham, or 5 days for a 10 kg ham.
Before putting the ham in the oven, take it out of the refrigerator and let it come closer to room temperature.
If you intend to put the ham in the oven in the evening, take it out during the early morning. The ham should be about 10 °C (50 °F) when you put it in the oven.
Use a wet paper towel to clean the ham a bit, then dry it.
Place the ham on a baking tray in the oven with some water on the tray. If you have a large roasting bag, there is no need for water.

Do not use only the oven rack, as nothing will catch all the liquid from the ham if the roasting bag fails. You can put the ham on the rack if you place a baking tray beneath it to catch drips. Aluminum foil can be used on the baking tray to protect it.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (390 °F) and let the ham roast for half an hour. You can skip this if you are not worried about possible bacteria on the ham.
Turn the temperature down and cook at 100–125 °C (210–260 °F) for about 1 hour/kg until a meat thermometer in the center reads 75–80 °C (158–176 °F). A 7 kg ham will take 7 hours or more.
Traditional ham is ready at 80 °C, but most people take the ham out of the oven at about 77 °C, when it has more water left in it and is considered tastier.
After taking the ham out of the oven, wait a little while before removing the thermometer. Do not pour the liquid from the bag or baking tray down the drain.
Wait until the ham is cool enough to handle, then remove the rind and cover it all over with mustard and breadcrumbs.
Bake in a 250 °C (480 °F) oven for 10 minutes.
The ham is ready to eat when it has cooled down a bit. It makes enough for 3 or 4 people for a week; freeze the rest if you will not eat it all within a week.

name: Vitumbua (Coconut Rice Pancakes)
description: Vitumbua are Tanzanian coconut rice pancakes, often eaten for breakfast or sold as street food. They are made from a base of rice flour with coconut milk, cardamom, and nutmeg, then pan-fried until golden.

ingredients.text: 2 cups finely-ground rice flour (or plain rice)
ingredients.name: rice flour

ingredients.text: 1 cup coconut milk (or coconut milk powder)
ingredients.name: coconut milk

ingredients.text: ½–1 cup sugar (brown, white, or coconut)
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: 8 tablespoons plain wheat flour (possibly whole wheat)
ingredients.name: wheat flour

ingredients.text: About ½ cup water if cooking with rice flour and/or coconut milk powder
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Soak the rice and let it soften for at least 4 hours, maybe over night.
Drain the rice.
Blend the rice with the other ingredients to a batter.
Mix all ingredients, adding water so that a rather thick batter forms.
Let the covered batter rise in a warm place until it at least doubled in size and bubbles form on the surface. This may take about 45–60 minutes, and some advise letting rise overnight.
Stir the batter.
If you have, you should use a vitumbua pan; otherwise, an ordinary pan has to suffice. Oil the pan and heat it.
Fill the 'holes' (of the vitumbua pan) about ¾ full with batter. Let it cook for about 2–3 minutes; it should starts to brown. Flip the vitumbua and cook the other side.
Let cool slightly.

name: Ume-shu (Japanese Plum Juice)
description: A refreshing Japanese plum drink made by preserving ume plums in rock sugar and honey. The resulting sweet, smooth, and acidic juice can be diluted with water and chilled for summer.
instructions: Wash plums and wipe dry.
Cram plums tightly into container with rock sugar. Add liquor if using.
Pour honey into container on top of ume.
Seal container, and leave in a cool, dark place until the plums are shriveled and leathery.
Remove fruit from container.
To drink, dilute the plum liquid with two times as much water.

name: Vegetable Spring Roll
description: Vegetable spring rolls filled with crisp-tender carrots, cabbage, mushrooms, and bean sprouts, then deep-fried until golden and served hot.
instructions: Sift the flour, then mix in salt, egg, and enough water to make a smooth batter.
Heat little oil in a flat non-stick pan and add enough batter so that it covers the base of the pan.
Cook both sides of the pancake until golden.
Repeat the cooking process until all the batter is used up.
Heat 2–3 tbsp oil in a wok, then add ginger, garlic, and mushrooms, and stir fry for 10–15 seconds.
Add leeks, and stir fry for about 1 minute.
Add carrots and cabbage, then cook, tossing the vegetables until they are crisp-tender.
Add the bean sprouts, salt, pepper, and soya sauce. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Set the filling aside to cool.
Place 2–3 tbsp of the filling in the center of each pancake.
Fold in the sides and form a tight roll, sealing the edge with a little flour and water paste.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden.
Serve hot.

name: Italian Meatballs
description: Tender veal meatballs seasoned with oregano, parsley, garlic, and Parmesan, pan-seared then finished in the oven.

ingredients.text: 500 g (18 oz/1½ lb) minced veal meat
ingredients.name: veal meat

ingredients.text: 30 g (1 oz/1 Tbsp) grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: parmesan cheese

instructions: Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl. Using your hands, squeeze all ingredients.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and drizzle on a little olive oil. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) in the meantime.
Use your hands to roll meat into bite sized balls.
Place the meatballs in the skillet and cook uncovered for 3 minutes, then roll them over and cook another 3 minutes.
Transfer the meatballs onto a baking sheet and bake in the oven for 20–25 minutes.

name: Nigerian Coco Pops
description: A quick Nigerian breakfast made by stirring coco pops cereal and milk into warm water. Serve it warm.
instructions: Pour water into a bowl.
Stir in the coco pops, then the milk.
Serve warm.

name: Knoephla (Small Flour Dumplings)
description: Knoephla are small flour dumplings commonly used in knoephla soup, a popular dish in the American Midwest.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (250 ml) milk or water
ingredients.name: milk or water

instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, egg, and then the milk or water.
Mix to form a firm dough that is not sticky.
Add a bit more flour if needed to keep dough from being sticky or a bit more liquid if too dry.
Roll pieces of dough between the hands to the length of a pencil (6 in / 15 cm).
Snip off small pieces with a knife or scissors.
Use the knoephla as specified in your given recipe.

name: Victorian Butter
description: A traditional Victorian-era recipe for homemade butter, churned from fresh cow's milk cream and optionally seasoned with salt and herbs.

ingredients.text: Herbs (e.g. thyme, rosemary, parsley, etc; optional)
ingredients.name: herbs

instructions: After washing one's hands and fingernails, scald all utensils that are to be used in making butter, including the wooden churn. Wooden pats and spoons should be left in bowl of scalding hot water and covered over with a clean cloth.
Let the fresh milk settle in pans overnight to allow the cream to rise to the top.
Scrape the cream from the milk, and pour it into the churn. It's preferable to pour the cream at a height so that the cream aerates, allowing it to churn quicker.

Begin the churning process: if a Victorian barrel butter churn is used, rotate the handle continuously, which propels the paddles; if a plunge churn is used, continuously move up-and-down the dasher-staff. It is important to maintain a measured and steady pace. The cream soon turns into whipped cream (the first stage).

After continued churning for 30–35 minutes more, the whipped cream begins to turn, becoming thicker and harder to churn, and slightly powdery so that it starts to separate. This is the second stage. The turned butter at this stage is quite pungent to smell.

With continued churning, one reaches the third stage, when buttermilk and butter begin to separate. This can be recognized by the distinct sound that the churning action makes, besides being harder to churn.
Drain the buttermilk into a separate pail by using a meshed cloth or strainer.
Remove the paddle from the churn, and scoop out all of the butter.
Wrap up butter in a clean cloth, tie it and squeeze out all excess liquid.
Open the wrapping, wash the butter in spring water, and allow it to drain. Washing in spring water prevents butter from becoming rancid.
Let the butter sit for at least 1 hour, allowing all water to drain off.
Divide the butter into smaller portions. Begin to pat it with butter paddles to get rid of any excess liquid.
Use the butter paddles to sparingly work salt and any herbs into the butter.

name: Nigerian Okra Soup II
description: A Nigerian okra soup combining meat, stockfish, palm oil, and okra with pepper, ground crayfish, and ogili. It is a dinner delicacy served hot.
instructions: Combine the meat, onion, and stock cube in a pot over medium heat. Cook for 3 minutes.
Cover everything in the pot with water, and bring to a boil.
Add the stockfish, and simmer until the meat is soft. Stir in the palm oil.
Grind together the pepper, crayfish, and ogili. Stir into the pot.
Stir in the okra, cover the pot, and let cook for 3 minutes.
Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Serve hot.

name: Barbecue Fried Rice
description: A quick 20-minute fried rice with minced pork, garlic, red onion, red chillies, barbecue sauce, and black soy sauce. Serve it with your choice of toppings.

ingredients.text: 2 red chillies, cut into 1 cm pieces
ingredients.name: red chili

ingredients.text: Vegetables like corn, carrot, and peas
ingredients.name: vegetable

instructions: Heat the olive oil and sesame oil in a non-stick pan. Fry the garlic and red onion until fragrant. Stir until the garlic and red onion are golden brown.
Add the red chilli and pork. Stir until the pork changes color.
Add horseradish, scallion, rice, barbecue sauce, black soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir until well-mixed.
Serve with toppings as desired.

name: Mbatata a Matenda (Malawian Cassava Fritters)
description: Crispy Malawian cassava fritters with a soft interior, made with grated cassava, egg, onion, and cornmeal. They can be enjoyed on their own or served with hot tea.

ingredients.text: 2 green chiles (optional, for heat), finely chopped
ingredients.name: green chile

instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the grated cassava, beaten egg, finely chopped onion, and finely chopped green chilies (if using).
Add the cornmeal to the mixture and mix well until everything is evenly combined.
Season the mixture with salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
In a frying pan, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Take spoonfuls of the cassava mixture and carefully drop them into the hot oil. Flatten the fritters slightly with the back of the spoon.
Fry the fritters until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides.
Use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and place them on paper towels to drain any excess oil.
Repeat the frying process with the remaining cassava mixture.
Allow the fritters to cool slightly before serving.

name: Veggie Salad
description: A light vegetable salad with a dash of spice, featuring fresh veggies, walnuts, and a blend of ground spices.
instructions: Cut the green pepper into long thin strips.
Toss vegetables together in a large bowl.
Using a mortar, grind the spices together, and sprinkle over salad.
Sprinkle walnut chunks over salad.
Serve.

name: Broccoli Stir Fry
description: A wok stir-fry of chicken or other meat with bright green broccoli, soy sauce, golden-brown sesame seeds, and optional ginger.

ingredients.text: Oil to fry with, possibly including sesame oil
ingredients.name: oil

instructions: Cut raw meat into small pieces.
Chop the broccoli head into medium-small pieces, perhaps 1.2-inch diameter. Cut the stalk into disks, ⅛-inch thick.
Place oil in a wok and turn on the heat.
High temperatures can produce a better result, but require rapid stirring to prevent burning. Slow beginners should use lower temperatures.

Split the cooking into batches as needed to ensure that your wok is not too full; there should be plenty of room to stir and toss the food in your wok. You may prefer to cook each ingredient separately, then mix them at the end.
Place sesame seeds into the wok. Stir fry them until they are golden-brown. Remove them, and put them aside for later.
Stir-fry the meat. Drain juices and add more oil as needed.
Add soy sauce. For a typical wok full of food, add 1 tablespoon. If using low-salt soy sauce, you can add much more without making the food too salty.
Add back the sesame seeds. If using ginger, add about 1/4 teaspoon, depending on taste. Ginger is somewhat hot.
Add the broccoli, stalks first. When done, the broccoli should be just slightly softened.
Broccoli should end up being very bright green, losing the bluish cast but not gaining any hint of a yellow-brown cast.

name: Speculaas (Dutch Spiced Cookies)
description: Traditional Dutch spiced biscuits with a crisp texture and rich blend of cinnamon and warming spices. Their distinctive molded shapes make them a delightful treat with tea or hot chocolate.
instructions: Cream together the butter, sugar, salt, and spices until you have a soft mass.
Add the egg and flours, and mix into a soft dough.
If desired, let the dough rest for 2 days in the fridge. This will give a stronger taste of the spices to the biscuits.
Sprinkle the speculaas mold with flour so the dough will not stick.
Press a piece of dough in the mold. Cut away the excess dough by using a string or by cutting with a knife, holding it flat against the template.
Flip the mold over, and smack it forcefully face-down on the kitchen worktop. This should get the speculaas out of the template.
Arrange the speculaas on a well-buttered baking sheet, leaving enough space between them to allow for spreading.
Bake the speculaas in a 170°C oven. Small cookies will take 20 minutes, while larger ones can take 30 minutes or more.
There is no telling when the cookies are done when still hot, so take one out and let it cool down. When it smells good and is crispy, it is done.
Let the speculaas fully cool. Enjoy with a cup of tea or hot chocolate.

name: Cheese Spaetzle
description: A comforting German-style dish of pan-fried spaetzle tossed with melted Emmental or Gruyère cheese and topped with golden caramelized onions.
instructions: Slowly fry diced onions with butter. When the onions are browned, remove them from the pan.
Fry the spaetzle in butter on low heat.
Grate the cheese over the frying spaetzle, and toss well.
Add the onions to the spaetzle and cheese, and toss well.
Serve with a green salad.

name: Sesame Shrimp Toast
description: Crispy golden toasts topped with seasoned shrimp, coated in sesame seeds and fried to perfection. A classic dim sum-style appetizer.

ingredients.text: 3 slices (or more as needed) sandwich bread
ingredients.name: sandwich bread

instructions: Remove shells, tails, and back veins from shrimp, then chop into a very small dice.
Beat 1 egg, cornstarch, salt, pepper, and finely-chopped green onions in a small bowl until blended.
Add shrimp to egg mixture and toss until completely coated.
Remove crusts from bread and cut each slice into quarters.
Place one spoonful of shrimp mixture on each piece of bread and gently press to adhere.
Brush or rub a small amount of egg mixture over each shrimp toast.
Dip the moist side into sesame seeds spread out on a plate.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 375°F (190°C).
Fry 3–4 shrimp toast pieces at a time in the hot oil until golden, 1–2 minutes on each side, then drain on absorbent paper.

name: Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Dumplings with Cheese)
description: A traditional Slovak national dish of soft potato dumplings topped with melted sheep's milk cheese and crispy bacon bits, served piping hot.

ingredients.text: 750 g potatoes, peeled and finely grated
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 250 g bryndze cheese, cut into very small pieces
ingredients.name: bryndze cheese

ingredients.text: 100 g bacon (údenej slaniny), cooked and cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: bacon

instructions: Combine the grated potatoes with the flour and salt to make a dough.
Shape the dough into small cylindrical pieces less than 3 cm in size.
Transfer the dumplings to a pot of boiling salted water. When the dumplings rise to the top of the boiling water, remove one to make sure they are thoroughly cooked.
Remove the dumplings from the pot with a slotted spoon, and transfer to a warmed plate.
Immediately after dumplings are placed on the plate, scatter the cheese over top, and let the cheese melt over the dumplings. Mix if desired.
Sprinkle the crispy bacon bits on top of the cheese.
Serve piping hot.

name: Eru And Water Fufu
description: A traditional Cameroonian soup made with eru leaves, waterleaf, assorted meats, fish, and palm oil, served alongside water fufu. It is a beloved staple among the Manyu people of the southwest region of Cameroon.

ingredients.text: ½ kg cow skin, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: cow skin

ingredients.text: White wrappings of water fufu mixture
ingredients.name: water fufu mixture

instructions: Wash the meat and fish. Combine in a pot with 1 maggi cube and a pinch of salt, then steam for about 30 minutes.
Add water leaf to the pot and cook for 3 minutes.
Add eru, and stir until the mixture is soft.
Serve with water fufu.
Soak the eru leaves for 3–6 hours OR soak for 1 hour and boil with baking soda for 30 minutes.
Boil the beef skin for 30 minutes, then add the previously cleaned and cut meat. Don't forget to salt it.
Boil for 10 minutes or until the desired gravy is achieved.
Season with hot pepper if desired.
At the very end of cooking, add the soaked fish. The juice must be saved because it will be necessary for the remaining cooking.
Stir in the spinach or waterleaf to a saucepan. Cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the eru. Boil, stirring occasionally.
Mix in the palm oil, and cook for 15 minutes.
Mix in the crayfish, and cook for 5–10 minutes.
Serve with water fufu.
Place water fufu in a saucepan and stir with water until lumps are gone.
Place over a burner and stir with a wooden stick at regular intervals for about 45 minutes.
Check to see if it is properly cooked.
Shape into desired forms, then serve hot with eru.

name: Tchakpolo (Togolese Meat and Vegetable Stew)
description: A flavorful traditional Togolese stew of tender meat and vegetables simmered with aromatic spices and thickened with peanut butter. Best served hot with steamed rice or fufu.

ingredients.text: 500 grams meat (beef, goat, or chicken), cut into chunks
ingredients.name: meat

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
ingredients.name: parsley or cilantro

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and minced garlic, and sauté until they become soft and translucent.
Add the meat chunks to the pot and cook until they are browned on all sides. Stir occasionally to ensure even browning.
Once the meat is browned, add the diced tomatoes and bell peppers to the pot. Continue cooking for a few minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
In a small bowl, mix the tomato paste with a little water to form a smooth paste. Add the tomato paste mixture to the pot and stir well to combine with the meat and vegetables.
Add the ground ginger, ground coriander, ground cloves, ground nutmeg, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to evenly distribute the spices.

Pour in the water or beef broth, ensuring it covers the meat and vegetables. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for about 1–1.5 hours, or until the meat is tender.

In a separate bowl, mix the peanut butter with a little water to create a smooth paste. Add the peanut butter mixture to the pot and stir well to incorporate it into the stew. This will thicken the sauce and add a rich flavor.
Add the sliced carrots to the pot and continue simmering for an additional 15–20 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.
Taste the tchakpalo and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt and pepper to taste.
Once the stew is ready, remove it from the heat. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley or cilantro.
Serve hot with steamed rice, fufu, or another preferred side dish.

name: Prepared White Mustard
description: A tangy homemade condiment made with white mustard seeds, egg yolks, garlic, whole wheat flour, vinegar, and honey.

ingredients.text: ½ cup natural apple vinegar or wine vinegar
ingredients.name: vinegar

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp honey, treacle, or date syrup
ingredients.name: honey

instructions: Toast mustard seeds in a skillet without oil. Let cool.
Pound the seeds with a mortar and pestle.
Crush the boiled yolks, and add to ground mustard seeds.
Crush the garlic and add to the mixture.
Toast the flour in a skillet without oil and add to the mixture.
Mix in vinegar, salt, and honey.

name: Zucchini Pie
description: A savory Italian supper pie filled with fresh zucchini, mozzarella cheese, and herbs in a flaky homemade crust.

ingredients.text: 4 cups thinly-sliced zucchini (from about 3 small squash)
ingredients.name: zucchini

ingredients.text: ½ cup chopped onion (about ⅓ large onion)
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: ¼ cup parsley (or 2 tablespoons parsley flakes)
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F/191° C/Gas mark 5.
Sift flour and salt into a bowl. Cut in shortening until mixture forms coarse particles. Add water, 1 tablespoon at a time, and mixing to make a pliable dough.
Roll out the pie crust to a circle and then fit it into a pie plate; bake for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a Dutch oven. Add the zucchini and onion. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the onions are translucent (about 10 minutes).
Stir the seasoning into the vegetable mixture and set aside.
Combine 2 beaten eggs and grated cheese in a bowl, then stir into the vegetable and spice mix.
Pour the filling into the pie crust and bake for 20 minutes, or until center is set.
Serve hot.

name: Kosan Rogo (Nigerian Cassava Cakes)
description: Crunchy cassava cakes from northern Nigeria, seasoned with pepper and onion, shaped into patties and deep-fried until golden brown.
instructions: Peel the cassava, cut into small chunks, and rinse well.
Pound the cassava with a mortar and pestle, then transfer to a bowl.
Mix in the pepper and onions.
Squeeze out all excess water from the mixture. A cheesecloth can be helpful here.
Transfer the mixture to a dry bowl, and mix in the salt and seasoning cube.
Shape the mixture into small balls, and flatten them with your palm.
Heat enough vegetable oil for deep frying in a deep pan. Aim for about 350°F (180°C).
Place the flattened pieces in the pan one at a time and deep fry on both sides until golden brown.
Remove from the oil, and place on paper towels to drain.
Serve hot.

name: Cottage Cheese Eggs
description: Fluffy scrambled eggs whisked with creamy cottage cheese and seasoned with Mexican spices, a quick and protein-rich breakfast.

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon Mexican seasoning or chili powder
ingredients.name: mexican seasoning

instructions: Preheat a large metal or non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Whisk eggs and cottage cheese together in a small bowl; place in skillet.
Sprinkle Mexican seasoning on eggs (to taste).
As eggs begin to cook, start folding them together, turning as needed, until done cooking.
Serve with or on wheat toast.

name: Kipspek (Bacon-wrapped Chicken)
description: Cubed chicken wrapped in bacon, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs, then fried until golden brown for an easy snack.
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Wrap each cube of chicken in a strip of bacon.
To make sure the bacon doesn't roll off the chicken, stick a toothpick from one end to the other.
Roll the kipspek in the breadcrumbs.
Whisk the eggs, and dip each kipspek in the eggs.
Roll the kipspek through the breadcrumbs once again. Leave them for about half an hour to dry out the surface.
Heat the oil in a deep pot.
Fry the kipspeks until they're golden brown all over.
Serve with ketchup or mustard—don't forget to remove the toothpick before taking a bite.

name: Liberian Palm Oil Stew
description: A rich, hearty Liberian stew made with palm oil, chicken, fish, and tender vegetables. Its deep flavor is often enjoyed with rice or fufu.

ingredients.text: 1 Scotch bonnet chile pepper, finely chopped (optional, for spiciness)
ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet chile pepper

ingredients.text: 1 pound fish, cut into steaks or fillets
ingredients.name: fish

instructions: In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
Stir in the diced green and red bell peppers and chopped Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for a few minutes until the peppers start to soften.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot and cook until they are lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and tender.
Once the chicken is cooked, add the fish steaks or fillets to the pot and let them simmer in the stew for an additional 5–10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
Stir in the sliced okra and diced eggplant. Let the stew simmer for another 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
Season the stew with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Obuwunga (Ugandan Traditional Bread)
description: A hearty Ugandan bread made with millet flour or cornmeal and steamed until firm. It is traditionally served with various stews and dishes.
instructions: In a bowl, combine the millet flour or cornmeal with the salt.

Gradually add water to the flour, mixing it with a mixing stick or spoon until it forms a smooth and thick dough. The amount of water needed may vary, so add it gradually until the right consistency is achieved.
Once the dough is ready, form it into a round or oval shape, smoothing the surface with wet hands.
In a pot, add some water and place a steaming rack at the bottom. Alternatively, you can use banana leaves to line the pot to prevent sticking.
Carefully place the shaped dough on the steaming rack or banana leaves.
Cover the pot with a lid and steam the bread over medium heat for about 30–40 minutes, or until the bread is cooked and firm.
Remove the bread from the pot and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.
Serve with various stews and dishes, using the bread to scoop up the stews.

name: Minestrone alla Casalinga
description: A traditional Italian minestrone made with blanched vegetables, rice, good stock, and minestrone seasoning, served with grated cheese.
instructions: Blanch vegetables in boiling salted water, then drain them and fry in butter.
Add plenty of good stock, and put over low heat.
Boil rice in stock until well-done.
Add the stock and vegetables.
Season with minestrone seasoning condiment, and serve with grated cheese handed separately.

name: Tvorog (Russian Farmer Cheese)
description: A traditional Russian farmer cheese made simply from milk and cultured buttermilk, left to ferment and then gently heated to separate curds from whey.
instructions: Mix milk and buttermilk in a pot, and cover with a lid.
Let stand for 1–2 days, until the mixture thickens to a consistency of thin yogurt.
Heat mixture gently, without letting it boil, until the whey separates from the curds.
Pour out through cheese cloth.
For a drier tvorog, hang it up for 1–12 hours to let it drain.

name: Yeasted Kifli
description: Yeasted Hungarian kifli crescents made with butter and sour cream, then filled with walnut filling or jam and rolled in sugar before baking.
instructions: Mix together milk, yeast, and 1 tsp sugar, then set aside. Ensure it does not clump.
Using a pastry knife, mix flour, butter, salt in a bowl until crumbly.
Add 3½ tbsp sugar and baking powder to the flour mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks. Add the yeast mixture, then the sour cream and vanilla.
Mix the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. You should get a dough with the consistency of peanut butter cookie dough. Add additional flour if the dough is too sticky.
Knead dough well and let stand 2 hours in a warm place.
To allow the dough to rise, place the bowl with the dough, covered with a tea towel, onto the top rack of the oven.
Place a bowl of hot water on the lower rack. Leave the oven off; this setup will gently warm and allow the dough to rise.
Divide the dough into 5 equally-sized balls.
Sprinkle sugar on a board, put a dough ball on the board, and roll out into a circle about 12 inches across.
Flip the dough over and put more sugar on the board. Cut like a pizza into wedges about 1½ inches at the widest.
Put about 1 tsp filling on each wedge and roll in sugar.
Bake on a cookie sheet at 325°F for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Fireweed Vinegar
description: A fragrant homemade vinegar infused with fireweed blossoms, steeped slowly and stored for long-lasting use.

ingredients.text: 1 cup rice or white wine vinegar
ingredients.name: vinegar

instructions: Rinse blossoms in a colander and let dry.
Place blossoms in a sterilized jar and pour vinegar over the top.
Place mixture in a dark place and allow it to steep for 3 to 4 weeks.
Strain vinegar through a strainer or a paper coffee filter.
Store in the refrigerator.
For longer storage, process in a boiling water bath for 5 minutes.

name: Ukrainian Cornmeal Stuffing (Nachynka)
description: A traditional Ukrainian side dish of cornmeal cooked with butter and milk, enriched with eggs and baked until golden brown on top.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a pot on medium heat.
Add cornmeal. Stir mixture to warm up the cornmeal.
Add milk. Stir until mixture has thickened.
Beat eggs. Beat in salt, sugar, and baking powder.
Slowly add some of the thickened cornmeal mixture to the egg mixture while mixing to temper the eggs.
Stir the egg mixture into the rest of the cornmeal.
Pour the mixture into a greased casserole dish.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30–40 minutes or until the top has browned.

name: Carrot Kugel
description: A traditional Jewish baked dish of grated carrots and apple with orange and lemon juice, finished with a golden-brown crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Grease a 1-litre casserole dish.
Beat the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy and pale in color.
Very finely grate the carrot and apple, then squeeze out and discard all the liquid.
Mix the grated carrot, apple, orange rind, orange and lemon juice, and flour.
Combine the egg and carrot mixtures.
Whip the egg whites until they are very stiff, and fold into the carrot mixture.
Spoon the mixture into the greased casserole dish.
Bake for 35 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Thong Yib (Thai Candied Egg Yolks)
description: A sweet, juicy Thai dessert of candied duck egg yolks shaped like flowers and served during auspicious ceremonies for blessings.
instructions: Combine 2 cups of sugar and 2 cups of jasmine water in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, and wait until the sugar is dissolved.
Remove from the heat and let cool.
