Bring 5 cups of sugar and 4 cups of jasmine water to a simmer in a saucepan. Wait for it to dissolve without stirring.
Separate the egg yolks from egg white.
Whisk the egg yolks constantly for about 3–5 minutes. The more you whisk the egg yolks, the softer the egg. If too soft, it will be hard to crimp once the eggs are cooked.
When the syrup is boiling, remove from the heat.
Immediately use a spoon to pour dollops of egg yolk into the hot syrup. The yolks will spread into circles.
Return the pot to the heat, and keep flipping the egg yolks until completely cooked.
Spoon the cooked yolks into the cooled syrup. Cool slightly, then crimp into flower-like shapes of 3, 4, or 5 petals.
Put the crimped yolks in small bowls and wait for them to cool down completely.
Serve.

name: Croque Monsieur
description: A crunchy French sandwich filled with ham and Gruyère cheese, topped with smooth béchamel sauce and grilled until golden brown.

ingredients.text: 2 slices of cheese, such as gruyère
ingredients.name: cheese

instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan.
Add the flour and stir over a medium heat until blended.
Gradually add the milk, whisking continuously into a smooth sauce.
Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Mix in the mustard, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Preheat a grill to high. Lightly toast the bread on both sides under the grill.
Arrange slices of ham and cheese on each slice of bread, then top with béchamel sauce.
Place back under the grill to brown the béchamel and melt the cheese until golden brown and delicious.
Serve hot.

name: Tuwo Masara (Nigerian Corn Fufu)
description: A Nigerian swallow dish made from corn flour, popular amongst the Hausa and Fulani people. Also known as Corn Fufu, it is cooked into a thick, stretchy dough and served in balls.
instructions: Boil water in a pot.
Add corn flour gradually, stirring until it forms a thick and stretchy mix.
Add a little water to the mixture until it reaches your desired consistency.
Cover the pot and cook for a few minutes.
Mould tuwo masara into balls and serve.

name: Wonton Wrappers
description: Thin wonton wrappers made from a simple flour-and-egg dough, suitable for wonton soup, potstickers, and egg rolls.
instructions: Sift flour and salt into a large bowl; create a well-like indentation in the center.
Beat egg lightly, pour into indentation in the flour and mix well.
Sprinkle with cold water, wet your hands, and knead the mixture into a smooth dough.
Place dough in a bowl and cover with a damp cloth, refrigerate for 30 minutes to an hour.
Sprinkle a wide work area or board with flour.
Roll out the dough until it is paper thin and its edges are even in thickness. The wonton skins will be partially transparent.
Cut dough in 2–3-inch (5–7.5 cm) strips and flour lightly.
Stack one on top of the other and cut the strips into 2–3-inch (5–7.5 cm) squares.
Place skins on tray and cover with a damp cloth until ready to use.

name: Stovies
description: A traditional Scottish dish of potatoes stewed with onions and leftover meat in fat, often served with brown sauce and fresh herbs.

ingredients.text: 50 g (2 oz) beef drippings or butter
ingredients.name: beef dripping

ingredients.text: 125–250 g (4–8 oz) cooked beef or lamb (leftovers from a roast dinner)
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: 2–3 tbsp finely chopped parsley, chives, or spring onions
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: Peel potatoes if they are "main crop", but leave the skins on new potatoes. Slice about 5 mm (¼-inch) thick, or slice roughly in different thicknesses so that the thin ones make a mush when cooked while the others stay whole.
Heat fat in a large heavy-base pot with a tight-fitting lid and add the onions. Cook until lightly brown. Add the potatoes and stir well, coating all sides with the fat.
Put the lid on and cook over a very low heat, shaking the pot once or twice to prevent sticking, until the potatoes are cooked.
Add the meat, mix through, and turn up the heat to brown a little.
Serve with brown sauce, parsley, and optional seasonings.

name: Beef Tongue with Chiles, Corn and Tomato (Lengua de Res)
description: A traditional Venezuelan dish featuring tender beef tongue simmered until no longer pink, then sautéed with roasted green chiles, tomatoes, and sweet corn.

ingredients.text: 2 cans (30 ounces) whole kernel corn, drained
ingredients.name: corn

instructions: Wash tongue and place in a large pot of water to cover. Simmer until no longer pink (about 50 minutes per pound of tongue). Remove from water and let rest until cool enough to handle. Peel skin from tongue and trim gristle. Cut into ½-inch slices.
Place whole peppers in a skillet over medium-high heat and roast, turning, until all sides are charred. Let cool, rub off skins. Remove stems and seeds.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté chili peppers, onion, and garlic until onion is translucent.
Stir in tongue and continue to cook until tongue is brown, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in tomatoes and cook until limp, 5 minutes. Pour in corn and heat through, 2 to 5 minutes.
Season with salt, and serve.

name: Baked Tilapia with White Wine
description: Delicate whole tilapia baked with white wine, garlic, fresh herbs and salad onions, finished with a light creme fraiche sauce.

ingredients.text: 2 fresh whole tilapia, approximately 8–10 oz each, gutted and descaled
ingredients.name: tilapia

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon cornstarch, blended with a little cold water
ingredients.name: cornstarch

instructions: Arrange the tilapia side-by-side in a lightly oiled roasting tin or ovenproof dish.
Pour the wine over the fish, then sprinkle over the chopped garlic, most of the herbs, the salad onions, and seasoning to taste. Place half the butter on each fish.
Cover with a sheet of lightly oiled foil to seal in the fish, then bake in a preheated 350°F oven, for 30–35 minutes.
Transfer the tilapia to a serving dish and keep warm. Pour the juices into a pan, stir in the blended corn flour, and simmer for 2 minutes. Stir in the creme fraiche.
Pour the sauce over the fish, and serve immediately, sprinkled with the remaining herbs.

name: Field of Dreams Guacamole
description: A festive guacamole decorated to look like a ballpark, topped with a cream cheese baseball adorned with red bell pepper stitching.

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon packaged dry buttermilk salad dressing and seasoning mix
ingredients.name: buttermilk seasoning mix

ingredients.text: 3 large fresh ripe avocados, halved, pitted, and peeled
ingredients.name: avocado

ingredients.text: ½ cup chopped, prepared roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.name: roasted red bell pepper

instructions: In bowl, blend cream cheese and buttermilk seasoning. Place in plastic wrap, roll into a ball, and chill in freezer for 1 hour or refrigerate overnight.
In bowl, coarsely mash avocado with lime juice, garlic, salt and red pepper sauce.
Stir in red onion and roasted bell pepper.
Using rubber spatula, scoop guacamole onto square plate. Spread out evenly, making a slight mound in center to create a 'pitchers mound'.
Spoon sour cream into pastry bag with fine tip or plastic bag with ⅛-inch corner cut out. Pipe thin 'base lines' onto guacamole 'field'.

To create the red 'stitching' for the baseball, cut the red bell pepper into 1 inch strips. Using a sharp knife, carefully remove fleshy inside of the pepper, reserving the red shiny skin. Slice the skin into very thin strips to create stitch lines for baseball.

To make baseball: Remove cream cheese from freezer or refrigerator. Roll to make a round baseball shape. Remove plastic wrap. Using a wooden pick, form the stitch lines on the ball. Use the very thin pieces of red bell pepper skin to lay over stitch lines. Place 'baseball' on the 'mound' in the center of the guacamole 'field'.
Use thin wheat crackers for 'bases'.
Serve crackers, tortilla chips and/or bell pepper strips as dippers.

name: Egyptian Okra
description: A well-liked Egyptian-style okra dish, known as bamya in Egyptian Arabic, simmered with onion, bell pepper, garlic, tomato paste, and chicken stock.
instructions: Heat a pot over high heat. Add the butter and let it melt.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Cook for about 2 minutes, or until they start to gently brown.
Add the tomato paste and chicken stock. Stir to combine well.
Add the okra and cook for about 15 minutes until soft.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

name: Moroccan Couscous
description: Fluffy couscous scented with cumin and coriander, cooked in chicken broth with hot pepper paste and preserved lemon.
instructions: Combine liquids in a bowl. Set aside.
Heat a large pot over medium high heat.
Pour some oil into the pot and add couscous. Sauté until the couscous is slightly browned.
Add the liquid mixture and remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Cover, remove from the heat, and set aside for 5 minutes or until the couscous is tender and all the liquid has been absorbed.
Open the pot and fluff the couscous thoroughly with a fork or chopsticks.
Serve immediately with lamb.

name: Preserved Lemon
description: Preserved lemons are a characteristic flavoring for slow braises and tagines, and they also make an unusual cocktail garnish.
instructions: Poke holes in the lemons with a sharp knife.
Pack the lemons in an airtight jar, separating them from one another with salt.
Cover the jar and store it in a dark place for a day.
If the lemons have not released enough liquid to cover them, add additional salt and reseal the jar.
Store in a cool dark place for approximately 2 weeks, then refrigerate.

name: Proja (Serbian Cornbread)
description: A Serbian cornbread made with cornmeal, flour, eggs, oil, yogurt, and cheese, baked until golden and served with kiseli kupus and pavlaka.
instructions: Mix everything together to make a batter.
Bake the batter in a 5 cm deep greased pan until golden.
Serve with kiseli kupus and pavlaka.

name: Whiskey Barbecue Sauce
description: A whiskey-based barbecue sauce blended with ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, cider vinegar, and chicken broth.
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes.
Refrigerate in a nonreactive container for up to 2 months.

name: Tahdiq (Crisped Persian Rice)
description: A classic Persian dish featuring a crispy golden crust of layered potatoes and basmati rice. The prized tahdig at the bottom of the pot is the crunchy, savory centerpiece of this traditional preparation.
instructions: Peel and slice the raw potatoes into ½ inch thick slices.

Rinse and drain the rice. Bring 4–5 cups of water to a boil in a 3-quart pot, adding salt if desired. Add the rice and continue to boil, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes. Check to be sure the rice doesn't cook completely at this point.
When the rice is roughly half cooked, drain into a colander.

Pour ¼ cup of cooking oil into the pot and lay the potato slices in the bottom close together in a single layer. Add a small amount of salt (if desired). Layer the half-cooked, drained rice loosely atop the potatoes.
Place the pot on the stove over medium high heat for 4–5 minutes or until the rice begins to steam.
Lower the heat and add 5 tbsp water and 2–3 tbsp oil on top of the rice. Cover and let simmer for about ½ hour or until cooked and tender. The higher the heat, the crunchier the tahdig.
Scoop out the rice and use a soft spatula to remove the tahdig at the bottom, or try to make the contents of the pot come out as an entire cake of rice on the serving dish.

name: Crab Cakes
description: Crisp, golden-brown crab cakes served with a tangy mayonnaise sauce flavored with capers, garlic, Worcestershire, and lemon.

ingredients.text: 1 lb (450 g) crabmeat or imitation crabmeat
ingredients.name: crabmeat

instructions: Combine crabmeat, Italian style breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, egg, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl for the cakes.
In a separate bowl, combine remaining ingredients, except the oil, to make the sauce.
Shape crab cake mix into 3-inch (7.5 cm) patties (about 2 per serving) or smaller for appetizer-size.
Add oil to a skillet.
Pan fry the cakes for 3–4 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Remove from skillet and drain on paper towels.
Serve cakes topped with the sauce.

name: Egyptian Grilled Pigeon (Fattah Meshaltet)
description: Succulent grilled pigeons coated in a fragrant blend of cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil. This traditional Egyptian dish is served hot for special occasions and gatherings.
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the ground cumin, ground coriander, ground paprika, ground cinnamon, ground black pepper, salt, minced garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil. Mix well to form a marinade.
Place the cleaned and gutted pigeons in the marinade, ensuring they are evenly coated. Massage the marinade into the birds, ensuring they are thoroughly seasoned.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the pigeons marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or overnight to allow the flavors to penetrate the meat.
Preheat the grill or barbecue to medium-high heat.
Remove the pigeons from the marinade and shake off any excess. Reserve the marinade for basting.
Place the pigeons on the grill and cook for about 6–8 minutes on each side, or until they are cooked through and nicely browned, basting occasionally with the reserved marinade.
Ensure the internal temperature of the pigeon reaches a safe temperature of 165°F (74°C) to ensure they are fully cooked.
Once cooked, transfer the grilled pigeons to a serving platter and let them rest for a few minutes before serving.
Serve hot as a main course, garnished with fresh herbs and accompanied by traditional Egyptian side dishes like rice or bread.

name: Albanian Mixed Vegetables
description: A traditional Albanian mixed vegetable dish (Turli perimesh) featuring peppers, eggplant, okra, zucchini, and potatoes sautéed with onions and tomatoes, then simmered until tender.

ingredients.text: 2 lbs of various vegetables (peppers, eggplant, okra, zucchini, potatoes, etc.)
ingredients.name: vegetables

instructions: Cut off inedible tips of vegetables. Wash and slice them into 1-inch squares.
Sauté vegetables in half the oil and remove them from the frying pan.
Sauté onion and tomatoes in the remaining oil, and season with parsley, salt, and pepper.
Put everything in a stock pot with a cup of water, cover tightly, and simmer until almost all moisture has cooked away.
Serve hot, accompanied by steak, meatballs, or any other main dish.

name: Mishti Doi (Bengali Sweetened Yogurt)
description: A traditional Bengali sweet yogurt made with reduced milk, caramelized sugar, and whisked yoghurt, then chilled until set.
instructions: Place a heavy-bottomed pan on the heat. Add milk, and warm it on medium heat.
Keep aside ⅓ of the sugar and add the rest of sugar to the milk.
Reduce the heat and continue to heat the milk until it reduces by half. Remove from the heat and keep aside.
Add the remaining sugar to another pan over medium heat. Allow the sugar to get warm and then melt. You will gradually notice the sugar browning and caramelizing.
When it gets to the point of a golden bubbly mixture, add a tablespoon of water in the caramelized sugar and then pour this mixture into the heavy-bottomed pan with milk. Stir well until combined.
Once milk cools off, add the whisked yoghurt, stir well and pour the mixture into earthen pots.
Let the doi set in a warm place for few hours. Once set, refrigerate and serve chilled.

name: Sourdough Starter
description: A bubbly, naturally fermented sourdough starter cultivated with all-purpose flour and sterilized, boiled-and-cooled water over several days.
instructions: Mix ½ cups of the water with ½ cup of the flour in a bowl.
Cover the bowl with a dish towel in a warm place (~70–80°F) and place in an open, clean spot on the counter to catch wild yeast floating in the air.
On the second day, add ½ cup flour to the mix and enough water to make it like a thick pancake batter. It should have had a few bubbles on the surface before you fed the mix.
On the third day, the starter should have a lot of bubbles all over coming up from deep inside. Feed it again with ½ cup flour and water.

On the fourth day, when it is very bubbly, you can start making bread with it and feed it again with flour and water. If you don't have a lot of bubbles you may need to keep going for a few more days or start all over with a clean bowl.
Repeat the boiling and cooling of the water every day to make sure it's sterilized.

name: Romanian Grilled Sausages (Mititei)
description: A classic Romanian street food of skinless grilled sausages made from seasoned minced meat, typically served with mustard and bread.
instructions: Combine all ingredients to form a paste.
Shape meat mixture by hand into 7–8 x 2–2.5 cm (3 x 1 inch) sausage shapes. Each should be about 50 grams.
Grill the sausages until cooked through. Do not let them dry out.
Serve with salt, mustard, and bread.

name: Kondre (Cameroonian Plantain and Meat Stew)
description: A simple, plantain-based Cameroonian meat stew seasoned with spices, basil, and vegetables, slow-cooked until the meat and plantain are tender.
instructions: Peel and rinse the plantain well, then cut it in half and let it soak in cold water.
Wash the meat and pat dry. Sprinkle with some salt, and let it sit for 10 minutes.
In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the meat and cook until browned. Remove the meat and set aside.
If desired, toast the pebe, rondelles, cloves, djansang, and white pepper in a separate small pan over high heat for extra flavor.
In a blender or food processor, combine the basil, leek, celery, garlic, ginger, tomato, and toasted spices. Blend the ingredients until you achieve a smooth mixture.
Return the meat to the pot and add the soaked plantain, half of the blended mixture, salt, and enough water to cover everything. Cover the pot and let it cook for approximately 45 minutes.

Add the remaining blended mixture, palm oil, and bouquet garni to the pot. Cover it again and continue cooking for an additional 60 minutes, or until both the meat and plantain are tender and flavorful. Stir the pot occasionally to prevent any sticking or burning.
Season with additional salt to taste before serving.

name: Matoke and Beef Stew
description: A hearty East African stew featuring tender plantains simmered with aromatic spices, tomatoes, peppers, and optional beef in a flavorful broth.

ingredients.text: Beef stew meat (optional), cut in bite-size pieces
ingredients.name: beef stew meat

instructions: Peel the plantains and cut into cubes. Toss with lemon juice and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pan. Add the tomatoes, onions, peppers, and garlic. Fry together.
Stir in the curry spice to taste, then the meat and stock. Cook, stirring, until the meat is nearly done or the mixture is boiling.
Stir in the plantains. Cover and simmer over low heat until the plantains are tender and the meat is fully cooked.
Season with salt and chili pepper to taste.
Serve and enjoy your delicious meal.

name: Khichdi (South Asian Rice and Lentils)
description: A comforting South Asian one-pot dish of rice and lentils seasoned with turmeric, popular in Gujarat as a wholesome dinner.

ingredients.text: 1 teacup dal (e.g. moong dhal, arhar dal or masoor dal or combination thereof)
ingredients.name: dal

instructions: Wash rice and lentils and soak them for 10–15 minutes in water.
Add salt and turmeric powder.
Pressure cook with 3–4 cups of water.
After the first whistle, reduce the heat and cook for 4–5 more minutes.
Allow to cool. Serve with ghee or buttermilk.

name: Dump Cake
description: A fast and easy layered cake with crushed pineapple, cherry pie filling, yellow cake mix, butter, and chopped pecans.

ingredients.text: 1 can (20 ounces) crushed pineapple with juice, undrained
ingredients.name: pineapple

instructions: Preheat Dutch oven in a 350°F oven. Grease the Dutch oven.
Dump in pineapple with juice and spread evenly.
Dump in pie filling and spread evenly over the pineapple.
Sprinkle cake mix evenly over cherry layer.
Dot with butter.
Bake about 50 minutes at 350°F.
Sprinkle chopped pecans on top.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Grease 13x9-inch cake pan.
Proceed as in the Dutch oven method above, starting with step #2.

name: Oatmeal Stout Brownies
description: Decadently chocolatey oatmeal stout brownies with a marbled cream cheese layer and a nicely balanced texture. Malt and oats from the beer enhance the chocolate flavor, while eggs make the brownies surprisingly light.

ingredients.text: 6 tablespoons unsalted room temperature butter, cut into cubes
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 1 ½ cup superfine or granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: 1 ¼ cups (10 ounces) oatmeal stout beer (room temperature)
ingredients.name: oatmeal stout beer

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup superfine or granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with nonstick foil (or grease and flour, or parchment paper…your call).
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, and salt until evenly combined. Set aside.
Melt butter, bittersweet chocolate, and white chocolate chips in a double-boiler over very low heat, stirring constantly until melted. Remove from heat.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add melted chocolate mixture, beating until combined.
Beat reserved flour mixture into melted chocolate mixture.
Whisk in stout beer. The batter will seem a bit thin.
Pour into prepared baking pan.
Drop semisweet chocolate chips evenly on top of batter (some will sink in).
Beat cream cheese in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Gradually beat in sugar.
Beat in vanilla and 1 egg just until blended.
Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie batter in pan.
Cut through mixture with knife several times for marbled design.
Bake for 25–35 minutes on center rack in the oven, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out almost clean.
Let brownies cool, uncovered, to room temperature.
Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving if desired.

name: Potato Pie
description: A savory pie of thinly sliced potatoes layered with onion, salt, and pepper, then covered with golden puff pastry and baked until tender.

ingredients.text: Puff pastry, rolled out ⅛ inch thick
ingredients.name: puff pastry

instructions: Peel and slice your potatoes very thin.
Layer the potatoes in a pie dish, adding some onion, salt, and pepper between each layer.
Add a dash of water to the potatoes, and scatter the chopped butter over top.
Cover the filling with the rolled-out puff pastry.
Bake at 375°F until golden and cooked through (about 1½ hours).

name: Dumboy and Pepper Soup
description: Dumboy, Liberia's national dish, is served as sticky cassava balls alongside a pepper soup made with meat, shrimp, okra, and habanero peppers.

ingredients.text: Cassava tubers, peeled and cut into chunks
ingredients.name: cassava

ingredients.text: 3 lb goat, chicken, or beef, cut into bite-size pieces
ingredients.name: meat

instructions: Rinse the cassava chunks, then boil in a saucepan of water for 20 minutes. Drain and cool.
If desired, slice the boiled cassava into smaller chunks.
Mash the cassava in a mortar until it begins to form a sticky dough. Occasionally, you can moisten the pestle with a little water if necessary.
When the desired consistency is reached, mould the dough into nicely shaped balls, and set them aside.
Combine the meat, onions, bay leaves, and habanero pepper in a large dutch oven. Add a reasonable amount of water and season with a generous pinch of salt and crushed bouillon cubes.
Cover the pot and boil for about 30 minutes until the meat becomes tender.
Add the shrimp and okra to the soup. Stir and simmer for another 10 minutes over medium heat.
Serve the soup with the prepared dumboy.

name: Yetsom Beyaynetu (Ethiopian Vegan Platter)
description: A traditional Ethiopian vegan platter featuring a colorful variety of flavorful vegetable and lentil dishes served with injera, the traditional Ethiopian flatbread. This nutritious platter is a staple during fasting periods and is enjoyed by both vegans and non-vegans alike.

ingredients.text: Cooking oil, for greasing the pan
ingredients.name: cooking oil

instructions: In a large pot, combine the red lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes or until the lentils are tender. Drain any excess water and set aside.
In a skillet or frying pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until they become translucent.
Add the minced garlic and diced tomatoes to the pan. Cook for a few minutes until the tomatoes start to soften.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, cumin, turmeric, and salt. Mix well to coat the onions and tomatoes with the spices.
Add the carrots, potatoes, cabbage, collard greens, and spinach to the skillet. Stir to combine the vegetables with the spice mixture.
Cover the skillet and cook for about 15–20 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender but still retain their shape. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
In the meantime, prepare the injera batter. In a mixing bowl, combine the teff flour, water, and salt. Whisk well until the batter is smooth and free of lumps. Let the batter rest for 15–20 minutes.
Heat an injera pan or non-stick skillet over medium heat. Lightly grease the pan with cooking oil.

Using a ladle, pour a thin layer of the injera batter onto the pan, swirling it around to evenly distribute the batter. Cook for about 1–2 minutes until the surface is covered with small bubbles and the edges start to lift.
Remove the cooked injera from the pan and repeat the process with the remaining batter. Stack the injera on a plate as you go.
To serve, arrange the cooked lentils and vegetable dishes on a large platter. Place the injera alongside the dishes.
Tear off pieces of injera and use them to scoop up the lentils and vegetables. Enjoy the vibrant flavors and textures of yetsom beyaynetu!

name: Turon (Filipino Plantain Spring Rolls)
description: Crispy deep-fried rolls filled with plantains and ripe jackfruit, coated in caramelized brown sugar.
instructions: Lay a lumpia wrapper on your work surface. Arrange a piece of banana and jackfruit in a line down the center.

Fold the sides of the wrapper towards the center, then roll everything up. Brush the overlapping end of the wrapper with a little water, then press against the roll to seal. Repeat to make a total of 10 rolls.
Heat an inch of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the rolls and fry until golden brown on all sides. Remove from the pan and let any excess oil drain.
Add the sugar to a heavy-bottomed pan. Carefully heat over medium heat, stirring periodically, until the sugar is fully melted. Make sure not to let it burn.
Remove the melted sugar pan from the heat. Immediately add the rolls to the pan and turn to coat with caramelized sugar. Remove the rolls from the sugar and serve.

name: Beef Yakiniku Pizza
description: A fusion pizza topped with Japanese-style yakiniku beef stir-fry, featuring tenderloin pieces in a savory mirin, soy, and oyster sauce on a homemade dough.

ingredients.text: ½ red capsicum, cut into 10 pieces
ingredients.name: red capsicum

ingredients.text: 600 g tenderloin beef, cut into 2 x 1 x 1 cm pieces
ingredients.name: beef tenderloin

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp cornstarch, dissolved with 20 ml water
ingredients.name: cornstarch

instructions: Combine flours, yeast, sugar, water, and salt to make a dough.
Cover with plastic wrap, and rest the dough 10 minutes until expanded.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Add the onion and capsicum, and sauté for 10 seconds.
Add the tenderloin and the water. Add the mirin, soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Add the dissolved cornflour, salt, and sugar. Stir until well-mixed and slightly thickened.
Separate the solids from the extra sauce. Reserve the sauce to serve with the pizza.
Roll out the pizza dough to a 10 cm diameter. Spread the meat topping on top.
Bake pizza in the oven at 220°C for 20 minutes.
Serve hot with the dipping sauces.

name: Paella de Marisco
description: A traditional Spanish seafood paella from the Valencian coastal region, featuring crab, shrimp, mussels, squid, and Norway lobsters simmered with saffron-infused rice in a wide paellera.

ingredients.text: 500 grams (1.1 lb) yellow onion, cut into quarters
ingredients.name: yellow onion

ingredients.text: 8 Norway lobsters (or very large crawfish or shrimp if Norway lobsters aren't available)
ingredients.name: norway lobster

ingredients.text: 8–10 strands of saffron (or 1½ teaspoons food coloring; see notes)
ingredients.name: saffron

instructions: Boil the broth ingredients in water, allowing the liquid to reduce until there's 2 liters of broth. Occasionally mash the ingredients against the bottom of the pot with a ladle or potato masher to squeeze out their flavors.
Strain the broth and set aside.
Heat oil in a paellera over a medium flame.
Add mussels and cover with a pot lid. The lid should cover the mussels but not the entire paellera. Cook until they open, then remove and set aside.
Add Norway lobsters and sprinkle them each with a pinch of salt.
Sear the lobsters, then remove.
Add the diced squid and sauté for about 2 minutes.
Add the shrimp and sauté for about 2 minutes.
Add garlic and sauté until golden brown. This should take about a minute.
Add grated tomatoes and sauté for about 4 minutes to make sofrito.
Add rice and braise until completely coated with sofrito.
Add paprika and sauté for about 2 minutes.
Add 2 liters of the seafood broth.
Add saffron (or food coloring). Mix well and simmer for about 3 minutes.
Taste the broth and invite your dinner guests to do so as well. If the broth is bland, add salt a pinch at a time until everyone approves.
Replace the lobsters and mussels, and continue cooking.
Begin tasting the rice after it's been simmering for about 20 minutes and reduce the heat a bit. Make sure the rice doesn't get too soft.

Check the rice again every 10 minutes and reduce the heat slightly after each taste. Your goal is to wind up with rice that has a slightly underdone center. The time it takes to reach this point can vary from 30 minutes to an hour depending on your cooking gear.

Your paella is done once the rice is slightly firm to the bite (al dente), the paella is a little moist but not soupy, and there is a bit of toasted rice on the bottom of the paellera. This is considered a delicacy throughout the Spanish-speaking world.
Remove the paellera from the heat and cover it with a white towel (not foil). Allow it to sit for 5 minutes before serving.

name: M'semen (Layered Algerian Flatbread)
description: A flaky, layered Algerian flatbread made from a simple dough of flour, semolina, and water, folded into square envelopes and pan-fried until golden.
instructions: Combine both flours, sugar, salt, and yeast in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the warm water until you get a soft dough. If it feels too sticky, mix in a little more all-purpose flour. If too dry, mix in some more water.
On a lightly-floured surface, knead the dough for 10 minutes or until it is smooth.
Divide the dough into smaller pieces, and roll each out into very thin rounds.
Brush each dough round with oil.
Fold the rounds into square envelope shapes, making 4 folds into the center.
Cook each flatbread in a hot, lightly-greased skillet until browned.

name: Confederate Cush
description: A hearty American Civil War-era dish of fried bacon and cubed beef combined with cornmeal mush, served warm like hash.
instructions: Put bacon into a hot iron skillet, and fry the grease out of it.
Add the beef, then slowly add 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil.
Add cornmeal mush and stir until dry.
Remove skillet from fire, and let cool.
Serve warm, like hash.

name: Spelt Burger
description: A hearty vegetarian burger made from spelt and oat flakes, flavoured with leek, onions, cumin and chillies, then pan-fried until golden.
instructions: Grind the spelt coarsely (if you have entire corns).
Soak the spelt with oat flakes in some water, in order to get a viscous substance. The burgers will be more compact if you add more oat flakes.
Cut onions and leek in small pieces.
Fry onions and leek with some oil.
Mix the substance with onions, leek and spices of your choice (cumin is a good choice).
Form flat burgers in a hot, oiled pan.

name: Mexican Rice II
description: A savory Mexican-style rice dish prepared with white rice, red chile, garlic, onion, ancho enchilada sauce, and chicken broth.

ingredients.text: 1 fresh red chile, seeded and finely diced (or 1 dehydrated chile that has been rehydrated)
ingredients.name: red chile

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp Ancho Enchilada Sauce, strained through a medium mesh
ingredients.name: ancho enchilada sauce

ingredients.text: 4 cloves of garlic, peeled and crushed
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: ½ small onion, peeled and finely diced
ingredients.name: onion

instructions: Sauté garlic, onions, and red chile in oil over medium heat for about 1 minute.
Add in the rice and stir frequently until rice begins to brown.
Mix chicken stock and chile sauce in another saucepan and bring to a boil. When mixed, make sure liquid mixture equals out to 2 cups of liquid.
Add chicken stock and chile sauce mixture to rice and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and bring rice to slow simmer. Cook for 25–30 minutes with the lid on.
Remove lid and fluff rice with a fork.

name: Microwave Peanut Brittle
description: An easier version of classic peanut brittle that can be prepared in under 10 minutes using a microwave, with a sweet, crunchy finish.
instructions: Lightly grease a cookie sheet and set aside.
In a 1½-quart casserole dish, stir together sugar and syrup. Microwave on high for 4 minutes.
Stir in peanuts. Microwave on high for 3–5 minutes or until light brown.
Add butter and vanilla, mixing well. Microwave at high 1–2 minutes more. The peanuts will be lightly browned and syrup very hot.
Add baking soda and stir gently until light and foamy.
Pour mixture onto greased cookie sheet. Let cool ½–1 hour.
When cool, break into small pieces and store in airtight container.

name: Grilled Eggplant with Garlic Butter
description: Smoky grilled eggplant slices seasoned with salt and pepper, brushed with olive oil, and topped with a pat of homemade garlic butter that melts into the charred flesh.

ingredients.text: 2 medium eggplants, sliced ½ inch thick
ingredients.name: eggplant

instructions: Fold garlic into butter. Shape into a narrow log using parchment or wax paper, and refrigerate until needed.
Sprinkle all sides of eggplant with salt. Let sit 15 minutes or until it "sweats". Leave it without touching.
Rinse eggplant. Pat dry with paper towels, and brush with olive oil.
Season liberally on both sides with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Add eggplant to grill, and cook until marked and slightly charred on both sides.
Place a pat of butter mixture on top of each piece and wait until butter is melted before serving.

name: Firecracker Grilled Shrimp
description: Firecracker-marinated shrimp are threaded onto bamboo skewers and charcoal-grilled until pink and slightly charred.
instructions: Pour marinade into a gallon size zip-top bag. Add shrimp and toss to coat. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Drain shrimp and discard remaining marinade. Thread 4 shrimp onto each skewer.
Preheat your charcoal grill using a chimney starter, not lighter fluid to medium high.
Reapply the grate and add shrimp. Cook, turning often, until shrimp is pink and slightly charred.
Remove shrimp from skewers and discard skewers. Serve warm.

name: Fanke (Hausa Puff Puff)
description: Fanke is a Nigerian fritter made with wheat flour or semovita, commonly enjoyed in Northern Nigeria, especially among the Hausa people.
instructions: Sift the flour into a clean bowl. Mix in the yeast, sugar, and baking powder.
Stir in the warm water and vanilla to make a thick batter.
Cover the bowl, and let rise for about 1 hour.
Heat enough oil in a pan for deep-frying.
Shape the batter into balls, and drop them into the hot oil in batches.
Deep fry the fritters until golden brown on all sides.
Remove from the oil and let drain.

name: Kids' Vegetable Puree
description: A smooth, creamy purée of carrots, tomato, cucumber, and chicken breast, blended to a soft texture ideal for toddlers and babies unable to chew.

ingredients.text: 100 g (3.5 oz) chicken breast, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: chicken breast

instructions: Put the carrots, tomatoes, and chicken breast in a pot. Add water to the same level as the ingredients.
Cover, and cook on medium heat until the chicken is well done and the carrots are soft.
Add the diced cucumber, olive oil, and salt. At this point, you can top up the water to the same level as the ingredients if most of the water has dried.
Cover the pot and leave to boil until the cucumbers are soft.
Turn off the heat and leave to cool down completely.
Blend into a smooth purée using a kitchen blender. No need to add more water.

name: Hongshao Rou (Red Braised Pork Belly)
description: A traditional Chinese pork belly dish braised slowly in a thick, sweet, dark sauce with ginger, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine until the meat is tender and richly flavoured.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, over high heat, heat the oil and sugar together until the sugar melts and turns brown.
Add the cubed pork to the sugar and oil and brown all over.
Reduce the heat, add the stock, ginger, star anise, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine to the pan.
Cover tightly and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent it burning at the bottom.
Remove the lid and add the spring onions.
Boil the sauce until only a thick, dark gravy is left.
The dish may be served now, but if possible, refrigerate for a day to allow the flavours to develop.
Serve with rice, garnish with sliced spring onion.

name: Honey Mustard Salad Dressing
description: A creamy honey-mustard dressing whisked with lemon juice, salt, pepper, and safflower oil.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon (7.5 ml) freshly-ground black pepper
ingredients.name: black pepper

instructions: Combine the mustard, honey, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Gradually whisk the safflower oil into the mixture to form a creamy dressing.

name: Onion Chutney
description: A delicious sweet-and-sour chutney used as a side dish for many South Indian snacks and breakfast items, and one of the components used in masala dosa assembly.
instructions: In a shallow pan, heat the oil. Add the chana dal, and stir until the dal is roasted.
Add the onions, and stir fry them till they become transparent and the edges turn golden brown. Turn off the heat and let them cool for a few minutes.
When cooled, blend together the onion mixture, coconut, chillies, tamarind, and salt until it makes a smooth paste. Add a few teaspoons of water if necessary.

name: Chicken Curry
description: A fragrant chicken curry marinated in aromatic spices and coconut yogurt, slow-cooked with potatoes and tomatoes for a rich, flavorful dish.
instructions: Clean the chicken and cut into small pieces.
Combine with all the marinade ingredients and mix well. Set aside for 30 minutes to let flavors seep in.
Fry cumin, fennel, and mustard seeds on a medium heat in a large pan.
Add garlic and ginger paste and fry.
Chop the onions into small pieces and fry in the pan.
Add the potatoes and fry.
In a separate pan, sear the chicken in batches and add it to bowl separately.
After the onions turn golden brown add the marinated chicken.
Add curry powder, coconut yogurt and turn to a low heat. Leave to cook for 35–40 minutes.
Finely chop fresh coriander and a dash of lemon juice to the curry.
Serve with rice or naan bread.

name: Simple Buttercream
description: A simple buttercream frosting made by creaming butter with vanilla and powdered sugar, then finishing with milk for a smooth, spreadable icing perfect for filling, coating, and decorating cakes.
instructions: Cream together butter and vanilla using a mixer.
Beat in powdered sugar one cup at a time, scraping sides and bottom of bowl regularly. Mixture will be very dry.
When all the sugar is incorporated, add milk and beat until incorporated.

name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cabernet Reduction
description: Duck breasts are pan-seared and oven-finished, then served with a flamed shallot-and-garlic Cabernet Sauvignon reduction.
instructions: Score skin of duck in a diamond pattern and season liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Set aside.
Heat a 12-inch cast iron skillet over medium high heat. Add duck breasts, skin side down, and cook 10 minutes. Flip and cook 3 minutes.
Move pan to a 400°F oven and cook 12 minutes. Remove duck from pan and keep warm.
Pour off extra fat. Place 1 Tbsp back into pan and add shallot and garlic. Sauté over medium high heat until garlic is golden.
Add wine off of the heat and carefully ignite with a long match or firestick. Shake pan until flames die (might wanna have a fire extinguisher).
Boil over medium high heat until reduced by half. Drizzle over duck and serve warm.

name: Corn on the Cob with Husks
description: Corn on the cob is soaked to help prevent the husks from burning, then grilled and served with butter and salt.

ingredients.text: Corn on the cob, with husks left on
ingredients.name: corn

instructions: Carefully peel back husk without detaching it and remove silk.
Replace husks and soak ears in cold water for ½ hour.
Place corn on grill or on a rack above an open fire.
Cook for about 15 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Serve with butter and salt.

name: Tomato and Onion Salad
description: A chopped salad of tomatoes, red and white onions, cucumber, black olives, and spring onion, tossed with a vinegar and lemon juice dressing.
instructions: Mix all salad ingredients together.
In a separate bowl, mix dressing ingredients.
Stir dressing into salad.
Serve with flat bread and feta cheese.

name: Nigerian Rice Pudding
description: A thick, creamy rice pudding made with milk, egg, sugar, and cinnamon.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Stir in the rice, and boil for 5 minutes.
Drain the rice, and rinse with water to remove excess starch.
Bring milk and a pinch of salt to a boil. Stir in the rice, and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until the rice is soft.
Reduce the heat to low, and stir the rice continuously until it has thickened and become creamy. Make sure to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom of the pan and burning.
Combine the egg and sugar in a boil, then quickly stir the mixture into the rice pudding.
Remove from the heat, and let cool.
Season with a pinch of cinnamon, and serve.

name: Panamanian Ropa Vieja
description: A hearty Panamanian-style shredded beef stew simmered with bell peppers, onions, carrots, olives, and aromatic spices in a tomato, wine, and broth sauce.

ingredients.text: 2 lb flank steak, cut into large pieces
ingredients.name: flank steak

ingredients.text: Green and red bell peppers, cubed
ingredients.name: bell pepper

ingredients.text: 4–6 cloves of garlic, cut in quarters
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: ½ cup pitted green olives, sliced
ingredients.name: green olive

instructions: Season the beef with salt, sazón, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, and pepper, and coat well.
Whisk together the tomato paste, wine, and broth in a medium bowl. If you're cooking this dish on the stove, use 3 cups of broth—you'll need more since some of it will evaporate on the stove.

Sauté the vegetables: If using an Instant Pot, set it to the sauté setting. Add the oil and then the onions, bell peppers, and garlic. Cook for 3–4 minutes until softened. Then press cancel. If using the stove, sauté the vegetables in a large Dutch oven on medium-high heat.
Nestle the meat into the onions so half are on the bottom and half are above the meat. Add the carrots, olives, bay leaves, and cilantro (if using). Pour the tomato mixture over everything.

Cook: If using an Instant Pot, put the lid on, and cook on high for 45 minutes. Once done, unplug the pot, and do a natural release. If using the stove, bring the pot to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer until the meat easily shreds. It should take about 1½–2 hours. Add more water if it gets too dry.
Shred the beef, discard the bay leaves, and top with more cilantro if desired.

name: Umxhanxa (Zimbabwean Melon Soup)
description: A traditional Zimbabwean porridge made from yellow watermelon, sun-dried maize, and sugar, simmered together into a smooth, sweet dish.
instructions: Place the maize in a pot, and cover with a large volume of water.
Bring the pot to a boil. Simmer until the maize is very soft, adding extra water if necessary.
Drain the water, and reserve the cooked maize.
Slice the yellow watermelon into thick slices in the same manner as you would a red watermelon. Remove all of the seeds.
Remove and discard the melon rind. Cut the melon into large chunks.
Transfer the melon to a pot, and add 250 ml water. Bring to a boil, and simmer for 30 minutes until soft.
Use an egg beater or blender to process the melon until soft and smooth.
Mix the maize into the melon mixture.
Stir in the sugar, and simmer for no more than 15 minutes.
Serve hot.

name: Pesto II
description: A fragrant Italian pesto made by blending fresh basil with pine nuts or walnuts, garlic, olive oil and Parmesan cheese.

ingredients.text: 1 packet of pine nuts or walnuts
ingredients.name: pine nut or walnut

ingredients.text: 2 large plants worth of fresh basil
ingredients.name: basil

instructions: Whatever you may have been told, use an electric blender or a liquidiser to make pesto. Faffing about with a pestle and mortar is for the birds.
Again, whatever you have been told, put a good quantity of olive oil in the blender first and start it running, otherwise the blades will gum up and you risk burning the basil.
Drop basil leaves through the top into the olive oil so that they are mulched up by the blades.
Add some nuts so they are also mulched up.
When the developing pesto sticks and becomes too thick, simply add more olive oil until the whole lot starts to mulch again.
Continue adding basil leaves, nuts and the garlic cloves, always making sure the mixture remains fluid.
Once you begin to run out of basil leaves and nuts, add a handful of Parmesan cheese (though not too much; remember the taste should be predominantly of basil).
The end result should be a wondrous smelling, glutinous mass of green, which should be then emptied out of the blender into its own container.

name: Mhadjeb (Algerian Stuffed Flatbread)
description: A thin, flaky Algerian flatbread made from semolina and filled with onion, tomatoes, and spices. A traditional favorite among Algerian households, prized for its simplicity and economical cost.
instructions: Combine the semolina, flour, and salt together in a bowl. Gradually stir in water with your hands until you get a smooth and soft dough.
Wet a plastic bag in warm water, cover the dough while still dripping, and let it rest. Afterwards, uncover the dough and knead lightly for a few minutes.
Coat your hands in oil, and shape the dough into balls, arranging them beside each other. Cover and allow to rest once more.
Peel the tomatoes, then dice them into small pieces.
Heat some oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions, and stir regularly until they become translucent and soft.
Add the diced tomatoes, seasonings, and salt. Cover the pan and allow the mixture to cook over low heat, stirring occasionally to prevent it from sticking.
Let cool.
On an oiled surface, roll out the first ball of dough and give it a light coating of oil.
Place some filling in the center, and fold the dough over it on four sides to form a square.
Lightly oil the top of the dough and move it to a hot pan over medium-low heat. Cook until the first side is well-browned, then flip it to the other side and brown again. Remove from the pan.
Repeat the shaping and cooking process with the remaining dough and filling.
Serve hot and enjoy!

name: Cauliflower Cheese
description: A filling and cheesy cauliflower gratin, great as a side to a roast dinner or any other dish.

ingredients.text: 300 ml (10 oz / 1 ¼ cups) white sauce
ingredients.name: white sauce

instructions: Cut your cauliflower into small florets, and place them heads down into a bowl of salty water to dress them for an hour.
Drain florets, and add them to a saucepan of salted boiling water.
Cook, uncovered, regularly checking the feel of the cauliflower with a knife to see when they are ready. Your knife should go smoothly, but with some firmness to the cauliflower still.
Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan/390°F/gas 6).
Once the cauliflower has cooked, drain the florets and lay them in a dish of your choice.
Combine the white sauce with ⅔ of the parmesan cheese, and pour over the cauliflower.
Sprinkle over the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese.
Place your dish into the oven for about 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve immediately.

name: Dodo Ikire (Fried Leftover Plantain)
description: A traditional Nigerian dish of mashed overripe plantain seasoned with salt and pepper, then fried until darkened and shaped into balls.
instructions: Mash the plantain and transfer it into a bowl.
Stir in salt and crushed pepper until well-combined.
Heat oil in a frying pan for a few minutes, but don't allow to smoke (3–4 minutes is enough).
Scoop the plantain mixture into the hot oil. Cook until darkened but not burnt.
Remove the dodo ikire from the oil, and drain any excess.
Re-mould the dodo ikire into balls. Sprinkle with some pepper.

name: Muffuletta Sandwich
description: A New Orleans sandwich layered with salami, ham, mortadella, Swiss and provolone cheeses, and olive spread on a muffuletta loaf.

ingredients.text: 1 muffuletta bread loaf (or other round bread loaf, approximately 10 inches/25 cm in diameter)
ingredients.name: muffuletta bread loaf

instructions: Slice the bread loaf in half horizontally and spread each cut side with olive spread.
For the authentic Central Grocery muffuletta, layer the bottom half of the loaf with salami, ham, Swiss cheese, provolone, mortadella, and a second layer of salami.
Cover with the top half of the loaf and press down.
Quarter the muffuletta and serve or wrap the muffuletta tightly in plastic wrap to save for later.

name: Tacos
description: A traditional Mexican dish of seasoned beef served in a corn or wheat tortilla with a variety of fresh toppings like cilantro, onion, cheese, and salsa.

ingredients.text: Ground, finely sliced, or chopped beef
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: Corn tortillas or ready-made taco shells
ingredients.name: tortilla

ingredients.text: 1–4 tsp per pound (450 g) of beef of cumin
ingredients.name: cumin

ingredients.text: Shredded mild cheddar cheese, if desired
ingredients.name: cheddar cheese

ingredients.text: Salsa, or hot sauce, as hot as you would like
ingredients.name: salsa

instructions: If you would like to have 'build-your-own' tacos, dice the optional ingredients as needed and place in separate bowls for use on the table.

Place the beef in a wide pan on a large burner. Ground beef will need to be broken up as it cooks; chopped or sliced beef needs to be stir-fried and may require oil. When using high-fat ground beef, you may wish to drain and very lightly rinse the beef in a colander, or add water to float the fat, cool to solidify the fat, remove the fat, drain the water, and reheat.
Add lots of cumin to the beef. Cumin is the magic ingredient that makes a taco taste like a taco. You may also add a bit of salt, a bit of chili powder and/or diced onion.

Prepare the outside covering: Pre-made shells can be reheated in the microwave as the package directs. Plain corn tortillas can be used for soft tacos, although, for soft tacos, either a double layer of corn tortillas or a single layer of flour tortilla works best. The tortillas should be microwaved, covered, in 15+ second stages, flipping between stages, until warm, and kept covered and warm prior to use. You could make your own hard taco shells from corn tortillas, but soft corn tortilla tacos are absolutely the most traditional. If you need hard shells and cannot find them pre-made, you may use a deep-fat process, going one at a time and using a large spoon to form the shells into the normal U shape. Pan frying in ¼ inch to ½ inch of oil will also work; be sure not to let the tortillas stiffen prior to being bent into the U shape you desire.

Place hot beef into a hard shell or down the middle of a warm soft tortilla (two for corn). A very simple, and quite authentic, taco would be to then add a sprinkling of finely diced onion and cilantro into the inside of the taco, fold the tortilla over (if soft) and serve with lime quarters for squeezing into the taco.

You may also continue on to place cheese onto the beef. The heat of the beef should slightly melt the cheese. You may wish to microwave the taco a bit, especially if the cheese is cold or if you are using low-fat cheese.
Add other toppings as the cook desires.

Serve the tacos with a small or large assortment of items that people can add. Traditionally, in a restaurant, this would amount to only pico de gallo or a hot sauce. However, 'build-your-own' tacos with a good assortment of items to add can add a bit of fun to a gathering or family dinner.

name: Chipotle BBQ Chicken Nuggets
description: Crispy chicken pieces double-dredged in cornmeal and seasoned with a smoky chipotle BBQ rub, then deep-fried until golden. Served with a sprinkle of black pepper for a flavorful, crunchy bite.

ingredients.text: 4 boneless skinless chicken breast halves, cut into 1 ½ in pieces
ingredients.name: chicken breast

instructions: Place cornmeal in a pie pan and lemon juice in another pie pan.
Dip chicken pieces in lemon juice then season with BBQ rub. Dip again in lemon juice.
Dredge pieces, three at a time, in the cornmeal, then dip in lemon juice again then dredge again in cornmeal.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry pieces in batches for 6 minutes. Drain on a cooling rack but not paper towels.
Sprinkle with black pepper and serve.

name: 40 Cloves in a Roast Chicken
description: A seasoned roast chicken stuffed with 40 garlic cloves and roasted with lemon, thyme, rosemary, and parsley.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup Country Roast Chicken Seasoning
ingredients.name: chicken seasoning

instructions: Rub the Country Roast Chicken Seasoning under the skin of the chicken. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Tie the chicken's legs together and wing tips under the back with butcher's twine.
Heat garlic in a microwave on low for 6 minutes.
In this step, work quickly. If using a bag, place garlic in and stuff it in the cavity. If not, just stuff it in.
Coat chicken with olive oil. Place herbs in the bottom of a roasting pan and put lemon slices on top.
Put chicken breast side up on top and bake in an oven for 45 minutes at 375°F (190°C).
Turn the temperature up to 425°F (220°C) and bake for 45 more minutes or until the internal temperature in both the thigh and breast reaches 165°F (75°C) and the juices run clear.
Let rest for 10 minutes and serve.

name: Rava Dosa (Indian Semolina Pancake)
description: A savory Indian pancake made with rice flour, all-purpose flour, semolina, buttermilk, green chiles, and cumin, cooked on a griddle and served with tomato or peanut chutney.
instructions: Mix all the ingredients together to a watery batter.
Heat a griddle or pan, and grease it with oil.
Sprinkle the batter on the pan with your hand.
Cook it on medium temperature for 3–4 minutes, or until it is completely cooked.
Serve it with tomato or peanut chutney.

name: Risotto ai Funghi
description: A classic Italian risotto made with porcini mushrooms, arborio rice, and Parmesan cheese, slowly cooked with white wine and chicken stock for a creamy, comforting dish.

ingredients.text: 250 g arborio, vialone nano, or carnaroli risotto rice
ingredients.name: risotto rice

ingredients.text: 1 small (150 g) white onion, finely chopped
ingredients.name: white onion

ingredients.text: 200 g fresh porcini mushrooms,or about 50 g dried
ingredients.name: porcini mushroom

ingredients.text: 100 g freshly grated Parmesan Reggiano cheese
ingredients.name: parmesan cheese

instructions: If using dried mushrooms, soak them for at least 20 minutes in 200 ml warm water. Once they have reconstituted properly, chop about ½ of them into small pieces and roughly chop the rest. There's no need to soak fresh mushrooms.
Melt half the butter in preferably a medium sized frying pan or saucepan, on a medium heat.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the butter until the onion is translucent. Under no circumstances should the onions and garlic burn.
Now add the rice and swirl it around in the pan until it is also coated in the butter. Leave for about 30 seconds.
Now splash in the wine—it should fizz and steam dramatically—and wait for it to evaporate.
Add about half the stock slowly, one ladle at a time.
Stir the rice about every 2 minutes to release the starch and add more stock if there is the slightest chance of the rice drying out.

After about 5 minutes of cooking add the mushrooms and their juice (or liquor as it is called). If using dried mushrooms, make sure to avoid adding the dirt that has sedimented at the bottom of the container in which they've dried.

The secret of risotto is that the rice should be cooked until al dente, which means the rice should have a bit of bite left, rather than be squashy and flaccid. This takes anywhere from 15–20 minutes, but be sure to start testing small spoonfuls after about 15 minutes of cooking. The rice should be fairly glutinous and not too runny. Ideally it should spread out on its own across the plate when served, not remaining in a lump in the middle.

When you feel the rice is cooked, take it off the heat and add the chopped parsley, the remaining butter and about 2 tbsp of the Parmesan cheese and mix it all in together. Adjust the seasoning as well.
Let it stand for about 2 minutes (the Italians call this the Mantecatura period) and serve.

name: Sunshine Cake
description: A light, attractive sponge cake that is not too rich, making it especially nice to serve alongside a frozen dessert.
instructions: Whip the yolks with a rotary beater until they are thick and lemon-colored.
Whip the egg whites until they are foamy, add the cream of tartar, and continue whipping until they are dry.
Fold the sugar into the egg whites, then fold the yolks into this mixture.
Sift the flour several times and add it.
Add the lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour batter into a sponge-cake pan, and bake.

name: Breakfast Waffles
description: Simple and fluffy breakfast waffles made with a quick batter of eggs, milk, and flour. The egg whites are beaten separately and folded in for a light, airy texture.
instructions: Mix egg yolks and milk.
Add flour, baking powder, sugar, salt and mix well.
Add the oil.
Whip the egg whites until stiff and then fold into the batter.
Preheat a waffle iron.
Ladle a scoop of batter into the waffle iron, and cook until browned and cooked through.
Remove waffle and repeat cooking process with remaining batter.

name: Mató de Pedralbes (Spanish Maize Custard)
description: A traditional Spanish custard dessert made with milk, maize flour, egg yolks, and cinnamon, gently cooked until thickened and served chilled with jam or rosemary honey.
instructions: Stir the maize flour into a glass of the cold milk.
Put the rest of milk in a saucepan, add sugar and yolks, and beat together until blended.
Add cinnamon sticks and heat the mixture. When it begins to boil, add the glass of milk and flour, and mix well. Cook until thickened.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and take out the cinnamon sticks. Pour it into four oval molds and refrigerate until cool.
To serve, unmold the custards and serve with jam or some rosemary honey.

name: Chips Cheese and Gravy
description: A Manx takeaway classic featuring golden oven-baked chips topped with melted cheddar and savory beef gravy.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and spread the chips onto an oiled baking tray.
Bake the chips for around 15–20 minutes until they are slightly golden.
After about 5 minutes add grated cheese on top of the chips and continue cooking.
In a small saucepan melt in the butter and flour and mix continuously.
Cook on a low heat and slowly add the beef broth and black pepper. Stir continually.
When the chips are ready, divide between plates and add the gravy as desired.

name: Gobi Bhagi (Spiced Cauliflower Stew)
description: A spiced cauliflower stew with tomatoes, onions, green chiles, ginger, garam masala, and pepper.
instructions: Boil the cauliflower in hot water for 5 minutes. Drain and cut into big pieces.
Heat some oil in a pan, and add the onions. Add the tomatoes, and fry until the tomatoes leave the oil.
Add the cauliflower, green chiles, ginger, chili powder, and some water. Pressure cook for 6–7 minutes.
Stir in garam masala, pepper, and salt.
Serve with chappati or naan and pulao.

name: Christmas Pudding II
description: A festive steamed Christmas pudding made with dried fruits, suet, spices and brandy, traditionally served with cream or custard.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the raisins, currants, sultanas, and mixed peel.
Stir in the breadcrumbs, suet, flour, and brown sugar until well combined.
Add the mixed spice, cinnamon, and nutmeg, mixing thoroughly.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs with the brandy and milk, then pour over the dry ingredients.
Add the chopped almonds and mix everything together until evenly distributed.
Cover and let the mixture rest overnight in a cool place.
Grease a 2-pint pudding basin and fill with the mixture, pressing down firmly.
Cover with a layer of greaseproof paper and foil, tied securely with string.
Place the basin in a large steamer or pot with water reaching halfway up the sides.
Steam for 8 hours, topping up the water as needed.
Remove from the steamer and let cool completely before storing.
On serving day, steam for an additional 2 hours to reheat.
Turn out onto a serving plate and serve with brandy butter, cream, or custard.

name: Ossobuco Alla Milanese
description: Slow-braised veal shanks become meltingly tender in a rich, creamy tomato-and-wine sauce, with the marrow and connective tissues dissolving into the sauce.

ingredients.text: 4 slices veal hind shank, about 2.5–4 centimeters (1–1½ inches) thick
ingredients.name: veal shank

ingredients.text: 3 ribs celery with leaves, chopped fine
ingredients.name: celery

ingredients.text: 240 ml (1 cup) dry white wine or white vermouth
ingredients.name: white wine

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
If the butcher has not done so, tie the shanks around the middle with kitchen twine; this will keep them from falling apart during cooking.

Choose a heavy, covered roasting pan or Dutch oven which will just accommodate the veal shanks in one layer. Put the butter, two tablespoons of the oil, the onions, celery and carrots in the pan and sweat over medium heat until the vegetables have wilted—about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and lemon peel and sweat until they're fragrant, about 2 minutes more. Remove from the heat.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a skillet until it is near the smoking point. Lightly flour the veal shanks and slip them into the oil. Richly brown the shanks on both of the cut sides, then place them in the roasting pan on top of the vegetables.
Place the wine in the skillet and boil until reduced by one-half, deglazing the bottom of the pan. Pour this over the veal shanks.

Heat the beef broth to a boil in the skillet, whisking in the tomato paste and anchovies. Add this to the veal shanks, along with the herbs, several grindings of pepper, and a large pinch of salt. The liquid should cover three quarters of the shanks. If not, add extra water.
Bring the pot to a simmer, cover, and place in the oven. Cook for approximately 2 hours, turning and basting the shanks every half hour.
If you notice that the cooking liquids have nearly evaporated, add hot water, about one half cup at a time. The veal is done when it is fork tender and falling from the bone.
Transfer the shanks to a platter, remove the strings, and cover to keep warm.

If the sauce seems watery, as is probable, place the pan on the stove top over high heat and reduce the cooking liquid until the sauce has a thick, creamy consistency. Pour the sauce over the shanks and serve.

name: Mesquite BBQ Salmon
description: Wild salmon filets are marinated in lemon and olive oil, rubbed with a smoky spice blend, and grilled over mesquite wood chips before being glazed with barbecue sauce for a charred, crispy finish.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24 ounces) skin-on wild salmon filets, pin bones removed
ingredients.name: salmon

ingredients.text: ¾ cup mesquite wood chips, soaked in water for 30 minutes
ingredients.name: mesquite wood chips

instructions: Combine lemon juice and olive oil in a gallon-size zip-top bag. Add salmon, toss to coat, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Wad up a sheet of newspaper and moisten with vegetable oil. Place under chimney full of coals, which you have put in the bottom of the grill, then light. Wait 15 minutes.
While charcoal heats, combine seasonings and sugar. Rub into salmon filets.

Dump coals evenly around grill and toss in wood chips. Re-apply grate, then quickly swab grill with the towel. Add salmon filets, skin side down, to the hottest part of the grill and cook 2–3 minutes per side for medium rare, rotating 90 degrees halfway through cooking to make grill marks.
Brush meat side with sauce and cook until charred and crispy on the meat side, about 30 seconds. Serve immediately.

name: Simple Syrup
description: A quick, versatile syrup made by dissolving sugar in water, ideal for sweetening cold beverages. Refrigerated, it stays usable for up to a week.
instructions: Combine the sugar and cold water in a saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, stirring constantly.
When all of the sugar has dissolved, remove from the heat and allow to cool to room temperature. This should only take a few minutes.
Transfer to a storage container, and refrigerate until needed.

name: Tofu in Spiced Coconut Sauce
description: A fragrant tofu dish simmered in a creamy sauce of sour cream, yogurt, and coconut milk, spiced with cardamom, coriander, and cumin, and studded with currants and toasted almonds.

ingredients.text: 1 extra-firm or firm tofu block, cut into ¾-inch cubes
ingredients.name: tofu

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (or more) slivered almonds, lightly toasted
ingredients.name: almond

ingredients.text: ⅛ cup toasted coconut threads or flakes (optional)
ingredients.name: coconut

instructions: Crack open the cardamom pods. Reserve the seeds; discard the shells.
Heat oil to quite hot but not smoking in a pan. Add spices and bay leaf. Cook until seeds crack (1–2 minutes).
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and garlic, then cook until tender and translucent.
Reserve onion, garlic, spices to a side dish.
Season tofu with salt and pepper. Fry, adding oil if needed. When tofu is heated through, sauté until lightly brown (5–8 minutes).
Add reserved onion/spice mixture.
Add currants and sauté for 3–5 minutes. At this point, the tofu may be cooled and chilled for re-heating the following day.
Add sour cream, yogurt, coconut milk, and butter. Simmer until sauce has cooked down a little.
Add toasted almonds and toasted coconut.
Serve hot with Saffron Sweet Rice.

name: Macaroni and Cheese I
description: Creamy macaroni and cheese coated in a smooth white sauce made with butter, milk, cheddar, and Parmesan or Monterey Jack cheese, with cayenne pepper for warmth.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (8 tbsp / 1 stick / 125 g / 4.4 oz) butter
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 1 cup (125 g / 4.4 oz) Parmesan or Monterey Jack cheese
ingredients.name: parmesan or monterey jack cheese

ingredients.text: ½ tsp cayenne pepper, or to taste
ingredients.name: cayenne pepper

ingredients.text: 1 pound (450 g) macaroni noodles, boiled and drained
ingredients.name: macaroni

instructions: Make a roux using the butter and flour.
Add the heated milk, and whisk until smooth to complete the white sauce.
Mix in the cheese and cayenne pepper.
Mix the cheese sauce into the cooked macaroni noodles until well-coated.

name: Boiled Cocoyam
description: Tender cocoyam simmered with salt and served with garden egg stew, egg sauce, or fried pepper.
instructions: Wash the cocoyam to remove dirt from the surface, and cut into smaller pieces without peeling.
Transfer cocoyam to a pot, and cover with water.
Add a pinch of salt, and simmer for several minutes until tender.
Drain the cocoyam, and remove the peel.
Serve with garden egg stew, egg sauce, or fried pepper.

name: Grilled Lamb Chops
description: Thick-cut bone-in lamb loin chops rubbed with garlic, fresh herbs, and bold spices, then grilled to a perfect medium rare.
instructions: Rub the cut side of the halved garlic head all over lamb chops. Brush with olive oil and rub seasonings into meat. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Grill chops over high heat for 1 ½ minutes. Rotate 90° and cook for another 1 ½ minutes. Flip and repeat these steps on the other side of the chops.
Move meat to medium heat and cook, turning often, until internal temperature reaches 140°F for medium rare.
Remove and let rest 7 minutes. Serve warm.

name: Quinoa (Cooked)
description: A simple method for cooking fluffy quinoa, soaked to remove bitterness and then simmered until tender. Perfect as a base for bowls, salads, or side dishes.
instructions: Place quinoa in a bowl and cover completely with water. Soak for 3–4 hours, then discard the water. Replace with fresh water and soak for another hour or so. Drain again.
Combine the drained quinoa with the 2 cups water and pinch of salt in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, and simmer on the lowest heat setting for 16–18 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let rest for 5 minutes.

name: Southern Clam Chowder
description: A creamy Southern-style clam chowder with tender potatoes, salt pork, and clams in a rich milk broth. This North Carolina classic is best when made a day ahead.
instructions: Remove black parts from clams, saving the liquor.
Cut pork into small pieces and fry until crisp and golden brown, then remove small pieces of pork from the fat. Discard fat.
Add potatoes and onion, with just enough hot water to be seen through the potatoes.
Cook over low heat-just simmer-until done.
When potatoes are done, add clams and pork and cook for 2 minutes after coming to a boil. Longer cooking will make the clams tough.
Remove chowder from heat and let stand for few minutes, then add hot milk, the clam liquor and seasoning to taste. If seasonings are added before hot milk, the chowder may curdle.
Serve hot. May add butter to each bowl for extra taste.

name: Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Chili Chicken)
description: A traditional Peruvian shredded chicken dish in a spicy sauce flavored with cheese, garlic, nuts and Peruvian chili peppers, served over rice and garnished with potatoes, eggs and olives.

ingredients.text: 3 hot yellow South American chilis (seeds and filaments removed): Adjust quantity for individual taste.
ingredients.name: chili

ingredients.text: 1.6 kg (3.5 lbs) boiled rice (flavored with chopped garlic and salt)
ingredients.name: rice

instructions: Boil chicken in salted water together with the stock cube. Remove bones and break into bite size pieces, keeping the resulting chicken stock.
In a saucepan, heat oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and finely chopped chili peppers and add salt and pepper. Fry this until the onions are cooked and golden.
Soak the bread in two cups of the stock from the boiled chicken and place in a blender for a couple of minutes and then add the resulting liquid to the saucepan.
Cook slowly for ten minutes, stirring to thicken.

While the Ají de Gallina is cooking slowly, boil the rice: first fry the garlic for a couple of seconds, then add the rice and the salt, then add the water. When the water starts to boil, let the rice cook in a closed pot very slowly for about 20 minutes or until the water has completely evaporated.

Back to the Ají de Gallina: add the chopped pecans, grated cheese, and chicken pieces. Cook until it has a thick creamy texture. About five minutes before serving, add the evaporated milk and continue cooking on low heat.
Serve over the boiled rice and garnish with halved potatoes, eggs quartered lengthwise, and olives.

name: Grilled Peaches with Vanilla Maple Sauce
description: Ripe yellow peaches are dipped in a warm vanilla-maple butter sauce, coated with sugar, and grilled until marked and slightly charred.

ingredients.text: 4 ripe yellow peaches, halved and pitted
ingredients.name: peach

instructions: Combine all ingredients except peaches and sugar. Bring to a boil over high heat in a large saucepan, and simmer until reduced by half.
Dip cut side of peaches into hot mixture. Sprinkle cut side liberally with sugar.
Place peaches cut-side down on a high-heat grill until marked and slightly charred.
Serve warm with remaining sauce.

name: Simple Roasted Oysters
description: A simple preparation of live oysters quickly heated in their shells until they open, then seasoned with salt and pepper.
instructions: Rinse the oysters in a colander and drain well.
Put the live oysters in the shell in a large sauté pan on medium-high heat and leave them till their shells open a little.
Take them off the heat, open them on a plate, and season with salt and pepper.

name: Chuck Wagon Beans
description: A hearty baked bean dish featuring browned bacon, ground chuck, onions, molasses, barbecue sauce, and warm spices.

ingredients.text: ½ pound bacon, cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: bacon

instructions: Brown bacon, ground chuck, and onion.
Stir in remaining ingredients in order; mix well in between each addition.
Bake at 350°F for about 40 minutes, or until thickened.

name: Steakhouse Dinner
description: Herb-grilled strip steaks brushed with olive oil and butter, cooked to a perfect medium rare, served with crispy roast potatoes and sautéed bell peppers for a steakhouse-quality dinner at home.

ingredients.text: 2 pounds redskin potatoes, cut into 2-inch cubes but left unpeeled
ingredients.name: redskin potato

ingredients.text: 4 assorted bell peppers, sliced into 3-inch strips
ingredients.name: bell pepper

ingredients.text: Few glasses red wine or cognac
ingredients.name: red wine

instructions: Set up a charcoal grill for direct and indirect heat.
Heat a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Shock potatoes in a bowl of ice water, drain, and pat very dry with paper towels.
Place potatoes on a cooling rack and let dry for 2 hours.
Combine remaining roast potatoes ingredients in a large stainless steel bowl. Add dry potatoes and toss to coat.
Place potatoes on a 13x9-inch baking pan and bake at 450°F for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the steaks: Brush steaks with extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper and rub herbs into flesh.
Grill steaks, covered, over direct heat, for 1¼ minutes, then rotate 90° and cook for another 1¼ minutes. Flip and repeat 1 more time.
Move steaks to indirect heat and cook, turning often, until internal temperature reaches 143°F for medium rare.
Remove to serving platters and top each with 1 tablespoon of the butter. Keep warm in a 200°F oven.
Meanwhile, heat a 10-inch straight-sided sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add oil and peppers to pan and cook, shaking the pan often, 8 minutes. Remove to serving platters.
Place potatoes on serving platters. Garnish with sprigs of rosemary, if desired. Serve.

name: Seafood Kebabs with Zhoug Sauce
description: Charcoal-grilled squid, prawn, and fish kebabs served with a rich, spicy zhoug sauce made from herbs, garlic, chilies, and toasted spices.

ingredients.text: ½ kg large prawns/shrimp, peeled and deveined
ingredients.name: prawn

ingredients.text: ½ kg fish fillets, cut into 2½ cm (1 in) cubes
ingredients.name: fish fillet

ingredients.text: ½ kg squid, cleaned and cut into 2½ cm (1 in) pieces
ingredients.name: squid

ingredients.text: 5 cloves garlic, peeled and finely chopped
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (180 ml) extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.name: olive oil

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (180 ml) dry white wine
ingredients.name: white wine

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 g) coriander leaves, washed, dried, and chopped
ingredients.name: coriander

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 g) parsley, washed, dried, and chopped
ingredients.name: parsley

ingredients.text: 8 jalapeños, seeded and chopped (adjust the quantity according to your heat tolerance)
ingredients.name: jalapeño

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (60 ml) extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.name: olive oil

instructions: Combine all the marinade ingredients in a nonreactive (glass or ceramic) mixing bowl. Add the seafood and mix to coat well. Refrigerate overnight.
Dry roast the cumin, caraway and cardamom seeds for 2–3 minutes in a cast iron skillet or wok over low heat. Cool, then add the peppercorns and pound in a mortar and pestle to a fine powder.
In a blender or food processor, blend the coriander, parsley, spices, garlic, chilli peppers and olive oil together with ½ cup water until a thick, smooth paste is formed.

Transfer the paste into a saucepan, heat until it starts bubbling, then reduce the heat and simmer, stirring constantly, until the water is evaporated. Cool, transfer to an airtight container and chill.
Remove the seafood from the marinade and drain in a colander. Save the marinade for basting the kebabs later. Thread the seafood onto skewers or satay sticks.
Char-grill the kebabs over hot coals, basting and turning every few minutes. It should take about 10 minutes to cook.
Serve with the zhoug sauce as a dipping sauce.

name: Figolli (Maltese Easter Pastries)
description: Sweet almond-filled Maltese Easter pastries, traditionally decorated with chocolate covering or decorative icing.
instructions: Sift the flour into a bowl, and rub in the margarine until the mixture returns to a powdery consistency.
In a separate container, mix the eggs and sugar until well blended.
Mix the orange zest into the egg and sugar.
Fold the egg mixture into the flour mixture.
If necessary mix in some water to help the mixture form a dough.
Add the water very carefully, drop by drop, as you will only need a little bit, and too much will ruin the pastry.
In a small skillet, gently heat the water and dissolve all the sugar into it.
Once the sugar has completely dissolved, bring the water to the boil, and immediately remove from the heat.
Stir the ground almonds into the hot sugar solution. Mix well until you get a paste-like filling.
Flour a clean surface, and roll out about a quarter of the dough with a rolling pin.
Cut two identical figolli shapes from the dough and remove the excess.
Spread about a quarter of the filling on one of the shapes. Leave a 1–2 cm border without any filling on it.
