Place the second identical shape on top of the first, making sure to align both shapes properly.
Press the edges of the two pieces of dough all around so they seal.
Wetting the fingers with some cold water can help if the 2 layers are difficult to combine.
Repeat the above steps for the other 3 figolli.
To bake, preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Place double layer of baking paper on a baking tray, and place the figolli gently on paper.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top turns golden and the edges start becoming dark (about 30 minutes).

name: Pasta Marinata
description: A simple Italian batter of semolina, eggs, and melted butter or olive oil, ideal for frying meat, fish, vegetables, or sweets.
instructions: Mix the semolina flour, egg yolks, a little salt, and melted butter.
Add the water so as to form a liquid substance.
Whip the egg whites to soft peaks, and fold into the batter.

name: Palatschinken (Czech/Austrian Crepes)
description: Thin, tender pancakes similar to French crêpes, made from a simple batter of milk, flour and eggs. A versatile dish that can be filled with sweet or savory fillings, rolled up, or cut into strips for broth.

ingredients.text: Mineral water (optional, makes the dough more fluffy)
ingredients.name: mineral water

instructions: Mix the flour with the milk, stirring thoroughly. Mix in the eggs one-by-one, then stir in the salt and rum. If desired, thin the batter with a bit of mineral water.
Heat the pan well. Add a drop of oil and rub it over the pan with a kitchen towel.

Ladle a dipperful of the batter into the pan, tilting the pan so that the batter spreads as evenly as possible over the whole pan. Alternatively, you can accomplish this by using a special wooden tool used to spread crêpes.
Let cook about 45 seconds to 1 minute until the top of the palatschinke is dry.
Flip the pancake over, and allow it to brown for about 30 seconds on the other side. Remove from the pan, and set aside.
Repeat the cooking process until you have used up all the batter.

name: Beurre à la Bourguignonne (Garlic Scallion Butter)
description: A garlic-forward compound butter with shallots and parsley, creamed until very soft.

ingredients.text: 1–3 cloves garlic, mashed or grated with a microplane
ingredients.name: garlic

instructions: Cream the butter until it is very soft.
Beat the shallots, garlic and parsley into the butter.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Atkins-Friendly Chocolate Mousse
description: A rich, low-carb chocolate mousse made with half and half, heavy cream, and chocolate shake mix, lightly sweetened with stevia extract.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 ml) or 1 part half and half
ingredients.name: half and half

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 ml) or 1 part heavy cream
ingredients.name: heavy cream

ingredients.text: 4 scoops or 1 part Atkins Chocolate Shake Mix
ingredients.name: chocolate shake mix

ingredients.text: 2 tsp or 1/24 part stevia extract or other sugar replacement
ingredients.name: stevia extract

instructions: Lightly whip half and half and cream in a blender.
Add other ingredients into blender.
Blend everything together until smooth and enjoy.

name: Roasted Redskin Potatoes
description: Tender red-skinned potatoes are boiled, then tossed with olive oil, garlic, and aromatic herbs before roasting until brown.
instructions: Put potatoes and bay leaves in a large Dutch oven. Put enough water to cover and bring to a rolling boil. Cook for 15 minutes or until tender.
Drain and shock. Drain again and discard bay leaves. Pat dry with paper towels.
Whisk together oil and remaining ingredients. Add potatoes and toss to coat.
Bake in a 425°F oven for 10 minutes or until lightly to deeply brown. Serve.

name: Homemade Coconut Milk
description: A creamy, lactose-free milk made by blending fresh coconut flesh with water and straining it through a fine mesh. It is a wonderful alternative to cow's milk for those who are lactose intolerant.
instructions: Crack open the coconuts and drain out the clear juice.
Use a knife to separate the coconut flesh from the pod. If necessary, rinse the coconut flesh under running water before cutting it into cubes.

Put the coconut flesh in a blender with the water, and process for a full minute at the maximum speed to create a smooth paste. If you don't have a blender, chop up the coconut flesh into manageable pieces, and grate them to a smooth paste.
Put the blended coconut in a bowl, add 1 cup of water, and combine with your hands.
Drain the milk by pouring the blended coconut milk through the fine mesh. To remove every drop of liquid from the sieve, press with your hand.
The coconut milk will be strained out when you add another cup of water and the coconut flesh back to the dish.
Use the coconut milk right away or store it in the refrigerator. Always shake the coconut milk thoroughly before using.

name: Sauteed Mushrooms
description: Garlicky morel mushrooms and onion are sautéed in olive oil and finished with pan juices, almost like a sauce for steak.
instructions: Sprinkle mushrooms and onion with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in large sauté pan over medium high heat.
Add garlic and cook 30–45 seconds.
Add remaining ingredients and cook for 7–10 more minutes.
Remove from pan and drizzle with pan juices. Serve.

name: Hutspot (Dutch Mashed Vegetables)
description: Hutspot is a hearty Dutch mash of potatoes, carrots, onions, and ham, enriched with butter and seasoned with cheese, salt, and pepper.

ingredients.text: Add cheese, salt, and pepper to your liking
ingredients.name: cheese

instructions: Cook the potatoes in a pan of water, adding salt to taste, until done. Drain.
Cook the carrots, onions, and ham, adding a small amount of salt, until the carrots are done. Drain, reserving the water from the carrot, onion, and ham pot.
Mash all the ingredients, adding enough of the reserved juices from the carrots to reach a mashed potato consistency.
Add 2 to 3 chunks of butter while mashing, to taste.

name: Basic Mayonnaise
description: Homemade mayonnaise made by whisking egg yolks with Dijon mustard, lemon juice or vinegar, and oil. Adding the oil slowly helps create a rich, creamy sauce.

ingredients.text: 2½ teaspoons (12.5 mL) lemon juice and/or vinegar
ingredients.name: lemon juice or vinegar

instructions: In a large bowl, beat the egg yolk with a wire whisk for about a minute.
Then add the mustard, salt, and half the lemon juice. Whisk for another minute - the mixture should thicken very slightly.

Then, very slowly, add half the oil with one hand whilst whisking with the other. Start drop by drop, incorporating each drop before adding the next, and build up to a trickle. Keep going until the oil is whisked in.
Add the rest of the lemon juice and whisk to combine.
Add the rest of the oil in the same manner as before. Keep going until all the oil is whisked in.
If desired, stir in flavourings such as crushed garlic, or use the mayonnaise as a base for other sauces.

name: Colonial Goose
description: A New Zealand classic made from a carefully boned leg of mutton stuffed with honey, dried apricots and breadcrumbs, then marinated in red wine and baked. The strained marinade liquor is used to make gravy for the carved meat.

ingredients.text: 125 g (½ cup) dried apricots, finely diced
ingredients.name: apricot

ingredients.text: 1 not-quite-full cup of red wine such as claret
ingredients.name: red wine

instructions: To prepare the stuffing, melt the butter and honey over low heat, add the other ingredients, and combine well.
Force the stuffing into the cavity in the meat, and sew it up with fine string.
Combine all marinade ingredients.
Place the leg into a plastic bag in a large bowl, and add the marinade mixture to the bag. Let marinate for 8 hours.
Bake mutton in oven at 180 °C for 2 hours, checking on progress at 90 minutes. If the meat looks like it is over-browning, it can be covered by foil.
Remove the string before carving.
Strain the marinade and use 3–4 tablespoons of the liquor to make gravy.

name: Biscuit Cake
description: A traditional 18th century cake made by creaming eggs, butter, and sugar, then folding in flour, nutmeg, and caraway seeds for a richly spiced treat.

ingredients.text: 1 pound butter, softened and cut in pieces
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Beat together the eggs, butter, and sugar until very creamy.
Combine the flour, nutmeg, and caraway seeds.
Add the dry mixture to the egg mixture, and beat for 1 hour.
Transfer to a pan, and bake for 1 hour.
Let cool and unmold.

name: Grilled Salmon with Mango Salsa
description: Grilled wild salmon pairs with a bright mango salsa flavored with lime, jalapeño, mint, and honey.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24 ounces) wild salmon fillets with skin on one side
ingredients.name: salmon fillet

ingredients.text: 1 large mango, peeled and finely diced
ingredients.name: mango

instructions: First, make the salsa. In a large bowl, combine mango, lime juice, jalapeños, mint, honey, and sea salt. Refrigerate until needed.
Heat about 28 charcoal briquets in a large chimney starter. Once hot, disperse evenly around the bottom of a grill. Reapply the grate.
Quickly grease the grate with the oil-soaked towel.
Brush salmon liberally with olive oil. Sprinkle liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Place salmon on grill, skin side down, and cook, covered, turning often, until fish is pink throughout and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Move to a plate and cover with aluminum foil.
Let rest 5–7 minutes before serving with salsa.

name: Muboora (Zimbabwean Pumpkin Leaves Stew)
description: A rich Zimbabwean stew made from tender pumpkin leaves, tomatoes, onions, garlic, and peanut butter, simmered into a creamy, flavorful dish.
instructions: Wash the pumpkin leaves thoroughly and remove any tough stems or veins. Chop the leaves into small pieces and set them aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat. Add the onions and garlic. Sauté until they become translucent and fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and curry powder to the pot. Cook until the tomatoes break down and form a thick sauce, stirring occasionally.

Reduce the heat to low. Gradually spoon in the peanut butter, stirring continuously. Continue stirring until the peanut butter is well blended with the tomato sauce. This should create a creamy, thick mixture.

Start adding the chopped pumpkin leaves to the pot in batches. Stir and allow each batch to wilt and mix with the sauce before adding more. Continue this process until all the pumpkin leaves are in the pot.
Pour in enough water to cover the mixture, making it into a stew-like consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir everything together, ensuring the leaves are submerged.

Cover the pot and let the muboora simmer on low heat for about 20–30 minutes. Stir occasionally and check for desired tenderness of the pumpkin leaves. Add more water if necessary to maintain the desired consistency.
Once the pumpkin leaves are tender and the flavors are well blended, your muboora is ready to be served.

name: Pan-Fried White Brined Cheese (Saganaki)
description: A traditional Greek dish of salty brined white cheese pan-fried in olive oil until lightly crusted, served with a squeeze of lemon. A simple, classic meze to start a meal.

ingredients.text: 1 large slice of salty, brined white cheese (e.g. feta, sirene)
ingredients.name: white brined cheese

instructions: Heat a small frying pan over medium-high heat.

While the pan heats, cut the cheese into slices of the desired size and thickness. Thicker slices will take longer to melt through and may result in burning, while thinner ones will have less chance to brown.

Optionally, dredge the slices in flour—this will create a darker and slightly crispier crust, but is an optional step as the cheese will acquire a very slight crust on its own by virtue of the oil and high heat. It will also reduce the spitting somewhat.
Add the oil to the hot pan and swirl it around. When the oil shimmers and seems to become more fluid, it is ready. Add the cheese and step back—it will spit due to the brine-water on the cheese.
Flip the cheese after a minute or two. A slice of ¾ centimeter should get about 1–2 minutes per side.
Serve immediately, with lemon and (optionally) bread.

name: Jambalaya I
description: A classic Creole Jambalaya from New Orleans featuring turkey, rice, tomatoes, and aromatic spices simmered together in one pan. This simple, hearty one-pot meal brings the flavors of Louisiana to your table.

ingredients.text: 14.5 ounces (411 g) canned tomatoes, diced or torn apart
ingredients.name: canned tomato

ingredients.text: 2 cups cooked and chopped turkey or chicken
ingredients.name: turkey

ingredients.text: 1 small can of sliced mushrooms (optional), drained
ingredients.name: mushroom

instructions: Mix the salt, savory, basil, thyme, and cumin together, then grind them to a powder.
Prepare the canned tomatoes: tear them up, remove the stem ends, remove the seeds, etc. Keep the juice.
Heat a wide pan with a lid. Lightly fry the celery in the butter. Soften the celery but do not brown it.
Add everything to the pan. You can add the basil, meat, and mushrooms later if you prefer.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for about 20 minutes. The rice will absorb the liquid.
Discard the bay leaf.

name: Snails with Garlic Butter (Escargots à la Bourguignonne)
description: A French dish of snails with garlic butter, parsley, and shallots, served with French bread for soaking up the garlic butter.

ingredients.text: 24 snail shells, with snail serving dishes, and snail tongs OR 4 glazed indented earthenware snail serving dishes OR 24 small mushroom caps, trimmed and de-gilled
ingredients.name: snail shell

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Drain and rinse the snails.
Combine the butter with the shallots, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper, and blend well.
Sauté the mushroom caps, if using, in a small amount of garlic butter until cooked but still firm. Remove from the heat.
If using snail shells, place a snail in each shell and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter.
If using a snail dish without the shells, place a snail in each indentation and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter.
If using mushroom caps, place 2–3 snails in each cap and top with a generous amount of garlic butter.
Heat the snails in the oven for 5–7 minutes, and serve with copious quantities of French bread for soaking up the garlic butter.

name: Gambian Chicken with Lemon and Mustard (Yassa)
description: A tangy and flavorful Gambian dish featuring chicken or fish marinated in a zesty blend of onions, lemons, and Dijon mustard, then browned and simmered to perfection.

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves (or 1 teaspoon of dried thyme)
ingredients.name: thyme

ingredients.text: 500 g chicken or fish, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: chicken

instructions: In a large bowl, combine the sliced onions, lemon juice, vegetable oil, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, thyme leaves, paprika, black pepper, and salt to make a marinade.

Add the chicken or fish pieces to the marinade and mix well to ensure they are evenly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to develop.
Remove the chicken or fish from the marinade, reserving the marinade for later use.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken or fish to the hot skillet and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the sliced onions from the marinade and sauté until they become soft and translucent.

Return the cooked chicken or fish to the skillet with the sautéed onions. Pour the reserved marinade over the meat and onions. Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer for about 15–20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Serve hot with steamed rice, couscous, or bread.

name: Tuna Casserole
description: A comforting tuna casserole combines egg noodles, peas, carrots, corn, and cream soups, then bakes beneath a fried onion topping until lightly browned.

ingredients.text: 1 can each of cream of celery soup, cream of chicken soup, and cream of mushroom soup (substitute cream of potato if you don't like mushrooms)
ingredients.name: cream soup

ingredients.text: 1 bag of frozen vegetables (peas, carrots, and corn)
ingredients.name: frozen vegetables

ingredients.text: 1 can of fried onion rings, 1 packet potato chips, or 1 small packet corn flakes
ingredients.name: topping

instructions: Cook egg noodles as directed on package.
While boiling water, preheat oven to 400°F.
Drain egg noodles. Mix together all ingredients except fried onion rings.
Put in a casserole dish or a 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle fried onion topping on top of baked casserole.
Bake for an additional 3 minutes, or until fried onion is slightly brown.
Let cool for 5 minutes and serve.

name: Acorn Squash with Orange Marmalade
description: A quick and easy vegetable side dish featuring tender baked acorn squash topped with a sweet orange marmalade and butter glaze, lightly broiled for a golden finish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C).
Remove seeds and strings from squash halves.
Cut a small piece off the outside of each half to make a flat space on which the half can stand level.
Place halves in a shallow pan or casserole in ¼ inch (6 mm) water with insides facing down. Bake for 35 minutes.
Combine marmalade and butter in a small bowl.
Remove squash from oven, and invert in pan or dish. Salt lightly.
Spread marmalade and butter mixture on edges of squash, allowing excess to run into center.
Place under broiler for 5 minutes or until lightly browned.

name: Chraime (Sephardic Fish and Vegetable Casserole)
description: A traditional Sephardic Jewish casserole layering potatoes, bell peppers, and white fish fillets with garlic, jalapeño, tomatoes, and sweet paprika, simmered until tender. Often served as a first course at Rosh Hashanah with challah.

ingredients.text: 2 medium red bell peppers, cored, seeded, and cut into ½-inch thick wedges
ingredients.name: red bell pepper

ingredients.text: 1 small jalapeño or other hot chili pepper, quartered and seeded
ingredients.name: jalapeño pepper

ingredients.text: 1¼–1½ pounds of white fish fillets (e.g. sole, halibut, or cod)
ingredients.name: white fish fillet

ingredients.text: 1 cup chopped fresh cilantro or parsley
ingredients.name: cilantro

instructions: In a large flame-proof casserole or Dutch oven, set the potato slices on the bottom. Scatter the bell peppers, garlic, and jalapeño pepper on the potatoes. Sprinkle with salt.
Place the fish on top and sprinkle it with paprika and salt. Add the tomatoes and cilantro or parsley.
Pour the water in at the edges. Sprinkle the top with oil and sprinkle generously with salt.

Set the pan over high heat, cover, and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce the heat slightly and simmer for 25–30 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the fish is cooked through. Check the pan after 20 minutes; if there seems to be too much liquid, uncover the pan for the remaining cooking time.
Serve hot or warm with challah.

name: Tri-Colored Autumn Rice Balls
description: Sweet Japanese rice balls filled with chilled bean paste and coated with sesame-sugar or roasted soybean powder. A simple autumn tea sweet inspired by the autumn equinox celebration.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup toasted black sesame seeds, lightly crushed
ingredients.name: black sesame seeds

ingredients.text: 1 cup smooth Japanese bean paste (koshi-an), chilled
ingredients.name: Japanese bean paste

ingredients.text: ½ cup roasted soybean powder (kinako) or toasted ground pecans
ingredients.name: roasted soybean powder

instructions: Mix sesame seeds and sugar in a small bowl.
Moisten your hands with water and divide warm rice into 12 equal portions.
Shape 4 portions into balls. Moisten a clean dish towel and squeeze it dry.
Place 2½ tablespoons bean paste on towel; pat into a 4-inch circle.
Place 1 rice ball in the centre of the bean paste circle and use towel to mould bean paste around the rice ball.
Repeat this 3 more times, using another ½ cup of bean paste and the other 3 rice balls.
Place these on a nice serving tray. Flatten the remaining eight rice portions.
Form the remaining bean paste into 8 balls (about 2 teaspoons per ball). Place a bean paste ball in the centre of each piece of flattened rice and shape the rice around it.
Mould these stuffed rice balls into oval shapes. Roll 4 ovals in the sesame-sugar mixture. Roll the other 4 balls in the roasted soybean powder. Add these to the serving tray.

name: Lo Mein
description: A quick, flexible lo mein of stir-fried meat and vegetables tossed with lo mein noodles and soy sauce. A popular combination is pork with water chestnuts and asparagus.

ingredients.text: 1 part stir fry meat (e.g. pork, beef, shrimp)
ingredients.name: meat

ingredients.text: 1 part stir fry vegetables (e.g. water chestnuts, asparagus, broccoli, squash, bamboo shoots)
ingredients.name: vegetable

ingredients.text: Enough soy sauce to heavily coat all the ingredients
ingredients.name: soy sauce

ingredients.text: Enough olive oil to coat a skillet
ingredients.name: olive oil

instructions: Cook noodles in a pot according to the package directions.
Coat a skillet with olive oil and place on stove with medium to low heat. Add garlic if desired, but don't let it burn.
Add meat and vegetables to skillet, season with salt and pepper, lightly coat with soy sauce, and cook everything until it's done (about 8–10 minutes).
If using, add bean sprouts right before everything is finished cooking, and cook them until they turn mildly translucent.
Strain noodles and add them to the stir fry.
Coat with soy sauce and cook for roughly 1 minute in order to sear in the flavor.

name: Idli (Steamed Rice and Black Gram Bread)
description: Round, fluffy idlis made from fermented rice and urad dal with fenugreek and salt, traditionally served with sambar.

ingredients.text: 2 cups chlorine-free water for fermenting (see note)
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Wash rice and urad dal thoroughly.

Soak the rice and urad dal in separate bowls for no more than 2 hours. Soak methi seeds along with the urad dal. You will need about twice as much water in the bowl as urad dal, as it expands as it soaks up water.
Drain the rice and urad dal. Do not discard the dal soaking water, but do discard the rice soaking water.
Grind the urad dal to a fine paste in a blender. If needed, add some of the reserved soaking water.
Grind the rice to a paste with about 1 cup of chlorine-free water (less if you can). Grind coarsely if the batter will only be used for idli, but grind finely if it will later be used for dosa.
Mix the rice and urad dal pastes together well, and season with salt.
If desired, stir in the fermentation starter and mix well (see note).
Set aside somewhere warm to ferment for 8 hours (see note).
Grease one or more idli pans well with ghee or vegetable oil.
Gently spoon the batter into the round indentations of the idli pans. Do not stir or otherwise break the batter. The trapped bubbles should not escape, as they are necessary for a fluffy texture.
Steam for 12 minutes in a steamer (16 minutes if using brown rice).
Remove idli from pans with a sharp knife or thin spatula.

name: Italian Tomato Sauce
description: A simple, savory tomato sauce made with tomato paste, garlic, and a blend of herbs and Italian seasoning.
instructions: Combine all ingredients.

name: Nigerian Fruit Skewer
description: A typical Nigerian snack made by threading chunks of assorted fruit onto skewers.
instructions: Cut all the fruit into small chunks.
Thread the fruit chunks onto a skewer.

name: Ghormeh Sabzi (Iranian Herb Stew)
description: A popular Persian herb stew made with meat, beans, fresh herbs and dried limes, slow-cooked until the meat is fork-tender. It is served with plain and saffron-coloured rice.

ingredients.text: 800 g beef or lamb which has some fat (such as the meat for boiled beef)
ingredients.name: beef or lamb

ingredients.text: 1 can (about 400 g) fried ghormeh sabzi herbs
ingredients.name: ghormeh sabzi herbs

instructions: Boil the red beans for 1 hour.
Remove unnecessary fat from the meat, and cut the meat into smaller pieces.
Heat a bit of normal olive oil in a big pot with lid. Add the onions, and fry at high temperature for 1–2 minutes.
Stir in the meat, and cook for another 1–2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to the lowest level. The meat will release a significant amount of juice which will contribute to the flavor of the stew.
Stir in the parsley, spinach, coriander leaves, and ghormeh sabzi herbs.
Stir in boiling water (about 0.5 L or until the consistency is right).
Stir in the cooked, drained beans. Simmer for about ½–3 hours over low heat. The longer the better.
Soak the dried limes in hot water for 15 minutes, and puncture each of them with a fork.
Add the dried limes, turmeric, pepper, and salt to the stew. Simmer for another ½–1 hour.
If desired, for the best taste, let the stew cool down and store it in a fridge. The taste is better over the next two days.
Steam the rice.
Grind the saffron and sugar together in a mortar. Add about 1 tablespoon boiling water. Toss some of the cooked rice with the saffron water to color it.
Serve the stew hot in its own bowl. Serve the plain rice in a separate bowl, topped with the saffron rice.

name: Murghi Korma (Chicken Korma)
description: A mild Indian chicken korma marinated with yogurt and aromatic spices, then simmered in a creamy coconut and single-cream sauce. Finished with saffron, rosewater, and toasted almonds.

ingredients.text: Whole chicken, skinned and cut into medium pieces; ideally into 6 pieces if using baby chicken
ingredients.name: whole chicken

ingredients.text: Black pepper, crushed, according to taste
ingredients.name: black pepper

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp toasted flakes of almonds for decoration (optional)
ingredients.name: almond

instructions: Combine the chicken with all the marinade ingredients, cover the bowl with cling film, and leave in the fridge to marinate for 1–3 hours.
Fry the onions in ghee until it starts to turn brown but still soft. Do not fry to crispiness. Take out the onion with slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the marinated chicken to the hot ghee and cook over medium heat.
Dry toast the whole spices in a hot frying pan for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add the whole spices and black pepper to the chicken.
Stir occasionally and cook covered.
When water starts to separate from the chicken, add coconut cream, salt and sugar.
Add boiling water if chicken starts to dry up before its cooked.
Warm the single cream in microwave and add saffron to it.
Stir in cream when almost cooked.
Remove from the heat, and serve with fried onions, rose water, and almonds.

name: Mince Pie Tartlets with Pork
description: Golden shortcrust tartlets filled with citrus-spiced fruit mince and browned pork.

ingredients.text: 800 g cored and sliced apples (from about 12 large apples)s
ingredients.name: apple

instructions: Preheat oven to 150 °C (300 °F).
In a pot, bring the sugar, wine, cider, orange, and lemon juice to a simmer. Add mace, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Split the vanilla pod and scrape seeds into the pot. Discard the vanilla pod.
Stir in sliced apples and fruit mix.
Grease the muffin tins and line with pastry dough to make tartlet cases. Trim to fit.
Place cases into the oven and bake until lightly golden. Remove from the oven and let cool.
Melt butter in a pan. Add minced pork and sauté until browned.
Remove the cinnamon stick from the fruit mixture and mix in the pork.
Using a tablespoon, fill tartlet cases with the filling—it will probably be mounded.
If desired, trim with excess pastry.
Bake each tray at 120 °C (250 °F) for half an hour.

name: Sudanese Ful Medames
description: A traditional Sudanese breakfast and light meal made with tender fava beans seasoned with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and coriander. Serve it warm or at room temperature with fresh toppings.

ingredients.text: Optional toppings: chopped parsley, diced tomatoes, chopped onions, hard-boiled eggs, feta cheese
ingredients.name: toppings

instructions: Rinse the dried fava beans under cold water and place them in a large pot. Add 4 cups of water and let the beans soak overnight, or for at least 8 hours, to soften the beans and reduce the cooking time.
Drain the soaked fava beans and rinse them under cold water. Return them to the pot, add 4 cups of fresh water, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the beans for about 1–1½ hours, or until tender. Stir occasionally and skim off any foam that forms on the surface.
Drain the tender beans using a colander or strainer and transfer them to a mixing bowl.
Add the minced garlic, extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt. Mix everything together, ensuring the beans are coated evenly with the seasoning.
For a smoother consistency, lightly mash some of the beans with a fork or potato masher. Adjust the amount to your preference.

Transfer the seasoned ful medames to a serving dish. Serve warm or at room temperature with optional toppings such as chopped parsley, diced tomatoes, chopped onions, hard-boiled eggs, or crumbled feta cheese. It is commonly served with bread or as a side dish alongside other Sudanese specialties.

name: Sylheti Beef Curry
description: A rich and aromatic beef curry from the Sylhet region, slow-simmered with whole spices, ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and the distinctive citrus fruit hatxora for a tangy depth of flavor.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon chile powder (adjust to taste)
ingredients.name: chile powder

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add the cloves, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves. Sauté for a minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until they turn golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add the beef cubes and cook until they are browned on all sides.
Stir in the cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and chili powder. Cook for a couple of minutes to toast the spices.
Add the hatxora, chopped tomatoes and green chilies. Cook until the tomatoes are soft and the oil starts to separate from the mixture.
Pour in enough water to cover the beef, season with salt, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let the curry simmer for about 1.5–2 hours or until the beef is tender and the flavors meld.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice or naan.

name: Obe Eja Kika (Nigerian Smoked Fish Stew)
description: A hearty Nigerian stew of smoked hake fish simmered in a rich blend of tomatoes, peppers, onions, and palm oil, finished with aromatic scent leaf.
instructions: Coarsely grind the tomatoes, habanero pepper, tatashe, green bell peppers, and onions.
Heat the palm oil and vegetable oil in a pot. Add the ground pepper mix, and cook, stirring, for about 10–15 minutes.
Stir in the fish seasoning powder, shrimp powder, salt, and stock cube. Add the panla fish, and stir.
Add some water to loosen up the stew, stir, and simmer for 10–15 minutes on low heat.
Stir in the scent leaf, and remove from the heat.
Serve with rice, pasta, or boiled yam.

name: Mango Coconut Sticky Rice
description: A sticky rice dessert prepared with coconut milk, coconut water, pandan leaves, mango, and young coconut meat. Brown sugar adds sweetness to the coconut-rich dish.

ingredients.text: 2 cups uncooked sticky rice, rinsed well
ingredients.name: sticky rice

instructions: Bring coconut milk to a boil with pandan leaves. Add a little salt to taste.
Stir in the coconut water. Stir in the sticky rice, and simmer about 15 minutes over low heat.
Stir in the mango, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add sugar and stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Add the coconut meat.
Serve.

name: Liberian Meat Sauce
description: A hearty, savory Liberian meat sauce made with tender pieces of meat and simmered in a rich tomato-based sauce. This versatile sauce pairs well with rice, pasta, or other starches.

ingredients.text: 1 pound meat (beef, chicken, or fish), cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: meat

instructions: Heat the palm oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until the onion is softened and translucent.
Add the meat and cook until browned and thoroughly cooked through.
Stir in the chicken broth or water, tomato, bell pepper, cayenne pepper, and hot pepper, if using.
Simmer for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the flavors blend.
Serve hot with rice, pasta, or another starch.

name: Alicha Wot (Mild Ethiopian Stew)
description: A mild and flavorful Ethiopian beef stew seasoned with aromatic berbere spices, garlic, ginger, and warming spices. Slow-simmered until the beef is tender and the flavors have melded together.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon salt, or to taste
ingredients.name: salt

ingredients.text: Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped, for garnish
ingredients.name: cilantro

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions to the pot and sauté until they become translucent and slightly browned.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot and sauté for an additional minute until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, tomato paste, ground turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine the spices with the onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add the beef to the pot and stir to coat it with the spice mixture. Cook the beef for a few minutes until it is browned on all sides.
Pour in the beef broth or water, ensuring that the beef is fully submerged in the liquid. Bring the mixture to a boil.

Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the beef is tender and the flavors have melded together. Stir occasionally and add more liquid if needed to maintain the desired consistency.
Taste the stew and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve hot with injera or bread.

name: Creamy Cornstarch Scrambled Eggs
description: Tender, creamy scrambled eggs made with a cornstarch and milk slurry for a silky texture, cooked in sizzling butter and finished with black pepper.
instructions: In a cup, whisk together the milk and cornstarch until it is free of lumps.
Add the cornstarch mixture to your eggs, and beat until smooth. Season with salt.
Heat a non-stick skillet over high heat until hot, then add the butter—it should sizzle right away.
Wait until the butter's melted and bubbly, but before it browns. Add the beaten eggs. Wait without stirring anything, until the edges of the eggs start to bubble up (about 3 seconds).

Remove the skillet from the heat. Start stirring the eggs, making 1 full circle per second, for about 11–12 seconds. The eggs will have absorbed all the butter but remain partially undercooked. Do not wait until they look fully cooked!
Transfer them onto a plate.
Season with black pepper to taste and serve.

name: Spring Onion Spelt Spread
description: A vegan spread made primarily with tofu, oat flakes and raw spelt flour, combined with spring onions, pickled gherkins and seasoning.

ingredients.text: 3 or more whole spring onions, chopped
ingredients.name: spring onion

ingredients.text: Rapeseed oil or other vegetable oil
ingredients.name: rapeseed oil

instructions: Combine tofu, oat flakes, raw spelt, and some water.
If desired, mix in the lecithin to act as an emulsifier.
Mix in the spring onion and gherkins.
Mix in a spoonful of margarine and/or rapeseed oil.
Add salt and pepper to taste.

name: Firecracker Marinade
description: A fiery habanero-based marinade blended smooth with citrus, garlic, white wine, butter, and olive oil. A bold, spicy kick for grilled meats or vegetables.
instructions: Run everything in a blender until smooth.
Keep refrigerated for up to 1 ½ weeks.
Shake well before using.

name: Welsh Rarebit
description: A classic British dish featuring a rich, creamy sauce of Cheddar cheese, beer, and cream, served over crisp toast.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: black pepper

ingredients.text: 2 fl oz (60 ml) beer such as porter (Guinness will do)
ingredients.name: beer

instructions: In a medium saucepan over low heat, melt the butter and whisk in the flour.
Cook, whisking constantly for 2–3 minutes, being careful not to brown the flour.
Whisk in mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Add beer and whisk to combine.
Pour in cream and whisk until well combined and smooth.
Gradually add cheese, stirring constantly, until cheese melts and sauce is smooth; this will take 4–5 minutes.
Pour over toast and serve immediately.

name: Salt Cod and Potato Casserole (Bacalhau à Zé do Pipo)
description: A traditional Portuguese cod casserole layered with mashed potatoes, olives, and fried onions, then topped with mayonnaise and bread crumbs and baked until toasted.

ingredients.text: 500 g (18 oz / 1.1 lbs) white or golden potatoes
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 400 g (14 oz / 0.9 lb) salted dried cod
ingredients.name: salted dried cod

ingredients.text: 200 g (7 oz / ½ lb) of onions
ingredients.name: onion

instructions: Roast the potatoes in the oven until tender. Cool slightly.
Mash the potatoes, mixing in the milk, pepper, lemon juice, and eggs, if using.
Mix in the olives. Season with salt to taste.
Prepare the cod by leaving it for 24 hours in water, changing the water once or twice.
After the 24 hour period is up, put the cod in a pot with milk.
Boil the cod until slightly cooked, then season with salt and pepper. The milk will make the fish soft.
Slice the onions into rings, and fry in pan with garlic and lots of olive oil until slightly browned.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Place the cod in the center of a casserole or baking dish.
Surround the fish with 500 g of the mashed potatoes, then top it with the fried onion.
Cover the onion with a thick layer of mayonnaise, and sprinkle bread crumbs all over.
Bake until toasted on top.
Serve with a green wine from the north of Portugal.

name: Date Smoothie
description: A date milkshake is a delicious and refreshing beverage.
instructions: Soak the dates in water for a few minutes to soften the tough texture. Drain.
Place the soaked dates in the blender, and add a small amount of water.
Add cinnamon, sugar to taste, and ice.
Turn on the blender until smooth.

name: Kurma (Trinidadian Fried Dough in Syrup)
description: A sweet Trinidadian fried dough coated in a clear sugar syrup, with ginger, cinnamon, and coconut cream in the dough.

ingredients.text: ⅔ tin (1 ¼ cups) sweetened condensed milk
ingredients.name: sweetened condensed milk

instructions: Mix flour, ginger, cinnamon, and butter in a large bowl.
Mix evaporated milk, coconut cream, condensed milk, and Angostura bitters in a separate bowl.
Pour the liquid mixture into the mixture of dry ingredients a little bit at a time. Mix until a dough forms. The dough should be "tough;" that is, not stretchy.
Divide the dough into two balls. This makes it more manageable. Roll each ball out until about 1 cm thick.
Cut dough into strips.
Heat ½ cup of oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry batches of the kurma dough in the oil, turning often.
Remove when golden brown on all sides.
Heat sugar and water over medium heat.
Stir so that sugar is completely wet.
When the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is clear, remove from heat.
Pour over kurma, and stir quickly to coat evenly.

name: Kale and Garlic Pasta
description: Blanched kale and garlic are cooked until tender, then tossed with linguine, chili flakes, and melted Parmesan. The slow cooking softens the greens and reduces their bitterness.

ingredients.text: 1 head garlic, cloves peeled and sliced thin
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: 1–2 bunches kale, deboned and cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: kale

instructions: Add butter and olive oil to a large frying pan. Heat over medium heat until the butter melts.
Add the garlic and chili flakes to the pan. Cook, stirring, until the garlic is softened. If the garlic starts to brown, turn off the heat until time to add the kale.
Cook the kale in a large pot of very salty boiling water for about 4 minutes. It will turn bright green.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the softened kale to the pan with the garlic. Try to leave as much water behind as possible.

Cook the kale and garlic over medium heat, stirring, until most or all of the liquid evaporates. The greens should become very dark and soft. Add a splash of water or olive oil if they stick to the pan too much.
Boil the pasta in the same salted water as the kale. When al dente, use tongs to transfer the pasta to the hot pan with the greens.
Toss the pasta and greens together. If the pan is too small, transfer everything to a large bowl and continue tossing until the pasta is well-coated.
Add the grated Parmesan, and continue tossing until it is melted and well-incorporated.
Serve hot.

name: Tempe Mendoan I
description: A deliciously piquant dish of thin tempeh coated in a seasoned rice-and-wheat batter and fried until hardened and well done. Traditionally from the Banyumas territory, tempeh is sliced very thin and wide.
instructions: Combine rice flour, wheat flour, garlic, shallot, coriander, pepper, salt, water, and green onion to make a thin batter.
Dip each piece of tempeh into the batter, and coat entirely.
Warm the oil in a frying pan, and put it on the stove until hot. Put each piece of coated tempeh into hot oil.
Fry the tempeh until hardened and well done. Don't wait until it becomes yellow and crispy.
Remove the tempeh from the oil, letting the oil drip from the tempeh so that there is not much oil on it.
Serve tempeh with soy bean sauce and sliced small chilies.

name: Grotten Hans (Steamed Sweet Bread)
description: A traditional steamed sweet pudding from the German areas of Russia, served with a sweet raisin sauce flavored with cinnamon and lemon.
instructions: Cream together lard, sugar and salt. Mix in eggs.
Combine flour and baking powder. Add this flour mixture to the lard mixture alternatively with the milk. Mix well.
Pour batter into a well-greased 2-pound coffee can or other heat-safe mold.
Place a piece of parchment paper on the bottom of the can to prevent sticking. Cover with foil, and tie this on with a string.
Set this tin into a large pot of hot water a few inches (~3) deep. Let steam for 2 hours.
Mix raisins, water, lemon juice, cinnamon and sugar in a saucepan. Simmer for 1 hour.
Mix in a bit of cornstarch, and cook until thickened.
Unmold the grotten hans, and serve with the sauce.

name: Kaiserschmarrn (Austrian Shredded Pancake)
description: A traditional Austrian shredded pancake made with eggs, milk, flour, and raisins, then cooked in butter and dusted with icing sugar.
instructions: Separate the whites from the yolks.
Put yolks, milk, sugar and salt in a bowl and whip well.
Fold in the flour while stirring thoroughly until the mass is pasty.
Add the raisins to the mixture.
Whisk the whites until they are stiff and then fold them into the mixture.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, and add the dough.
Cook until the pancake gets solid at the bottom.
Divide the mass into quarters with a wooden spoon or spatula and turn them over.
After a little while start scrambling the quarters.
Keep turning the Kaiserschmarrn until it is done.
Serve with icing sugar on top.

name: Sesame Noodle Salad
description: A refreshing chilled noodle salad tossed with sesame oil, fresh cilantro, scallions, and thinly sliced carrots.

ingredients.text: 1 cup or more finely-chopped fresh cilantro
ingredients.name: cilantro

instructions: Cook angel hair pasta according to package instructions, then drain.
Add sesame oil, olive oil, and salt (to taste) to drained pasta.
Toss in cilantro, scallions, and carrots.
Chill before serving.

name: Orange Chocolate Chip Muffins
description: Chocolate chip muffins made with orange juice and orange rind, with a blend of milk and white chocolate chips.
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (350°F).
Sift flour into bowl, then rub in butter.
Add sugar, chocolate bits, eggs, milk, orange juice, and orange rind.
Mix well.
Spoon heaped tablespoons of mixture into greased muffin pans.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until cooked through.

name: Cheese Ravioli Filling
description: A simple ricotta or cottage cheese filling with Parmigiano Reggiano, finely chopped onion, egg, and salt for homemade ravioli.
instructions: Stir all the ingredients together in a bowl.
Set aside while you roll the dough.

name: Nigerian Beans and Yam
description: A hearty Nigerian lunch dish of dried beans and yam simmered with onion, stock cube, and palm oil.

ingredients.text: Yam, peeled and cut into chunks
ingredients.name: yam

instructions: Wash and drain the beans, then transfer to a pot with the onion, stock cube, salt, and pepper.
Add enough water to cover everything in the pot. Boil until the beans are almost soft.
Add the yam, and boil until the yam and beans are soft.
Stir in the palm oil, and cook for another 3 minutes.
Serve.

name: Isombe na Kariyo (Cassava Leaves with Pumpkin)
description: A flavorful Rwandan dish of tender cassava leaves cooked until tender and mixed with sautéed pumpkin, onion, and garlic.
instructions: Remove the tough stems from the cassava leaves, and wash them thoroughly under running water. Chop the leaves into smaller pieces.
In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion is translucent and fragrant.
Add the diced pumpkin to the pot and cook for about 5 minutes, until it begins to soften.
Add the chopped cassava leaves to the pot and stir well to combine with the pumpkin and onion mixture.
Pour in the water and season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir again to distribute the ingredients evenly.
Cover the pot and let the mixture simmer for about 30–40 minutes, or until the cassava leaves are tender.
Stir occasionally during cooking, and add more water if needed to prevent sticking and to achieve the desired consistency.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Remove from heat and transfer to a serving dish.
Serve hot as a main course or as a side dish with Rwandan staples like ugali or steamed rice.

name: Amala (Yoruba Yam Swallow)
description: A traditional Nigerian swallow made from yam flour, native to the Yoruba people. It is stirred into boiling water to form a smooth, stretchy dough and served alongside hearty soups.
instructions: Heat water in a pot and bring to boil.
Pour and stir the yam flour, mixing continuously to avoid lumps.
Adjust the amount of water or yam flour to get your desired consistency.
Stir well, cover, and cook for about 10 minutes.
Serve with soups.

name: Flammekueche (Bacon and Onion Flatbread)
description: A traditional Alsatian flatbread with a thin yeast crust topped with crème fraîche, caramelized onions, and bacon, baked in a very hot oven until bubbly and lightly browned.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup moderately hot water, about 110 °F (45 °C)
ingredients.name: water

ingredients.text: 1 medium (3 oz / 85 g) onion, finely chopped
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: 1 cup crème fraîche, commercial or home made (see note)
ingredients.name: crème fraîche

instructions: Mix the starter ingredients together in a small bowl, cover tightly, and set aside in a warm place for 30 minutes.
When the starter is light and bubbly, mix the beer and milk into the mixture.

Put the flour and salt into a food processor, then, with the motor running, add the yeast mixture through the feeding tube. Process the dough until it forms a ball, then process until it is smooth, elastic, and warm, about 45 seconds to 1 minute. Add very small amounts of additional flour or milk if necessary.
Butter a medium-sized bowl, roll the ball around in the butter, then cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled. Punch down and let rise a second time.
While the dough is rising, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a nonstick skillet. Add the onion and cook, stirring, over low heat for 5 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool.
Combine the crème fraîche, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Add the cooled onion.
Heat the remaining oil in the skillet and fry the bacon until lightly browned, stirring constantly. Remove and drain through a strainer.
Preheat the oven to 450 °F (220 °C) or as hot as it will go. If using a pizza stone, preheat the oven for at least 30 minutes.

Lightly oil a 14 x 16 inch (35 x 40 cm) baking sheet. Roll the dough until slightly smaller than the baking sheet. Place it on the sheet. If using a pizza stone you may roll the dough onto a sheet of parchment paper.
Spread the onion mixture over the dough, leaving a very small raised rim all the way around, then dot with the bacon.
Bake for 4 to 20 minutes depending on oven temperature. The tart should be lightly browned and bubbling. Burned/blackened edges are traditional. Serve very hot.

name: Puerto Rican Chicken Soup (Asopao)
description: A hearty Puerto Rican chicken and rice soup with bell peppers, tomatoes, and aromatic spices, finished with fresh parsley and a splash of lemon.

ingredients.text: 1 medium green bell pepper, cored and chopped
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

instructions: In a wide, shallow bowl combine flour, salt, black pepper, hot pepper, oregano and garlic. Roll chicken pieces in flour mixture.

In a large pot, melt margarine over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook for 3–5 minutes or until brown. Remove from pot and set aside. Add a bit of white wine or grappa to deglaze and pour drippings over chicken.
Add green pepper and onion to pot, and sauté until onion is translucent.
Add rice, tomatoes, broth, and a dash of lemon juice. Stir. Salt and pepper to taste. Cover and cook over low heat for 12 minutes.
Return chicken to pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until chicken is tender. Add a bit more oregano and some chopped parsley.

name: Breakfast Burrito
description: Breakfast burritos layered with hash browns, bacon or breakfast sausage, eggs, cheese, and Hollandaise sauce, then rolled up in a tortilla.

ingredients.text: 8 eggs either scrambled, sunny-side up, or poached
ingredients.name: egg

ingredients.text: 8 strips of cooked bacon or 1 lb (400 grams) cooked breakfast sausage
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: Hollandaise sauce, cheese, salt, and pepper to taste
ingredients.name: Hollandaise sauce

instructions: Place one-quarter of the hash browns in a tortilla.
On top of this place 2 strips of bacon or one quarter of the breakfast sausage.
Add two eggs, cheese, salt, and pepper.
Roll up the tortilla to enclose everything. If you used poached or sunny-side up eggs you can squeeze the burritos to pop the egg yolks and then work the yolk around to form a sauce.

name: Frog's Eye Salad
description: A sweet dessert salad common in the American Midwest, made with acini di pepe pasta, pineapple, mandarin oranges, whipped topping, and miniature marshmallows.
instructions: Cook pasta in a large saucepan.
Drain and rinse pasta.
Drain cans of pineapple and oranges, reserving juice.
Mix juices, sugar and egg yolks in a medium saucepan.
Bring to full rolling boil, stirring frequently until thickened.
Pour hot sauce over pasta.
Cool and refrigerate overnight.
Add fruit and mix well, then fold in whipped topping and marshmallows.

name: Ibaba Soup
description: A typical Nigerian soup made with ibaba seeds, which serve as a thickener. It is served with akpu, semo, or pounded yam.
instructions: Place meat in a pot, and cover with water. Begin cooking.
Add the blended pepper, onions, seasoning cube, and salt.
Once meat is soft, add dryfish and cook for few minutes.
Add palm oil and ground ibaba seeds.
Add shredded uziza leaves and ground crayfish.
Stir and serve.

name: Deep Fried Pretzels
description: Quick deep-fried pretzels finished with savory seasoning make a delicious snack to serve as an appetizer.

ingredients.text: 1 cup canola oil or vegetable oil
ingredients.name: canola oil

ingredients.text: ¼ tsp seasoned salt, garlic salt, or Italian seasoning
ingredients.name: seasoned salt

instructions: Fill a deep saucepan partially full of canola oil. Heat up the oil.
Cover a paper towel with seasoning (the paper towel will help absorb moisture). Then set the paper towel on a plate.
Use a spatula to drop the pretzels into the oil. Only leave them in for 2–3 seconds.
Remove the pretzels and lay them out on a bed of seasoning to dry. The oil may be used for multiple batches.

name: Sindhi Chickpea Confection
description: A traditional Sindhi sweet made by toasting gram flour in ghee with sugar, finished with a generous garnish of chopped nuts. Enjoy it warm or chilled.
instructions: Heat the ghee in a pan. Add the gram flour, and stir until toasted.
Remove from the heat, and stir in the sugar.
Return to the heat, and stir until the sugar melts.
Transfer mixture to a bowl, and garnish with nuts.
Serve hot or cold.

name: Southwestern Scramble
description: A spicy scrambled eggs dish loaded with red onion, green chile, and bell pepper for a hearty Southwestern-style breakfast.

ingredients.text: Butter, margarine, or cooking spray, for frying pan
ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.text: 1 medium green chile pepper, such as jalapeño, seeded and chopped
ingredients.name: green chile pepper

ingredients.text: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and sliced
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

ingredients.text: Serve with hot sauce, such as Tabasco sauce
ingredients.name: hot sauce

instructions: Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl, add the milk, and beat until well combined.
Place a large frying pan over medium heat, add the butter, margarine, or cooking spray, and allow to melt. Add the onions, chili, and bell pepper, and sauté for 2–4 minutes.
Add the eggs to the pan, and allow to cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until they just begin to set.
Turn the heat up to high, and begin scrambling the eggs by scraping the bottom of the pan with a spatula and folding the cooked egg into the egg mixture.
When the eggs are still moist, but mostly cooked, remove from the fire and plate.
Serve while still hot.

name: Injera (Ethiopian Teff Flatbread)
description: A traditional Ethiopian and Eritrean flatbread made from teff flour, fermented to develop a pleasantly sour taste and a signature airy, bubbly texture. It is served as the base for stews and other dishes in Ethiopian cuisine.

ingredients.text: 1½ cups warm but not hot water
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Mix the flour with the water, and the salt. Add your fermentation starter if using one.
Set aside to ferment overnight, or at least 12 hours. There should be bubbles on the surface from fermenting, before you use it.
Heat a large, flat pan until it is hot enough to make a droplet of water sizzle. Oil it very lightly, just enough to make the pan shine.
Pour or ladle some batter onto the pan, spiralling outwards from the centre. Only a thin layer is required—a little thicker than a crêpe but not by much.

As it cooks, the surface of the injera will become covered in holes or pits. When the entire injera has changed colour and the edges start to lift from the pan, remove it and set aside, then pour the next injera and repeat until finished.

name: Panna Cotta (Basic)
description: A classic Italian dessert of sweetened vanilla cream set with gelatin and chilled until silky smooth. Serve chilled with fresh fruit, balsamic vinegar, or a sweet sauce.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (60 g) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: 1½ tsp vanilla essence or 1 small vanilla bean
ingredients.name: vanilla essence

instructions: Allow the gelatin to bloom in 1 Tbsp of the cream for about 5 minutes.
Combine the remaining ingredients in a medium saucepan over medium heat, and stir occasionally until the sugar dissolves and tiny bubbles appear around the edge of your pan.
Remove from heat and add the gelatin, stirring until it is thoroughly incorporated.
Pour the cream mixture into small ramekins and allow to set in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, up to overnight.
Serve with fresh fruit, balsamic vinegar, port, or a sweet sauce.

name: Ta'ameya (Falafel)
description: Ta'ameya, the Egyptian take on falafel, features seasoned balls of ground fava beans fried until golden and crisp. Often stuffed in pita with tahini, fresh vegetables, and hot sauce, it makes a satisfying street food or meal.
instructions: Place the fava beans in a large bowl and cover them with several inches of water. Allow the beans to soak for 8–12 hours.
Drain the soaked fava beans.
In a food processor, combine the soaked fava beans, red onion, parsley, cilantro, dill, garlic, coriander, salt, and cumin. Process the mixture until it reaches a dough-like consistency.

Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add sesame seeds to the heated skillet and cook them, stirring occasionally, until they become toasted, which usually takes around 5 minutes. Do not let them burn. Transfer the toasted sesame seeds to a large plate.
Shape the bean mixture into balls. Roll the fava bean balls in the toasted sesame seeds, ensuring they are coated evenly.
Fill a large saucepan approximately ¼ full with oil and heat it over medium heat.
Fry the bean balls in batches until they turn golden brown (typically around 3–5 minutes).
Remove the falafel from the oil and place on paper towels to remove any excess oil.

name: Artichoke Dip with Parmesan
description: A creamy, savory dip made with equal parts artichoke hearts, mayonnaise, and Parmesan or Romano cheese. Serve it at room temperature with vegetables and chips, or broil it until lightly tan for a warm dip.

ingredients.text: Artichoke hearts, drained and chopped or squeezed
ingredients.name: artichoke heart

instructions: Combine all ingredients to make dip.
Serve at room temperature with vegetables, potato chips, and other common party snacks.
For a warmed-up dip, place it into a small, shallow, heat-resistant dish and broil just until the top turns slightly tan.
Alternatively, keep the dip warm in a fondue pot, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
For a sandwich, spread the dip onto a good Italian roll and broil it.
When the dip turns a nice tan color, remove it from the broiler and finish the sandwich with lettuce and tomato.

name: Original Texas-Style Chili
description: This original Texas-style chili con carne combines seared beef, chile pods, garlic, oregano, cumin, cayenne, and optional Tabasco sauce. Masa harina thickens the chili and adds a subtle tamale-like flavor, with no vegetables other than chile peppers.

ingredients.text: 3 lbs (1.3 kg) beef or other meat
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: 4 chile pods, skinned and blistered, or sun-dried chiles
ingredients.name: chile pod

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon Tabasco sauce (optional but frequently included)
ingredients.name: hot sauce

ingredients.text: 2 garlic cloves, chopped (or more, to taste)
ingredients.name: garlic clove

instructions: If using fresh peppers, they should have been prepared by being boiled, peeled, and chopped. If using dried peppers, they need to be soaked in hot water for 1 hour before being chopped.
Sear beef in a little cooking oil (not lard) until lightly browned.

Add the seared beef, suet, and chile pods to a large iron skillet or pot (at least four quarts), and enough water (the reserved pepper water if you prepared the pods yourself) to keep the meat from burning. Bring to a boil, then lower heat, cover, and simmer about 30 minutes.
Take pot off the stove and add spices and garlic. Put back on the stove, bring to a boil again, lower heat, and simmer another hour, keeping the lid on as much as possible.
Stir when necessary, but remember that too much stirring will tear the meat. Add a little more water if anything seems seriously in danger of burning, but as little water as possible.
Take pot off the stove and skim off all or most of the grease.
Mix in masa harina, which tightens or thickens the chili con carne and adds a subtle tamale-like flavor.
Simmer about 30 minutes more, until meat is done.
Do a lot of tasting during this time, both to adjust the seasoning and because a chili cook should do a lot of tasting.

name: Bruschetta
description: Toasted slices of Italian or French bread rubbed with garlic, seasoned with salt and pepper, and generously drizzled with extra-virgin olive oil. Serve warm with seasonal toppings such as tomatoes, herbs, beans, mushrooms, or pancetta.

ingredients.text: 1 loaf of Italian or French bread, sliced ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick on the bias
ingredients.name: bread

ingredients.text: Toppings of your choice (see examples below)
ingredients.name: toppings

ingredients.text: Chopped tomatoes with arugula or basil
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: Cooked white beans (topped, if you like, with sautéed kale)
ingredients.name: white bean

ingredients.text: Minced anchovies flavored with wine vinegar and herbs
ingredients.name: anchovy

ingredients.text: Thinly-sliced pancetta crisped under the broiler
ingredients.name: pancetta

ingredients.text: Pugliese-style chopped mixture of summer vegetables (red onion, cucumber, tomatoes, oregano, flat-leaf parsley, basil, and red pepper flakes)
ingredients.name: summer vegetables

instructions: Toast the bread slices in a toaster oven, under a broiler, or on a grill, until they turn golden.
Immediately rub the bread with the cut side of the garlic. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper, and drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
Serve warm topped with whatever combinations of seasonal ingredients you choose.

name: Bua Loi (Rice Balls in Sweet Coconut Milk)
description: A traditional Thai dessert of glutinous rice flour and taro shaped into small balls and served with sweet coconut milk. The bua loi can be brightly colored with pumpkin or pandan and are best served hot.

ingredients.text: 1 cup steamed and mashed taro root
ingredients.name: taro

instructions: Combine rice flour, mashed taro, and water to make a dough.
Shape the dough into small balls, using additional rice flour to prevent sticking.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the dough balls to the boiling water. They will initially sink but will gradually float to the surface as they cook.
Remove the cooked bua loi from the pot, and drain the water.
Transfer the bua loi to a dish, and serve with coconut milk. This dish is best served hot.

name: Amala Ọgẹdẹ (Nigerian Plantain Fufu)
description: A typical Nigerian swallow made from plantain flour, served with ẹgusi, ogbono, or okro soup.
instructions: Boil some water in a pot.
Slowly stir in the plantain flour until smooth and lump-free.
Add some water and cook for few minutes.
Serve with the soup of your choice.

name: Ale, Mustard and Winter Vegetable Pie
description: A hearty vegan pie with creamy mashed root vegetables and a rich mushroom, TVP, mustard and dark ale sauce. The winter filling is baked until the top begins to brown.

ingredients.text: ½ small turnip or rutabaga, chopped
ingredients.name: turnip

ingredients.text: ¼–½ cup dried TVP (textured vegetable protein)
ingredients.name: textured vegetable protein

ingredients.text: 2 heaped tablespoon wholegrain mustard (try a green peppercorn mustard, if available)
ingredients.name: wholegrain mustard

ingredients.text: 200 ml (¾ cup) rich, dark ale (try a nice Porter)
ingredients.name: ale

instructions: Drop the potato, turnip or rutabaga, and ½ parsnip in a saucepan of rapidly boiling water. Bring back to the boil, and simmer until potato is soft (about 20 minutes).
When cooked, drain off the water, add the margarine, and mash until creamy smooth. Set aside.
Reconstitute the TVP by mixing the TVP, boiling water and marmite. Let sit.
Put olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat, then add the leek, garlic and carrot and ½ parsnip. Sauté until the carrot is soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook a minute or two more.
Add the flour and stir like mad for a solid 30 seconds.
Still stirring, add the TVP and its soaking broth to soak up the flour and thicken.
Add the mustard, ale and some black pepper. Stir to mix all very well. Simmer for about 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Pour into a casserole dish, top with the potato/rutabaga/parsnip mash, and smooth the top.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 20 to 30 minutes or until top is beginning to brown.
Remove from oven, let rest a minute, then serve.

name: Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce (Holubtsi)
description: Hearty cabbage rolls filled with seasoned ground beef and rice, baked in a tangy tomato sauce.

ingredients.text: 2 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with ½ cup cold water
ingredients.name: cornstarch

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Put cabbage into pot of boiling water, cover, let sit for three minutes, then drain.
Combine ground beef, milk, egg, rice, onion, pepper, and salt. Divide into twelve portions.
Place 1 meat portion on each cabbage leaf.
Roll leaf around filling and fasten with toothpick.
Place the rolls in a baking dish.
Combine tomato paste, tomatoes, sugar, water, and vinegar, then pour over cabbage rolls.
Cover baking dish, and bake at 350°F (175C) for 40 minutes.
Remove cabbage rolls from pan, and take out toothpicks. Place on the serving dish.
Add cornstarch and water to sauce mixture and stir together. Warm, if needed, to allow the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce.
Pour the completed sauce over the rolls on the serving dish.
Garnish as desired and serve.

name: Cochinita Pibil (Mexican Braised Pork)
description: A traditional Mexican slow-roasted pork dish from the Yucatán, marinated in a fragrant blend of annatto, citrus, and spices, then wrapped in banana leaves and baked until tender enough to shred with a fork.

ingredients.text: Banana leaves and/or heavy-duty aluminium foil
ingredients.name: banana leaf

ingredients.text: White or Spanish rice, taco shells, or tortillas for serving
ingredients.name: rice

instructions: Place the annatto, cumin, peppercorns, allspice, and cloves in a spice grinder and process to a fine powder. You can use an electric coffee grinder for the spices, but it will not be suitable for coffee afterwards.
Remove the seeds and veins from the habanero chiles and chop coarsely. If you want a hotter dish, leave some of the veins and seeds in.
Process the orange juice, vinegar, chiles, salt, garlic, and the spice powder in a blender or food processor until liquefied. Add the lemon juice and tequila.
Cut the pork into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks. Leave the fat on the meat, to keep the pork moist while roasting; you can remove it after cooking if you wish.
Place pork in a large, self-sealing plastic bag with the marinade. Seal bag and turn to evenly coat the meat. Refrigerate for 8 to 24 hours, turning occasionally.

Heat oven to 325°F (160°C). Dump the meat and the marinade in a roasting pan lined with banana leaves or foil, making sure to wrap tightly so no steam escapes. If using banana leaves, an outer wrapping with foil will help seal in the steam.
Bake for 4 hours. Open packet carefully; the meat should shred easily with a fork.
Serve over rice, or shred and serve with taco shells or tortillas.

name: Lemon Drizzle Cake
description: A simple butter cake flavored with lemon zest and juice, and topped with a lemony icing.

ingredients.text: 280 g (9.9 oz/2¼ sticks) unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (374 °F). Grease and line a 20 cm (7.9 in) square cake tin.
Beat the butter and sugar in a mixing bowl until soft and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs, one at a time, then lemon juice and zest.
Fold the flour and baking powder into the mixture.
Spoon the mixture into the cake tin.
Bake for 25 minutes until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Transfer the cake to a wire rack and leave it to cool.
Mix the icing sugar and lemon juice in a bowl until it is thick enough to coat the back of the spoon.
Drizzle the icing over the cake. Enjoy!

name: Fattah (Egyptian Layered Bread Dish)
description: A hearty Egyptian dish of layered bread, rice, and lamb or beef, topped with a garlicky tomato-yogurt sauce and fresh parsley and mint.

ingredients.text: 4–6 pieces of pita bread or Egyptian flatbread
ingredients.name: pita bread

ingredients.text: 500 grams cooked lamb or beef, cubed
ingredients.name: lamb or beef

ingredients.text: Chopped fresh parsley and mint leaves for garnish
ingredients.name: parsley and mint

instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Tear the pita bread or flatbread into bite-sized pieces and spread them in an even layer at the bottom of a baking dish.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooked rice and cubed cooked lamb or beef. Season with ground cumin, ground paprika, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to ensure the flavors are evenly distributed.
Spread the rice and meat mixture over the layer of torn bread in the baking dish, creating an even layer.
In a separate bowl, mix together the tomato sauce, yogurt, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt.
Pour the tomato-yogurt sauce over the rice and meat layer, covering it evenly.
Place the baking dish in the preheated oven and bake for approximately 15–20 minutes, or until the dish is heated through and the flavors meld together.
Remove the fattah from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Garnish the fattah with chopped fresh parsley and mint leaves.
Serve the fattah warm as a main dish or as part of a larger meal.

name: Turkey Biscuit
description: Leftover holiday turkey is combined with onion, cream of chicken soup, ranch dressing, milk, and cheddar, then topped with frozen biscuits and baked.
instructions: Sauté the onion until tender.
Combine all the other ingredients except the cheese and biscuits in a small bowl.
Stir this mixture, then place it into a baking dish, and bake for 15 minutes at 350°F until it is quite warm throughout.
Remove the baked mixture from the oven and sprinkle the shredded cheese on it.
Add a layer of frozen biscuits on top. Bake for about 20–30 minutes longer, then serve.

name: Dashi (Japanese Soup Stock)
description: A traditional Japanese broth made from konbu seaweed, dried fish, or mushrooms, used as the base for miso soup and other dishes.

ingredients.text: Dried young "flying fishes" (飛魚;tobiuo or あご;ago,unique name to Japanese-oceanside.)
ingredients.name: flying fish

instructions: If using sardines or anchovies, remove the heads and intestines. Discard these, keeping the bodies.
Boil fish in water, as if you were making tea.
Filter the liquid or scoop the solids out of it. The liquid is your dashi.

name: Steak Enchiladas
description: Tender, juicy, marinated skirt steak rolled with Monterey Jack cheese sauce in corn tortillas, baked until bubbly and drizzled with a tangy green chile purée.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (8–10 pounds) inside skirt steak, cut into 2 equal pieces and 1 smaller piece
ingredients.name: skirt steak

ingredients.text: 4 serrano chiles, minced (you can seed it if you want)
ingredients.name: serrano chili

instructions: Combine oil, lime, chipotles, adobo, salt, pepper, and cumin in a blender. Pour into a gallon size zip-top bag and add steak. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat a charcoal grill, but use a chimney or else you will have a solvent flavored steak. Ditch the grate and place the steak right on the coals and cook 60 seconds per side for medium rare.
Remove and wrap tightly with aluminum foil. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, purée the chiles with the vinegar in a blender until smooth. Pour into a large saucepan and bring to a boil over medium high heat until reduced by ⅓. Keep warm over low heat.
Melt butter in a saucier over medium heat. Cook until bubbling ceases. Add the flour and whisk continuously until it looks like blonde library paste.
Melt in cheese. Heat to just below a simmer then reduce heat to low and cook until slightly thickened. Set aside.

Slice steak as thinly as possible across the grain. Place a nice handful into each tortilla and top with some cheese sauce. Roll and place seam side down on a parchment-lined sheet pan. Repeat until all tortillas have been used up. While you're at it, eat any remaining steak.
Pour remaining cheese sauce evenly over the tortillas and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes or until browned and bubbly on top. Remove to serving platters.
Drizzle the chile purée over each enchilada and serve warm.

name: Fruity Cheese Dogs
description: A fun, kid-friendly dish of pan-cooked hot dogs smothered in melted cheese and topped with crunchy fruity breakfast cereal.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 ml) cheese (Mozzarella, Cheddar, Swiss, or any cheese that melts easily and is not very creamy)
ingredients.name: cheese

ingredients.text: ⅛ cup (30 ml) crushed froot loops (or any equivalent fruity breakfast cereal)
ingredients.name: froot loops

instructions: Cook the hot dogs in any manner; the original recipe used a pan on a stove, but a toaster oven would suffice.
Once the hot dogs have cooked and split, remove them from the heat.
Melt the cheese either in the oven or the microwave (microwave works best).
Pour the melted cheese on the hot dogs.
Sprinkle the crushed Froot Loops over the cheese, and let cool.

name: Swiss Meringue
description: A meringue made by heating egg whites and superfine sugar over a double boiler before whipping to stiff peaks.
instructions: Put the egg whites and sugar into a stainless steel bowl.
Place the bowl over simmering water and whip with a wire whisk until the mixture is 120°F (50°C).
Remove the bowl from the heat and continue whipping until the meringue is completely cool.
Use as desired or as directed in your recipe.

name: Microwave Applesauce
description: A quick microwave applesauce made with diced apples, apple jelly, maple syrup, orange juice, and cinnamon, with options for a chunky, slightly smoother, or smooth pureé texture.

ingredients.text: ¼ cup Grade B Amber maple syrup (Grade A Dark Amber would be okay too)
ingredients.name: maple syrup

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a microwave-safe container.
Cover container, leaving 1 corner open, and microwave on high 7–8 minutes or until apples are easy to mash.
Remove cinnamon stick and discard.
For a chunky sauce, mash the apples with a potato masher. For a slightly smoother sauce, use a hand mixer. For a smooth pureé, use an immersion blender.

name: Liver and Onions
description: A hearty British-style dish of flour-dusted lamb or ox liver fried with onions, served with mashed potatoes and green vegetables, all brought together with a rich pan gravy.

ingredients.text: Fresh or frozen green vegetables, such as peas, kale, cabbage, broccoli, etc.
ingredients.name: green vegetable

ingredients.text: A splash of milk, cream, crème fraîche, or similar
ingredients.name: milk

ingredients.text: about 500 g lamb or ox liver, sliced
ingredients.name: liver

ingredients.text: Henderson's relish, Worcestershire sauce, or similar (optional)
ingredients.name: worcestershire sauce

instructions: Wash (and optionally peel) the potatoes and put in a pan of boiling water.
Fry onions gently in a large frying pan with some of the oil.
While the onions are frying, prepare the green vegetables.
Prepare a plate or wide bowl, covering it in flour mixed with a bit of salt and pepper for dusting the liver prior to frying.
Once the potatoes are cooked, drain and then mash them, adding butter and cream or milk until you have the desired consistency. Put a lid on the pan to keep warm.
Once the onions are soft, remove them from the pan with a slotted spoon, squeezing the oil or butter back into the frying pan as you remove them. Put them in a bowl on one side.
Turn the heat of your frying pan up as high as possible and add a bit more oil or butter if necessary.
Arrange the liver, flour and frying pan in a straight line.

Start the process of dusting the slices of liver with flour on both sides and adding them to the hot pan as quickly as possible. Do not over-crowd the pan—if you find the liver takes up more surface-space than is available then leave the remains on one side and fry in a second batch.

Cook the liver quickly, for only about a minute on each side so the slices are still pink within. Turn them over a couple of times. Quite a bit of the flour and blood will stick to the bottom of the pan—don't scrape it off as it will be used for the gravy in a moment.
Once the liver is done to your satisfaction remove it from the pan and put directly onto warmed plates. Have someone else serve out the mash and vegetables while you finish the gravy.

Leaving the pan on a high heat, put the onions back in, add a good splash of Hendersons, and stir vigorously while adding boiling water, dissolving the juices stuck to the bottom of the pan. The gravy should thicken from the flour already stuck to the bottom of the pan. If it doesn't get thick enough you can add a bit more flour or cornflour (mixed with a little cold water in a small cup to avoid lumps).
Once the gravy is hot and thickened, spoon generously over the plates.

name: Steamed Sweet Rice
description: A traditional Japanese-style steamed glutinous rice, soaked for hours and gently steamed until tender and sticky.

ingredients.text: 1½ cups (360 ml) sweet glutinous rice (mochi gome)
ingredients.name: sweet glutinous rice

instructions: Place sweet glutinous rice in a medium bowl.
Wash rice thoroughly in cool water, rinsing and repeating until water is clear, drain, then return rice to bowl.
Add 3 cups (720 ml) water to the rice. Soak for 6 hours or overnight.
Drain well, spread rice evenly in a round, 8–9 inch (20 cm) shallow baking pan, and add ⅓ cup (80 ml) water.
In a wok, bring about 4 cups (950 ml) water to a boil over medium high heat.
Place a steamer tray in the wok.
Cover the pan of rice and place on the tray over the boiling water.
Steam for 30 minutes. If rice is not tender, sprinkle with 2–3 tablespoons of water, and steam it for 5 minutes more.
When tender, remove steamer tray from wok.

name: Tex-Mex Sliders
description: Seasoned ground chuck patties are cooked on a griddle, topped with melted Monterey Jack cheese, and served in toasted buttered buns.

ingredients.text: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.name: black pepper

ingredients.text: 16 ea. 1-inch buns, split in half and toasted
ingredients.name: buns

instructions: Preheat an electric griddle to 350°F.
Combine seasonings. Set aside.
Place meat out on a parchment-lined sheet pan and cover with plastic wrap. Roll out with a rolling pin until meat fills pan.
Remove entire sheet of parchment, including meat, from pan. Remove meat and cut into 16 equal patties with a pizza cutter.
Sprinkle both sides of each patty with seasoning mixture. Cook on preheated griddle 1 minute per side, putting cheese on cooked side after flipping.
Meanwhile, spread butter on each bun. Place a patty in each bun and close. Serve warm with desired condiments.

name: Vancouver Cheesecake
description: A light, crustless baked cheesecake made with cream cheese and ricotta. It is served chilled with fresh berries and a warmed sauce.
