ingredients.text: 500 ml cream cheese, softened to room temperature
ingredients.name: cream cheese

ingredients.text: 1 vanilla bean, or 10 ml pure vanilla extract
ingredients.name: vanilla

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Beat the cream cheese and ricotta together until smooth, continue beating as you mix in the sugar, then the eggs.
Slowly beat in the whipping cream, then add the lemon juice.

To add the bean, using a sharp knife, slice down the length of the bean, peel open and scrape down the bean to collect the contents. Using a spatula or second knife, scrape the contents of the bean into the mixture. Fold in.
Pour into a large baking pan, or a series of loaf pans.
Bake at 150°C for 45 minutes or so, slightly less time in loaf pans. The cake should still be jelly-like in the centre when done. Remove and allow to cool, then refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours.
Purée the raspberries and strain through cheesecloth into a saucepan.
Place the berry mix on a burner over medium heat, add the water and stir occasionally.
When warm, stir in the sugar and rum of choice, and turn the burner to high. Increase the stirring rate.
After the sauce has reached a boil, turn down to a low-medium range and allow to simmer for 15 minutes, stirring constantly. Then remove from the burner and allow to cool.
Slice the cheesecake. Sprinkle with berries and drizzle with sauce. Serve.

name: Pastry for Cornish Pasties
description: A simple, sturdy pastry dough made with flour and a blend of fats, designed for Cornish pasties. Neither too rich nor too flaky, it rolls out easily and bakes to a golden brown.

ingredients.text: ½ lb (225 g) mixture of lard, butter, and/or suet (equal ratios)
ingredients.name: lard, butter, and/or suet

instructions: Combine the dry ingredients, then gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff dough.
Roll dough to about a ¼ inch thick.
Cut our rounds with a tea plate.
Lay rounds on a pastry-board with half the round propped on a rolling-pin. Add the filling, and fold dough over filling.
Dampen the edges with water, and press to seal. Crimp the edges, then make slit in middle of each pasty.
Place on baking sheet, bake in hot oven until golden-brown.

name: Atkins-Friendly Mock Tiramisu
description: A rich, creamy Atkins-friendly dessert inspired by tiramisu, featuring sour cream, cream cheese, eggs, cocoa, and espresso powder without cake, ladyfingers, or added sugar.
instructions: Blend everything together until smooth.
Enjoy!

name: Chapati Za Maji (Tanzanian Pancakes)
description: Thin Tanzanian pancakes similar to crêpes, made with a simple flour-and-milk batter and cooked until faintly browned on both sides.
instructions: Combine the milk, eggs, and water.
Combine the flour, sugar, and salt.
Gradually whisk the wet mixture into the dry mixture until you get a thin batter similar to crêpe batter. If it feels too thick, add some additional water.
Cover the batter and let rest for 30–60 minutes.
Preheat a frying pan over medium heat.
Grease the pan with a small amount of canola oil, swirling the pan to coat the entire surface.
Scoop or pour a small amount of batter into the pan. Immediately tilt the pan in all directions to coat the whole surface with a thin film of batter.
Cook the pancake for about 1 minute. Then, carefully raise the edge with a spatula, flip it over, and cook for another minute. The pancake should be faintly browned on both sides.
Remove the pancake and set aside.
Repeat the greasing and frying process until all the batter is used up.
Serve hot.

name: Espagnole Sauce (Escoffier)
description: A slow-simmered brown sauce made with roux, brown stock, tomato paste, mirepoix, and bouquet garni, then strained and degreased for a smooth finish.
instructions: Dissolve the cold roux in a bowl by stirring in some of the cold brown stock.
Heat the rest of the stock in a deep, thick saucepan over a medium-high flame and bring to a boil. Lower the heat.
Temper the roux by ladeling some of the stock into the roux while whisking vigorously.
Stirring constantly, slowly pour the tempered roux into the simmering stock.
Dissolve the tomato paste with some of the stock and stir it into the sauce. Add the mirepoix and the bouquet garni.
Simmer slowly, partially covered for 2 or 3 hours. From time to time skim off any scum.
Add more stock if the sauce thickens too much. You should end up with a sauce that coats a spoon lightly.
Adjust the seasoning to taste. Strain and degrease thoroughly.
Refrigerate or freeze if not using immediately.

name: Herbed Tomato Soup
description: A fragrant tomato soup simmered with fresh basil and thyme, finished with a splash of balsamic vinegar and delicate basil strips.

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon fresh snipped basil (or 1 teaspoon dried)
ingredients.name: basil

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon fresh snipped thyme (or ¼ teaspoon dried)
ingredients.name: thyme

ingredients.text: 4–6 fresh basil leaves (optional), sliced thinly into strips
ingredients.name: basil leaf

instructions: In a 2-quart saucepan, sauté onion in olive oil until tender but not browned.
Add tomatoes, broth, tomato sauce, basil, thyme and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in vinegar, if desired, just prior to serving.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with basil strips.

name: Tuna Melt Fishcakes
description: Practical and tasty tuna and ricotta fishcakes that can be served hot or cold, perfect for a quick main course, picnic, or buffet.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180ºC before beginning preparation.
In a bowl beat the eggs and mix in well the drained tuna with the ricotta.
Add a little salt and pepper, the lemon zest, basil or parsley, Parmesan and half the bread crumbs.
Distribute a trickle of olive oil in an ovenproof dish.
Work the ingredients well and, with the help of two spoons, form medium-sized balls to be covered in the other half of the breadcrumbs and lay them in the ovenproof dish.
Bake in the oven for 25–30 minutes and serve warm or cold drizzling with lemon juice and accompanied by a green salad.

name: Nigerian Barbecued Chicken Wings
description: Chicken wingettes coated in a seasoned flour and cornmeal mixture, then marinated and grilled or baked until cooked through. Serve them as a side dish or alongside grains such as jollof rice and fried rice.
instructions: Combine the flour, cornmeal, pepper, salt, sugar, ginger, and paprika in a bowl.
Add the chicken and rub the mixture into them well so they are completely coated.
Set in the fridge and allow the chicken to marinate for 1 hour.
Arrange the chicken in a baking tray or on a grill. Grill or bake until cooked through (about 45 minutes baking).

name: Tuna Glop
description: A simple, quick-to-make pasta meal combining elbow macaroni with cream of mushroom soup, tuna, and frozen vegetables, finished with a crunchy topping of crushed potato chips.

ingredients.text: 1 can (10 oz / 300 g) cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.name: cream of mushroom soup

ingredients.text: 1 can (6 oz / 170 g) chunk tuna in water
ingredients.name: tuna

ingredients.text: 2 cups frozen vegetables, such as peas and carrots
ingredients.name: frozen vegetables

instructions: Prepare macaroni according to directions on the package, but without salt. Drain and return to pot.
Add cream of mushroom soup.
Drain tuna and add.
Add frozen vegetables and mix well.
If you prefer crunchy vegetables, heat for 5 minutes over low heat, stirring frequently. Heat longer if you prefer softer vegetables.
Serve topped with crushed potato chips (crisps).

name: Focaccia with Onion Marmalade, Blue Cheese, and Walnuts
description: A golden-baked focaccia topped with sweet-and-sour onion marmalade, crumbled blue cheese, and coarsely chopped walnuts.

ingredients.text: 1½ cups Sweet and Sour Onion Marmalade
ingredients.name: onion marmalade

ingredients.text: ¼ pounds blue cheese, crumbled or cut into ½-inch pieces
ingredients.name: blue cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F.
When the focaccia is fully risen and ready to bake, gently spread onion marmalade evenly over the surface.
Evenly distribute blue cheese over the onion marmalade and scatter walnuts over the top.
Place the sheet pan on the middle shelf of the oven, lower the temperature to 450°F, and bake for 20 minutes.
Rotate the pan 180 degrees and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the dough is golden on the bottom and top.

When the baking is complete, set up a cooling rack inside a sheet pan and immediately remove the focaccia from the pan using a metal spatula or pastry blade to break all contact with the walls of the pan.
Place the spatula or blade between the focaccia and the parchment or pad and lift the edge up.
Jiggle the focaccia out of the pan onto the cooling rack and pour any excess oil from the pan over the top.
Let the focaccia cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Maffé (West African Peanut Stew) III
description: A rich West African peanut stew made with beef, peanut butter, tomato paste, onion, and black pepper.
instructions: Boil meat in a pot with salt and onion.
Fry the meat in a pan of oil.
Blend together the tomato, pepper, and garlic until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and add the peanut paste. Stir until thick.

name: Harissa bil Djaj (Libyan Chicken Harissa)
description: A flavorful and aromatic Libyan chicken dish featuring tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, spicy tomato sauce infused with harissa and warm North African spices. Often served with bread or couscous to soak up the bold, comforting sauce.

ingredients.text: ½ teaspoon ground cayenne pepper (adjust according to spice preference)
ingredients.name: ground cayenne pepper

instructions: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot and brown them on all sides.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato paste, harissa paste, cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, coriander, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper. Mix well to coat the chicken with the spices.
Pour in the water or chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a lid, and let simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with freshly chopped parsley. Accompany with bread or couscous to soak up the flavorful sauce.

name: Kari Ayam (Indonesian Chicken Curry)
description: A spicy yet sweet Indonesian chicken curry with garlic, ginger, candlenuts, turmeric, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves, simmered in coconut milk.

ingredients.text: 1 lb (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken parts
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: 5 Asian shallots, sliced (or ½ cup chopped onions)
ingredients.name: Asian shallot

ingredients.text: ½ tsp turmeric root, ground or grated
ingredients.name: turmeric

ingredients.text: ½ tsp galangal root, ground or grated
ingredients.name: galangal

instructions: Wash chicken parts.
In a food processor or mortar and pestle, grind the garlic, ginger, kimiri nuts, turmeric, galangal, hot chilies, and terasi into a paste (bumbu).
In a wok or skillet, cook the paste over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the chicken parts to the wok, and brown them.
Add the shallots, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and salam leaves to the wok, and sauté for another minute.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a light boil.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.

name: Braised Collard Greens
description: Savory shredded collard greens simmer until tender in a ham-hock and garlic broth, with vinegar adding a bright kick to this southeastern U.S. side.
instructions: Place ham hocks, garlic cloves and a healthy pinch of sea salt in the 2 quarts of water, and slowly bring to a boil in a large stew pot until the ham hocks become tender.
Meanwhile, wash the greens thoroughly with cold water to remove dirt.
Wash them once in the vinegar (do not pat dry after vinegar wash).
Next, remove the stems and shred the leaves into thin strips.
When the water is boiling, add the greens by the handful and turn the temperature down to medium.
Simmer the greens uncovered until they are quite tender and the broth has reduced.
Serve with hot pepper vinegar, Tabasco, or red pepper flakes.

name: Kerala Pachadi (Coconut Mango Condiment)
description: A traditional Kerala condiment of ripe mango blended with coconut and tempered with mustard and dried chilies. Best served with plain rice.
instructions: Peel and cut the mango into small pieces. Mix with salt and set aside.
Grind the coconut with water and 2 of the dried chilies until well-blended.
Add the coconut-chili mixture to the mango, and mix well.
Heat oil in a kadai; add the mustard and remaining dried chilies, and fry.
Pour into the mango coconut mixture, and cook briefly.
Serve with plain rice.

name: Garlic Lemon Dressing
description: A garlic-and-lemon dressing with rosemary and olive oil, ready to drizzle over steamed vegetables, seafood, pasta, potato salad, or other salads.

ingredients.text: 1 strip lemon peel (1 x ½ inch)
ingredients.name: lemon peel

instructions: Place the garlic and rosemary on a cutting board and lightly crush with the flat side of a heavy knife.
Put the rosemary, garlic and lemon peel in a clean bottle with a tight-fitting cap.
Pour in the oil and lemon juice. Cap the bottle and shake well.
Refrigerate and use within one week.
Shake before serving. Drizzle on steamed vegetables, or seafood, pasta, potato salad, or other salads.

name: Chakarai Pongal (Sweet Rice and Black Gram Pudding)
description: A sweet, buttery South Indian pudding made with rice, lentils, jaggery, milk, and ghee, traditionally prepared for Makar Sankranti. Cashews and raisins are fried in ghee and folded through the warm pongal.
instructions: Cook the rice and dhal together with cups of water in a pot or pressure cooker until mushy.
Meanwhile, melt the jaggery with 1 cup of water in a pan.
Add the cardamom to the jaggery as it melts.
Mush the rice and paruppu (dal) mixture well and add to the pan of jaggery.
Stir well and cook on low heat till the mixture comes together well.
Heat 4 tablespoons of the ghee in a separate pan and fry cashews to golden brown.
Add raisins and fry for a few more seconds or until they swell up.
Add the nuts and raisins to into the pongal.
Serve hot with an additional dollop of neyyi or ghee.

name: Frikadelle (Meat Balls)
description: South African-style meatballs made with ground meat, onions, eggs, and bread, formed into flat patties and pan-fried until cooked through.

ingredients.text: Ground meat (e.g. beef, ostrich, lamb, fish, pork, or veal)
ingredients.name: ground meat

instructions: Soak the bread in water, then squeeze out the water.
In a bowl, combine the meat, onion, eggs, bread, mustard, stock cube, parsley, and pepper. Knead until you get an even mixture.
Form meat mixture into flat patties no bigger than the palm of your hand.
Pan-fry the patties in a skillet of olive oil until cooked through.

name: Boiled Cucumber and Grated Coconut (Pachadi)
description: A quick and tasty Kerala-style accompaniment made with cucumber and grated coconut, seasoned with cumin and mustard seeds.

ingredients.text: 1 cucumber (large variety, with dark green and yellow skin)
ingredients.name: cucumber

instructions: Skin the cucumber. Cut in half along the length and remove the central core of seeds. Discard the seeds.
Grate the cucumber. Alternatively, cut into very small pieces.
Cook the cucumber in the microwave for about 4–5 min.
Meanwhile, make a fine paste from the grated coconut and the cumin seeds.
In a deep pan (kadhai), heat the oil. Add the mustard seeds and red chillies, and let them splutter.
Add the cooked cucumber and the coconut paste and salt to taste. Mix well and let it cook on slow fire. Do not allow it to boil—it just needs to be warmed.
As the mixture starts to boil, take it off the stove. Serve.

name: Three Bean Confetti Salad
description: A colorful salad of pinto beans, red kidney beans, black beans, corn, and tomatoes tossed with Italian dressing and seasoning. Serve it chilled or at room temperature.

ingredients.text: 1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: pinto bean

ingredients.text: 1 can (15 oz) red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: red kidney bean

ingredients.text: 1 can (12 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: black bean

ingredients.text: 1 can (8¾ oz) whole kernel corn, drained
ingredients.name: corn

ingredients.text: 1 can (14½ oz) diced tomatoes with roasted garlic, undrained
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: ½ cup fat-free Italian salad dressing
ingredients.name: Italian salad dressing

instructions: In a bowl, mix together beans, corn, tomatoes, Italian salad dressing, Italian seasoning and pepper.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

name: Tartiflette
description: A rich French bake of tender Yukon Gold potatoes, bacon or salt pork, onions, cream, and reblochon cheese, finished golden under the broiler.

ingredients.text: 1¾ pounds Yukon Gold potatoes (5 or 6 medium-sized ones, all the same size) or waxy boiling potatoes
ingredients.name: yukon gold potato

ingredients.text: 5–6 ounces slab bacon or salt pork, cut into lardons about 1 x ¼ x ¼ inch
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (about 6 ounces) medium onion, finely chopped
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: ¼ cup dry white wine or dry vermouth
ingredients.name: white wine

ingredients.text: 6 tablespoons (¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons) heavy cream
ingredients.name: heavy cream

instructions: Preheat the broiler.
Slice the potatoes into thin rounds, about 1/8 inch thick.
Layer the potatoes, bacon, and onion in a baking dish.
Add the wine or vermouth and butter.
Cover and bake until the potatoes are tender.
Pour the cream over the potatoes and top with reblochon cheese.
Broil until golden and bubbling.

name: Garlic Croutons I
description: Crispy homemade croutons made from day-old French bread infused with garlic and olive oil, perfect for topping salads like Caesar.
instructions: Pour the olive oil into a shallow bowl over the garlic and let it soak. Soaking it longer will yield more garlic flavor.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F (~180 °C).
Strain the olive oil into a frying pan and fry the bread cubes in it, tossing to coat with oil.
Spread the bread cubes on a baking sheet and sprinkle with salt. Bake for 10 minutes or until crispy and dry.

name: Basic Scrambled Eggs
description: Soft, creamy scrambled eggs cooked in butter with a touch of milk, seasoned simply with salt and black pepper. A quick and satisfying breakfast for one.

ingredients.text: ⅛ tsp black pepper (or to taste)
ingredients.name: black pepper

instructions: Crack eggs into a measuring cup.
Add the milk (if desired) and salt.
Using a whisk or fork, beat the mixture until foamy.
Melt butter in a frying pan on medium heat.
Pour eggs into frying pan.
Stir mixture to break up the egg as it cooks and allow more liquid to touch the hot pan. Stirring rapidly will create small curds, while slower stirring will create larger curds.

Cook until just before you feel that they are done, since the eggs will continue to cook after being removed from the pan. The eggs are done when the sheen disappears; stop cooking just before this happens.
Transfer to a plate. Season with black pepper (black pepper will burn and become bitter if seasoned before cooking).
Eat as is or with ketchup (tomato sauce), salsa, and/or butter on toast.

name: Homemade Tomato Paste
description: A rich, concentrated homemade tomato paste made by slowly reducing tomato pulp with sweet red bell peppers and salt, then preserved in jars for long-term storage.

ingredients.text: 1 cup sweet red bell peppers, chopped
ingredients.name: red bell pepper

instructions: Cook the ingredients over low heat in a large wide covered stockpot for an hour.
Pass the mixture through a food mill several times starting with the coarsest grid and progressing to the finest.

Return the pot to the stove and heat uncovered over very low heat for 3 hours or more until very thick, stirring frequently to avoid burning. Use a heat diffusing mat or trivet. A double boiler would be ideal as it would prevent burning but will take longer.
Pour into new sterilized ½-pint preserving jars leaving ¼-inch of space at the top. Cover with new seals and screw on the lids securely but not too tightly.
Process in a boiling water bath for 45 minutes.
Remove from the water bath with tongs and allow to cool on an inverted oven rack for 12 hours.
Test the seal by pressing the centre of each lid with your forefinger. If the inner lid does not move, remove the outer ring.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.

name: Nigiri Sushi
description: A classic Japanese sushi where a topping is placed on a small hand-formed bed of seasoned sushi rice, optionally bound with a strip of nori and a dab of wasabi.
instructions: If making nigirizushi that requires a band of nori to hold the sushi together, cut the nori into strips about ¼ inch wide and long enough to wrap around the finished sushi with at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) of overlap. Place one such strip on the preparing surface.

Hand form the sushi rice into suitable sized sushi bases, generally a rectangular block about ½–1 inch wide, 1–1½ inch (2.5–4 cm) long, and ½–¾ inch (1.5–2 cm) high. Wetting the hands in water prior to forming each sushi base keeps the rice from sticking to the hands.
For nigirizushi requiring wasabi between the rice and topping, add a small dab of wasabi on the rice.
Add the selected topping on top of the sushi rice.

If nori is used, wrap one of the nori band ends up and over the nigirisushi topping firmly, so that it sticks to the rice and topping. Wet the other nori band end with a small amount of water, and wrap it up and over the topping so that it overlaps the other nori end. The water causes the nori ends to stick together.

name: Asida (Sudanese Porridge)
description: A traditional Sudanese porridge made from cooked wheat or sorghum flour, often sweetened with honey or dates and flavored with spices. Its smooth, rich texture makes it a nourishing choice for family gatherings and festive celebrations.

ingredients.text: 2 cups wheat flour or sorghum flour
ingredients.name: wheat flour or sorghum flour

instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the flour and salt. Mix well to ensure the salt is evenly distributed.
In a large saucepan or pot, bring the water to a boil. Gradually add the flour mixture to the boiling water, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula to prevent lumps from forming.

Reduce the heat to low and continue stirring the mixture until it thickens to a porridge-like consistency. This usually takes around 10–15 minutes. Be sure to scrape the sides and bottom of the pot while stirring to prevent sticking.

Once the porridge thickens, remove the pot from heat. Wet your hands with cold water to prevent sticking, then shape the hot asida into a smooth, round mound or ball. You can also shape it into individual portions if desired.
Make a small well in the center of the asida and fill it with honey or place a few dates. Sprinkle ground cinnamon or cardamom over the top for additional flavor, if desired.

Transfer the asida to a serving dish or individual plates. Drizzle a little clarified butter or vegetable oil over the top for added richness and shine. Asida is traditionally eaten by tearing off a piece of the porridge with your fingers, rolling it into a small ball, and dipping it into the honey or date filling. It can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature.

name: Chow Mein
description: A vegan take on the classic Chinese stir-fried noodle dish, made with seitan, fresh vegetables, and shiitake mushrooms in place of oyster sauce for deep umami flavor.

ingredients.text: Vegetable oil for frying, as needed
ingredients.name: vegetable oil

ingredients.text: ¼ cup water or low-sodium vegetable broth
ingredients.name: water

instructions: 1–2 hours before cooking, rinse the mung bean sprouts so that they have time to drain thoroughly.
Cut the seitan into thin strips. Add the marinade ingredients, adding the cornstarch last. Marinate the seitan for 20 to 25 minutes.

While the seitan is marinating, prepare the sauce: in a small bowl dissolve the 1 tablespoon cornstarch with the 4 tablespoons water. Whisk the water or vegetable broth with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, salt, pepper and cornstarch and water mixture and set aside.
Soften the noodles by placing them in boiling salted water. Plunge into cold water to stop the cooking process and drain thoroughly.

Wash all the vegetables as needed. Cut the celery and the bok choy into ½-inch pieces on the diagonal. If substituting broccoli for bok choy, peel the stalks until no more strings come out, and slice thinly on the diagonal. Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth and slice. Cut the red bell pepper in half, remove the seeds and cut into chunks. Peel and chop the onion. Dice the green onion.
Heat a wok or frying pan over medium-high to high heat. Add 2 tablespoons oil. When the oil is hot, add the noodles. Fry in batches until golden. Remove the noodles from the pan.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Add the onion and the seitan, keeping remaining marinade aside for later use. Let the seitan brown briefly, then stir-fry until the redness is gone and the seitan is nearly cooked through. Remove the cooked seitan and onion from the pan.

Cook the rest of the vegetables separately, except for the green onion, seasoning each with a bit of salt while stir-frying if desired. When cooking the bok choy or broccoli, add ¼ cup of water and cover while cooking. Remove each of the vegetables from the pan when finished stir-frying. Add more oil as needed.

Give the sauce a quick re-stir. Add all the ingredients back into the wok, making a "well" in the middle of the wok for the sauce. Add the sauce and any remaining marinade, stirring quickly to thicken. Mix everything together. Stir in the green onions. Pour the cooked vegetable and sauce mixture on top of the noodles. Garnish the chow mein with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.

name: Mpoto Mpoto (Yam Pottage)
description: A Ghanaian pottage made with cocoyam or yam cooked with onion, tomatoes, fresh pepper, and fish, then finished with palm oil and salt.
instructions: Peel and wash the cocoyam or yam, then cut into small chunks.
Place yam in a pot with the onion, tomatoes, and pepper. Cover with water and boil for 25–35 minutes.
Add dried herring and fish to the pot. Cook until tender.
Remove the cooked tomatoes, pepper, and onions. Grind to a paste.
Stir the tomato-pepper paste back into the cooked yam, and cook for a few minutes.
Add palm oil and salt to taste. Reduce heat, and cook for a little while, stirring intermittently.

name: Nigerian Oatmeal
description: A filling, well-balanced Nigerian oatmeal served warm with banana and milk, or enjoyed straight.
instructions: Soak the oats in enough milk or water overnight in the fridge.
Bring a pot of water to a boil with a pinch of salt. Stir in the soaked oats and a pinch of sugar.
Cook the oats, stirring, until they have absorbed the liquid and become soft.
Remove from the heat. Serve warm with banana, milk, and/or yogurt.

name: Khatti Dal (Spiced Tamarind Pigeon Peas)
description: A thick, tangy South Asian dal made with split pigeon peas, tamarind and aromatic spices. Serve it with roti or over rice alongside vegetables, pickle or chutney.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (240 ml) toor daal (split pigeon peas)
ingredients.name: pigeon pea

instructions: Wash toor daal and boil for about 20 minutes until soft. Drain and smash the dal.
In a kadai, heat the oil until hot. Add curry leaves, mustard seeds and jeera seeds. Fry for a minute. They will pop at first, so a cover will help to avoid a mess.
Add onion and fry until slightly brown.
Add ginger and garlic paste. Fry for a minute, then add the tomatoes. Cook until the oil separates.
Add tamarind pieces, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder. Cook it for 4–5 minutes.
Add the toor daal and enough water for your desired thickness.
Add salt to taste, and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve with a roti or poured over rice.

name: Fresh Tomato Galette
description: A rustic French-style galette with ripe tomatoes layered on flaky puff pastry, seasoned with thyme, mustard, and Parmesan, then baked until golden.

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp panko or fine dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.name: panko

instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Slice the tomatoes to 0.5 cm (¼ inch) thick, and set aside.
In a bowl, combine 2 tbsp grated Parmesan with the thyme and mustard powder.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper and lay your puff pastry on top.
Spread 2 tbsp panko or breadcrumbs, leaving about 4 cm (1½ inch) of the border uncovered.
Sprinkle the cheese mixture evenly on top.
Starting at the centre, arrange the tomato slices in concentric circles, overlapping each other.
Sprinkle the remaining breadcrumbs and Parmesan on top, season with a little pepper if you like, and carefully fold the leftover dough over the tomatoes.
Brush the galette with the beaten egg, and bake for about 30–40 minutes or until the dough is cooked through and golden brown.
Allow the galette to cool down slightly before decorating with fresh basil leaves, and serve.

name: South Texan Pinto Beans
description: Pinto beans seasoned with paprika, chili powder, garlic, onion, and bay leaves are simmered until tender and served in the cooking liquid, an important aspect of the dish.

ingredients.text: 1 ½ tbsp paprika OR ½ tsp each of paprika and pepper
ingredients.name: paprika

ingredients.text: 1 ½ tbsp granulated or brown sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp salt OR 2 tsp salt and a ham hock
ingredients.name: salt

ingredients.text: 1 ½ tbsp dehydrated onion OR ½ small onion, finely diced
ingredients.name: onion

instructions: Wash beans carefully and soak overnight in 8 cups of water.
Drain and refill with 5 cups of water.
Add all the other ingredients.
Bring to a boil and simmer at least an hour, or until tender.
Remove bay leaves.
Do not drain prior to serving, as the liquid is an important aspect of the dish. It can be served using a slotted spoon, to allow draining, or with a ladle into small side-dish bowls.

name: Glazed Sweet Potatoes
description: Tender sweet potatoes simmered in a buttery maple glaze, finished with crunchy pecan halves for a classic sweet side dish.

ingredients.text: 1 can (40 oz / 1100 g) sweet potatoes, drained
ingredients.name: sweet potato

instructions: Bring syrup and butter just to boil in large skillet on medium heat.
Reduce heat to low, and simmer about 2 minutes.
Add sweet potatoes and cook on low heat 10 minutes, gently turning sweet potatoes frequently to glaze.
Garnish with pecan halves, if desired.

name: Sweet Charoset
description: A sweet charoset made with apples, bananas, lemon, orange, dates, walnuts, cinnamon, and red wine, finished with honey to taste.

ingredients.text: Juice and zest of ½ lemon
ingredients.name: lemon

ingredients.text: Juice and zest of ½ orange
ingredients.name: orange

instructions: Mix apples, bananas, lemon juice, lemon zest, orange juice, orange zest, dates, and nuts in a bowl.
Add cinnamon, wine, and matzo meal, and blend thoroughly.
Mix in honey to taste.

name: Boliche (Cuban Chorizo-Stuffed Roast)
description: Boliche is a Cuban roast of eye round beef stuffed with quartered chorizo and covered in a tomato sauce seasoned with saffron, garlic, olives, capers, and red wine.

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp green Spanish olives with pimentos
ingredients.name: green Spanish olive

instructions: Cut slits into eye round roast, and stuff with quartered chorizos, following the grain of meat.
Lightly rub meat with adobo seasoning.
Brown the meat on all sides in a sauté pan to seal in the juices. Remove and place in a large covered roasting pan.
In the same pan as the beef was browned, add saffron, garlic, onions, peppers, bay leaves, oregano, olives, capers, and the Sazon seasoning. Sauté until the onions are translucent in color.
Deglaze with red wine, turn heat down, and simmer about 5 minutes. Add the cilantro and the tomato sauce and stir well.
Pour this mixture over the beef, and roast at 325 °F for 1 ½–2 hours, or until meat is tender.
Turn the roast over and baste with the sauce once in a while to assure full flavor penetration and even cooking.
Serve.

name: Rhubarb Crumble III
description: A sweet rhubarb crumble with a tender stewed filling and a golden brown topping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F / gas mark 5).
Cut the rhubarb into pieces and stew for a short time with the caster sugar and water until tender.
While the rhubarb is stewing, combine the flour and butter in a bowl until it resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the brown sugar.
Place the cooked rhubarb in a deep pie dish (1 L / 2 pt).
Spoon over the crumble topping and spread out evenly.
Bake crumble for about 25 mins until the crumble is golden brown.

name: Windsor Pudding
description: A traditional British steamed pudding made with shredded suet, dried fruits, apples, and sweet wine, boiled in a basin and served with a white wine sauce and sifted sugar.
instructions: Combine the suet, french roll, nutmeg, and lemon zest.
Mix in half a pound of apples, currants, raisins, stoned and chopped, wine, eggs, and a pinch of salt.
Mix all thoroughly together, and boil it in a basin or mould for 3 hours.
Sift fine sugar over it when sent to table, and pour a white wine sauce into the dish.

name: Cazuela Gallega (Egg, Ham, and Cheese Casserole)
description: A delicious egg, ham and cheese casserole baked in a foil-lined bowl, good for breakfast or dinner.

ingredients.text: ½ cup of ground Parmesan cheese
ingredients.name: parmesan cheese

instructions: Place 3 sheets of aluminum foil (approx 15 x 15 inches or 35 x 35 cm) into a bowl with a 5-inch (12 cm) diameter and 2-inch depth. Press gently the foil downwards in order to give it the shape of the bowl.
Spread the butter all over inside walls of the aluminum-shaped bowl.
Place one slice of ham in the bottom of the bowl. Cut the additional slice in three strips. With each strip, cover inside walls of aluminum bowl.
Add both eggs to the bowl.
Add the peas, spreading them all over the eggs. Be careful with the yolks—don't break them. Add 1 teaspoon of the liquid from the can.
Add a pinch of salt, and the ketchup, trying to cover all the area.
Carefully remove foil with the casserole from the bowl. Top with the cheese and bake 30 minutes in a preheated 400°F (205C) oven.

name: Mực Nhồi Thịt (Vietnamese Stuffed Squid)
description: A Vietnamese dish of tender squid stuffed with a savory mixture of pork fat, chopped tentacles, mushrooms and aromatics, then baked with vegetables in a rich caramel-coloured sauce.

ingredients.text: 12 small squid, cleaned, with tentacles removed and reserved
ingredients.name: squid

ingredients.text: 2 dried black mushrooms, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes and quartered
ingredients.name: dried black mushroom

ingredients.text: 30 grams bamboo shoots, drained and sliced
ingredients.name: bamboo shoot

ingredients.text: 2 dried black mushrooms, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes, stems removed, and finely chopped
ingredients.name: dried black mushroom

instructions: Combine chopped squid tentacles, minced pork fat, and garlic.
Add spring onion and mushrooms to the squid mixture, along with nước mắm, sugar, salt and pepper.
Stuff into the squid heads and secure the openings with toothpicks.
Place stuffed squid in a casserole dish or clay pot along with the sliced carrot, bamboo shoots, spring onions, quartered mushrooms and soaking liquid, caramel sauce, chicken stock, and nước mắm.
Place in a preheated 350 °F oven, and bake for 20 minutes.
Serve in the pot accompanied by steamed rice.

name: Rujak Cingur (Indonesian Cow Snout Salad)
description: A traditional Surabaya salad combining cow’s snout, fresh vegetables, tempeh, tofu, and rice cake with a blended peanut sauce and crunchy crackers.

ingredients.text: 3 bird’s eye chiles, or to taste
ingredients.name: bird's eye chile

ingredients.text: 100 grams boiled or fried cow’s snout (cingur)
ingredients.name: cow's snout

ingredients.text: 1 bunch of water spinach (kangkung), leaves picked and boiled
ingredients.name: water spinach

ingredients.text: 1 lontong rice cake, cut into pieces as desired
ingredients.name: rice cake

instructions: Prepare all the ingredients in advance.
To make the sauce, grind the fried peanuts, garlic, chiles, palm sugar, terasi, and salt together until smooth.
Add the petis sauce and tamarind water as needed. Mix until well blended.
Arrange all the ingredients for assembly onto a serving plate, starting with the cingur, then water spinach, bean sprouts, cucumber, tempeh, tofu, and rice cake.
Drizzle the sauce over the ingredients, and top with the crackers.

name: Gyuveche (Bulgarian Casserole) II
description: A traditional Bulgarian casserole layered with cheese, herbs, and optional meats or vegetables, finished with a baked egg on top. A flexible dish that uses whatever leftovers you have on hand.

ingredients.text: Any kind of cooked chicken, pork, or beef (optional)
ingredients.name: meat

ingredients.text: Any kind of sausage or hot dogs (optional)
ingredients.name: sausage

ingredients.text: Vegetables (optional), such as tomatoes, peppers, small hot pepper, mushrooms, cooked potatoes
ingredients.name: vegetables

ingredients.text: Fresh greens (optional), such as parsley, dill, celery leaves
ingredients.name: fresh greens

instructions: Chop or dice everything you want to put in.
Alternate layers of cheese, meat, and vegetables in a baking dish. Finish with cheese on top.
Bake in the oven at 200 °C (375 °F) for 20 minutes or until the cheese is melted.
Break the egg on top and put back in the oven for another 5–10 minutes depending on how well-done you like your eggs.
Serve with fresh bread or toast.

name: Arroz Negro (Valencian Squid Rice)
description: A traditional Valencian dish of cuttlefish or squid and rice, similar to seafood paella. Its distinctive dark color comes from squid ink, which enhances the rich seafood flavor.

ingredients.text: 1 medium green or red bell pepper
ingredients.name: bell pepper

instructions: Cut one onion and one bell pepper into quarters and place in a large pot with the rest of the broth ingredients.
Boil for about 30 minutes. Occasionally press the ingredients against the bottom of the pot with a potato masher or ladle to squeeze out their flavors.
Strain the broth and set aside. Discard the boiled seafood.
Pour enough oil into a paellera to cover the bottom and heat over a medium flame.
Add 1 teaspoon of salt to cubanelles and sauté until soft.
Add squid and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add garlic and sauté until brown (be careful not to burn).
Add rice and braise until coated with oil.
Add paprika and sauté for no more than 15 seconds then quickly add four cups of broth to prevent the paprika from burning.
Add squid ink and mix well.
Bring broth to a boil and then simmer for 2 minutes.
Taste the broth and invite your dinner guests to do so as well. If it tastes bland, add 1 teaspoon of salt at a time until everybody approves.
Add the rice.

Begin tasting the rice after it's been simmering for about 20 minutes and reduce the heat a bit. Make sure the rice doesn't get too soft. Check the rice again every 10 minutes and reduce the heat slightly after each taste. Your goal is to wind up with rice that has a slightly underdone center. The time it takes to reach this point can vary from 30 minutes to an hour depending on your cooking gear.

Your paella is done once the rice is slightly firm to the bite (Italians call this al dente), the paella is a little moist but not soupy, and you have a bit of toasted rice on the bottom of the paellera.
Remove the paellera from the heat and cover it with a white towel (NOT ALUMINUM FOIL). Allow it to sit for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Kid-Friendly Pizza
description: A fun whole-grain pizza that children can help assemble with tomato sauce, shredded cheese, red bell pepper, and optional chicken.

ingredients.text: ½ cup cubed cooked chicken breast (optional)
ingredients.name: chicken breast

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Spread the tomato sauce on the pizza shell.
Top it with half of the shredded cheese.
Add the chicken and red pepper on top of the pizza crust in whatever design you want. Have fun with it!
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top.
Bake it for 10–12 minutes.

name: Kwek-Kwek (Deep-Fried Quail Eggs)
description: A bite-sized Filipino street food featuring hard-cooked quail eggs dipped in a simple flour batter and deep-fried until light golden, typically served with spicy vinegar.
instructions: Gradually but vigorously whisk the water into the flour. The wet mixture should be thick but flow like a pancake batter.
Dip the eggs in the batter to coat them completely.
Heat several inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot. You're aiming for about 350°F (180°C).
Add the coated eggs to the hot oil, and deep fry until very light golden and cooked through. Remove from the oil and drain off any excess.
Serve with spicy vinegar.

name: Meat and Potatoes in Broth (Niku Jaga)
description: A comforting Japanese household dish of sliced beef, potatoes, and shirataki noodles simmered in a savory broth of mirin, soy sauce, sugar, and ginger.
instructions: Cut potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Set aside to soak in cold water.
Combine mirin, soy sauce, sugar, ginger, and beef in a saucepan. Boil lightly for 2–3 minutes.
Remove beef from pan. Add potatoes, sliced onion, and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered until the broth reduces to about ⅓ by volume.
Replace beef in pan, add shirataki noodles, and simmer for roughly 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and serve.

name: Minestrone alla Capucina
description: An Italian soup made with anchovy, butter, onion, boiled rice, and stock, cooked until it has the consistency of rice pudding.
instructions: Pound anchovy.
Fry it in butter with the onion and rice until the rice is golden brown.
Remove the onion and season with salt.
Gradually add some stock, cooking until the dish is of the consistency of rice pudding.

name: Rolex (Ugandan Flatbread-Rolled Omelet)
description: A nourishing, vegetable-filled omelet wrapped in warm chapati flatbread and seasoned with tomato, onion, cabbage, cilantro, salt, and pepper. It is best enjoyed hot for almost any meal.

ingredients.text: 1 medium-sized cabbage, finely chopped or grated
ingredients.name: cabbage

ingredients.text: ½ tablespoon salt or to taste
ingredients.name: salt

instructions: Heat a pan over medium heat.
Crack the eggs in a medium sized bowl. Whisk in the onions, tomato, cabbage, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil to the hot pan, and pour in half the egg mixture. Allow it to cook for about 3 minutes.
When the top is only a little wet, place a chapati over it.
Flip the omelette and chapati over so the chapati is at the bottom. Allow the chapati to warm for 2 minutes.
Roll the omelet up with the chapati on the outside.
Wrap in foil and serve it immediately.
Repeat the steps above with the remaining egg mixture and chapati.

name: Tempura Baked Halibut with Cilantro Aioli
description: Golden-baked tempura halibut is paired with a creamy aioli made from mayonnaise, olive oil, garlic, cilantro, lemon juice, and black pepper.

ingredients.text: 1 pound halibut fillet, portioned into 2 ea. 2-inch chunks.
ingredients.name: halibut

instructions: Whisk the egg in a medium bowl. Add very cold ice water.
Add flour. Mix, but not too much.
Spray a baking pan with nonstick canola cooking spray.
Dip the fish in the batter and place it in the prepared pan.
Bake the fish in a 350°F oven for 20 minutes or until slightly golden.
In a small bowl, whisk mayonnaise, olive oil, garlic, cilantro, lemon juice, and black pepper for the aioli.
Serve and enjoy.

name: Beurre Monté
description: A silky French emulsion of cold butter and water that can be served plain or enhanced with savory or sweet ingredients.

ingredients.text: 8 parts by weight of butter, cold
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Bring the water to a low boil in an appropriately sized cooking vessel, such as a saucepan.
Add butter, gradually whisking until smoothly incorporated. Make sure the butter is completely emulsified in before adding the next chunk.
Season to taste as desired.
Keep warm until use. Don't overheat, as this will break the emulsion.

name: Naan (Yeasted)
description: Soft, pillowy Indian flatbread made with a yeasted dough of bread flour, yoghurt and milk, baked until lightly puffed and served fresh from the oven.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 140°C/275°F/Gas 1.

In a small bowl, mix the yeast with 1 tablespoon of warm water. Stir in the sugar and leave it in a warm place for 5 minutes until the yeast is covered with froth. This will show that the yeast is ready to use.
Mix together the flour, onion seeds, salt and baking powder. Stir in the oil, yoghurt and milk, then stir in the activated yeast mixture.

To knead the dough, clench your hand into a fist, wet your knuckles with a little water, then press them repeatedly into the dough. Continue pressing and kneading until you have a soft, pliable dough. It should take about 10 minutes. Leave to rest for 10 minutes and then knead again for another 5 minutes.
Place the dough in a mixing bowl, cover it with cling film and leave it in a warm place to rise for 20–30 minutes.
Divide the dough into four balls and place on a floured surface or board. Roll each into a long oval shape about 0.5 cm (¼ inch) thick.
Place them on a greased baking tray and put them in the centre of the oven for 10–15 minutes. They are ready when they have puffed up a little. Serve fresh from the oven.

name: Boston Baked Beans
description: A classic American dish of kidney beans baked with bacon, molasses, brown sugar, and rum for a rich, smoky-sweet flavor.

ingredients.text: 6 rashers thick cut bacon, sliced (or 5 drops liquid smoke)
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: 4 cups canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: kidney bean

ingredients.text: ¼ cup blackstrap molasses, plus more as needed
ingredients.name: blackstrap molasses

instructions: Cook bacon. Separate the meat from the fat, and chop the bacon.
Place 1 tbsp of the bacon fat into a large stainless steel pan. Add kidney beans and sauté over medium-high heat.
Add rum and tilt to ignite. If you do not have a gas stove, simply light with a fire stick.
Add remaining ingredients and chopped bacon and fold to combine.
Bake in a 325°F oven for 1 ½ hours, adding blackstrap molasses occasionally to prevent drying.

name: Date Nut Bars
description: Date and nut bars made with whipped egg whites and finished with a tangy lemon-vanilla glaze.
instructions: Grind the nuts and dates; sift in the granular sugar.
In another bowl, whip egg whites until stiff.
Gradually add the sugar mixture, whipping constantly. Fold in the cream.
Sift the flour, then re-sift the flour with the baking powder. Fold into the egg mixture.
Grease and flour a baking sheet.
Pat dough ½-inch thick on the baking sheet, and bake for 10 minutes at 350°F (175°C).
Mix confectioner's sugar with lemon juice and vanilla in a blender.
When the cookies are still hot, spread the glaze over them.

name: Ukpo Oka (Nigerian Corn Pudding)
description: A traditional Nigerian corn pudding from the Ika-Ibo people of Delta State, blended with pepper, onion, and crayfish, then steamed to a soft set.
instructions: Blend together the corn, pepper, onion, and crayfish with a small amount of water.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, and stir in salt and palm oil to taste.
Pour the mixture into a mold. Place in boiling water, and steam for 45 minutes.

name: Flourless Chocolate Cake
description: A dense, rich flourless chocolate cake made with melted chocolate, butter, eggs, and sugar. After baking, it is chilled to set, then turned out and garnished.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (120 g) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: white granulated sugar

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (150 g) chocolate (suitable for melting)
ingredients.name: chocolate

instructions: Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl set above another pan of simmering water (or use a double boiler).
Lightly whisk chocolate mix until smooth, then remove from heat and allow to cool, whilst still stirring.
Beat eggs and sugar in a bowl until the mixture is creamy.
Gradually mix in the melted chocolate along with any other variants (see below).
Pour mixture into mould (baking tray or 8 individual moulds).
Cover moulds with aluminium foil and place the moulds in a deeper baking tray.
Pour boiling water into the deep baking tray at a depth that is half that of the moulds.
Bake for approximately 30 minutes in a preheated oven at gas mark 2 (300°F or 150°C). Insert a skewer to check if ready: if skewer comes out clean, then it is ready.
Remove from oven and allow to cool at room temperature.
Cool for approximately 10 hours in a fridge.
Remove from mould, place on a plate and garnish.

name: Chocolate-coated Marshmallow Treats (Flødeboller)
description: A classic Danish confection of soft meringue tops on marzipan biscuits, dipped in tempered dark chocolate. The combination of chewy meringue, almond marzipan and crisp chocolate shell makes these treats irresistible.
instructions: Mix icing sugar and egg whites in a bowl.
Mix the egg-sugar mixture into the marzipan in several stages until the dough is uniform.
Use a pastry bag to make flat, round biscuits, approximately 5 cm in diameter.
Bake in oven at 190°C until golden, approximately 10 min.
Cool to ambient temperature.
Mix 250 g of sugar, the water and glucose syrup in a saucepan, and heat to exactly 117°C.
Meanwhile, beat the egg whites lightly with 15 g of sugar.
Gradually pour the hot sugar mixture directly into the egg whites, while still beating.
Whip the egg white mixture until very stiff.

Split open vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds, mix these with the icing sugar. Add this to the egg white mixture along with any flavoring, and stir slowly until uniform in appearance. Avoid deflating the meringue.
Use a pastry bag to pipe 5 cm tall meringue tops on the marzipan biscuits. Make sure the foam adheres to the biscuit, otherwise it will fall off while coating.
Leave at room temperature or put in refrigerator while preparing chocolate coating.
Finely chop the chocolate.
Melt half the chocolate carefully in a bain-marie (or a pot floating in water in a bigger pot). Aim for 48–50°C.

Put the other half of the chocolate into a bowl (make sure it is big enough for the entire cake can be submerged in chocolate). Add ⅔ of the melted chocolate, and let the two melt together WITHOUT HEATING! Only add more melted chocolate if the lumps do not melt away. The temperature must not exceed 34°C. This will keep the chocolate shiny and crunchy.
Dip the meringue tops into the chocolate. Make sure all the meringue is covered. The biscuit is up to you.
Sprinkle or roll in desiccated coconut, then leave to set. Do not reheat the chocolate if it starts to set, use instead some of the warm melted chocolate.

name: Baked Eggplant
description: A festive baked eggplant dish with shells stuffed with a savory sauté of mushrooms, tomatoes, walnuts, and capers, seasoned with cinnamon and garlic.

ingredients.text: ¼ lb (113 g) button mushrooms, sliced
ingredients.name: button mushroom

instructions: Cut eggplants in half lengthwise, leaving a ¼-inch (0.5 cm) rind.
Scoop out flesh using a curved serrated grapefruit knife, and coarsely chop it.
Place chopped eggplant into a large, deep skillet or flat-bottomed wok.
Rub inside of eggplant shells with olive oil and set aside on a baking sheet.
Add mushrooms, tomatoes, onions, garlic, salt, cinnamon, pepper, and olive oil to skillet, and sauté 5 to 10 minutes until soft but still chunky.
Place eggplant shells under the broiler, and broil 3 inches (7.5 cm) from heat source for 8–12 minutes, until fork tender (be careful not to burn). Remove from heat source and set aside.
Coarsely grind walnuts, add to skillet along with capers and tomato paste, and mix well.
Fill eggplant shells with sautéed mixture and top with tomato slices.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Bake uncovered at 375°F for 25–35 minutes.

name: Breakfast Casserole
description: A hearty layered breakfast casserole combining sausage, bacon, eggs, ricotta, and cornbread, topped with Monterey Jack and breadcrumbs and baked until golden and bubbly.

ingredients.text: 5 small sausage links, cooked and finely chopped
ingredients.name: sausage link

instructions: Combine sausage and bacon. In another bowl, combine ricotta, eggs, butter, salt, pepper, and cornbread.
In a greased large roasting pan, place just enough cornbread mixture to cover the bottom. Add just enough meat mixture to cover that layer, and repeat the layering until all mixtures have been used.
Combine Monterey Jack and breadcrumbs. Sprinkle evenly over layers and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes or until browned and bubbly on top.
Serve warm.

name: Fried Chicken
description: A classic Southern American fried chicken brined in salty buttermilk and coated with a custom spice rub and flour. Three cooking methods are offered: deep frying, pan frying, or pressure frying.

ingredients.text: Dry ground seasonings as desired (e.g. pepper, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, etc.)
ingredients.name: seasoning

ingredients.text: 1 fryer chicken, cut up (see notes below)
ingredients.name: fryer chicken

ingredients.text: A quantity of oil suitable for the desired cooking method (see notes below)
ingredients.name: oil

instructions: Combine all seasonings in desired quantities to make a spice rub.
Pour the buttermilk into a bowl and dissolve in the salt.
Piece by piece, roll the chicken around in the spice rub.
Submerge each chicken piece in the buttermilk.

Cover the bowl of buttermilk and chicken and refrigerate. You can get by with as few as two hours if you are in a hurry, but the flavor will suffer. You can also park it overnight, but in this case you should reduce the salt to ⅓ cup.
Shortly before you want to cook the chicken, remove it from the buttermilk and drain. Roll it around in flour so that it is well covered in flour. Shake off the excess flour.

The safest cooking method is deep frying. Immerse chicken in 360°F oil. Cook breasts for 10 minutes, drumsticks for 12 minutes, thighs for 13–14 minutes, and wings for 10 minutes. Drain the chicken on a wire rack over a sheet pan.

The most traditional cooking method is pan frying in a cast iron skillet. Heat enough oil (or shortening) to come 3–4 mm up the side of the pan to 325°F. Carefully place chicken in pan, skin side down. Cook until brown (10–12 minutes). Turn over and cook other side, placing slow-cooking meat (such as thighs) more intensely than fast-cooking meat (such as wings and breasts). Drain the chicken on a wire rack over a sheet pan.

Pressure frying gives excellent results, but special equipment is needed. Put the chicken pieces into hot oil (larger pieces first) and fry about 3 minutes until very light brown. Then put on the lid and lock it. Cook at a pressure of 5–6 pounds for about 7 minutes. Drain the chicken on a wire rack over a sheet pan.

name: Smokehouse Burgers
description: Seasoned ground chuck patties are grilled, topped with pepper jack cheese, and served in toasted hamburger buns with smoked paprika and garlic.

ingredients.text: 4 hamburger buns, split in half and toasted
ingredients.name: hamburger bun

instructions: Form meat into 4 equal patties, about ¾ inch thick. Make a depression in the center with your thumb and set aside.
Brush patties with oil. Sprinkle on both sides with seasonings.
Preheat grill. Add patties and cook, turning often, until desired "doneness" is achieved.
Remove to a plate, top each with a slice of cheese, and cover tightly with aluminum foil. Let rest until cheese is melted.
Brush cut sides of bread with oil. Add a patty onto the bottom half of a bun, then top with the upper half. Repeat with remaining meat and serve immediately.

name: Kid-Friendly Pasta
description: A simple, child-friendly pasta dish made with whole-wheat spaghetti, carrots, and green beans tossed in tomato sauce.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add spaghetti and carrots to the boiling water, and cook for 4 minutes.
Add green beans, and cook for another 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the tomato sauce.
Drain the spaghetti and the vegetables, then mix it with the heated sauce.
Add a pinch of salt if needed.
Serve.

name: Apple Glazed Pork Chops
description: Seasoned, grilled bone-in pork chops finished with a reduced glaze of apple cider, cider vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce.

ingredients.text: Grill Seasoning for Chops, as needed
ingredients.name: grill seasoning

instructions: Rub seasoning on pork chops. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine remaining ingredients in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, and cook until reduced by ⅓. Remove from heat and set aside.
Grill pork chops over high heat for 2 minutes, covered.
Brush with cider mixture, rotate 90°, and cook for 2 minutes.
Flip and repeat 1 more time.
Remove and let rest for 7 minutes.
Serve with remaining cider mixture.

name: Gboma Dessi and Akoume (Togolese Spinach Stew with Corn Swallow)
description: Gboma dessi, also called sauce feuille, is a Togolese meat and spinach stew seasoned with gbotemi spices, tomato paste, and hot peppers. It is served with akoume, a hand-shaped corn-flour swallow.

ingredients.text: 5 tablespoons palm oil or vegetable oil
ingredients.name: palm oil or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 3 medium size garlic cloves, finely minced
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: 3 lb meat, cut into large cubes
ingredients.name: meat

ingredients.text: Gbotemi spice blend (cloves, aniseed, ajwain, and cardamom, toasted and ground with ginger powder)
ingredients.name: gbotemi spice blend

instructions: Put a pressure cooker on the fire and pour some oil into it. Add and sauté some of the sliced onions, minced garlic, and ginger powder for 2 minutes.
Add the meat, hot pepper, 2 bouillon cubes, and salt to taste.
Add enough water to slightly cover the meat. Reduce the heat and cook for about 40 minutes or more, depending on the meat and the pressure cooker.
While the meat is cooking, wash the spinach leaves and boil in salted water for 15 minutes. Then, drain and cut into thin slices.
Remove the meat from the pressure cooker, drain it and put it in a bowl. Keep the broth in the pot.
Season the meat with the gbotemi spice blend.
Sauté the remaining onions and garlic cloves in a saucepan with the remaining palm oil or vegetable oil.
Add the tomato paste, and cook, stirring regularly for at least 10 minutes.
Season with the remaining bouillon cube and hot pepper, then stir in the reserved broth. Boil over medium heat for 25 minutes.
Add spinach then the meat. Simmer for at least 15 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Pour 2 cups of water in a saucepan. Add the corn flour and mix with a wooden spoon.
When the water boils, add the all purpose flour and stir vigorously.
Dilute the starch potato in 1 cup of water and pour into the pan.
Stir vigorously for 3 minutes, then cover the pot and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Once the dough is ready, you can shape it to any form of your desire.
Serve the gboma dessi on top of this akoume in a banana leaf, or serve the gboma dessi on the side of the akoume in a big plate.

name: Sweet Potato Applesauce Latke
description: A savory-sweet fritter of grated sweet potato and applesauce, seasoned with cumin and fried in bacon fat, served with a side of bacon.
instructions: Squeeze most of the liquid from the grated sweet potatoes.
Combine the sweet potato, apple sauce, a little honey, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Form into patties; it's a little difficult but not impossible to get these to stay together without egg.
Fry in bacon fat.
Serve with a side of bacon.

name: Tiramisu Paninis
description: Grilled sandwiches that capture the classic flavors of tiramisu, with mascarpone cheese, coffee-soaked bread, and a dusting of cocoa powder.

ingredients.text: 1¼ cups strong coffee or espresso, cooled
ingredients.name: coffee

instructions: In a 13x9-inch roasting pan, pour in coffee. Add bread slices and add a weight if they float. Let sit for ½ hour.
Remove bread from pan, and discard any remaining coffee.
Toast bread again, but not in a sideways electric toaster, as the liquid would make this hazardous.
Spread slices of bread liberally with mascarpone cheese.
Attach 2 slices of bread to each other, cheese facing in. Brush outside liberally with hazelnut oil.

Heat a grill pan over medium high heat. Add sandwiches, working in batches if needed, and cook until brown on both sides and cheese is melted. Dust with cocoa powder, drizzle with hazelnut oil, and serve warm.

name: Nsima (Cornmeal Swallow)
description: A thick, smooth maize-flour porridge with a texture similar to mashed potatoes or stiff porridge. Serve it hot with flavorful meat, vegetable, or fish relishes.
instructions: Measure out the maize flour and set it aside.
In a large cooking pot, bring the water to a boil.
Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low and gradually add the maize flour to the pot while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon or a stiff whisk.
Make sure to pour the flour in a slow, steady stream to prevent clumping.
Keep stirring the mixture vigorously to combine the maize flour and water thoroughly.
Continue stirring for about 5 minutes until the mixture starts to thicken.
Increase the heat to medium-low and cover the pot with a lid.
Cook for about 10–15 minutes to allow the maize flour to cook fully and eliminate the raw taste.
Remove the lid and stir the mixture again, scraping the sides and bottom of the pot to prevent sticking or burning.
Continue cooking the nsima, stirring frequently, for another 10–15 minutes until it reaches the desired consistency.
It should have a thick, smooth texture similar to mashed potatoes or stiff porridge.
If it is too thick, add a little more water and continue stirring until the desired consistency is achieved.
Once the nsima is cooked to your liking, remove it from the heat and let it sit for a few minutes to cool slightly before serving.
Serve the nsima hot with your choice of relishes such as meat, vegetables, or fish.
Popular relishes include chicken stew, beef and vegetable stew, fried fish, or a variety of sautéed greens.

name: Fried Eggs
description: Quick fried eggs can be cooked over-easy, over-medium, or over-hard to suit your preferred yolk doneness. They are often served with toast or other fried dishes.
instructions: Melt the butter in the pan over low to medium heat.
Crack open the eggs into the pan and let fry until the yolks begin to harden at the edges (indicated by a lightening in the yolk color).
Using the spatula, flip the eggs over and allow to cook 10 seconds for over-easy, 30 seconds for over-medium, or up to 1 minute for over-hard.
Add salt and pepper to taste, and serve.

name: Chipotle Chili
description: A moderately spicy variation of chili con carne made with sweet chiles, chipotles, ground hamburger, tomatoes, beans, and hoppy beer. Serve it plain or with tableside additions such as sour cream and shredded cheese.

ingredients.text: 3–4 leftover hamburger patties, grilled and chilled
ingredients.name: hamburger patty

ingredients.text: 1 small can of chipotle chiles in adobo sauce
ingredients.name: chipotle chile

ingredients.text: 12 oz (330 ml) hoppy beer (recipe developed with Lagunitas IPA)
ingredients.name: beer

ingredients.text: 1 large can (14.5 oz / 411 g) of chopped tomatoes, or more
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: 1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: black bean

ingredients.text: 1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) dark kidney beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.name: kidney bean

ingredients.text: tableside additions such as sour cream, shredded cheese, Fritos, Cheese-its, etc.
ingredients.name: sour cream

instructions: Using a food processor, grind the leftover hamburger patties into a coarse powder.
In a bowl, mix the ground hamburgers with the cumin, chili powder, and salt. Set aside. Don't bother cleaning the food processor after grinding the meat.
Add the sweet chiles to the food processor one-by-one, and grind until they're reduced to small bits.
Add the chipotles along with the adobo sauce, grinding until the chipotles are thoroughly integrated into the sauce. You can leave this in the food processor or move it to a bowl.
Heat a stockpot over medium heat and add the oil. Swirl the oil in the pan to coat, and turn the heat down to medium-low.
Sauté the onions and garlic until soft and golden.
By now the onions should be pretty well cooked down. Turn the heat up to medium and stir continuously.
The onions may start to brown and stick to the bottom of the stockpot. Add half the beer to deglaze the pan.
Add the ground meat and spices, tomato products, beans, chile paste, and remainder of the beer, stirring after each addition to combine.
When the pot comes to a boil, turn the heat down to low and cover.
Simmer for at least half an hour.
Serve in bowls, either plain or with accompaniments suggested above.

name: Apple Cobbler
description: A comforting dessert of tender apples in a thick, sweet filling beneath a simple biscuit-like topping.

ingredients.text: 6 cups sliced, peeled, and cored baking apples
ingredients.name: baking apple

instructions: Stir together apples, ⅔ cup sugar and 4 Tbsp water in a large saucepan. Simmer, covered for 5 minutes or until fruit is tender.
Add 2 Tbsp water and 1 Tbsp cornstarch. Cook, stirring, until thick and bubbly.
In a medium bowl stir together flour, 2 Tbsp sugar, and baking powder.
Cut in butter until mixture resembles large crumbs. Set aside.
In a small bowl stir together the egg and milk. Add to flour mixture, just to moisten.
Transfer filling to 2-quart square baking dish.
Using a large spoon, drop topping into small mounds on top of the filling.
Bake for 20–25 minutes in a 400 °F (205 °C) oven.

name: Basic Cobbler
description: Fresh fruit is spread over a simple batter of flour, milk, butter, sugar, and baking powder, then baked uncovered until golden brown.

ingredients.text: Salt (optional; add only if butter is unsalted)
ingredients.name: salt

ingredients.text: 1 cup fresh fruit (e.g. peaches, blackberries, cherries, etc.)
ingredients.name: fruit

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place the butter in a deep 9½ x 12-inch baking dish. Put dish in oven to melt butter while preparing other ingredients. If butter is unsalted, add a touch of salt to the pan as well.
Add flour and sugar to a bowl and sift together lightly. Create a well in the center of the mixture, and pour the milk into the well. Mix together with a wire whisk until smooth.
Remove pan from oven. Pour batter into dish on top of melted butter. Do not stir. Spoon the fresh fruit out evenly across the top, but again, do not stir.
Place cobbler in oven and bake uncovered until golden brown.

name: Party Mix
description: A savory blend of corn, rice, and wheat cereal squares with mixed nuts, pretzels, and bagel chips, coated in butter and seasonings for serving company.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (120g) garlic-flavor bite-size bagel chips or regular-size bagel chips, broken into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.name: bagel chip

instructions: Heat oven to 250°F (120°C).
In an ungreased large roasting pan, melt butter in oven.
Stir in seasonings.
Gradually stir in remaining ingredients until evenly coated.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Spread on paper towels to cool, about 15 minutes.
Store in airtight container.
In large microwavable bowl, microwave butter uncovered on high about 40 seconds or until melted.
Stir in seasonings.
Gradually stir in remaining ingredients until evenly coated.
Microwave uncovered on high 5–6 minutes, thoroughly stirring every 2 minutes.
Spread on paper towels to cool.
Store in airtight container.

name: Kabab Kobide (Persian Minced Meat Kebab)
description: A traditional Persian kebab of seasoned minced meat molded onto skewers and grilled with tomato and onion. Served with rice or naan and finished with a sprinkle of sumac.
instructions: Combine ground meat, pepper, sumac, turmeric, onion, and salt. Cover and chill for 4 hours, or up to overnight. The meat should turn slightly yellow from the turmeric.
Shape meat mixture around skewers.
Grill skewers, tomato, and onion until cooked through.
Serve kebabs, tomato, and onion with the rice or naan. Garnish with additional sumac to taste.

name: Maltese Rabbit Stew (Stuffat tal-Fenek)
description: A traditional Maltese rabbit stew slow-cooked for hours with potatoes, tomatoes, red wine, and Mediterranean spices, yielding rich, tender meat in a deeply flavoured sauce.

ingredients.text: 800 g canned crushed tomatoes or canned 'Pelati'
ingredients.name: canned crushed tomatoes

instructions: Cut up the rabbit at the joints. Cut the rib section into 3–4 pieces, and divide the legs at all the joints. Split the head of the rabbit in half. The whole animal should be cut into about 10–12 pieces so they are large and chunky, but small enough that they can be easily manipulated with a large spoon. Remove and keep internal organs apart.

Mince the garlic. Heat the oil in a large frying pan. Heat some of the garlic in the oil. Add some rabbit pieces and cook through. Remove cooked meat from the pan and place in a large container. Cook the rest of the meat in the same way in batches, adding some garlic with every batch. The meat should be well cooked but not very brown.
Fry the internal organs whole in the same oil until well-cooked. Take some of the smaller pieces of meat without bone and add them to the organs. Keep these apart from the main meat.
Cut the potatoes into large irregular chunks, slightly smaller than the pieces of meat.

In a stock pot, place the fried rabbit, the potatoes, the chopped carrot, the tomato pulp, wine, sugar and laurel leaves. Add salt, pepper, mixed spice and Tabasco carefully. Cover and simmer on a low flame for 4 hours. Stir occasionally during the first hour.
Once done, add the peas, and cook until tender (about 10 minutes).

name: Pork Spare Rib Soup (Bah Kut Teh)
description: A Hokkien herbal soup of tender pork spareribs simmered with garlic, ginseng, cinnamon, star anise and peppercorns. Often served with Chinese doughnuts, white rice, and a small dish of cut red chillies in dark soy sauce.

ingredients.text: 1½ lb (680 g) pork spareribs, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces
ingredients.name: pork sparerib

ingredients.text: 1 whole bulb garlic, unpeeled and slightly crushed
ingredients.name: garlic

ingredients.text: 2 inches (5 cm) ginseng root, peeled and slightly crushed
ingredients.name: ginseng root

ingredients.text: 6 shallots, finely sliced and fried until golden brown (optional)
ingredients.name: shallot

instructions: Soak dried shitake mushrooms in 240 ml boiling water to reconstitute. Slice into strips when soft; reserve liquid for cooking.
In a stockpot, cover spareribs with cold water, then parboil ribs until froth rises to the surface.
Drain, briefly rinse spareribs under cold running water, and drain again.
In a casserole pan add the parboiled spare ribs, garlic bulb, ginseng root, shitake mushrooms, reserved liquid and additional water (to cover the meat).
Wrap cinnamon, star anise, white and black peppercorns in cheesecloth, tie with string, and add to the pan.
Gradually bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to simmer until pork is very tender (about 45–60 minutes); occasionally skim off fat from the surface.
When the meat is almost falling off the bones, discard spice bag, season with salt and pepper and add dark soy sauce and sugar.

name: Qarabagħli Mimli (Maltese Stuffed Summer Squash)
description: Maltese summer squash is hollowed and filled with one of three savory mixtures—pork and bacon, ricotta, or rice with Bolognese-style meat sauce—then finished with breadcrumbs or semolina and grated cheese.

ingredients.text: ½ ea. small onion, finely chopped
ingredients.name: onion

ingredients.text: 2 rashers rindless smoked back bacon, finely chopped
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: 2 heaped tbsp grated salt-cured cheese (e.g. sheep or goat's milk, or Parmigiano-Reggiano)
ingredients.name: salt-cured cheese

ingredients.text: 1 slice of day old bread, soaked in milk and wrung out
ingredients.name: bread

instructions: Choose one of the three savory fillings, hollow out the summer squash, fill it, top with breadcrumbs or semolina and grated cheese, and bake until golden and cooked through.

name: Kanachi (Armenian Herb Salad)
description: A fresh, aromatic assortment of herbs, radishes and green onions served raw as an appetizer or side dish.
instructions: Remove extra stem endings, yellow leaves, and damaged parts from all herbs and wash them thoroughly. Drain.
Remove roots from green onions and radishes and majority of radish leaves (leaving only the younger ones). Wash them thoroughly and drain.
Mix them up or arrange them on a plate.
Eat raw and enjoy!

name: Colcannon
description: A rich Irish mashed potato dish with cabbage, butter, cream, and melted Gouda cheese, balanced by a peppery seasoning.

ingredients.text: 450 g potatoes (floury Maris Piper or Golden Wonders are best; leave skin on if you want)
ingredients.name: potato

ingredients.text: 450 g white or savoy shredded cabbage
ingredients.name: cabbage

ingredients.text: 2 small leeks or 1 bunch of spring onion tops, chopped
ingredients.name: leek

instructions: Boil or steam the potatoes until soft, then shake the drained spuds in a deep pot with the lid on, until they crumble.
Mash the crumbled potatoes up with a fork and season with the salt, pepper, and mace/paprika, before stirring in the cream.
Add 100 g of the butter in pieces and put the lid back on, leaving the butter to melt, then stir. Transfer the mix to a clean bowl.
Blanch the cabbage in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the leeks in the remaining butter for a few minutes, then add the cabbage and toss around for a few more minutes.
Spoon the cabbage into the bowl and mix with the mashed potatoes.
Stir the gouda into the mix, leaving a little to coat the top. Put the bowl in an oven on 2/3 heat for 20 minutes or until the cheese is melted.

name: Poisson Braise (Ivorian Grilled Fish)
description: A flavorful Ivorian grilled fish marinated in olive oil, garlic, lemon, and aromatic spices, served with a baked tomato paste sauce and fresh vegetables.

ingredients.text: 3 pinches grated red or black pepper
ingredients.name: pepper

ingredients.text: 4 tablespoons all-purpose fish seasonings (e.g. grated garlic, cilantro,basil, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper)
ingredients.name: fish seasonings

ingredients.text: 2 medium-size yellow bell peppers, neatly diced
ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper

instructions: Combine 4 tablespoons of the extra-virgin olive oil in a large bowl, then add all the finely chopped garlic, lemon juice, 2 pinches of salt, 2 pinches of either the red or black pepper, and all of the fish seasonings. Mix them together very well to make a marinade.
Add the fish to the marinade, cover, and marinate in the fridge for about an hour.
Combine the tomatoes, onions, yellow pepper, zucchini, tabasco sauce, remaining extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Set aside.
Remove the fish from the fridge.
Heat a greased stovetop grill or skillet over medium heat. Add the fish and cook for at least 5 minutes. Flip and cook the other side for about another 4 minutes.
While the fish is cooking, put half of the tomato paste mixture onto a sheet pan and bake in a 350°F oven for about 7 minutes.
Put the remaining half tomato paste mixture on the plate followed by each one of the sword fish fillets. Garnish with the slice from the remaining lemon.
Serve with a side dish such as white rice or attieke.

name: Purple Plum Pie
description: A fresh plum pie with a cinnamon-spiced filling and a crumbly topping, baked until bubbly and golden brown.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. 9-inch unbaked deep dish pastry shell
ingredients.name: pastry shell

instructions: In a bowl, combine the plums, sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, and lemon juice. Transfer them to the pastry shell.
For the topping, combine the sugar, flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a small bowl; cut in butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle over the pie filling.
Bake at 375°F for 50–60 minutes or until bubbly and golden brown. Cover edges of crust during the last 20 minutes to prevent over-browning.
Cool on a wire rack.

name: Anchovy Herb Salsa Verde
description: A vibrant herb-packed salsa verde blending cured anchovies with fresh parsley, rosemary, thyme, and mint in extra-virgin olive oil. Serve with chips or grilled meat.

ingredients.text: 9 cured anchovy fillets, drained, patted dry, and minced
ingredients.name: anchovy fillet

ingredients.text: 6 tablespoons finely-chopped fresh flat-leaf curly parsley
ingredients.name: parsley

instructions: In a small bowl, mix together all ingredients.
Serve with chips or grilled meat.

name: Nigerian Lentil Porridge
description: A simple, traditional Nigerian dish of tender lentils simmered with palm oil, blended pepper, and onions. Easy to prepare and full of comforting flavor.
instructions: Pick debris and dirt from lentils then rinse.
Transfer the lentils to a pot, and cover them with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender.
Stir in the palm oil, blended pepper, and onion. Cook for few minutes.
Season with salt, and serve.

name: Apple Crusted Ham
description: A city ham baked slowly and topped with cola, chop rub, and finely minced dried apples.

ingredients.text: 1 bone-in cooked city ham, skin removed
ingredients.name: city ham

ingredients.text: ½ cup dried apples, minced finely
ingredients.name: dried apple

instructions: Place ham in a large roasting pan large side down.
Bake at 250°F for 1 hour.
Take ham out from oven and brush generously with cola. Pat on the chop rub, and then pat on apples.
Bake for another 1 ½ hours at 250°F.
Remove and let rest 10 minutes. Slice thinly and serve.

name: Sangah (Cameroonian Corn and Cassava Leaf)
description: A traditional Cameroonian dish made with corn, cassava leaf, and palm kernel extract, simmered together for a hearty, savoury meal.
instructions: Combine the water and palm nut cream in a pot. Boil for a few minutes.
Stir in the pounded cassava leaves. Cover with the lid, and boil for 20 minutes.
Stir in as much corn as desired. Season to taste with homi.
Serve hot.

name: Fried Rice
description: A simple, adaptable fried rice made with leftover rice, vegetables, egg, tofu, and soy sauce, with optional meat or seafood.

ingredients.text: Cooked rice (leftover rice that has been left refrigerated works well)
ingredients.name: rice

ingredients.text: Seafood (add curry powder for curry flavor)
ingredients.name: seafood

instructions: If using tofu, cook it.
If using onions, dice them into whatever size you prefer.
If using bok choy, separate the stalk part from the leaf part. Slice the leaf part crosswise into ¾-inch-thick strips, then tear the strips into 2-inch pieces.
