Cover the bowl with a warm and damp cloth and leave in a warm place for 2 hours.
Return to the now frothy batter. Dissolve the rest of the bicarbonate of soda in the lukewarm milk and slowly add it to the batter.
Heat a lightly greased griddle or frying pan until very hot. Using one spoonful at a time, cook the mixture for about 2 minutes on each side, turning when the bubbles that form dry out.

name: Candied Apricots
description: A very easy preparation of dried apricots simmered in a sugar syrup until reduced to a light syrup.
instructions: Soak dried apricots in a large volume of water for around 10 minutes.
Combine the 1 cup water and the sugar, and taste to adjust sweetness.
Bring sugar mixture to a boil and add apricots.
Simmer until the liquid is reduced. The traditional consistency is close to a light syrup.

name: Pulse Chutney
description: A vegan Indian chutney made from sprouted green mung beans blended with fresh ginger, green chilies, and a squeeze of lemon juice.

ingredients.text: 1 ½ inch (3 ½ cm) piece of ginger root
ingredients.name: ginger root

instructions: Soak the green mung beans for 3–4 hours. Allow to sprout.
Mince the green chilies, fresh ginger, and salt.
Grind to a paste in a mortar and pestle or food processor.
Season with lemon juice to taste.

name: Savory Pumpkin Scones
description: Savory pumpkin scones combine spring onions and nutmeg, bake until golden, and are served with cottage cheese or butter.

ingredients.text: Cottage cheese or butter, for serving (optional)
ingredients.name: cottage cheese or butter

instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (430°F).
Combine the flour, milk powder, onion and nutmeg.
Fold in the pumpkin, buttermilk and mineral water to make the dough.
Pat out the mixture onto a lightly floured board and roll out to a thickness of about ⅝ inch.
Using a 2-inch scone cutter, press out 12 rounds.
Place these on a lightly floured baking tray and bake at 220°C for 12–15 minutes or until golden.
Serve with dollops of cottage cheese or butter.

name: Peas Supreme
description: Green peas are combined with sliced mushrooms, water chestnuts, and a butter-and-flour sauce, then baked with an optional breadcrumb topping.

ingredients.text: 1 can (4 ounces) sliced mushrooms, juice reserved
ingredients.name: mushroom

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cook peas according to package instructions, then drain.
In a separate pan, melt butter.
Add mushroom juice and flour to melted butter. Stir until thickened.
Add mixture to peas, then add water chestnuts and mushrooms.
Place in medium baking pan coated with cooking spray.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs on top if desired.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until heated through.

name: Mascarpone Chocolate Sauce
description: Mascarpone cheese makes this sauce light and fluffy, while chocolate adds flavor and richness.

ingredients.text: ½ cup (125 g/4.4 oz) chocolate syrup
ingredients.name: chocolate syrup

instructions: Whisk together all ingredients in your serving bowl.
Serve as a dipping sauce with beignets or fruit; or, serve over ice cream.

name: Irish Pastie
description: A savory Northern Irish pastie made with seasoned meat, onion, parsley, breadcrumbs, and mashed potatoes, dipped in batter and deep-fried until golden brown.

ingredients.text: 1 lb ground pork or beef, cooked and drained
ingredients.name: ground pork or beef

ingredients.text: 3 medium-sized potatoes, boiled, mashed, and cooled
ingredients.name: potato

instructions: Combine the cooked meat, breadcrumbs, cooked onion, parsley, salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, water, coriander, and mashed potatoes.
Form the mixture into a disc about 3 inches in diameter.
Dip the disc into the batter so it's completely covered.
Deep-fry in 375°F oil, and remove when golden brown.
Serve hot with chips (French fries).

name: Crème Chantilly
description: A classic French whipped cream, lightly sweetened and flavoured with vanilla. It is often attributed to the 17th-century chef François Vatel, who is said to have served it at the Château de Chantilly.

ingredients.text: 1–2 tsp vanilla extract, or cognac, rum, or liqueur
ingredients.name: vanilla extract

instructions: In a chilled 3-quart bowl, whip the cream until it forms soft peaks.
Fold in the powdered sugar and flavouring.
Refrigerate until ready to use.

name: Hollandaise Sauce
description: A rich, emulsified French sauce made with egg yolks and melted butter, seasoned with lemon juice, salt, and a hint of cayenne and white pepper.

ingredients.text: 1 ½ sticks (170 g) unsalted butter, cut into pieces
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

instructions: Melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop in a small saucepan.
Pour a small amount of water into a medium-sized double boiler, making sure the water does not touch the bowl (put bowl off to the side). Bring to a simmer over medium heat, and reduce the heat.
Place egg yolks and the dry and liquid ingredients into the bowl and whisk for 1–2 minutes.
Gradually add the melted butter a little at a time, and whisk until the butter is well incorporated and mixture expands.
Place the mixture over the simmering water and whisk for 3–5 minutes, until the mixture is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
If the mixture become too thick or separates, add very small amounts of hot water until corrected.

name: Scotch Bonnet Pepper Poppers
description: Spicy Scotch bonnet peppers stuffed with a savory filling of Italian sausage, ricotta, Parmesan, and onion, then baked until tender. A fiery appetizer perfect for cocktail hour.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Fry sausage on medium-high heat, chopping as it cooks until it is the size of small peas. Drain and cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix ricotta, Parmesan, and onion with sausage to form the filling.
Cut tops of peppers about ¼ inch below the stem. Set tops aside.

With a sharp knife, scoop out seeds and membrane from each pepper. Mix as much of the seeds and membrane into the filling as needed to regulate heat. For example, moderate poppers use seeds and membrane from 6–8 peppers. For very hot poppers, leave the seeds and membranes in each pepper.
Using your fingers, stuff each pepper with filling. Replace tops.
Place poppers on parchment-lined tray and bake 15–20 minutes or until desired.
Cool slightly before serving.

name: Marinated Green Olives
description: Green olives are marinated with garlic, lemon, oregano, thyme, rosemary, and warm spices for a savory Spanish-style appetizer. Serve them with toasted almonds and fresh bread.

ingredients.text: 2 cups (16 oz/450 g) unpitted large green Spanish olives
ingredients.name: green olive

instructions: Lightly crush the olives with a mallet, or make slight slits on each olive with a knife, to ensure that the marinade permeates them.
Place the olives in a sealable glass jar and add the remaining ingredients.
Fill the jar with water and shake well.
Marinate at room temperature for several days to a week.
Serve the olives with toasted almonds and fresh bread.

name: Grapefruit and Crab Cocktail
description: A refreshing starter of chopped grapefruit piled with asparagus tips and crab, finished with a touch of mayonnaise and parsley.
instructions: Cut the grapefruits in half. Carefully remove and chop the flesh.
Divide the chopped grapefruit between 4 grapefruit hulls or 4 serving glasses.
Toss the asparagus tips with the oil, lemon juice and seasoning. Pile on top of the chopped grapefruit, and top each with a little crab.
To decorate, put 1 teaspoon mayonnaise on each portion, and garnish with parsley.

name: Apricot Wine
description: A sweet homemade apricot wine fermented with raisins, citrus, ginger, and sugar for a full month.
instructions: Wash the apricots in several changes of water, then dry and cut in halves.
Place apricots in a large crock, and pour on the warm water. Reserve ½ cup of water, and dissolve the yeast cake into it.
Stir in the sugars, fruit, raisins, and ginger.
Add the dissolved yeast and mix well.
Cover with the top of the crock and let stand.
Stir every other day.
After thirty days, strain the mixture and bottle it.

name: Asun (Goat in Pepper Sauce)
description: A Nigerian Yoruba delicacy of grilled goat meat in pepper sauce, often found at parties.

ingredients.text: Goat meat, washed and cut into smaller pieces
ingredients.name: goat meat

instructions: Place goat meat in a clean bowl. Add salt and stock cubes, and give a good massage. Marinate for at least 2 hours to properly season the meat.
Place the marinated goat meat on an electric barbecue grill or oven grill. Rub some vegetable oil on the meat.
Cover the grill, and grill for about 20 minutes. If you are using an oven grill, grill it for about 40 minutes at 180˚C.
In a food processor, blend the habanero pepper, and onions to a chunky paste.
Place a pan on medium heat. Add the grilled meat along with about ¾ cup water to introduce moisture. Let cook for about 5–10 minutes.
Stir in the pepper and onion mixture, and let cook for about 5–7 minutes.
Add the chopped bell pepper and onion. Combine thoroughly, and add salt to taste.
Add a tablespoon of vegetable oil, and combine very well. Leave to simmer for about 2 minutes.
Serve.

name: Breaded Chicken Livers
description: Traditional chicken livers are trimmed, coated in seasoned flour, and fried in hot oil until golden brown on the outside and just pink on the inside.
instructions: Trim the sinews from the livers.
Coat the livers in flour and knock off any excess.
Carefully place the livers in a hot, oiled pan.
Fry for 2–3 minutes on each side, until golden brown on the outside and just pink on the inside.
Serve hot.

name: Zwiebelrostbraten with Red Wine Onion Gravy
description: A classic Austrian dish of seared beef slices topped with caramelized onion rings and served with a rich red wine onion gravy. Perfect with sautéed potatoes or your favorite side dish.

ingredients.text: 2 slices of beef (200 g each, standing rib roast cut)
ingredients.name: beef

ingredients.text: ½ ea. onion, sliced into thin rings
ingredients.name: onion

instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil.
Add tomato paste, sugar, and Hungarian paprika, and let it sauté just a little before finally deglazing the pan with red wine.
Add broth and let it boil down until it has achieved the desired consistency. This will take about 25 minutes. Do not forget to stir the gravy every once in a while.
While the gravy is being reduced, slightly beat the meat with a meat mallet. This helps the meat to stay tender. Then rub it in mustard and add salt and pepper.
Sear the meat on both sides and cook it for another 4–5 minutes on medium heat.

Add the onion rings to the juices remaining from the meat and let them soak up the delicious flavor. Depending on how much oil and juices there are still left in the frying pan, you might have to add some oil or water in order to let the onions absorb the flavor properly.
Finally top the meat with the onion rings, add the gravy, and serve it with the desired side dish. Enjoy!

name: Couscous bil Khodra (Libyan Vegetable Couscous)
description: Fluffy couscous is cooked with a colorful medley of vegetables, chickpeas, and aromatic spices in this hearty Libyan dish. The seasoned vegetable mixture is folded together and served hot with fresh herbs.

ingredients.text: 1 cup green beans, trimmed and cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.name: green bean

ingredients.text: 1 cup canned chickpeas, rinsed and drained
ingredients.name: chickpea

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
ingredients.name: parsley or cilantro

instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the diced carrot, zucchini, bell pepper, and green beans to the pot. Stir and cook the vegetables for a few minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced tomatoes, chickpeas, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir well to coat the vegetables with the spices.
Pour the vegetable broth into the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let the vegetables simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until they are tender.
Meanwhile, prepare the couscous according to the package instructions. Typically, couscous is steamed or soaked in hot water until it becomes fluffy and tender. Fluff the cooked couscous with a fork.
Once the vegetables are cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Gently stir in the cooked couscous, ensuring that it is well-incorporated with the vegetables.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed. You can add more salt, pepper, or spices according to your preference.
Serve hot, garnished with freshly chopped parsley or cilantro.

name: Bison Meatballs Baked in Hoisin Sauce (Marvin)
description: A quick and tasty variation on meatballs, these tapered bison shapes are seasoned with onion, garlic, spices, fish sauce, and basil, then coated with hoisin sauce and baked.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Oil the bottom of a 9x12-inch Pyrex baking dish.
Thinly slice the onion to create long thin slices.
Microwave the onion slices and garlic on high for 5 minutes.
Grind the cumin, coriander, peppercorns, cloves, and salt together using a mortar and pestle.
Roughly mix the softened onions and garlic, bison, rice, spice grind, fish sauce, and basil.
Shape the meat mixture into tapered cylinders (similar to small sweet potatoes) and place into the baking dish. The Marvins should be about 1¼ inch diameter in the middle and 5 inches long.
Coat the Marvins with hoisin sauce.
Bake for 20–25 minutes in the preheated oven.

name: Saj Bread III
description: A Turkish-style flatbread made from flour, water, milk, and yeast, rolled out and cooked on a heated griddle.
instructions: Mix ingredients and knead thoroughly.
Cover the dough and let rest for about 30 minutes.
Once again knead the dough, and divide into smaller portions.
Roll out each portion over a flat surface with a rolling pin. Surface should be sprinkled with flour to prevent sticking.
Take up rolled-out dough with a wooden rod and apply it to heated griddle. Turn over and cook on the reverse side.
Remove and let cool. Fold and store.

name: Loco Moco (Rice with Egg and Hamburger)
description: A hearty loco moco with steamed rice layered with a hamburger patty, sunny-side-up eggs, and hot gravy.
instructions: Cook the eggs sunny side up.
Cook the hamburger to your preference.
Steam the rice, and heat up the gravy.
Assemble the components in the following order: Rice on bottom; Hamburger on top of rice; Eggs; Gravy.

name: Yamarita (Nigerian Fried Yam)
description: A Nigerian dish of tender yam pieces dipped in a spiced egg and flour batter, then deep-fried until golden brown.

ingredients.text: Yam, peeled and sliced into rectangles
ingredients.name: yam

instructions: Rinse the yam pieces in water.
Bring a pot of water to boil. Add the yam pieces, and boil for a few minutes until the yam is tender.
Drain the yams.
Combine the eggs, pepper, salt, and seasoning cubes.
Combine flour, thyme, and curry. Stir this mixture into the eggs. Add a little water as needed to get a thin batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot. Aim for about 350–375°F.
Dip the yam pieces in the batter, and transfer the battered pieces to the hot oil. Fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove yamarita from the oil with a slotted spoon, and drain any remaining oil.
Serve hot.

name: Microwaved Scrambled Egg
description: A quick and easy scrambled egg cooked in the microwave, ready in just about a minute. Simply crack eggs and butter into a cup and heat in short bursts.
instructions: Crack the eggs and butter in a coffee cup.
Microwave on high power for 30 seconds.
Remove from the microwave, stir, and replace.
Cook for another 30 seconds on high.

name: Vorschmack (Finnish Ground Meat)
description: A traditional Finnish dish of lamb and beef roasted with onions, then ground with herring and anchovies and slow-baked to a thick, porridge-like consistency. Serve hot with pickled beetroot, pickled cucumber and sour cream.

ingredients.text: 4 lb (1800 g) boned leg of lamb, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
ingredients.name: lamb

ingredients.text: ½ lb (225 g) boned beef, diced
ingredients.name: beef

instructions: Let the herring fillets soak in cold water over night. Dry the fillets on paper towels.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (220°C). Arrange the meat and onion in a greased baking dish and roast on the medium shelf until golden brown (about 15–20 minutes).

Let the dish cool, and then grind the contents with the herring and anchovy using a meat grinder. In a large bowl, add some water to the mixture to give it the consistency of thick porridge. Season with white pepper and garlic.
Place the contents in a baking dish. Spread out some tomato paste over the surface of the mixture. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 2 hours.
Add water if the Vorschmack looks dry. If the consistency is too light, continue baking to evaporate excess water. The consistency should resemble thick hot porridge.
Serve hot with baked potatoes, smetana, and a shot of ice cold vodka, filled to the rim.

name: Undhiyu (Gujarati Mixed Vegetables)
description: A traditional Gujarati mixed vegetable dish featuring spiced dough balls (muthia) and stuffed vegetables, slow-cooked with aromatic spices and fresh herbs.
instructions: Grind the ingredients for each chutney, and mix them together. It's best to make and serve all three, as they will each balance each other.
Combine the flour and channa powder. Mix in rice flour, oil, chilli powder, lemon, green chillies, and sugar to make a dough. Adjust consistency with water as needed.
Add methi leaves, then shape the mixture into small, elongated balls.
Fry the muthia in oil, and keep aside.
Crush the thoghari dal, green chillies, garlic, and ginger. Mix in the coriander powder, all the other spices, fresh grated coconut, and coriander leaves to make a masala paste.
Cut slits in the eggplant and potatoes, and stuff with the masala mixture. There will be masala left over.
Heat a small amount of oil in a pot. Add the mustard seeds, hing, onion, ghenasu, yams, carrots, peas, lima beans, and remaining masala. Stir well to combine.
Add the stuffed potatoes and eggplants. Add the muthia along with a little water to keep from burning.
Cook in a pressure cooker—just one whistle is enough.
To serve, pour a little of each chutney on top of the undhiyu. Top it with coriander leaves and coconut. Serve along with warm jalebi.

name: Chocolate Chip Pancakes I
description: Chocolate chip pancakes made with milk, eggs, vanilla, and melted butter, cooked until golden brown and served hot.

ingredients.text: 6 oz (170 g) semisweet chocolate chips, or less to taste
ingredients.name: semisweet chocolate chip

instructions: Combine the butter and milk in a small saucepan.
Place over low heat just until warm and the butter is melted. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt; mix well.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with a fork. Whisk in the milk mixture.
Add the dry ingredients and mix just until barely blended.
Add the chocolate chips and mix.
Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium heat.
Add about 1 teaspoon of butter and melt until bubbly.
Ladle 3 tablespoons of batter for each pancake onto the hot surface and cook until bubbly on the top and golden brown on the bottom.
Flip and cook until golden brown on the other side, about 30 seconds more.
Repeat until all the batter is used.
Serve hot.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken
description: Tender chicken pieces cooked in a sweet honey and garlic sauce that thickens and caramelizes to a rich golden glaze.
instructions: Chop chicken into small pieces.
Coat frying pan with a thin layer of olive oil.
Add chicken pieces to frying pan.
Cover the chicken with honey and add garlic.
Cook over medium heat until the mixture thickens and darkens and the chicken is cooked. Don't let it go on too long or the sauce can burn.

name: Baba Ganoush
description: A creamy, smoky Middle Eastern and Mediterranean dip made from roasted eggplant blended with tahini, garlic, and olive oil. Perfect with pita bread or flatbread.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (1 to 1½ pounds) medium-large eggplant, any variety
ingredients.name: eggplant

ingredients.text: Paprika or cayenne pepper, as a garnish
ingredients.name: paprika

instructions: Roast the eggplant. This can be done in a variety of ways, but the flesh should be fully cooked and the skin should be burned and falling off easily.

An effective method is to prick the eggplant and place it a few inches under a broiler, turning it as the exposed skin blackens, about every 3-4 minutes. Place a pan underneath to catch the juices, and discard them.
Scrape off the eggplant skin. It's alright if you miss a few burned bits.

Finely chop or blend the eggplant flesh with the rest of the ingredients. The consistency should be smooth. Reserve a bit of the olive oil, and drizzle that over the top. Sprinkle with some paprika or cayenne.

name: Skillet Cornbread
description: A delicious, easy-to-make Southern cornbread baked in a skillet for a golden-brown crust, often served beside a pot of brown beans.

ingredients.text: 1 ¼ cups yellow or white cornmeal
ingredients.name: cornmeal

ingredients.text: 2–3 tbsp melted butter or pan drippings
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C)
Grease the skillet with bacon drippings (ideal) or oil. Butter isn't recommended, since it can burn when you preheat the skillet.
Preheat the skillet until the drippings/oil is smoking. This ensures a good crust on the bottom of the cornbread.
In a bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Thoroughly mix the sifted ingredients together and add the corn meal.
In a second bowl, beat the egg well. Add the melted butter (or pan drippings) and the milk and continue to beat until well mixed.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix using fast strokes. Take care not to overmix.
Pour the batter into the skillet and place in the oven.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. The cornbread should have a golden brown color when done, and a knitting needle or knife-point will come out "dry" when inserted in the bread.

name: Queen's Soup
description: A smooth rice soup made with milk and butter, then finished with fowl stock for a rich, comforting bowl.
instructions: Put the ground rice into a saucepan. Gradually add the milk.
Cook gently for 12 minutes in a bain-marie, stirring the whole time, until very smooth.
Add the butter, and pass through a sieve.
Mix the fowl stock, and serve immediately.

name: Coconut Cream Filled Cake with Meringue (Bienmesabe)
description: A layered sponge cake soaked in coconut-rum syrup and filled with rich coconut custard, topped with a toasted meringue. This beloved family dessert combines fluffy cake, creamy coconut filling, and crisp meringue in every bite.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
In the bowl of an electric mixer, beat the eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy.
Add the flour, baking powder, and vanilla extract; mix until just combined.
Transfer the batter to the prepared pan. Bake 30–35 minutes at 350°F or until a toothpick inserted in the center tests clean.
Cool cake completely on a wire rack. Meanwhile, make coconut cream filling.
In a large bowl, whisk together sugar, coconut milk, yolks, shredded coconut, and cornstarch.
In a large saucepan, combine milk and remaining 1 cup sugar; heat over medium until sugar dissolves and milk is steaming.
Gradually whisk the hot milk into egg mixture; return the custard mixture to the saucepan.
Cook, stirring, until custard thickens, 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour the custard into a heat-proof bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Set aside to cool completely, about 1 hour (or up to overnight in the refrigerator).
While coconut cream and cake cool, make cake syrup: combine water and sugar in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Transfer to a bowl with coconut milk and rum and stir to combine.
For the meringue, combine sugar and water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar, for 4 minutes.
In the bowl of an electric mixer, beat the egg whites and remaining 1 tablespoon sugar. With the motor running, gradually beat in the syrup mixture in a slow, steady stream.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Use a serrated knife to cut cake horizontally into 2 layers.
Brush the bottom layer with syrup and spread with coconut cream.
Add the second cake layer and repeat with syrup and coconut cream.
Spread the meringue over the cake.
Transfer the cake to the oven for 2 to 3 minutes or until the meringue is toasted.

name: Shortbread
description: A classic crumbly butter cookie made from a simple ratio of butter, sugar and flour, baked until lightly golden.

ingredients.text: 380 g (1 ½ cup / 13 ½ oz) all-purpose flour
ingredients.name: flour

ingredients.text: 110 g (½ cup / 4 oz) white granulated sugar
ingredients.name: sugar

instructions: Preheat the oven to 140°C (275°F or Gas Mark 1).
Cream the butter with the sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift the flour and salt into the mixture and work into the fat and sugar until completely amalgamated.
Shape the dough into a ball and roll out to about 1.3 cm (½ inch) thick. The dough may need to be chilled for 10–15 minutes for easier handling.
Cut into squares or rectangles and prick the tops with a fork in two parallel lines.
Bake in the oven for 30–40 minutes or until the shortbread is lightly browned.
Leave them on a cooling rack to cool.
Store in a cool place in an airtight container.

name: Christmas Cake
description: A traditional fruitcake packed with currants, sultanas, glacé cherries, raisins, candied peel, and almonds, steeped in spirits before a slow bake.

ingredients.text: 300 g lightly-salted soft margarine (The "Stork" brand is traditional)
ingredients.name: margarine

instructions: Place all the fruit in a large bowl and pour the spirits over the mixture.
Cover the bowl in foil and leave in a cool place.
Mix and stir the fruit every day for at least three days; after a fortnight most of the alcohol will have soaked in and further soaking has no benefit.
Beat together the sugar and margarine with the eggs.
Add the almonds and black treacle, and mix further.
Sieve the flours and the mixed spice into the mixture, beating until a smooth mixture results.
Combine with the pre-prepared fruit (above) and place in a cake tin lined with baking parchment.
Bake at a low temperature (140°C / 275°F / Gas mark 1) for at least 4 hours. It may take up to 5 hours, depending on the oven.
Once a knife comes out clean, remove from the oven and allow to cool fully.
Stored in an airtight box the cake should keep for at least four months.

name: Shepherd's Pie III
description: A hearty British-style shepherd's pie with minced lamb and mixed vegetables in a rich gravy, topped with creamy mashed potatoes and baked until golden.

ingredients.text: 5 ml olive oil or other cooking oil
ingredients.name: olive oil

instructions: Peel and chop the potatoes. Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes whilst preparing the rest of the meal.
Cut the minced lamb and add the garlic.
Next gently heat some olive oil in a frying pan and add the meat and garlic.
Then add the vegetables, ketchup, stock cube (or gravy) and cook on a very low heat for 5 minutes.
Add flour and water and mix well.
Cook the mixture for about 25 minutes and stir every few minutes.
Once the potatoes are ready drain them, add a touch of milk and butter (or margarine) and mash.
Pour the mixture into an oven dish then add the mashed potatoes on top. Cover all of the lamb mixture.
Bake in the oven at 200°C for about 15–20 minutes and take it out when the potatoes are turning golden.

name: Garlic Seared Halibut
description: Tender halibut fillets are marinated in garlic, white wine, and lemon, then pan-seared until golden and finished with a silky butter-wine sauce.
instructions: Combine garlic, ¼ cup white wine, lemon, and ½ cup chicken broth in a gallon-size zip-top bag. Add fish and toss to coat. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Take fish out of marinade and reserve marinade. Sprinkle on both sides liberally with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper and set aside.

Melt 1 tbsp butter with olive oil in a 12-inch stainless steel sauté pan over medium high heat. Add fish and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 3–4 minutes per side. Remove and keep warm.
Deglaze pan with reserved marinade and reserved wine and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cook until reduced by ⅓.
Whisk in butter 1 tbsp at a time, waiting until the tbsp before it is melted before adding a new one. Spoon sauce over halibut and serve warm.

name: Firecracker Ribs
description: These ribs pack a kick from cayenne pepper, slow-baked in a foil pouch with white wine, soy sauce, and honey for a sweet-spicy glaze.
instructions: Season ribs with rub, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 225°F (110°C).
Combine liquid ingredients.
Place ribs in a large foil pouch, pour in liquid mixture, and seal pouch.
Bake at 225°F (110°C) for 5–6 hours.
Remove ribs from pouches and set aside. Save liquid.
Reduce liquid by half over high heat, then lightly brush some reduction on top of ribs and place under a preheated broiler. Watch carefully and remove when nicely browned.
Rest 15 minutes; serve.

name: Tofu Scramble II
description: A savory tofu scramble with vegetarian bacon, garlic, green onion, turmeric, and nutritional yeast, cooked until it resembles scrambled eggs.

ingredients.text: 2 strips Smart vegetarian bacon or other breakfast meat substitute
ingredients.name: vegetarian bacon

ingredients.text: ½ large block of firm tofu
ingredients.name: firm tofu

ingredients.text: A couple dashes of ground turmeric
ingredients.name: ground turmeric

instructions: Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high heat. Add the bacon and cook, but don't cook it too long. Once it's done, chop it into small pieces.
Press as much water from the tofu as possible, then use a cheese grater to grate the tofu into semi-small chunks. You could probably mash it a bit with a fork instead, but grating is a lot quicker.
Add the onion, garlic, bacon, turmeric, and liquid aminos to the tofu. Stir gently until you are satisfied that everything is well mixed.
Put it in the hot pan (it should sizzle a bit), and sprinkle the nutritional yeast flakes over the top.
Keep stirring occasionally for about 10 minutes or until you've got the desired look of scrambled "eggs."
Try serving with hash browns.

name: Gâteau Nantais (Nantes Cake)
description: A traditional French pound cake made with almond flour and rum, soaked after baking and finished with a rum glaze for a rich, moist treat.
instructions: Cream the butter and sugar for 2–3 minutes by hand or using a mixer at low speed.
Add almond flour, and mix to combine.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs with a fork. Incorporate them into the butter and sugar mixture.
Add the flour and 2 tablespoons of rum.
Pour the batter into a buttered cake pan.
Bake for 45 minutes at gas mark 5 (150 °C).
As soon as you take the cake out of the oven, sprinkle the cake with mix of 2 tablespoons of rum and 2 tablespoons of water. Cool completely, then unmold.
When the cake is cold, make the icing by combining the icing sugar and rum. Add a few drops of water if necessary, stirring well between each addition of water, to make a thick but flowing glaze.
Pour the icing on the cake, and spread it well.

name: Jerk Grilled Salmon
description: Salmon fillets are marinated in a vibrant jerk spice blend of Scotch bonnet peppers, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, thyme, and ginger, then grilled over charcoal until pink and flaky.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24 ounces) salmon fillets with skin on one side
ingredients.name: salmon

ingredients.text: 2 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, stemmed and seeded if you like
ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper

ingredients.text: ¼ tsp freshly-ground Grains of Paradise, or more pepper
ingredients.name: grains of paradise

instructions: In a blender or food processor, purée all ingredients except salmon and oil until smooth. With the machine running, slowly drizzle in the oil.
Pour into a gallon size zip-top bag. Add salmon and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes.
Heat about 28 charcoal briquets in a large chimney starter. Disperse evenly around the bottom of the grill.
Reapply the grate. Quickly grease the grate with the oil-soaked towel.
Add the salmon skin side down and cook, covered, turning often, until pink throughout and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Remove to a plate and cover with aluminum foil. Let rest 5–7 minutes before serving warm.

name: Stuffed Portabella Mushrooms
description: Portobello mushrooms are topped with garlic and balsamic vinegar, then filled with a savory mixture of egg, cottage cheese, mozzarella, and crushed crackers before baking.

ingredients.text: 4 oz mozzarella cheese (fresh or regular), diced or grated
ingredients.name: mozzarella cheese

ingredients.text: 10 Saltine crackers, crushed or ½ cup bread crumbs
ingredients.name: saltine cracker or bread crumb

instructions: Generously sprinkle vinegar over the mushrooms, and top with garlic. Leave for 30 minutes or so.
Combine the egg, cheeses, crackers and seasonings in a bowl. Mix well. Spoon the mixture onto the mushrooms.
Bake at 350°F for 40 minutes.

name: Spanish Flan
description: A classic Spanish custard dessert with a glossy caramel topping, made by blending eggs, vanilla, and two kinds of milk, then baking in a bain marie until set.
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F.
Combine all ingredients except caramel topping in blender. Blend for 2 minutes.
Place a thin layer of caramel topping on bottom of a round pie pan. Pour egg mixture on top of caramel topping.
Place the smaller pie pan in a larger pan filled with enough water so that it comes about 1 inch up the side of the smaller pan. This will act as a bain marie and stop the flan from burning.
Place both pans in oven. Cook for 1 hour or until center is firm.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Place a round dish over the top of the smaller pan, and flip it over to unmold it. The flan can be served on the dish.

name: Silvash Gombotz (Hungarian Plum Dumplings)
description: A traditional Hungarian dessert of warm potato dumplings filled with fresh plums, plum jam, or plum compote, served with breadcrumbs fried in butter.

ingredients.text: Fresh plums, plum jam or plum compote
ingredients.name: plum

instructions: Cook potatoes until very soft (at least an hour). Peel and mash with a fork.
Add the egg to the mixture, along with the little salt and oil. Mix well.
Mix in enough flour to make a smooth dough.
Knead the potato dough, then roll it out into a thin sheet (about 5 mm thick), and cut into squares.
Put half a plum or 1 tsp of plum jam on each square. Wrap the dough around the filling and seal the edges.
Cook in boiling water for 10–15 minutes.
Serve with bread crumbs fried in butter.

name: Tamate Ka Kut (Hyderabadi Tomato Curry)
description: A rich Hyderabadi tomato curry thickened with gram flour and tempered with cumin, curry leaves and dried chillies, finished with hard-boiled eggs and fresh herbs.

ingredients.text: 10 large, ripe tomatoes, washed and quartered
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: 2 dried red chillies, each split into two
ingredients.name: dried red chilli

instructions: Put the quartered tomato pieces in a large non-stick saucepan on medium low heat. Add a cup of water to it, mix, and cover with the lid. Let it cook till the tomatoes are mushy and soft, giving it a stir every once in a while. Let it cool.
Once cooled, pour the tomatoes into a blender container and add the gram flour. Blend until puréed. If you are using canned crushed tomato, add the gram flour to it and mix well.
Strain this mixture through a wire mesh strainer back into the saucepan. Throw away the leftover seeds and skin in the strainer. Add 2 cups water to it and let it simmer.

Pour oil into a small frying pan at medium heat and add the cumin seeds, whole red chillies, garlic pod, and curry leaves when the oil heats up. As they start to splutter, remove from heat and add this to the tomato sauce being cooked in the saucepan.

Add the cumin and coriander seed powder, red chilli powder and salt to the sauce and mix well. Bring it to a boil, and let it cook at medium low heat until the raw aroma of gram flour is gone. You can add a little water to it if required. Taste and adjust the salt and chilli powder.

Make light slits on all 4 sides of the eggs, making sure the slits are just on the surface and not deep into the yolk. Add these to the simmering tomato sauce. Cook the tomato sauce until the raw smell of the gram flour is gone, about 30 minutes. Keep stirring it occasionally.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and mint just before serving.
Pour it into a warm bowl and serve it warm.

name: Nigerian Spring Rolls
description: Crispy, deep-fried spring rolls with a savory filling of fish or meat, potatoes, and vegetables, prepared as a Nigerian variation.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water. Drain and mash with a fork.
Heat a few teaspoons of oil in a pan. Add the onion and garlic, and stir fry until the onions are translucent.
Add the minced fish/meat, and cook for about 10 minutes or until the meat is fully cooked.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and chopped tomatoes. Cook until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the carrots, cabbage, scallion, bell pepper, and chili peppers. Cook until vegetables are soft.
Stir in stock cube, and let cool.
Combine some flour and water to make a thin "glue".
Spread a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface. Spread 2 tablespoons of the cooked filling near the edge of the wrapper. Roll the wrapper up from the bottom until the filling is just enclosed.
Fold the left and right sides over the filling to make sure there are no gaps on the sides for the filling to squeeze out. Continue rolling up the spring roll into a small log.
Brush a little bit of the flour glue on the open edge of the wrapper, and fully fold the wrapper before placing the spring roll with the glued surface facing down.
Repeat the spring roll assembly process with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat enough oil in a pot for deep frying. Working in batches, add the spring rolls, and fry until dark golden and crispy on all sides. Remove from the oil and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot.

name: Pan-Seared Filet Mignon
description: Tender filet mignon crusted with smoky spices and seared in a cast iron pan, then finished with a fiery cognac sauce.

ingredients.text: 4 ea. (24–32 ounces) filet mignons, 1 ½ inch thick
ingredients.name: filet mignon

instructions: Heat a 10-inch cast iron skillet over high heat for 7–10 minutes.
Meanwhile, brush steaks with Dijon mustard. Combine seasonings and press into meat. Brush with olive oil.
Place steaks in pan and cook 2 minutes per side. Insert a probe thermometer into one of the steaks.
Place the pan in a 375°F oven and cook until internal temperature reaches 140°F.
Remove steaks from pan and keep warm.

Heat pan over high heat 4 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the cognac. If the pan is hot enough, the alcohol will ignite by itself. If not, carefully light with a long match or firestick. Shake pan until flames die.
Once flames die, return pan to high heat. Boil until reduced by half.
Drizzle over steaks and serve warm.

name: Pasta Romanov
description: A quick, stylish pasta dish tossed with melted mascarpone, tomato purée, vodka, and caviar, then finished with lemon.

ingredients.text: Pasta (taglietelli, spaghetti, or angel hair preferred)
ingredients.name: pasta

ingredients.text: Mascarpone cheese (or similar mild cheese like ricotta)
ingredients.name: mascarpone

instructions: Boil a pot of salted water, add the pasta, and cook until al dente. Drain.
Melt the cheese (do not overheat) and stir in a little tomato puree to turn it salmon pink.
Add a slug (a couple tablespoons) of vodka to the melted cheese.
Add caviar to the cheese and toss the drained pasta in it to coat.
Cut lemon into wedges and use as garnish with a teaspoon or two of caviar.
Serve with champagne or crisp white wine.

name: Green Chicken Curry with Coconut Milk
description: A hearty chicken green curry made with coconut milk, leeks, and bell peppers, then seasoned with basil and fish sauce.
instructions: Grind all the ingredients for the curry paste together with a mortar and pestle.
Fry the curry paste with oil for a couple of minutes in a big pot.
Add leeks and bell pepper.
Shortly after, add the coconut milk, cover, and let simmer 20–30 minutes.
Meanwhile, crush garlic into a bowl with some soy sauce and mix in the chicken meat cubes. Let marinate.
Fry the marinated meat with oil.
Add the cooked meat to the curry pot, then season with basil, salt, and fish sauce to taste.

name: Sour Cream Dip
description: A creamy, herb-packed dip blending sour cream and mayonnaise with fresh dill, chives, and parsley. Perfect for chilling and serving as a quick, refreshing accompaniment.

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp chopped fresh dill, or 1 tbsp dried and crumbled dill
ingredients.name: dill

instructions: Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, dill, onion, chives, and parsley.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then chill.

name: Surinamese Chicken Pot Pie (Pastei)
description: A traditional Surinamese pastei brought by Jewish settlers, featuring a buttery pastry crust filled with chicken, vegetables, and hard-boiled eggs. Best served with plain white rice.

ingredients.text: 3 large pieces of chicken (drumstick, thigh, breast, etc.)
ingredients.name: chicken

ingredients.text: Salt or bouillon cubes to taste
ingredients.name: salt

ingredients.text: 1 fresh chile pepper or bell pepper (optional)
ingredients.name: chile pepper

instructions: Cream the butter with an electric mixer or a wooden spoon. Keep adding little bits of the water until the butter has absorbed it all.

Sift the flour, baking powder and the salt all together and add this through the butter gradually. To see if the dough is rollable, press your finger on it and if the dough doesn't stick to it, it's fine. However, if the dough does stick, add about 25 more grams of flour.
Divide the dough in half, then roll out each piece.
Line a buttered baking pan or aluminum foil pan with one sheet of dough. Press the dough to the corners of the pan so that as much filling as possible can go in.
Wash the chicken if necessary.
Simmer the chicken, 100 g butter, some of the chopped onion, 2–3 bouillon cubes, fresh pepper, bay leaf, and some allspice in about 1–1½ cups of water for 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken, and strip it into little pieces, discarding the bones.
Put the rest of the butter in the broth in which the chicken had been boiled.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan, then add the remaining chopped onion.
Add the chicken. After a minute add the chopped tomatoes, the peas and carrots, and the celery. Every so often, add a little bit of the chicken broth to the pan so that it won't burn.
Add the chopped pickles.
After all the broth has been added and the whole seems good, taste to see if it has enough salt; if not, add some. Cool slightly, then mix in the ketchup and Worcestershire sauce.
Transfer the chicken mixture to the dough-lined pan until it is nicely filled.
Slice the boiled eggs and place them on top of the filling in the pan.
Top the mixture with the second sheet of dough. Seal the edges as best as possible.
Put the pastei in a preheated oven, and bake for about ¾ hour.
A few minutes before you take it out of the oven, you can lightly brush the top with some whisked egg to make the top shiny and a little crisp.

name: Rosto
description: Rosto is a traditional Italian one-pot dish that delivers two complete courses in one go: pasta with rich tomato sauce, followed by tender sliced pork with potatoes, carrots and mushrooms.

ingredients.text: ½ kg penne or macaroni pasta
ingredients.name: penne pasta

ingredients.text: 1 tin ‘tomate triturado’ (tomato paste, or three peeled, de-seeded and puréed tomatoes)
ingredients.name: tomato paste

instructions: Fry crushed garlic clove and chopped onions until soft.
Add tomatoes; fry for 5 minutes, then add pork loin and brown until sealed.
Add tin of tomate triturado and a dash of white wine.
Add potatoes and carrots, then cook until meat, potatoes and carrots are done.
Add the mushrooms about 10 minutes before the end.
Add salt, pepper and sugar to taste.
Boil the macaroni until al dente.
Remove the meat from the stew and slice.
Serve meat, potatoes and pasta on same plate, pouring sauce over pasta and topping with grated cheese.

name: Hamburger
description: A savoury hamburger made with hand-shaped ground beef patties, pan-fried or grilled and served on a bun with optional vegetables, cheese, and condiments. Let the patties rest before serving so the juices do not burst out at the first bite.

ingredients.text: Vegetables (lettuce, sprouts, tomato, onion etc; optional)
ingredients.name: vegetables

instructions: Shape the ground beef by hand into burger patties. You should get between 4–6 burgers from 500 g (1.1 lb) of beef.

If adding optional ingredients, either season the outside or mix into the beef before forming the patties. Overworking the beef will result in mushy meat that won't stick together, so only mix the minimum necessary and do so by hand.
Pan-fry or grill the patties for about 4–5 minutes on each side for burgers that aren't too thick.
Ensure your burgers are fully cooked through before serving.
If your burgers are quite thick or if you are unsure, you can cut one open to ensure the insides are browned. If the insides are red, there is a chance that the meat is not fully cooked.
Alternately, you can insert a meat thermometer into the center of the burger; if the temperature reads less than 71°C (160°F), your burger is undercooked.
Let the burger rest for several minutes before serving to let the juices cool down and not burst out at first bite.
Serve each burger on a bun, optionally with relish, sliced pickles, ketchup, mayonnaise, mustard, ranch dressing, cheese, lettuce, tomatoes and/or onions.

name: Niçoise Salad
description: A fresh French salad of raw vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, and anchovies or tuna, tossed with basil and olive oil.

ingredients.text: 200 g small fresh broad (fava) beans or green beans
ingredients.name: broad bean

ingredients.text: 12 small fresh artichokes, cut into rounds
ingredients.name: artichoke

ingredients.text: 12 anchovy fillets, or 300 g tuna steak
ingredients.name: anchovy

instructions: Cut the tomatoes in quarters and salt them lightly once.
Cut the eggs into quarters or slices.
Cut the anchovies into 3–4 chunks (if using tuna, cut into similarly sized pieces).
Peel the cucumber and finely slice it.
Cut the green peppers into thin rings, and do the same with the onions.
Cut the garlic in two and rub the sides and bottom of a large salad bowl with it.
Toss all the ingredients except the tomatoes into the bowl.
Drain the tomatoes, re-salt lightly and add to salad.
In a separate bowl, mix 6 spoonfuls of olive oil with the basil, pepper, and salt and pour over salad.
Refrigerate before serving.

name: Microwave Chocolate Chip Cookie
description: A quick single-serving chocolate chip cookie made in the microwave in just minutes. Soft, sweet, and perfect for a fast dessert craving.

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened at room temperature
ingredients.name: unsalted butter

ingredients.text: ¼ cup (45 g / 1.5 oz) light brown sugar
ingredients.name: light brown sugar

ingredients.text: ½ cup (70 g / 2.5 oz) all-purpose flour
ingredients.name: all-purpose flour

ingredients.text: ½ cup (40 g / 1.5 oz) dark chocolate chips
ingredients.name: dark chocolate chips

instructions: Line a large microwave-safe plate with parchment.
Beat the butter and sugar in a small bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Sift the flour and salt and fold into the butter mixture. Fold in most of the chocolate chips.
Scoop the dough into center of plate. Decorate with remaining chocolate chips.
Microwave the cookie for 1.5–2 minutes, depending on microwave's power.
Leave the cookie to cool.

name: Balangu Jollof (Nigerian Ram and Seasoned Rice)
description: A Nigerian rice dish made with ram meat, finely chopped onion, tomato paste, thyme, curry powder, and suya spice.
instructions: Season the meat with onion and salt, and fry in a pot of oil.
Stir in the tomato paste. Add some water, and boil for a few minutes.
Stir in the rice, thyme, curry powder, and suya spice.
Cover the pot and cook until the rice has absorbed the liquid.

name: Thousand Island Dressing
description: A smooth, tangy pink salad dressing made with mayonnaise, ketchup, white vinegar, and sweet pickle relish. It can also be served as a sandwich spread.
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a blender, and process till smooth. The goal is to have a pink smooth sauce.
Pour the sauce into a bowl and chill covered in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes prior to use.

name: Spaghetti Sauce
description: A simple spaghetti sauce made with canned tomato puree, oregano, and basil. Best served hot over lightly-cooked pasta, with optional mushrooms or meat added at the table.

ingredients.text: 29 ounces (922 g) plain canned tomato puree or ground tomatoes
ingredients.name: tomato puree

ingredients.text: Cooked ground beef or bits of steak (optional, may be added at the table)
ingredients.name: beef

instructions: For more efficient use of the herbs, grind them well with the salt. The salt helps to grind the herbs. If you skip this step, increase the amount of herbs. Also double the herbs if you prefer.
Mix everything in a pot.
Bring to a boil while stirring to prevent the sauce from burning to the bottom of the pan.
Immediately remove from the heat and serve. Hot tomato products lose tomato flavor, so don't delay.

name: Tomato Paste and Ham Sandwiches (Pan Tomaca)
description: A classic Catalan-style tapa of lightly toasted bread rubbed with garlic and topped with fresh tomato, olive oil, salt, and slices of cured ham. Simple, fresh, and perfect as a starter or sandwich.
instructions: Peel the tomatoes. Optionally remove the seeds.
Blend the tomatoes, 1 tbsp olive oil, and salt to taste in an appropriate vessel with an immersion blender.
Cut the French bread loaf in appropriate sized portions and open those in halves. Optionally toast them very lightly also to increase tenderness.
Spread the mixture on one surface and sprinkle with olive oil. Place a slice of cured ham on top, and optionally cover with the other portion of bread for a sandwich, or leave uncovered for a tapa.

name: Khao Pad Gai (Thai Chicken Fried Rice)
description: Thai-style fried rice with chicken, inspired by street vendors in the central region of Thailand. Cold cooked jasmine rice is stir-fried with eggs, vegetables, and Thai sauces, then plated with cucumber, tomato, and green onion garnishes.

ingredients.text: 1 large chicken breast, sliced in thin strips
ingredients.name: chicken breast

ingredients.text: 4 cups (900 g) cooked Thai jasmine rice, refrigerated overnight
ingredients.name: Thai jasmine rice

ingredients.text: ½ yellow onion, chopped into strips
ingredients.name: yellow onion

ingredients.text: ¾ roma tomato, cut into strips
ingredients.name: roma tomato

ingredients.text: ¾ cup (180 g) cilantro, finely chopped
ingredients.name: cilantro

ingredients.text: 3 slices cucumber, peeled (note: can run fork down all sides lightly if desired)
ingredients.name: cucumber

instructions: Make sure that all of the ingredients are prepared and set aside in small bowls by the stove.
Add about 4 Tbsp peanut oil to the wok, and turn the flame to high heat.
When the oil is almost smoking, add the chicken strips and push around vigorously with a wok spoon or spatula.
When the chicken seems as if it is starting to brown, push it up the side of the wok and crack the eggs into the wok.
Stir the eggs around a bit. When almost fully scrambled, mix in the chicken and stir around for 30 seconds more.
Push the eggs/chicken to the side, add some more oil, and throw in the tomato and onion.
Stir-fry for about 5 minutes. They will not look done, but in the end, they will be fine.
Add the cold cooked rice and mix it all in.
Turn the heat to low, then add a few splashes of fish sauce and soy sauce to taste.
Add sugar, salt, MSG, a splash of vinegar, and chili sauce if wanted.
Lastly, add the fried garlic on top. Stir it all in and turn off the heat.
On a large platter, arrange the garnishes on a lettuce leaf, and plate the fried rice next to it.
Eat the garnishes with the fried rice.

name: Chickpea Flour Dessert (Mysore Pak)
description: A sweet Indian confection made with roasted gram flour, sugar syrup, cardamom, and ghee, cooked to a crispy finish and cut into pieces.
instructions: Roast the gram flour in a small amount of ghee.
Combine the sugar, cardamom, and a splash of water in a saucepan. Boil it until the syrup reaches the single thread stage. If more than one thread can be drawn, then more water needs to be added.
Mix half the roasted gram flour into the hot sugar syrup, keeping the heat on.
Gradually stir half the ghee into the gram flour mixture. Keep stirring the mixture until the ghee is absorbed.
Repeat with the remaining gram flour and ghee. More ghee can be added just until the mixture stops taking in more ghee.
After the mixture is boiled, it turns into crispy, bubble form. Pour it in a pan, and let cool.
Cut it into pieces of desired shapes.

name: Classic Puff Pastry
description: A classic puff pastry dough made with bread flour, butter, and water, layered through multiple folds to create a flaky, buttery pastry.

ingredients.text: 2½ lbs (40 oz / 1125 g) room temp butter
ingredients.name: butter

instructions: Mix the salt in with the larger portion of flour, then add the cold water and work it into a dough.
Knead about 80 times to make a soft dough and build some gluten.
Flatten out the dough (allows quicker cooling) and refrigerate.
Combine the room temperature butter and the smaller portion of flour and mix well to form a soft paste that is easy to spread.
Take the chilled dough and roll it into a rectangle about ¼–½ inch thick.
Leaving a 1-inch margin around the edge, spread the butter out over ⅔ of the dough.
Fold the dough into thirds like you were folding a letter, starting with the portion of dough with no butter.
Refrigerate for 20–30 minutes to allow the dough to relax, and so the butter doesn't get displaced when rolling out again.
Roll out the dough again to a large rectangle the same size as the first.
Fold the dough so that the two short edges meet in the center and then fold the dough in half to give four layers (a four-fold).
Refrigerate the dough again and then roll out and do another four-fold. Repeat this step two more times. You now have classical puff pastry dough to use as you see fit.

name: Black-Eyed Peas and Kale
description: A tasty side dish of black-eyed peas and kale simmered with tomatoes, garlic, onion, cayenne, and bay leaf, suitable for vegans.
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil over medium heat for several minutes.
Add tomatoes and their juice, peas, cayenne and bay leaf. Simmer, covered, for 15 minutes.
Add kale and simmer uncovered until kale is tender but still green (5–10 minutes). Season to taste with salt and freshly-ground black pepper.

name: Tuscan Bean Soup
description: Cranberry or pinto beans and spelt simmer with sweet Italian sausage, kale, vegetables, herbs, and chicken stock in this Tuscan soup. Extra-virgin olive oil and freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese finish the bowl.

ingredients.text: 1 cup spelt or wheat berries (available at gourmet-food shops)
ingredients.name: spelt or wheat berry

ingredients.text: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil

ingredients.text: ½ pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: sweet Italian sausage

ingredients.text: 1 pound kale, preferably Tuscan, coarse stems removed, cut into thick ribbons
ingredients.name: kale

ingredients.text: 1 large rib celery, trimmed and diced
ingredients.name: celery

ingredients.text: 5 cups homemade chicken stock, or canned low-sodium stock, plus more if needed
ingredients.name: chicken stock

ingredients.text: 1 cup peeled, seeded, and diced tomatoes, or drained canned diced tomatoes
ingredients.name: tomato

ingredients.text: Sea salt and freshly ground pepper
ingredients.name: sea salt and pepper

ingredients.text: ½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
ingredients.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese

instructions: Soak beans and spelt overnight in separate bowls of cold water.
Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage and cook, stirring occasionally, until the meat begins to separate and brown (3–5 minutes).
Stir in kale, onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook until softened (about 10 minutes).
Add beans, spelt, chicken stock, and tomatoes, and bring to boil.
Stir in rosemary and sage, then reduce heat.
Simmer mixture for 60–70 minutes, until beans are tender; if soup is too thick, add chicken stock.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Ladle soup into bowls, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle on cheese. Serve immediately.

name: Ofe Owerri (Meat and Taro Soup with Dried Seafood)
description: A hearty Nigerian Igbo soup of pounded cocoyam, beef or goat, cow skin, stockfish, snails, dry fish, crayfish, and seasoned greens. The meat-and-cocoyam broth is cooked to your preferred consistency and served with eba, semo, starch, or wheat.

ingredients.text: Meat (beef or goat), cut in pieces
ingredients.name: meat

ingredients.text: Yellow and red habanero peppers, grated
ingredients.name: habanero pepper

ingredients.text: Nigerian pumpkin (ugwu) leaves, washed and minced
ingredients.name: pumpkin leaf

instructions: Put the cocoyam in a pot and cover it with water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and simmer until tender, topping up with additional water as necessary.
When the cocoyam is tender, drain and peel it. Pound it in a mortar until sticky, stretchy, and smooth.
Combine the beef, cow skin, stockfish, snails, and seasoning cube in a pot. Cook in its own juices for 15 minutes.
Add extra water and stir in the dryfish.
Stir in the crayfish and palm oil. Add the cocoyam mixture in small lumps; stir well and continue to cook over high heat until you get the consistency you want.
Stir very well, then add the grated habaneros, okazi, and ugwu leaves. Return to a boil and stir.
Adjust seasoning with salt and seasoning cubes as desired.
Stir and remove from the heat.
Serve with eba, semo, starch, or wheat.

name: Krummelpap (South African Maize Porridge)
description: A traditional South African maize porridge, slowly cooked with water and served at breakfast with milk, butter, and sugar or at dinner with gravy.

ingredients.text: 250 ml hot/boiling water, or more as needed
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Combine maize and salt in a large pot (like the one used for rice).
Add a third of the hot water, mixing with a fork to make little balls or crumbs.
Very gradually stir in more water. Don't add too much water.
Put the pot over low heat, and cover with a lid. Cook, stirring with a fork every 10 minutes.
Keep the lid on; it is the steam that cooks the maize.
Taste after 35 minutes to test if it is done.
If it still tastes like maize, continue cooking—the wonder of this porridge is that you can't overcook it, though you can burn it.
It takes approximately 50 minutes to cook.

name: Plantain Mosa
description: Nigerian plantain fritters made with mashed plantain, yeast, and flour, then fried until golden brown. They are often served as small finger foods at parties and weddings.
instructions: Combine your desired quantity of yeast with the warm water and a small pinch of flour, ensuring there are no lumps. Cover and let sit until foamy.
Peel the plantain with a knife, and mash it until almost smooth.
Combine flour and salt in a bowl. Mix well to combine.
Stir the yeast mixture into the flour mixture. Stir in the mashed plantain with a spatula. Cover with aluminum foil, and keep in a warm place for about 20 minutes until increased in volume.
Heat enough vegetable oil in a pot for deep-frying, aiming for a temperature of 350–375°F.
Scoop some of the batter with your fingers, and place it in the heated vegetable oil. Stir and fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove the mosa from the oil, drain away any excess, and serve.

name: Beer Batter
description: A light, crispy batter made with cornstarch, flour, and spices mixed with beer, perfect for coating vegetables, fish, or onion rings before deep-frying.
instructions: Stir together dry ingredients.
Stir in beer.
Mix together thoroughly.
Use in preparation of onion blooms.

name: Country Roast Chicken
description: A savory roast chicken seasoned with herbs and lemon, roasted until tender and finished with a rest before serving.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (3 lbs) broiler/fryer chicken, giblets removed
ingredients.name: broiler/fryer chicken

ingredients.text: ¼ cup Country Roast Chicken Seasoning
ingredients.name: country roast chicken seasoning

instructions: Loosen skin from chicken. Rub flesh with chicken seasoning.
Place lemon slices in the bottom of a roasting pan and place chicken on top.
Stuff chicken cavity with thyme, rosemary, and lemon wedges.
Place 1 tbsp butter under the skin of each breast.
Insert an oven-safe probe thermometer into the breast but not touching the butter.
Bake in a 325°F oven until breast internal temperature reaches 165°F and thigh meat reaches 170°F.
Cover with foil and let rest 10 minutes; serve.

name: Pizza Omelet
description: A quick omelet layered with tomato sauce, melted mozzarella, mushrooms, and green bell peppers.

ingredients.text: Salt, pepper, and other seasonings to taste (see tips below)
ingredients.name: seasoning

instructions: Mix spices and tomato sauce and allow to meld flavors while preparing the rest of the recipe.
Beat eggs well.
Heat a small skillet over low heat, sprayed with cooking spray.
Pour beaten eggs into skillet, then cover skillet.
Cook for 3 minutes. Eggs should be almost set.
Carefully flip omelet over. Cook another minute.
Combine mushrooms and peppers and cook 30 seconds in microwave oven.
Spread tomato-spice mix over omelet. Sprinkle cheese over tomato sauce. Top cheese with hot mushrooms and peppers.
Cover skillet. Cook another 2 minutes. Cheese should be melted.

name: Island Ceviche
description: A bright, citrus-marinated ceviche featuring pompano and mahi-mahi cured overnight in freshly squeezed lime, lemon, and orange juices.

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (8 ounces) pompano fillet, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: pompano

ingredients.text: 1 ea. (7 ounces) mahi-mahi fillet, thinly sliced
ingredients.name: mahi-mahi

instructions: Combine juices, salt, and pepper.
Pour into a gallon-size zip-top bag and add fish. Refrigerate overnight.
Serve.

name: Ponche de Crème
description: A creamy Caribbean Christmas beverage similar to eggnog, made with eggs, evaporated and condensed milks, aromatic bitters, nutmeg, and a splash of rum or brandy.

ingredients.text: 1½ cans (14 oz / 380 g) sweetened condensed milk, or to taste
ingredients.name: sweetened condensed milk

ingredients.text: ½ cup (120 ml) rum or brandy, or to taste
ingredients.name: rum

instructions: Beat eggs and lime peel until light and fluffy.
Add evaporated milk.
Sweeten to taste with condensed milk.
Add bitters, grated nutmeg and rum according to taste.
Remove lime peel and serve over crushed ice.

name: South African Traditional Fried Bread (Vetkoek)
description: Soft, bread-like South African fried dough with a crisp exterior, served with savory minced beef or turned into a dessert with cheese, syrup, honey, or jam.
instructions: Combine yeast, sugar, and warm water. Allow to stand for 5 minutes until the yeast softens and begins to bubble.
Sift the flour into a large bowl, and mix in the salt.
Mix the yeasted liquid to the flour, and stir until smooth. Stir or knead for 5–7 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Transfer the dough to a clean bowl, and cover with a clean cloth. Allow the dough to rise in a warm place for about 45 minutes, or until doubled.
Pinch off pieces of dough the size of tennis balls. Roll into balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying to 350°F (175°C). Fry 2–3 pieces of dough at a time in the hot oil about 3 minutes per side until golden brown all over.

name: Dum Aloo (Kashmiri Potato Curry)
description: A traditional Kashmiri potato curry made with baby potatoes first deep-fried, then cooked in a spiced onion-and-tomato gravy. It is served hot with cilantro and ginger strips.
instructions: Peel, wash, and prick baby potatoes all over with the help of a fork. In some recipes the potatoes are kept unpeeled; in this case, they should be washed properly.
Soak the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes.
Heat a sufficient amount of oil in a kadai, and deep-fry the potatoes over medium heat until golden-brown. Drain, place on absorbent paper, and keep aside.
Heat mustard oil in a pan to smoking point. Cool and heat again.
Add cumin seeds and asafoetida, and cook over medium heat until the cumin seeds change colour.
Add onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes, or until the onion turns light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute. Stir in a little water.
Add tomatoes and sauté for 1 minute. Add a little water and cook until the tomatoes turn pulpy.
Stir in red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and a little water.
Add the fried potatoes, stir to mix well, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add a little water and salt. Mix well and simmer for 5 minutes, or until the potatoes absorb the gravy.
Stir in garam masala powder.
Remove from heat and serve hot, garnished with cilantro leaves and ginger strips. It can also be served with jeera rice, fried rice, or rotis.

name: New Mexico Chili Verde
description: A classic New Mexican green chili stew made with green chiles, ground pork, and warm spices like cumin and oregano, simmered into a thinner, stew-like consistency. Often served in a bowl or ladled over burritos, enchiladas, and other dishes.

ingredients.text: 2 green bell peppers, chopped (not frequently used in New Mexico)
ingredients.name: green bell pepper

instructions: Combine bell peppers, chili peppers, water, tomatoes, bouillon, oregano, cumin, and coriander in a large pot. Cook over medium heat until peppers are tender.

Meanwhile, cook pork and onion in a skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, about ten minutes, or until pork is browned and crumbly. Drain pork and add to chile mixture. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Heat butter in the skillet over medium-low heat. Add flour. Cook, stirring frequently, until flour browns, about 2 minutes.
Add flour mixture to chile. Continue cooking and stirring until thickened to preference.

name: Noodles for Soup
description: A simple homemade egg noodle recipe from the 1881 Household Cyclopedia, made by kneading egg and flour into a stiff dough, rolling it thin, and slicing it into noodles for simmering in soup.
instructions: Beat the egg. Mix and knead in flour until you have a very stiff dough.
Roll the dough out into a thin sheet.
Sprinkle the dough with a good amount of flour to prevent it from sticking to itself. Tightly roll up the dough to make a log.
Use a sharp knife to cut the log cross-wise into thin slices, similar to how you would slice cabbage for slaw. Unroll the noodles and toss with flour.
Add the noodles to boiling soup. Simmer for 10 minutes.

name: Figgy Pudding
description: A rich British-style pudding of dried figs, apples, nuts, and warming spices, slowly steamed in the oven and drizzled with hard sauce.

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons rum extract (or flavored extract of your choice)
ingredients.name: rum extract

ingredients.text: 2 apples, peeled, cored, and finely chopped
ingredients.name: apple

ingredients.text: 2 pounds dried figs, ground or finely chopped
ingredients.name: dried fig

ingredients.text: Grated peel of 1 lemon and 1 orange
ingredients.name: lemon and orange peel

ingredients.text: 1 strip of bacon, finely crushed (optional; New England variant)
ingredients.name: bacon

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon of hard sauce, for drizzling
ingredients.name: hard sauce

instructions: Preheat oven to 325 °F. Generously grease an oven-proof 2-quart bowl or mold; set aside.
Cream together butter and shortening.
Gradually add sugar, egg yolks, milk, extract, apple, figs, lemon and orange peel.
Add next 6 ingredients, mixing well. Fold whipped egg whites into mixture.
Pour into prepared bowl or mold, place into large shallow pan, and place on middle rack in oven.
Fill the shallow pan half-full with boiling water, and slowly steam pudding in oven at 325 °F for 4 hours, replacing water as needed.

name: Scheiterhaufen (Austrian Bread Pudding)
description: A traditional Austrian sweet dish of stale white bread layered with apples and peaches, soaked in a milk, egg, and rum mixture, spiced with cinnamon and sugar, and baked until golden.

ingredients.text: 4 tsp (20 ml) rum or a few drops of rum aroma
ingredients.name: rum

instructions: Wash the apples and peaches, and peel them if desired. Cut them into slices approximately ¼ inch (1 cm) thick.
Cut the bread into slices about the same size as the fruit.
Pour the milk into a bowl and add the eggs. Mix well. Then take the slices of bread and let them soak in the mixture for a few seconds. This will take longer if you use stale rather than fresh bread.
Mix the refined sugar and the cinnamon in a cup or a small bowl.

Grease an ovenproof dish, then layer the slices, bread, and fruit alternately in the dish. Sprinkle a bit of the sugar-cinnamon mixture on top of every layer. For the best result, start and end with a layer of bread. You can decide whether you want an apple and a peach layer or whether you would like to mix the different kinds of fruit.
Scatter a few flakes of butter on top, and put the dish into the oven for 45 minutes at 180°C/350°F.
Enjoy!

name: Akarubi (Rwandan Grilled Banana)
description: A sweet and smoky Rwandan dessert of caramelized grilled bananas, optionally finished with cinnamon and honey.

ingredients.text: Butter or vegetable oil, for grilling
ingredients.name: butter or vegetable oil

instructions: Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Place the peeled bananas directly on the grill grates or grill pan.
Grill the bananas for 2–3 minutes on each side, or until they are lightly charred and softened.
Remove the grilled bananas from the heat and transfer them to a serving plate.
Optionally, sprinkle the grilled bananas with cinnamon for added flavor.
Serve hot as a dessert or snack. If desired, drizzle the grilled bananas with honey or maple syrup for additional sweetness.

name: Khachapuri (Georgian Cheese Bread)
description: A traditional Georgian stuffed bread filled with a rich blend of feta, smoked provolone, and Parmesan cheeses. Golden-baked and served hot, it's a hearty, cheesy treat perfect for any occasion.

ingredients.text: 2 cups flour, plus more to dust counter top, hands, etc.
ingredients.name: flour

ingredients.text: 8 oz feta cheese, grated or cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: feta cheese

ingredients.text: 12 oz smoked provolone cheese, grated or cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: smoked provolone cheese

ingredients.text: 2 oz grated Parmesan cheese, grated or cut into small pieces
ingredients.name: parmesan cheese

instructions: Add sugar to warm water in a large bowl. Add yeast and wait 5 minutes.
Add eggs, flour, and salt. Mix with fork until dough becomes too stiff.
Knead with hands until smooth, approximately five minutes, on floured surface. Add flour as needed if dough sticks to your hands.
Let dough rise in greased bowl for 30 minutes in a warm place or until doubled in size. Punch down dough, and let it rise again.
While dough is rising, mix ingredients for filling in separate bowl.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
When dough is ready, divide in half. With a rolling pin, flatten dough until it is the size and shape of your cookie sheet. Carefully lay flattened dough on greased cookie sheet.

Cover dough with cheese filling prepared as above, spreading evenly to within ½ inch of the edge of dough. Roll out the remaining dough to the same size as shape. Cover cheese filling with second layer of dough. Moisten the edges of the dough with water and press to seal.
Bake at 350°F for 10 minutes. Butter the top layer of dough liberally. Return Khachapuri to oven and continue cooking until dough is golden brown.
Cut with a pizza cutter or knife. Serve hot, cold, or reheated in the microwave!

name: Fruit for the Day Smoothie
description: A refreshing fruit smoothie blending mandarin oranges, frozen bananas, and strawberries with milk for a quick, nutritious treat.

ingredients.text: 1 can (397 g / 14 oz) Mandarin oranges (including syrup)
ingredients.name: mandarin orange

instructions: Add all ingredients to a blender in the order listed above.
Hold down the lid, and blend on low speed for 30 seconds.
Blend on high speed for 1 minute.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.

name: Tuwo Shinkafa (Nigerian Mashed Rice)
description: A traditional Nigerian swallow dish made from mashed non-parboiled short-grain rice, shaped into a soft dough and served hot as an accompaniment for soups and stews.

ingredients.text: 500 g (2 milk tin cups) short-grain non-parboiled rice
ingredients.name: rice

ingredients.text: Water (about twice the volume of the rice)
ingredients.name: water

instructions: Wash the rice thoroughly, then drain.
Add water to pot and bring to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice to the pot of boiling water.
Simmer the rice until the water is absorbed and the rice is soft and sticky. If the rice hasn't softened when all the water is gone, add additional water as needed.
Use the spatula to thoroughly mash the soft rice until it forms a soft dough.
Mold into desired container and allow to take shape of the container or wrap inside nylon.
Serve hot with your preferred soup.

name: Hard Tack
description: A simple, durable cracker made from just flour and water, historically used on long sea voyages and military campaigns. It keeps for months when stored dry and is typically dunked in liquid before eating.
instructions: Mix all the ingredients into a dough and press onto a greased cookie sheet to a thickness of ½ inch.
Bake in a preheated oven at 400°F (205°C) for half an hour. Don't cut now.
Remove from oven, and cut dough into 3-inch squares. Punch four rows of holes, four holes per row into the dough (a fork works nicely).
Flip the crackers and return to the oven for another half hour.

name: Rice and Lentils (Mejadra)
description: A simple Middle Eastern staple of lentils and rice seasoned with baharat, cumin, and cardamom, topped with crispy golden fried onions.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (80 g / 2.8 oz) uncooked rice or bulgur
ingredients.name: rice

instructions: Fry the lentils in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the first beans show signs of scorching.
Add salt, baharat, cumin, and ground cardamom to taste.
Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes or until all the water is absorbed by the lentils.
Fry the rice in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the grains change colour.
Add salt, black or white pepper, and ground cardamom.
Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer. After 5 minutes turn the heat off, and leave standing for another 10 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips (about 0.5x4 cm / 0.2x1.6 in).
Fry the onion in olive oil until crisp and deeply golden brown (this may take a while but will result in much fuller flavor).
Mix the lentils and rice, and top with the fried onion. Use 2 parts lentils to 1 part rice for a moist consistency.

name: Bran Muffins
description: A delicious batch of classic bran muffins made with wheat bran, buttermilk, and brown sugar, perfect for a warm breakfast.
instructions: Stir wheat bran and buttermilk together in a mixing bowl.
Cream together egg, brown sugar and margarine in another mixing bowl.
Combine remaining ingredients in a third bowl. Add to batter, and stir just to moisten.
Fill muffin cups ¾ full.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes.

name: Róbó (Fried Egusi Paste)
description: A Nigerian delicacy of fried melon seed paste seasoned with cayenne and onion, with a crusty exterior and a soft center. It can be enjoyed as a snack or served with pap, garri, cereals, and other meals.
instructions: Pick out all dirt and debris from the melon seeds.
Heat a clean, dry frying pan over low heat.
Add the seeds. Dry-fry them, stirring frequently, until golden all over. Do not let burn. Remove from heat and let cool.
Combine the toasted melon seeds and cayenne pepper. Grind to a smooth paste—no water is needed.
Blend the onions and spring onions to a fine smooth paste in a separate bowl.
Place the melon seed paste on a clean dry tray. Add about one-third of the onion paste, and gradually knead with both hands until the mixture begins to release oil.
Pour the released oil into a separate bowl, and reserve it for frying.
Continue to knead in the onion paste until it is used up and the melon seed paste does not release any more oil. By this time, the mixture should have become a semi-solid paste.
Season with salt.
Cut the paste into small pieces, and create any shape that takes your fancy.
Heat the reserved oil in a clean pan over medium heat. A deeper pan is preferable.
Add the róbó pieces to the hot oil, and fry until each piece develops a crusty outer shell with a relatively soft inside.
Remove from the oil, and drain away any excess.
Eat as a snack or an accompaniment to pap, garri, custard, oats, etc.

name: Fresh Herb and Cheese Ravioli Filling
description: Ricotta or cottage cheese, blue cheese, mozzarella, eggs, and fresh herbs blend into a flavorful ravioli filling. Serve with tomato sauce and spring vegetables.

ingredients.text: 4 oz (½ cup) ricotta or cottage cheese
ingredients.name: ricotta or cottage cheese

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp fresh finely-chopped herbs (basil, chives, parsley, thyme)
ingredients.name: fresh herb

instructions: Beat eggs and place in a bowl.
Beat in the cheeses with a fork until well blended.
Mix in the herbs and seasoning.
Refrigerate until the pasta dough is rolled out.

name: Radish Tart
description: A tasty and colorful pie with fresh red radishes and yellow cheese, best served hot from the oven.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (4 oz) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere cheese, divided (Cheddar is also acceptable)
ingredients.name: cheese

ingredients.text: ½–1 small bunch of red radishes
ingredients.name: red radish

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).

Sift and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; toss the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
Turn the dough into a 9-inch round pie pan. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
